Kolo Muani scored and assisted in a 2-1 win at AZ, keeping Juventus unbeaten in the Europa League with 10 points from four games. Juventus Women lost 6-0 at home to OL Lyonnes in the Champions League; OH Leuven visit Biella next on November 18. The Lead Six points off fourth, and a fortnight to fix it Bremer's header rescued a point in Florence, but another uneven night left Spalletti searching for consistency as the pressure follows Juventus into the international break. J uventus left Florence on Sunday night with a point, a grievance and a familiar diagnosis. Juventus needed Gleison Bremer ’s 66th-minute header to draw 2-2 at Fiorentina, having twice come from behind at the Artemio Franchi. The result left them seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth-placed AC Milan and 11 behind leaders Lazio after 11 rounds. The match followed a pattern Luciano Spalletti has described all autumn. Fiorentina scored after four minutes, Mateo Pellegrino heading in from a corner. Nick Woltemade levelled on 32 minutes from Randal Kolo Muani’s dribble and cross. Alieu Njie restored the lead on 54 minutes, tapping in after Guglielmo Vicario parried a shot, before Bremer beat David De Gea to a Douglas Luiz corner ( Juventus.com match report ). There was controversy too. Juventus wanted a penalty when the ball struck João Mário’s arm, and Radu Drăgușin’s 82nd-minute header for Fiorentina was ruled out for a two-handed push on Bremer. Juventus had complaints about referee Andrea Colombo. Asked about the penalty replay, Spalletti said he did not need one: he had already seen it on the pitch ( Football Italia ). “We tend to drown in a glass of water sometimes, and lose confidence in the way we play.” Luciano Spalletti to DAZN Italia, November 8 He added that his side “just can’t seem to be consistent throughout a match, as a team or as individuals.” A day later, asked about the media criticism, he struck a different tone: “Every time, you always ask the same questions, and this motivates us,” he told reporters, adding that he was “super motivated” ( beIN Sports ). What the numbers say Since the start of October Juventus have alternated almost perfectly in the league: a draw at Cagliari, a 3-0 home defeat by Lazio, a 2-0 win at Lecce, a 2-0 loss at Genoa, a 2-0 win over Napoli and Sunday’s draw. That is eight points from six games. In Europe they are unbeaten, with 10 points from four Europa League matches. All five league wins have come with clean sheets, a Stats Perform figure reported by SoccerNews after the Napoli game. The trouble starts when the first goal goes against them. In Florence it took four minutes, from a set piece, and the response was spirited rather than controlled: two equalisers, never a lead. Key facts Serie A 7th, 18 points from 11 games (W5 D3 L3), goal difference +3 The gap 6 points to 4th (AC Milan, 24); 11 to 1st (Lazio, 29) Europa League 10 points from 4 games (W3 D1), 11 scored, 4 conceded Last ten, all competitions W5 D3 L2 Next Venezia at home, Sunday, November 22, 3:30 a.m. Pacific The boardroom view The club’s public line has not moved. A Tuttomercatoweb analysis published on Thursday ( via Napoli Magazine ) says the club has confirmed its “full trust” in the coach, yet describes him as “increasingly alone and besieged”. Antonio Conte , it says, remains a ghost over Turin, and Zinedine Zidane has spoken of wanting to coach Juventus one day. Late October was more fraught. Sports Mole , citing La Stampa, reported on October 29 that a change “could happen quickly”, with Conte the favourite and Stefano Pioli and Didier Deschamps also named. Calciomercato framed Napoli, AZ and Fiorentina as a three-game test ( Get Italian Football News ). Juventus took seven points from nine: a pass, if not a convincing one. CEO Giovanni Carnevali , confirmed in post at the November 3 shareholders’ meeting, said in September that changing coaches “is not in my nature” ( Football Italia ). Tuttomercatoweb reads the January window as the real verdict: whether Spalletti gets the signings he wants will show whether he is still at the centre of the project. The two weeks ahead Help is coming from the treatment room. Tuttosport reports that Francisco Conceição, out since dislocating his left shoulder against Lazio on October 18, trained with the group on Wednesday. Nico González is recovering from a soleus strain and Andrea Cambiaso is recovering from fatigue; both are targeted for Venezia. Kenan Yildiz is not expected back before early December. Spalletti gave the players not on international duty four days off after Wednesday’s session, with work resuming on Monday. Venezia, 19th with six points, visit the Allianz Stadium on Sunday, November 22. On paper it is the kindest fixture of the autumn. Under this much scrutiny, it is also the one Juventus can least afford to fumble. Second feature Kolo Muani's night in Alkmaar, and the warning beneath it A goal and an assist won a tight game in the Netherlands, but AZ created the better chances and had a stoppage-time equaliser ruled out. Juventus won 2-1 at AZ last Thursday, and the night belonged to Randal Kolo Muani . He set up Teun Koopmeiners on 19 minutes, a goal against the club where the Dutchman made his name, with his brother Peer in the AZ starting line-up. On 37 minutes Kolo Muani finished himself after an exchange with Nick Woltemade. Flashscore named him man of the match. The underlying numbers were less flattering. Per beIN Sports , Juventus produced 0.57 expected goals to AZ’s 2.1, and only 0.12 after the break. Mexx Meerdink pulled one back on 88 minutes, and in stoppage time Guglielmo Vicario made what Football Italia called an extraordinary save before Mees de Wit’s finish from the rebound was ruled out for offside. The win ended AZ’s 17-match unbeaten home run in Europe, according to Flashscore, and kept Juventus unbeaten in the competition with a goal difference of plus seven. The top eight after eight matchdays go straight to the round of 16. Omonia visit Turin on November 26 ( UEFA fixtures ). Scouting the Next Opponent Venezia: bottom-three, but no longer pointless Davide Nicola has given the Lagunari a pulse. Juventus must break a side built to defend. Venezia arrive in Turin 19th with six points from 11 games (two wins, nine defeats, goal difference minus 13), according to FotMob . They lost their first six league games before turning to Davide Nicola , the specialist in relegation escapes, in mid-October ( Washington Post ). Under Nicola they have beaten Napoli 1-0 and Udinese 2-1 at home, and lost 1-0 at Genoa, 2-0 at home to Inter and 1-0 at Como. Six points from five games is relegation-survival form, and the narrow margins tell you how they play: compact, combative and hard to open up. Who to stop Akor Adams, the striker signed from Sevilla in the summer for a reported €16 million plus add-ons, has two league goals. Antoine Hainaut, with two goals and two assists, is their most creative outlet and has created the most big chances in the squad. Captain Gianluca Busio also has two assists, and Albion Rrahmani takes the most shots per game. FotMob lists Andrea Adorante (back) and Marin Šverko (thigh) as out, with Pasquale Mazzocchi, Thierry Correia and Bartol Franjić doubtful. No Venezia suspensions are listed. Where Juventus can hurt them Nobody at Juventus is suspended after round 11 ( JuveFC, on the sporting judge’s November 10 rulings ), though Kolo Muani, Bremer and Cabal each took their first booking of the season in Florence. The test is patience: against Napoli the breakthrough came only on 70 minutes. Set pieces may matter: Bremer, a centre-back, leads the squad with three league goals, and his equaliser in Florence came from a corner. Venezia at a glance Position 19th, 6 points (W2 D0 L9), goal difference minus 13 Coach Davide Nicola, appointed in October Danger men Akor Adams (2 goals); Antoine Hainaut (2 goals, 2 assists); Gianluca Busio (2 assists) Out Adorante (back), Šverko (thigh) Doubtful Mazzocchi, Correia, Franjić Head to head (FotMob) Juventus 2 wins, 2 draws; Venezia 0 wins Transfer News Spalletti's January list: a striker and a left-back With Yildiz still sidelined and the attack thin, the names are flowing. None has gone beyond the rumour stage. Juve Oggi reported on Thursday that Luciano Spalletti has two precise requests for January: a striker and a left-back. The striker names in circulation are Gianluca Scamacca of Atalanta, Alexander Sørloth of Atlético Madrid and Folarin Balogun of Monaco, a shortlist also carried in a OneFootball roundup ( via Yahoo ). Of those, only Scamacca has a reported structure: Tuttojuve says Juventus are considering a loan with an option to make it permanent ( JuveFC ). Certainty: rumour, single-sourced, no talks reported. For the left side, Juve Oggi cites La Gazzetta dello Sport on Manchester City’s Rayan Aït-Nouri, possibly on loan, with Nicolás Tagliafico and Maxi Araújo as alternatives. These are early names, not negotiations. Money frames all of it. Shareholders approved a capital increase of up to €250 million on November 3, but chief financial officer Stefano Cerrato told the meeting that the outlook for those funds is tied to sporting performance ( Tuttosport ). Vicario's option and Calhanoglu's contract On the permanent front, JuveFC reported on Wednesday that Juventus are increasingly considering triggering the €8 million purchase option on Guglielmo Vicario , on loan from Tottenham, and that Spurs are not keen to take him back ( JuveFC via Yahoo ). No primary outlet is named, so treat it as a lead. His two match-saving interventions this week make the case. Calciomercato reports that Juventus will keep working towards Hakan Calhanoglu , whose Inter contract has not been renewed, with a free transfer the scenario ( JuveFC via Yahoo ). Certainty: interest reported by one outlet; no talks. Spalletti is weighing how to fit them into an attack that has found goals hard to come by in Serie A. Randal Kolo Muani has been used on the right of the front three lately, and Spalletti praised his willingness to play anywhere after Fiorentina. Kolo Muani himself said his position does not matter as long as he has space to attack ( Juventus.com press room ). He has four goals in all competitions, level with Woltemade. That leaves the middle. Tuttosport reports Spalletti is considering Nico González, described as the squad’s best header of the ball, as a central striker for Venezia, alongside Kolo Muani and Woltemade. Goal listed a 4-3-3 in Florence; against Napoli, Football Italia saw Juventus switch to a 3-5-2 shape after half-time. Rotation and form Europe has been a proving ground. At AZ, Pape Matar Sarr, Lloyd Kelly, Federico Gatti and Andrea Cambiaso all started, and Juventus won. Vicario has been the standout of the week in both games. Woltemade’s goal in Florence was his first in the league, and Bremer’s three league goals make him the squad’s top Serie A scorer from centre-back. With captain Manuel Locatelli out until the new year, the midfield has leaned on Douglas Luiz, whose corners produced Bremer’s equaliser in Florence and Cabal’s header against the post versus Napoli. Koopmeiners has scored in both competitions this season. Juventus Next Gen lost 4-0 at Lecco on Sunday, November 8, in Serie C Group A ( JuveFC ). Massimo Brambilla’s side have won just one of their last 12 matches and sit 18th of 20 with 10 points from 11 games ( Italian League ). Before that came a 1-1 home draw with Pro Vercelli on November 2. They host Treviso on Sunday, November 15 (17:30 in Italy, 8:30 a.m. Pacific), then visit Giana Erminio on November 21. Ferrero told shareholders the club wants a dedicated stadium near Turin for Next Gen and Juventus Women. Under 20 and the youth sides The Under 20s drew 0-0 with Torino in the Primavera 1 derby on November 1 ( Juventus.com ). In the youth ranks the week of October 26 brought a 3-2 Under 18 win over Como, a 2-2 Under 17 derby draw with Torino and a 2-0 Under 19 women’s win over Inter ( club roundup ). Jeff Ekhator earned an Italy Under 21 call-up after coming off the bench in both of the first team’s games this week. Loan watch Loïs Openda (Lyon) suffered a hairline fracture of his right fibula at Lens in October; he had one goal in four Ligue 1 appearances before it ( Gradient Sports ). Jonathan David (Atlético Madrid) has three goals and three assists in 11 appearances ( VAVEL ). No fresh update this week on Fabio Miretti (Beşiktaş), Michele Di Gregorio (Bournemouth) or Vasilije Adžić (Sassuolo). Juventus Women Lyonnes deliver a hard lesson in Turin Two league wins lifted the mood. Then the eight-time European champions arrived. Juventus Women lost 6-0 at home to OL Lyonnes on Wednesday, November 11, in the fourth round of the Women’s Champions League league phase. Marie-Antoinette Katoto opened the scoring on 31 minutes and Wendie Renard added the sixth in stoppage time ( ESPN ). Lyonnes came in on seven points from three games, one ahead of their Italian hosts ( UEFA ). Isaac Guerrero’s side now have six points from four (two wins, two defeats) and were eighth of 18 in ESPN’s table after the round. League form The week had started well. Cecilia Salvai scored the winner in a 2-1 home win over Sassuolo on Saturday, November 7 ( Juventus.com via Yahoo ). That followed a 2-1 win at Fiorentina on November 2, captain Martina Rosucci’s 200th appearance, which she said mattered “after three defeats” ( Juventus.com ). Salvai had warned that Lyonnes would be “a completely different affair”. Next up in Europe is OH Leuven in Biella on Wednesday, November 18, then Paris Saint-Germain away on December 16 ( UEFA ). The Lead Inter give Como the ball and take the points Chivu's side had 43 percent of the ball and still controlled a top-four clash. The break arrives with Inter a point off Lazio, and Atalanta next. F or a team that came into the weekend with the highest average possession in Serie A, Sunday's win over Como was a change of character. Inter let Cesc Fàbregas 's side have 57 percent of the ball, struck twice in the first 19 minutes and then protected a 2-0 lead at San Siro with little fuss, according to SempreInter's match data . Francesco Pio Esposito opened the scoring after 12 minutes, meeting Djed Spence 's cross. Seven minutes later Marcus Thuram finished at the near post past Robert Sánchez after Álex Valle failed to deal with Piotr Zielinski 's ball across goal ( Football Italia , Flashscore ). It was Thuram's sixth Serie A goal of the season. The numbers show how one-sided the contest was despite the possession split. Inter had 14 shots to Como's five and an expected-goals tally of 1.86 against 0.23, with 10 of their attempts from inside the box. Josep Martínez made his first real save after 63 minutes, from a bouncing shot by Nico Paz , who later struck the woodwork on 84 minutes. Cristian Chivu called it complete. “Today we played well in every aspect,” he said, adding that his players had shown “a performance of maturity and quality” ( AFP via theScore ). A week earlier, after the derby defeat, he had admitted to “the wrong approach.” Two clean, controlled wins later, that sounds like a long time ago. “We counter-attacked with ferocity and were clinical in front of goal.” Cristian Chivu, after Inter 2-0 Como Why giving up the ball worked Como are built to keep the ball and to press high, and Inter's own pre-match analysis had flagged the goals they win from turnovers. Chivu's answer was to sit off, keep the middle closed and go direct when the ball was won. Both goals came from quick attacks, before Como had settled; after that, Inter could defend in shape and break when it suited them. The back three of Manuel Akanji , Alessandro Bastoni and Carlos Augusto kept Anastasios Douvikas , who scored a hat-trick at Lens the previous week, on the fringes. Goal's ratings credited Akanji's positioning with starving him of service. Como arrived on a six-match winning run, per AFP, and left fifth, a point behind Milan. Esposito, booked for what he called a foul he “had to make,” said he had been waiting for a goal at San Siro but that “the team's performance matters more.” Thuram spoke of “three important points, in a home game in front of our fans and against a very strong opponent” ( Inter.it ). Key facts: Inter 2-0 Como Sun Nov 8, Serie A, San Siro: Inter 2-0 Como (Esposito 12', Thuram 19'). Referee: Daniele Chiffi Possession 43-57, shots 14-5, expected goals 1.86-0.23, per SempreInter Serie A: 2nd, 28 pts from 11 games (W9 D1 L1), 1 behind Lazio, 1 ahead of Roma Champions League: 15th of 36 on 6 pts; Stuttgart visit on Wed Nov 25 Next: Atalanta away, Sun Nov 22, New Balance Arena, Bergamo The race at the break Four sides are now within five points. Lazio , still unbeaten under Gattuso, drew 1-1 at Napoli on Sunday, where on-loan Inter midfielder Davide Frattesi scored their goal; they lead on 29 ( AGI ). Roma are third on 27 after beating Sassuolo 3-0, and AC Milan fourth on 24 after winning 2-1 at Genoa. That run ended at Monza, where Nikola Krstovic scored after 49 minutes from a parried Lorenzo Bernasconi cross and later hit the woodwork, with goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi credited for protecting the 1-0 win. Como drop to fifth in Serie A on 23 points, one behind fourth-placed Milan and six behind leaders Lazio. Sporting director Carlalberto Ludi says January will be quiet and that Jacobo Ramón stays at Como for the whole season. The Lead Back to earth at San Siro: what Inter exposed, and what the break must fix Four days after a record 9-1 at Lens, Como were second best in a 2-0 defeat at Inter that ended a six-game winning run. Fabregas now has a fortnight to steady his midfield and get his injured forwards back before Cagliari. F our days is a long time in a debut Champions League season. On Wednesday, November 4, Como scored nine times at Lens. On Sunday evening at San Siro they managed a single shot on target, lost 2-0 to Inter and watched a six-match winning run end inside the first 19 minutes. Francesco Pio Esposito opened the scoring after 12 minutes, set up by Djed Spence according to Fox Sports' box score , and Marcus Thuram doubled the lead seven minutes later. Those were the only goals. The gap in chances was wider than the scoreline: Inter had 14 shots to five, and four on target to Como's one. Como had the ball, and it did not help them. They kept 57 per cent of possession and completed 92 per cent of their 292 passes, per VAVEL's match data . Inter let them circulate it, pressed the loose touches and attacked the space behind. Cesc Fabregas named the problem himself on DAZN: "Mi fa male come abbiamo perso, con palloni persi con troppa facilità" (what hurts is how we lost, giving the ball away far too easily), per Fantacalcio . He added that the confidence of recent weeks simply "wasn't there". Key facts Result: Inter 2-0 Como, Sunday, November 8, San Siro (Serie A, matchday 11) Goals: Pio Esposito 12', Thuram 19' Como (4-2-3-1): Sánchez; Couto, Ramón, Kempf, Valle; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas Changes: Ricci for Perrone 46', Smolčić for Baturina 46', Liberali for Couto 74', Caqueret for Da Cunha 74', Kaiki for Valle 74' (per CalcioMercato.com ) Stats: possession 57-43 to Como; shots 5-14; on target 1-4 (VAVEL) Crowd: 77,593, including 1,545 in the away section (CalcioMercato.com) Run ended: six straight wins in all competitions, from Fiorentina (October 18) to Lens (November 4) Table: Como 5th, 23 points, six behind Lazio The half-time rethink At half-time Fabregas took off Máximo Perrone and Martin Baturina and sent on Samuele Ricci and Ivan Smolčić . This was not a chase. "Ho cercato più solidità con Smolcic... Serviva più fisicità" (I wanted more solidity with Smolčić; we needed more physicality), he said, in the same interview. In his press conference he was blunter still. With only two fit central defenders, he said, "when I saw that this time we might be the ones conceding nine, my responsibility was to fix the defensive phase," per SOS Fanta . Trevoh Chalobah was among the absentees. The second half was steadier. Marc-Oliver Kempf stopped a Thuram breakaway around the 81st minute, and Como's best moments came late: a Jacobo Ramón header over the bar and a curling Nico Paz shot that struck the woodwork five minutes from time. Josep Martínez was rarely extended. “Inter deserved the victory, we have to shake their hands and move on.” Cesc Fabregas, after the defeat (via Football Italia ) The verdict The Italian press was not gentle. CalcioMercato.com gave Fabregas 4.5 under the headline "Fabregas torna sulla terra" (Fabregas comes back down to earth). Tuttosport's ratings were headlined "Ramón horror". Sky Sport Italia were kinder, at 5.5 for the coach. The one starter most outlets agreed had held his level was Luis Milla , rated 6 by both Sky and CalcioMercato. Fabregas leaned on his words afterwards: Milla, he said, keeps telling the squad they are "troppo buoni" (too nice). Inter committed 13 fouls to Como's handful, the coach noted, "and they do it well". Inter's Manuel Akanji twisted the knife this week. "What phenomenon? I've played against them four times and won all four," the defender said, per Sports Mole . "They still have a lot to learn." What it means, and what comes next The table cost is modest but real. Como slipped from fourth to fifth on 23 points, six behind leaders Lazio and one behind Milan in fourth, with Frosinone three points back in sixth, per Sky Sport Italia's standings . Fourth is the last guaranteed Champions League place, and it is a point away. The international break arrives at a useful moment. Como do not play again until Cagliari visit the Sinigaglia on Saturday, November 21 (6:00 a.m. Pacific). AEK Athens follow in the Champions League three days later, then Juventus on November 29. Fabregas said before the Inter game that Chalobah has "two weeks to prepare for Cagliari", per Fantacalcio . Assane Diao is chasing the same date after a hamstring strain, and Moise Kean is targeting Juventus, per Gazzetta's round-up via TuttoCagliari . The number Fabregas will watch most closely is 1,103: Tasos Douvikas 's minutes so far, by Gazzetta's count, in a piece headlined "emergenza attacco". With Kean and Diao out there has been no understudy at centre-forward, and the Greek is now away for two Nations League matches. San Siro was a reminder of the ceiling. Maldini is the man to stop: five league goals already, a career best, per TuttoMercatoWeb . The other key figure is at the other end. Elia Caprile has four clean sheets and was man of the match against Frosinone, tipping a shot onto the bar, per Flashscore . Cagliari have scored only ten league goals, so a goalkeeper-led, low-scoring game is their likeliest route to a result. Cagliari at a glance Position: 9th, 16 points (W5 D1 L5), goals 10-15 Coach and shape: Fabio Pisacane; 3-4-2-1 in the last game, a back four at Lazio Top scorer: Daniel Maldini, 5 league goals Last five: L 0-4 at Monza, L 0-2 v Bologna, L 2-4 at Roma, L 1-2 at Lazio, W 1-0 v Frosinone Away record: W3 L3, scored 7, conceded 11 Injuries: Aurelio, Idrissi, Mina, Obert, Winks, Fadera, Felici, Nzola, Trepy (Unione Sarda, November 10) Last meetings: Cagliari 1-2 Como (March 7, 2026); Como 0-0 Cagliari (November 8, 2025); Como 3-1 Cagliari (May 10, 2025) The vulnerability is obvious from the record. Cagliari conceded four at Monza and four at Roma in October, 12 goals in four straight defeats before the Frosinone win, per statz.ai's results list . Their treatment room is fuller than Como's: Unione Sarda listed nine absentees on Tuesday, including striker M'Bala Nzola and Como loanee Alieu Fadera , both doubtful. Como are unbeaten in their last three meetings with Cagliari. They won 2-1 in Sardinia in March, Baturina and Da Cunha scoring either side of a Sebastiano Esposito equaliser, per CalcioMercato.com . The one blank was a 0-0 at the Sinigaglia a year ago, which is the warning against assuming a home win. Transfer News Ludi sets the tone: a quiet January, and two 'signings' from the treatment room Como's sporting director says the squad needs completing, not rebuilding, and that the biggest January additions will be Kean, Diao and Jesús Rodríguez returning from injury. Como 's sporting director Carlalberto Ludi used the Social Football Summit this week to lower expectations for January. "Siamo molto soddisfatti della rosa," he told Gianluca Di Marzio : the club is very happy with the squad and knows which areas "can be completed, I don't say improved". His summary: "non faremo tanto" (we won't do much). He went further with CalcioMercato.com . January, he said, could effectively be the recovery of Moise Kean , Assane Diao and Jesús Rodríguez , and there will be no "operazioni incredibili". Players with little game time could leave. If an opportunity appears and there is a need, Como will act. Read that as the shape of the window rather than a promise of silence. The forward line is the obvious pressure point: Kean has barely played since his €40m move from Fiorentina, Diao is injured and Douvikas has carried the attack. That is where the one live rumour sits. Paz and Ramón: the Real Madrid buy-backs, explained Both stay this season. What happens in summer 2027 depends on Madrid, and on how much Como can make the most of the time in between. Every November brings a fresh round of Nico Paz to Real Madrid stories. Ludi joked this week that every November and every March brings talk of Madrid taking him back, per Sports Illustrated. The facts are settled. In June Como bought him outright for about €60m, with Madrid keeping a buy-back for 2027-28 reported at €80m, per Goal Italia and Calcio e Finanza . Fabrizio Romano was categorical on November 7: "a gennaio non va da nessuna parte" (in January he is going nowhere), noting that no clause applies mid-season, per SOS Fanta . Ludi called Paz "100% a Como player" and said a Madrid buy-back "would be a sale that would enhance our work", per Sports Illustrated . Jacobo Ramón is the quieter version of the same story. Madrid also hold a buy-back on the centre-back, and Matteo Moretto reported in September that Madrid expect to use it for the summer 2027 window, per Sports Mole . Ludi closed the January door this week: "sicuramente resterà con noi per tutta la stagione" (he will definitely stay with us all season), per Di Marzio . Ramón, called up by Spain for the first time this week, credited Como's coach. "I left Real Madrid to carve out a place for myself at the top level," he said, per Football Italia via Yahoo . "Cesc believed in me straight away." Camello: the striker Como keep coming back to Rayo Vallecano's forward is the one name linked for January. Certainty: concrete interest, not talks. Sergio Camello of Rayo Vallecano has been followed by Como for months as cover for Douvikas and Kean, according to CalcioMercato.com, relayed by Labaro Viola and Sportmediaset . A January deal would take about €10m. His contract runs to 2027. The complication is that Atlético Madrid reportedly retain a buy-back option on the 25-year-old. No bid has been reported and Ludi did not name him. Treat this as concrete interest from a club with a clear need, not a deal in motion. Ins & Outs In (summer 2026): Nico Paz (Real Madrid, permanent, about €60m); Moise Kean (Fiorentina, €5m loan plus €35m obligation); Trevoh Chalobah (Chelsea, £25.7m plus add-ons); Luis Milla (Getafe); Mattia Liberali (Catanzaro); Kaiki Bruno (Cruzeiro, loan with obligation); Yan Couto (Dortmund, loan); Willy Kambwala (Villarreal, loan); Samuele Ricci (Milan, loan); Robert Sánchez (Chelsea, loan) Out: Engelhardt (Freiburg); Vojvoda (Udinese); Posch (Mainz); Diego Carlos (Fenerbahçe); Audero (Rayo Vallecano); Morata (Leganés, loan); Fadera (Cagliari, loan with option); Van der Brempt (Sassuolo); Kühn (Gladbach, loan); Azón (Getafe); Cutrone (Monza); Sergi Roberto and Alberto Moreno released Window totals: €137.7m spent, €13.5m in sales (Calcio e Finanza) Since the window: Douvikas renewed to 2031 (official, October); no new signings until January 2 The Rumour Mill Smaller live threads, with where each one sits on the paper trail. Sergio Camello (Rayo Vallecano), in: concrete interest; about €10m; Atlético buy-back a complication (CalcioMercato.com, Sportmediaset). Nico Paz, out to Real Madrid: not before summer 2027; buy-back reported at €80m (Romano, Goal Italia). Official structure, no move in January. Jacobo Ramón, out to Real Madrid: buy-back exists; stays all season, per Ludi (Di Marzio). Summer 2027 open. Máximo Perrone, renewal: advanced talks; Sky's Demicheli said Como were "a un passo" in October; no announcement yet ( Napoli Magazine/Sky ). Fringe players, out: Ludi confirmed some low-minute players could leave in January; no names given. Martin Baturina: no new links this week; Leeds had a bid of about €30m refused in January 2026 ( Goal ). Background only. The Squad Fabregas waits on four forwards and a defender Chalobah is closest to a return, Diao is racing for Cagliari and Kean is aiming at Juventus. Douvikas has done the rest. Availability Trevoh Chalobah (defender): closest to returning; targeted for Cagliari, November 21 Assane Diao (forward): grade-one hamstring strain from Feyenoord on October 14; trying to be fit for Cagliari Moise Kean (forward): tibia problem, treated after advice from specialist Dr Ramon Cugat; target Juventus, November 29 (TuttoMercatoWeb has warned it could be December 5) Jaden Addai (forward): new muscle problem after his Achilles comeback; assessed this week Jesús Rodríguez (winger): out; CalcioMercato.com said "at least until December" Suspensions: none Shape, captaincy and the goalkeeper question Cesc Fabregas has settled on a 4-2-3-1: Máximo Perrone and Luis Milla as the double pivot, Nico Paz central behind Tasos Douvikas , with Lucas Da Cunha and Baturina or Caqueret wide. Da Cunha is captain and Paz vice-captain, a hierarchy set in September, per TuttoMercatoWeb . One pattern worth tracking: Jean Butez started at Lens and Robert Sánchez at Inter. Two matches is not a policy, but it fits a Champions League and Serie A split. Fabregas also admitted at Lens that he has "a weakness for left-footed players", per Football Italia ; five were on the pitch together that night. The scoring has narrowed. Douvikas has 11 goals in all competitions, five in Serie A and six in the Champions League, where he is the competition's top scorer, per statz.ai and ESPN . Paz and Baturina follow on six and five. Como have 37 goals in 15 games, 21 of them after half-time. Paz by the numbers Paz's numbers are the other headline. He has three goals and three assists in nine Serie A games and three goals and five assists in four Champions League games. That eight-goal involvement in Europe was the most in the competition after matchday four, per Calcionews24 . On contracts, Douvikas signed to 2031 in late October, per CalcioMercato.com . Perrone's renewal has been described as close since early October but is not yet official. Da Cunha's deal already runs to 2031. Off the Pitch The new curva goes to court, and the club pays a fine A residents' challenge to the Sinigaglia works reaches the regional administrative court on December 10. Meanwhile the losses, and the owners' cheques, keep growing. The fight over the Stadio Sinigaglia has moved to the courts. The residents' committee Tutela Zona Stadio, represented by lawyer Veronica Dini , appealed to the regional administrative court (TAR) on August 8 against both the overall project and the new Curva Ovest. The hearing is set for December 10, per EspansioneTV . The same report says the city fined Como for starting work before the required 30 days after filing, a fine the club has paid, and that a second filing on August 8 scaled the works back. The curva itself, 4,550 seats and built in 89 days, is already in use, per Archistadia . The full Populous redevelopment is a separate, slower process. La Provincia di Como reported in May that it was more than a year behind, with capacity trimmed to about 14,000 and the hotel dropped. A public-interest declaration, a second planning conference and the concession are all still to come. Fines and finances There was also a sporting-court fine: €10,000 for a roughly two-minute delay in coming out for the second half at San Siro, treated as a repeat offence, per Calcionews24 . On the money, the last filed accounts (to June 2025) showed a consolidated loss of €132m on about €55m of group revenue, with wages at €86m, per Pambianco . Last year's accounts were reported in December, per Calcio e Finanza , so the 2025-26 figures may land within weeks. UEFA's squad-cost and loss limits now apply. A guest analysis on The Esk , built from UK company filings, traces control to Robert Budi Hartono of the Djarum group and counts €297.4m of owner funding by November 2025. Its author estimates a further €100m or more will be needed this season. That is an estimate, not filed accounts. The president speaks President Mirwan Suwarso was everywhere. He told TNT that "in terms of football DNA, we want to become like Barcelona", with Brighton and Brentford as the business model, per Football Italia via Yahoo . He also said he had built a Como management-game prototype himself in three days, due for staff testing from November 9, per TuttoMercatoWeb . On Fabregas's future, Suwarso was striking on Piers Morgan Uncensored: "He can go wherever he wants, whenever he wants... I don't even need any compensation," per Sports Mole . The coach's contract runs to 2028. One reported suitor cooled this week, with Moretto saying Mauricio Pochettino will be Manchester United's next manager ( Napoli Magazine ). The Academy Comeback in Florence, and a call from Mancini The Primavera came from 2-0 down to win at Fiorentina, Riccardo Cassano earned a senior Italy call-up at 17, and Matteo Papaccioli's debut goal still echoes. Como 's Primavera, coached by Gianluca Falsini , came from two goals down to win 3-2 at Fiorentina 's Viola Park in Primavera 1 last weekend, with Ballone , Zamagni and Riccardo Cassano scoring, per Football Scouting . The win leaves them eighth on 15 points from ten games; Parma lead on 21. Cassano, born in 2009, then received a first senior call-up from Italy coach Roberto Mancini for the Nations League games against France and Belgium, per TuttoMercatoWeb . He moves on to Italy's squad for the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar afterwards; Italy open against Jamaica on November 20. In the UEFA Youth League the Primavera beat Manchester United 2-1 on October 21 but lost 2-1 at Lens on November 4, Cassano scoring, per LiveScore . They have four points and sit outside the play-off places. Papaccioli and Liberali The academy's headline of the season remains Matteo Papaccioli . Back from about nine months out with a cruciate ligament injury, the 18-year-old scored in stoppage time on his Champions League debut at Lens. TuttoMercatoWeb reported he is the second-youngest Italian to score in the competition. That record claim is single-sourced. Mattia Liberali , 19, is now a first-team regular and won his first senior Italy call-up this week, per TuttoMercatoWeb . Loan watch Alieu Fadera (Cagliari): set up Nzola's goal at Lazio on November 1, then went off injured; a hamstring tear makes him doubtful against Como. Ignace Van der Brempt (Sassuolo): played 90 minutes against Como on October 24; his loan carries a conditional obligation of about €6.5m. Álvaro Morata (Leganés, Segunda): no goals as of October, when he had lost his starting place and was sent off against Córdoba, per Flashscore Spain. Iván Azón (Getafe): played in the 2-0 defeat at Villarreal on November 8 without scoring. Nicolas Kühn (Gladbach): muscle-fibre tear after his debut, out for up to six weeks, per Bulinews. Emil Audero (Rayo Vallecano): competing for the starting job; back in Indonesia's XI in October. Others: Törnqvist (Monza), Cuenca (Sporting Gijón), Fellipe Jack (Cremonese), Le Borgne (Verona) and Gabrielloni (Palermo) are among those out on loan, per TuttoMercatoWeb's list . Women's Team A Roma reality check, then the derby nobody else has Como 1907's women lost 4-0 at home to the leaders but remain third. On Sunday they meet Como Women, the city's other Serie A club. First, a clarification for new readers. Como 1907 Femminile is the club's own women's team, promoted as Serie B champions last season. Como Women is a separate club, owned by the US fund Mercury13 and based in Meda. Both play in Serie A Women this season, as Il Post explained . This section covers Como 1907. The promoted side had flown out of the blocks: 4-1 against Milan on opening day, 2-1 at Napoli, then a 4-2 win at Juventus in Biella with two goals from Bonfantini , per Juventus.com . Draws with Sassuolo (2-2) and Ternana (1-1) followed. Saturday was a reality check. Leaders Roma won 4-0 at Lambrone, with Manuela Giugliano involved in all four goals, per OA Sport . Como 1907 remain third on 11 points (W3 D2 L1, goals 13-11), seven behind Roma, per DAZN's table . Mazzantini's squad, and Sunday's derby Coach Selena Mazzantini , with Patrizia Panico as assistant and Heather O'Reilly running the women's section, has a squad built to compete. Tessa Wullaert , last season's Serie A top scorer, rescued a point against Sassuolo with a stoppage-time penalty; captain Vero Boquete , Valentina Giacinti and Emilie Haavi , who scored twice against Milan, add depth. Next is the derby. Como 1907 host Como Women on Sunday, November 15, at 15:00 (6:00 a.m. Pacific) at Lambrone in Erba, per the club's ticket page . Como Women are sixth on eight points after losing 1-0 at Parma. The sides' summer Women's Cup meeting ended 2-1 to Como Women with a red card each. Players Away Eleven on the road, three for the first time The November window has scattered at least eleven Como players across Europe and South America, including three first senior call-ups. k: Milan sit fourth on 24 points after winning at Genoa, but a 2-0 home loss to Ferencvaros leaves them 28th in the Europa League and Amorim admitting the squad is not ready.
x: STOPPAGE TIME The Weekly AC Milan Digest Every Rossoneri story, every week Weekly edition · Thursday, November 12, 2026 · Milan, Serie A Season tracker Serie A: 4th, 24 pts , 5 behind leaders Lazio. Last ten, oldest first: W 3-0 LEC D 1-1 SAS W 4-0 SAL W 3-2 ATA L 0-3 BOU W 2-0 UDI L 2-4 BOL W 3-1 INT L 0-2 FER W 2-1 GEN Next: Milan v Frosinone, Sun Nov 22, 9:00 AM PT, San Siro. In this edition The Lead · Player Ratings · Scouting the Next Opponent · Transfer News · The Squad · The Academy · Milan Women · Players Away · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch If you read nothing else ■ Milan won 2-1 at Genoa through Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic and sit fourth on 24 points, five behind unbeaten leaders Lazio. ■ A 2-0 home loss to Ferencváros left Milan 28th in the Europa League; Ruben Amorim said the squad is “not ready” for two fronts. ■ Club Brugge want €60m for striker Nicolò Tresoldi, Gazzetta reports, while Milan have rejected a Brighton approach for Cisse. The Lead Amorim's split season: a Serie A contender, a Europa League emergency Eleven league games in, Milan are two points better off than at the same stage last season. In Europe they have lost three of four and fallen outside the play-off places. Amorim says that is on him. T he week told both halves of Milan 's season in five days. On Thursday, Ferencváros came to San Siro and won 2-0, Lenny Joseph scoring twice after the break. On Sunday a rebuilt side went to Marassi and beat Genoa 2-1, with Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic scoring inside 19 minutes. The league table smiles. The Europa League table does not. The numbers in Serie A are good. Ruben Amorim , appointed in June after Massimiliano Allegri was dismissed following a fifth-place finish, has 24 points from 33: seven wins, three draws and one defeat. Gazzetta's comparison, relayed by Milanreports , puts that two points ahead of Allegri at this stage last season and seven ahead of Paulo Fonseca's start. Milan are fourth, four points behind Inter , whom they beat 3-1 in the October 31 derby , and five behind Lazio , who are unbeaten on 29. The gap to fifth-placed Como is a single point, which is the more relevant margin for a club whose finances, Tuttosport argued this week, depend on returning to the Champions League. The European problem Europe is another story. Milan have one win and three defeats from four league-phase games: home losses to Benfica and Ferencváros, a 3-0 defeat at Bournemouth and a lone 4-0 win in Salzburg. Three points leave them 28th of 36. Flashscore called it Milan's worst start to a European league phase. The Ferencváros defeat exposed the depth problem. With Mike Maignan suspended after his red card at Bournemouth, 21-year-old Lorenzo Torriani made his first senior start. Amorim also started Filippo Terracciano, Davide Bartesaghi, Ardon Jashari and Omari Hutchinson. Milan had 62 percent of the ball at half-time and two shots to Ferencváros's seven, per Vavel . Both goals came from Kristoffer Zachariassen's work. First he stole in after Torriani fumbled a back-pass; then he squared on the counter for Joseph's second, according to Football Italia . Amorim made a triple change at half-time, sending on Pulisic, Diego Moreira and Mario Gila. Bamidele Yusuf's 77th-minute red card for the visitors changed nothing. “We are not ready to be competitive on two fronts. Probably, I didn't do enough to make sure the team was ready.” Ruben Amorim to Sky Sport Italia, November 5 Amorim did not hide. In his press conference he added: “We have to improve, otherwise it's over,” according to SoccerNews . Gazzetta reported a blunt dressing-room meeting afterwards in which Cisse, Jashari, Yunus Musah and Adrien Rabiot were among those discussed. What Genoa told us The reply at Marassi was efficient rather than dominant. The club's own tabellino lists a 4-4-1-1 with Musah at left-back and Cisse wide on the left. Rabiot crossed for Cisse's first-time finish on 13 minutes, and Gonçalo Ramos pounced on Alessandro Marcandalli's back-pass to set up Pulisic on 19, per Football Italia . After that, Genoa had the shots: 17 to Milan's six, five on target to two, according to Vavel . Maignan's save from Vitinha on 73 minutes mattered before Mikael Ellertsson's 88th-minute goal set up a nervous finish. Milan picked up five yellow cards. That is a pattern worth watching against Frosinone, who shoot more than almost anyone in Serie A. The verdict The honest reading is that Milan's league results have outrun their control of games, much as Statz argues Lazio's have at the top. The squad lacks a second layer good enough for Thursday nights. Corriere dello Sport reports the club wants a centre-back, a left-back and a striker in January. Four Europa League games remain to climb back into the top 24. Key facts Serie A: 4th, 24 pts from 11 (W7 D3 L1), goals 23-13. Europa League: 28th of 36, 3 pts from 4 (W1 L3). This week: Milan 0-2 Ferencváros (Nov 5, San Siro); Genoa 1-2 Milan (Nov 8, Marassi). Same stage last season: 22 pts under Allegri, per Gazzetta. The Lead Eleven straight wins, and PSG did it without their stars Since losing Kvaratskhelia, Dembélé and Marquinhos on one October night, with Nuno Mendes already out, Luis Enrique's side have not dropped a point. The break arrives at the right moment, and the cavalry is close. O n the night of October 20, Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 and lost half a team. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tore the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee; AFP reports he will be out for more than six months. Ousmane Dembélé and Marquinhos went off with thigh injuries ( Sud Radio/AFP ), and Nuno Mendes was already missing after a thigh problem at Strasbourg three days earlier ( Reuters via The Star ). What followed is the most convincing argument yet for the squad Luis Enrique has built. Lyon 2-0. Le Havre 5-1. Villarreal 0-6. Troyes 1-0. Four games, four wins, 14 goals for and one against. Count the seven wins up to and including the Barcelona night and PSG reach the international break on an 11-match winning run in all competitions, the club's longest since 2015-16 ( AllFootball ). Luis Enrique put it in his own terms after Troyes. "Eleven wins in a row, that's good," he said, adding that what stood out was winning every match between two international breaks for the first time under him ( SoccerNews ). PSG lead Ligue 1 on 23 points, two clear of Lille , and sit first in the Champions League league phase with 12 points from 12 and a +15 goal difference ( NBC Sports ). Key facts Run: 11 straight wins in all competitions, longest since 2015-16 Ligue 1: 1st, 23 points (7W 2D 1L), +12, two ahead of Lille Champions League: 1st, 12 points from 4 games, 20 scored, 5 conceded Since the Barcelona injuries: 4 wins, 14 goals for, 1 against Record: 4-0 up at Villarreal after 16:02, fastest four goals in Champions League history Out: Kvaratskhelia (ACL, 6+ months); Dembélé, Marquinhos, Mendes (thigh) targeting Nice; Akliouche (calf) A record in Spain The headline act was Tuesday, November 3, at the Estadio de la Cerámica. PSG led Villarreal 4-0 after 16 minutes and two seconds, the fastest four goals in Champions League history, through João Neves, Désiré Doué, Senny Mayulu and Fabián Ruiz. Ruiz added a second after the break and 17-year-old David Boly scored on his Champions League debut ( psg.fr ). It was PSG's biggest away win in the competition, built on 2.69 expected goals to 0.66 ( SoccerNews ). Luis Enrique refused to celebrate it. "This doesn't mean anything," he said. "In February and March, we'll have to prove everything" ( SoccerNews ). Days later he called the scoreline "almost bizarre" and "an accident". Grit against Troyes Troyes on Saturday was the opposite kind of test. With Hakimi rested and Marquinhos, Dembélé, Mendes and Kvaratskhelia out, PSG had 73% of the ball and 15 shots, but needed Illia Zabarnyi's header from Mayulu's cross on 39 minutes to break a stubborn defence ( psg.fr ). Troyes thought they had equalised late, but the goal was ruled out for offside ( Flashscore ). Grinding out a 1-0 is what title sides do between the statement nights. Vitinha completed 166 passes. Ferran Torres hit the target four times without scoring, extending his drought to nine games, and Luis Enrique shrugged it off: "That's how it is: a striker scores and misses goals" ( Sports Mole ). “If you think you're unplayable or invincible, you'll clearly lose the next match.” Luis Enrique, after Troyes (translated) The understudies The deeper story is who has stepped in. Mayulu has scored against Le Havre and Villarreal, assisted the winner against Troyes, made L'Équipe's Ligue 1 team of the week and, on Wednesday, earned a first senior France call-up ( Ouest-France ). Mika Godts, the summer signing from Ajax, scored at Le Havre and set up Mayulu against Lyon. Warren Zaïre-Emery filled in at right-back. Rotation has been relentless rather than reckless. At Le Havre the XI was heavily changed, with Vitinha, Neves and Doué on the bench, and Achraf Hakimi still scored a hat-trick from right-back ( psg.fr ). The coach has kept his 4-3-3 shape but shared the load, and his warning to the squad was blunt: "If you think you're unplayable or invincible, you'll clearly lose the next match" ( PlanètePSG , translated from French). The cavalry returns The two weeks off could not be better timed. The club's medical update on November 6 said Marquinhos, Dembélé and Mendes were back in individual training, and French media are targeting the trip to Nice on November 21 for their return ( Allez Paris , Kick Football ). Those dates are media estimates, not club ones. Maghnes Akliouche (calf) is being treated. Then comes the run that will define the autumn: Nice away, Roma at the Parc on November 25, Lorient three days later. PSG have won every game since September 9. Nobody inside the club pretends that streak survives forever. The point is that it has survived the worst injury week of Luis Enrique's tenure. The Parc The €2bn idea: rebuilding the Parc instead of leaving it L'Équipe says the owners are studying a 70,000-seat "Porte des Princes". Massy and Poissy are still in the race, and a decision on a priority site is due before the end of the year. The stadium saga took another turn on November 4. According to L'Équipe, PSG 's Qatari owners would put €1.5bn to €2bn into buying the Parc des Princes and rebuilding it, lifting capacity from about 48,000 to 70,000, with standing areas considered ( Kick Football , VIPSG , both relaying L'Équipe). The plan would take in the land around the ground, including car parks, a petrol station and the Stade Géo-André, which Stade Français wants to keep. PSG would decamp to the Stade de France during the works. L'Équipe was explicit: nothing is signed and there is no timetable. Three sites, one deadline In an October 17 statement, the club said it would pick a priority site in autumn 2026, while stressing that this would not be a final decision ( VIPSG ). Le Parisien reported on October 23 that no project was out of the race and that the QSI board would name its priority site before the end of the year ( Kick Football ). Massy's mayor, Nicolas Samsoen , told Le Parisien he had "no doubt the project works technically" ( PlanètePSG ). The gap on price is old and wide: PSG offered about €40m for the Parc in 2022, while valuations have ranged from about €200m to about €350m ( VIPSG ). Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire has had a mandate to negotiate since April. Transfer News No replacement for Kvaratskhelia, and the club means it Three reporters and the coach himself line up behind the same message: Godts gets the left flank, and January will be quiet unless something else breaks. The clearest transfer story of the week is a decision not to act. On November 4, Canal+ reporter Olivier Tallaron wrote that, barring another major injury to a key player, PSG will not go after anyone to replace Kvaratskhelia this winter ( Les Titis du PSG ). Certainty: club position, reported by Canal+ . That matches what RMC Sport's Fabrice Hawkins reported in late October: the club is counting on Mika Godts and is not necessarily targeting a direct replacement, though a young, high-potential player at a reasonable price is not ruled out ( Yahoo Sports ). Luis Enrique's own line on October 24 was that no injury means you have to sign, but the club stays open to opportunities ( VIPSG ). Dembélé's new deal is close, not done AFP describes talks as very constructive. Some outlets say it is signed; the reliable ones do not. Ousmane Dembélé , under contract to 2028, is negotiating an extension to June 2030. On November 6, AFP quoted a source close to the talks calling them "very constructive and positive", with the aim of reaching agreement quickly and "a few points to settle" ( Orange/AFP ). Mundo Deportivo also reports the sides moving closer. Certainty: advanced talks . Several French outlets have gone further and called it done pending an announcement; that is not confirmed by any tier-one source, and PSG have announced nothing. Reports also say talks with Kvaratskhelia on a longer deal continue despite his injury; that is single-sourced. Boly's choice: PSG or Frankfurt The 17-year-old who scored at Villarreal is the most urgent contract on the desk. David Boly 's aspirant contract runs to June 2027. RMC Sport reports PSG have offered a five-year professional deal, which he can sign once he turns 18 on January 22 ( Kick Football ). L'Équipe calls the offer attractive. Sky Germany's Florian Plettenberg reported on November 8 that Eintracht Frankfurt want him in January and would pay a fee ( VIPSG ). Certainty: offer made, no agreement announced . Paris Team reports the player wants to sign only with PSG; that is single-sourced. RMC also reports PSG want to extend forward Quentin Ndjantou, possibly to 2033. Scouting the Next Opponent Nice: Wahi's hot streak and a wing-back gamble Pantaloni's side are sixth and winning, but they have conceded 12 in 10 and are missing their best centre-back. OGC Nice host PSG at the Allianz Riviera on Saturday, November 21, the first game back after the break ( ligue1.com ). They come in sixth on 17 points after winning four of their last five, most recently 2-0 at Angers with goals from Sofiane Diop in the second minute and Jonathan Clauss late on ( Sports Mole ). Olivier Pantaloni , hired in the summer after Nice survived a relegation play-off, plays a 3-4-3 in which the wing-backs carry the side at both ends ( ligue1.com , Nice-Premium ). A typical XI has Clauss and Nkounkou wide, Axel Witsel as captain in midfield, and Wahi between Gauthier Hein and Mohamed Amoura. The players to stop Elye Wahi is the threat: six league goals and two assists in nine games, including a hat-trick, two from the penalty spot, in a 5-2 win over Rennes on October 30 ( Flashscore , ESPN ). Clauss has three goals from right wing-back; Diop has two goals and three assists; Hein has three assists. Where Nice can be hurt Nice are without Moïse Bombito after leg surgery, and Antoine Mendy and Laurent Abergel are out with ACL injuries ( Get French Football News ). Pantaloni has admitted his squad is not at full fitness and that the Nkounkou and Amoura left side is still finding its feet. A back three with advancing wing-backs leaves room behind for Hakimi and Doué to attack. The recent history is mixed. PSG won 4-0 in Nice in March ( psg.fr ) and 1-0 at home in November 2025 with a stoppage-time header ( psg.fr ), but it was Nice who ended PSG's unbeaten league season with a 3-1 win at the Parc in April 2025 ( ligue1.com ). The Lead Two tight wins, 21 points and the closest title race in years Dortmund beat Real Betis and Elversberg by a goal apiece with tired legs and a striker in the treatment room. The table calls them Bayern’s equals; the performances say the break has come at the right time. T he scoreline was the same twice, and so was the feeling afterwards. Borussia Dortmund beat Real Betis 2-1 in the Champions League on Wednesday and SV Elversberg 2-1 in the Bundesliga on Saturday. Neither was comfortable. Both were enough. Nine league games in, Dortmund are unbeaten on 21 points, level with Bayern Munich , who stay top only on goal difference after winning 2-1 at Mainz. Bundesliga.com calls it the tightest title race in years . Dortmund have not had 21 points after nine games since 2013-14, and they own the league’s best defence: seven conceded. The catch is the gap in goal difference, +20 to +9, which says Bayern have been more emphatic. Dortmund have been efficient. Wednesday: Betis lose their perfect record Betis arrived with nine points from nine. They left with their first Champions League defeat of the season. After a goalless first half, Fábio Silva followed in when Álvaro Vallés parried Jobe Bellingham ’s shot from five metres, 1-0 on 49 minutes, per the club’s match report . Aitor Ruibal equalised on 67 minutes from an Abde Ezzalzouli cross, after a mistake by Waldemar Anton . Five minutes later Konstantinos Karetsas , on for the injured Serhou Guirassy since the 34th minute, took Silva’s pass and drove a low 17-metre shot into the near corner. All Football says he was 18 years and 350 days old, the youngest Dortmund scorer of a Champions League winner . The win took Dortmund to nine points and 12th place in the league phase, per NBC Sports , before trips to Arsenal and Aston Villa. Niko Kovac reportedly put the target for the top eight at 17 or 18 points, so Dortmund probably need about three wins from their last four. “That’s something no one can take away from us.” Lars Ricken on 21 points from nine games, via bvb.de Saturday: Nmecha carries a weary side Three days later Kovac changed three players and the shape. With Guirassy out with a thigh strain, Dortmund lined up in what the club called a 4-3-3: Joane Gadou at right-back, Carney Chukwuemeka and Karetsas wide, Silva through the middle. Chukwuemeka lasted 34 minutes before a left-thigh problem ended his day, and Maximilian Beier came on. Felix Nmecha decided it. On 55 minutes he curled a 19-metre shot into the bottom corner from Silva’s pass. On 71 he hit a loose ball from 23 metres at 124 km/h, per the club report . Substitute Noel Futkeu’s overhead kick from a short corner made the last nine minutes tense, but Gregor Kobel was not beaten again. What the two games told us The honest reading came from inside the club. “Our fatigue showed in certain situations,” sporting director Ole Book told Sky. “After going up two-zero, we stopped attacking and didn’t have enough possession.” Kovac called it “very much a hard-fought victory,” adding that Dortmund came under pressure “because we gave the ball away too easily,” per the post-match reactions . Context matters. Elversberg was Dortmund’s ninth competitive game in 29 days. Kovac has used a back three against Betis, a back four in Munich and against Elversberg, and switched back to three at 67 minutes on Saturday when Julian Ryerson and Ramy Bensebaini came on. The flexibility is a strength. The cost is that few combinations have had time to settle. Then there is the striker question. Silva has stepped in well: a goal and an assist against Betis, the assist for the opener against Elversberg. Kovac said Guirassy’s absence costs height at set pieces and that the chance now falls to players such as Silva and Beier. The club hopes Guirassy is fit again after the break. Key facts: Dortmund’s week Wed, Nov 4: Dortmund 2-1 Real Betis (Silva 49’, Ruibal 67’, Karetsas 72’), Champions League, attendance 81,365 Sat, Nov 7: Dortmund 2-1 Elversberg (Nmecha 55’, 71’, Futkeu 81’), Bundesliga matchday 9, attendance 81,365 Bundesliga: 2nd, 21 points, 6 wins and 3 draws, goals 16:7 Champions League: 12th, 9 points from 4 games Injured in the week: Guirassy (thigh strain), Chukwuemeka (left thigh; Bild reports a muscle fibre tear) Next: at Gladbach, Sat, Nov 21; at Arsenal, Tue, Nov 24 Race tracker: the top two after nine games Bayern Munich: 21 points, 6-3-0, goals 29:9 (+20); won 2-1 at Mainz on matchday 9 Borussia Dortmund: 21 points, 6-3-0, goals 16:7 (+9); beat Elversberg 2-1 on matchday 9 Head-to-head this season: Bayern 2-2 Dortmund, October 31 Cautionary tale: in 2017-18 the two were level on 20 after nine; Bayern won the title by 21 points (Bundesliga.com) Secondary feature: the crown, the club and Felix Nmecha His goals kept Dortmund level with Bayern. His celebration has drawn in the president, the fans and the national team. Nmecha’s two goals against Elversberg were followed by a row that has reached the club president and the national team coach. After each goal, Nmecha mimes taking off a crown and laying it on the grass. ZDF links the gesture to “The King’s Return”, a campaign of the Christian players’ network Ballers in God, which posted about him after Saturday’s game. The club’s own fan and supporters’ department criticised the celebration, citing ARD research that accuses the network of calling homosexuality a sin, per the AP . The club told Bild it expects all players’ conduct to align with its values and said it would speak to Nmecha. On Monday, according to WDR , president Hans-Joachim Watzke told a meeting of that department the club would ask Nmecha to stop. Bild, relayed by BVBWLD , reports Dortmund want the network to stop using him in its promotion and are weighing legal steps if it does not. Nmecha wrote on Instagram that he had been told his celebration caused “some misunderstandings” and that he did not want to put himself or any organisation in the foreground. The network said on Tuesday it meets all people “with love and respect regardless of their faith.” Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has spoken with Nmecha at the national team camp; no details were released. DFB sporting director Rudi Völler stressed that freedom of religion applies and said the federation would talk to Nmecha again. The issue could surface at the club’s members’ meeting on November 22. For now, Dortmund’s best player of the week is also its most delicate conversation. Scouting the Next Opponent Gladbach: bottom, rebuilding, and dangerous on a good day Alexander Blessin has had seven weeks to fix the league’s worst start. A 17-year-old Germany debutant is the player to watch. Borussia Mönchengladbach are bottom of the Bundesliga with four points from nine games: one win, one draw, seven defeats, goals 12:25. They have already changed coach. Eugen Polanski left on September 13 after three straight defeats, and Alexander Blessin , formerly of St. Pauli, was appointed on September 22, per ZDF . There have been signs of life. Gladbach won 3-2 at Stuttgart on October 23 for their first points, then drew 0-0 with Paderborn. Last Friday they lost 3-1 at Hamburg, where Joe Scally equalised on 44 minutes before Ko Itakura was sent off for a second yellow card early in the second half, per Bulinews . Shape and the players to stop Blessin played a 3-5-2 in Hamburg, per the DFB data centre , with Scally and Ullrich as wing-backs and Shuto Machino alongside Wael Mohya up front. Mohya, 17, is the story: he scored and assisted in Stuttgart and has just been called up by Klopp for Germany, per dpa . Scally has scored in both of the last two away games. Itakura’s red card should rule the centre-back out, since a second yellow carries an automatic one-match ban. Goalkeeper Moritz Nicolas had a muscle problem at the end of October and Daniel Batz has been in goal. Tim Kleindienst and Franck Honorat were among nine absentees in late October; their status for the 21st is not yet confirmed. Where Dortmund can hurt them Twenty-five goals conceded in nine games is the worst defensive record in the league, and a three-man defence without Itakura will be short of experience. The warning is history: Gladbach beat Dortmund 1-0 at Borussia-Park last May, per statz.ai , and the game falls straight after an international break that has scattered 17 Dortmund players across Europe and beyond. Borussia Mönchengladbach at a glance Coach: Alexander Blessin, since September 22 Shape: 3-5-2 (at Hamburg, matchday 9) Bundesliga: 18th, 4 points, 1-1-7, goals 12:25 Last three: W 3-2 at Stuttgart, D 0-0 v Paderborn, L 1-3 at Hamburg Doubts: Itakura (red card at Hamburg), Nicolas (muscle), Kleindienst and Honorat (status unconfirmed) Last five meetings: Gladbach 1-0 BVB (May 2026), BVB 2-0 (Dec 2025), BVB 3-2 (Apr 2025), 1-1 (Dec 2024), Gladbach 1-2 BVB (Apr 2024) Transfer News Anton has a concrete offer, but no deal yet The centre-back wants a pay rise closer to the top of the squad; Bild says English clubs are circling. Dortmund have made Waldemar Anton a concrete offer to extend a contract that runs to 2028, but there is no agreement. Sport Bild reported last week that he rejected a first proposal. This week, per BVBWLD citing Sky, Dortmund have put a concrete offer to him, and both sides are said to be optimistic. Money is the gap. Sport Bild puts Anton’s current salary at €5.5m to €6m and says he wants “greater appreciation”. Bild reporter Jörg Weiler said on the club’s insider podcast that Anton “of course also has offers from England”; no clubs were named. According to Sport Bild via 90min , a deal to 2030 would suit him. Status: advanced contract talks, no agreement; English interest single-sourced to Bild. Kobel, Ryerson and Guirassy: the next three contracts All three run to 2028. Sport Bild sets out where each one stands. Anton is not the only key player tied to 2028. Sport Bild reports that Gregor Kobel has had no talks yet, but that the club will open them in the coming weeks, with Paris Saint-Germain said to have enquired repeatedly. Bulinews, via Yahoo Sports , carries the same line. Julian Ryerson has had first contact through his agents, Sport Bild says, but is also weighing a move abroad. For Serhou Guirassy , the internal plan is an offer to 2030, with talks around the turn of the year; his decision reportedly depends on whether Dortmund can compete for titles. The current table helps that pitch. Status: Kobel, planned talks with PSG interest; Ryerson, early talks; Guirassy, planned offer. All from Sport Bild. Book names the gap: full-backs The sporting director all but confirms where January money would go. Speaking to DAZN on the night of the Betis game, Ole Book hinted at January business on the flanks: “Perhaps it is no great secret that we do not have too many full-backs,” he said, adding “we will see what is possible,” per BVBWLD . Marcel Regula remains the name. The Zaglebie Lubin attacker is a player Dortmund want to retrain as a wide man. New this week: Polish outlet Kanal Sportowy says Lubin now want at least €10m, up from €7m to €8m, and fussballdaten.de claims Real Madrid are also interested, per BVBWLD . No bid has been reported. Status: stated need from the club; Regula, concrete interest, price rising; Real Madrid link single-sourced. Reggiani wants out The Italian youth international has had only two brief first-team outings. Centre-back Luca Reggiani , 18, has told Dortmund through his agent that he wants to leave in January because of a lack of minutes, Sky reports, via BVBWLD and GOAL . Dortmund reportedly want about €20m, possibly structured with bonuses and a sell-on share. AC Milan, who had a bid turned down in the summer, are named as likely buyers. Status: exit request reported; no bid. Single-sourced to Sky. Ins & Outs This week: no confirmed signings or departures; the winter window opens in January. Summer in: Karetsas (Genk, €30m), Konstantelias (PAOK, €26m), Veerman (PSV, €22m), Gadou (Salzburg, €19.5m), Prates (Cruzeiro, €7m), Lerma (Independiente del Valle, €4m), Nwaneri (loan, Arsenal) Summer out: Adeyemi (Barcelona, €22m), Campbell (Elversberg, €6m), Duranville (Lyon, €5m), Couto (loan, Como), Ramaj (loan, Copenhagen), Özcan (Beşiktaş, free) The Rumour Mill Yan Couto (Como): Book says “of course we watch him”, but Como coach Cesc Fàbregas wants to keep him; the purchase option is reported at about €22m ( 90min ). Likely exit. Joane Gadou: scouts from Real Madrid, Arsenal and PSG reportedly watched him; fussball-news.de mentions €40m to €50m ( BVBWLD ). Rumour, single source. Ismaelo Ganiou (Lens): Dortmund among several clubs to have scouted the injured centre-back, per 4-4-2.com ( BVBWLD ). Link only. Jobe Bellingham: a former Manchester United scout told Football Insider that Newcastle are the natural suitor ( BVBWLD ). Pundit opinion, not a report of interest. Martin Zubimendi (Arsenal): TEAMtalk lists Dortmund among clubs watching. Single source, not credible as a winter target. The Squad Guirassy and Chukwuemeka join the treatment room The break arrives at the right moment for a squad that played nine games in 29 days. Two more names joined the injury list this week. Serhou Guirassy hurt his thigh against Betis; Kovac confirmed it was “only” a strain and said “we hope he will be fit again after the international break,” per 90min . He has stayed in Dortmund rather than join Guinea. Carney Chukwuemeka went off against Elversberg with a left-thigh problem; Bild reports a muscle fibre tear and an absence of several weeks, per Neue Westfälische . The club has not given a timescale. Waldemar Anton , who had played 1,417 of a possible 1,440 minutes, withdrew from Germany duty with muscle problems, the club said . The Svensson let-off Daniel Svensson was fortunate on Saturday. Around the 20th minute he caught Elversberg captain Lukas Pinckert above the ankle; there was no card and no VAR review, and Pinckert later went off injured. Referee Harm Osmers told Sky it was “at least yellow” and that red could be debated. “We were lucky there,” Kovac admitted, per Flashscore , adding it was a split-second action. Form and rotation Felix Nmecha is in the form of his Dortmund career, and Joey Veerman looked at home at the base of the 4-3-3. Silva has a goal and two assists in the week. Konstantinos Karetsas, whose minutes Kovac has managed since his ankle problem, scored his first goal for the club. Bellingham, now an England player, said he owes much of his development to Kovac, per Bulinews . One positive note on the long-term list: Giannis Konstantelias is said to be ahead of schedule after his cruciate ligament tear, with Bild and Greek media now pointing to February or March, per GOAL . The club has set no date. Availability for Gladbach (Nov 21) Doubtful: Serhou Guirassy (thigh strain; club hopes he is back after the break) Out: Carney Chukwuemeka (left thigh; Bild reports a muscle fibre tear, several weeks), Emre Can (cruciate ligament), Giannis Konstantelias (cruciate ligament), Justin Lerma (muscle) Monitor: Waldemar Anton (muscle problems; withdrew from Germany squad) Back: Marcel Sabitzer (fit again after illness; a late cameo against Elversberg) The Academy Gardarsson keeps scoring as the U19s stay top Three goals in two games for the Icelandic forward; the U23s hold the leaders. Felix Hirschnagl’s U19s drew 2-2 with Real Betis in the UEFA Youth League on Wednesday. Justin Hoy scored after five minutes and Bjarki Gardarsson restored the lead after Ruben De Sa’s quick reply, before Fran Batan equalised on 36 minutes. Dortmund are 10th with seven points, per the club report , and go to Arsenal on November 24. On Saturday Gardarsson scored twice more in a 3-2 league win over VfL Osnabrück, and substitute Levin Vogt struck the winner in stoppage time, per bvb.de . The U19s went into the weekend top of their DFB youth league group with 21 points and unbeaten, per the club’s weekend preview . BVB II and the loanees Daniel Rios’s U23s lost their unbeaten record 1-0 to FC Gütersloh on October 31, then drew 0-0 at leaders Rot-Weiß Oberhausen in front of a season-high 6,116 on Saturday. They stay second in the Regionalliga West, three points behind, per the club . Sportfreunde Lotte visit on Friday, November 20. On loan, Yan Couto played the full 90 minutes of Como’s 9-1 Champions League win at Lens and 74 minutes of a 2-0 defeat at Inter, per FotMob . The Digest could not confirm any minutes this week for goalkeeper Diant Ramaj at FC Copenhagen. Women's Team Twelve from twelve, and a derby with a crowd target The first goal conceded all season barely dents a perfect start. Markus Högner’s side won 6-1 at SC Fortuna Köln on Sunday to make it 12 wins from 12 in the Regionalliga West. Annika Boden’s 74th-minute goal for Köln was the first Dortmund have conceded all season. Ronja Leubner and Rita Schumacher scored twice each, with Alexandra Popp and Jacqueline Meißner also on target, per the club report . The previous weekend’s result, unconfirmed in our last edition, was a 5-0 win at Recklinghausen with a Popp hat-trick, per bvb.de . Dortmund lead on 36 points with a goal difference of +58. Next is the Revierderby against Schalke at Stadion Rote Erde on Sunday, where the club is chasing a league-record crowd under the banner “Mission 17.555”. Players Away Bellingham joins Jude in the England squad Seventeen players travel; Guirassy, Chukwuemeka and Anton stay home. Seventeen Dortmund players are away this break, per the club . The headline is Jobe Bellingham ’s first senior England call-up, alongside his brother Jude, for the Nations League games against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday and in Spain on Sunday. “Playing alongside my brother Jude for England is a huge dream,” he said, per Bulinews. For Germany, Nico Schlotterbeck and Felix Nmecha are in Klopp’s squad for Serbia away on Friday and the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday. Anton withdrew injured and Ridle Baku was called up instead, per t-online . Joey Veerman and the Netherlands meet Karetsas’s Greece on Friday before Veerman faces his Dortmund teammates in Berlin. Kobel (Switzerland), Ryerson (Norway), Svensson (Sweden) and Silva (Portugal) also have two Nations League games each. Enzo dos Santos is with Luxembourg, Ramy Bensebaini with Algeria for Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers and Mathis Albert with the United States. Nwaneri (England U21), Gadou (France U21), Samuele Inácio and Filippo Mane (Italy U21) and Reggiani (Italy U20) play youth friendlies. Old faces Cole Campbell, sold to Elversberg in the summer, came off the bench at Signal Iduna Park on Saturday and had a chance two minutes later. Ethan Nwaneri, on loan from Arsenal, had cameos in both games and will face his parent club on November 24. Numbers of the Week 21 Bundesliga points after nine games, Dortmund’s best start since 2013-14, and level with Bayern. 124 km/h The speed of Nmecha’s 23-metre strike for 2-0 against Elversberg, per the club. 9 in 29 Competitive games Dortmund played in 29 days before the break, Elversberg being the ninth. 36 Points from 12 Regionalliga West games for the women’s team, with a goal difference of +58. Source: FC Bayern standings . In Brief Pokal date set: Eintracht Frankfurt v Dortmund in the last 16 is on Wednesday, December 2, at 8:45 PM in Germany (11:45 AM Pacific), per bvb.de . Referee’s admission: Osmers said Svensson’s foul deserved at least a yellow ( 90min ). Members’ meeting: the club’s annual members’ meeting is on Sunday, November 22, with the agenda and motions updated on November 10 ( bvb.de ). Tickets: Frankfurt cup tickets are for members only, with a limit of two each ( BVBWLD ). Full house: both home games this week drew 81,365, a sell-out ( bvb.de ). t: The Weekly Bayern Munich Digest: November 11, 2026
k: Harry Kane extends to 2029 at a reported club-record salary while Bayern lead the Bundesliga on goal difference without Kompany, Neuer, Musiala and Saibari.
x: STOPPAGE TIME The Weekly Bayern Munich Digest All Bayern, every week. From Säbener Straße to the Campus. Weekly edition · Wednesday, November 11, 2026 · Munich desk Bundesliga: 1st, 21 pts Top on goal difference (+20) from Dortmund (21 pts, +9) · Last ten, oldest first W 7-0 FCU D 2-2 FCA D 3-3 VIK W 6-1 RBL D 2-2 ARS W 3-1 SCF W 6-1 FCM D 2-2 BVB W 2-0 ATM W 2-1 M05 Next: Bayern v 1.
