FC Köln (15th, 9 pts) Competition: Bundesliga, Matchday 10 Date: Friday, November 20, 2026 Kickoff: 11:30am Pacific (2:30pm Eastern; 20:30 in Munich) Venue: Home, Allianz Arena, Munich Where to watch in the US: US broadcaster not yet announced. English-language Bundesliga rights this season sit with USA Network and Fandango ; check their weekly listing. In this edition The Lead · Player Ratings · Scouting the Next Opponent · Transfer News · The Squad · The Campus · FC Bayern Women · Players Away · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch If you read nothing else • Harry Kane signed a contract extension to June 2029 on November 5, reportedly worth about 25 million euros a year before tax. • Manuel Neuer has a partial tendon tear in his right foot, so Jonas Urbig takes over in goal with no return date set. • Bayern beat Mainz 2-1 and lead the Bundesliga on goal difference, unbeaten in all 16 competitive matches this season. The Lead Kane signs on to 2029 as Bayern lead the table into a bruising break Bayern have tied their Ballon d'Or winner down at a reported club-record salary. The harder question is what the deal asks of a squad without its coach, its goalkeeper and three attackers. T he announcement came on Thursday, November 5, and it settled the one question that had hung over FC Bayern since the summer. Harry Kane has extended his contract to June 30, 2029, ten days after winning the Ballon d'Or in London. He has scored 156 goals in 161 games for the club, per Stuttgarter Zeitung . The price is the story German media chased all week. Sport1 reports about 25 million euros gross a year plus bonuses. Abendzeitung says he can earn more than that, a club record. Neither figure is official; the club has not published terms. How the deal was done According to Sport1, talks turned concrete in August. CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen negotiated with Kane's brother Charlie and father Pat, and the hold-ups were image rights rather than money. The supervisory board signed off on Tuesday, November 3, and Kane put pen to paper the next day. Abendzeitung adds one detail that matters for the long view: Kane wanted a deal to 2030, and Bayern did not give him that year, nor an option on it. He will be 35 when this contract ends. Bayern have paid at the top of the market, but they have capped the exposure. He is worth every cent. Jan-Christian Dreesen, as reported by Volksstimme/dpa Dreesen admitted the club had stretched to the limit , and president Herbert Hainer called it a special moment. Not everyone agreed. Sky pundit Dietmar Hamann called the deal a risk, which drew a sharp reply from Max Eberl : in Germany, there is always someone who has to spit in the soup . The striker is now the playmaker The numbers explain why Bayern paid. Kane has 10 goals in 15 games in all competitions, per Sportsmole , though none in his last four. The more striking figure is creative: eight Bundesliga assists after nine matchdays, the most at this stage since data collection began in 2004-05, according to the club . Saturday at Mainz showed the shape of it. Kane won the ball from a loose pass for Joshua Kimmich 's opener and his blocked shot fell for Lennart Karl to make it 2-0. With Jamal Musiala , Serge Gnabry , Ismael Saibari and Luis Díaz out, Kane dropping in to create has been as valuable as Kane finishing. What it means for the next six months The deal arrives in an odd week. Head coach Vincent Kompany has not been on the bench since collapsing on October 23 with meningeal irritation, and Manuel Neuer is out with a partial tendon tear. Assistant Aaron Danks has gone four wins and a draw in five games in charge, yet Bayern only lead Dortmund on goal difference. Kane's signature removes one variable from a crowded spring. The next is Michael Olise , whose deal also runs to 2029; Dreesen said the club will talk at the appropriate time, and Fabrizio Romano calls it the next mission . Keeping both is the plan. Paying both at the top of the scale is the test. Key facts: the Kane deal Announced: Thursday, November 5, 2026 (official) New end date: June 30, 2029; no option year (Abendzeitung) Reported salary: about 25 million euros gross a year plus bonuses (Sport1; not confirmed by the club) Bayern record: 156 goals in 161 games This season: 10 goals in 15 games in all competitions; 8 Bundesliga assists Honours: 2026 Ballon d'Or, awarded October 26 Neuer's record day turns sour, and Urbig's moment arrives A 550th Bundesliga appearance ended with a partial tendon tear. At 40, the question is no longer only when he returns. Saturday was meant to be a milestone. At 40 years and 225 days, Manuel Neuer became Bayern 's oldest Bundesliga player in his 550th league appearance, per the club . Before half-time he flapped at the cross that led to Lee's disallowed goal and was hurt in the same play. On Sunday the club confirmed a partial tendon tear in his right foot and gave no timeline. Bild expects about two months, per ran . Eberl said it was the same problem he had in the foot before; Neuer had already missed three games with tendon inflammation. The worrying trend predates the injury. Opta data cited by TimesLIVE counts five errors leading to goals in his last 17 games, against ten in the previous 248. Neuer's contract ends in June 2027. For now, Jonas Urbig is in goal, and Eberl answered a flat no when asked if the hierarchy would change. Player Ratings Mainz 1-2 Bayern: Kimmich and Kane run the show Bundesliga, Matchday 9, Saturday, November 7, MEWA Arena. Goals: Kimmich 14', Karl 57'; Tietz 90+3'. These are the Digest's own ratings, informed by the Bundesliga match report , the club's analysis and ran's player grades . Bayern dominated: 3.25 expected goals to 0.82, 68.8 percent possession and 46 touches in the Mainz box. Mainz coach Urs Fischer called it a deserved win over 90 minutes. Danks was disappointed to concede late, and Kimmich called it no glittering performance but a very composed one. Ratings at a glance Joshua Kimmich 8.0 Harry Kane 8.0 Lennart Karl 7.5 Konrad Laimer 7.0 Dayot Upamecano 7.0 Aleksandar Pavlović 6.5 Michael Olise 6.5 Jonas Urbig 6.5 Alphonso Davies 6.5 Nathaniel Brown 6.0 Tom Bischof 6.0 Jonathan Tah 5.5 Josip Stanišić 5.5 Manuel Neuer 4.0 Chart: the Digest's marks out of 10 for Mainz 1-2 Bayern, highest first. Boey and Ito (four minutes each) are not rated. Joshua Kimmich, 8.0. Ran the midfield and opened the scoring from about 17 metres; fans' man of the match. Harry Kane, 8.0. Two assists: won the ball for the first goal and his blocked shot set up the second. Lennart Karl, 7.5. Scored for the second match running, pouncing on the rebound on 57 minutes. Konrad Laimer, 7.0. Combative and tireless at right-back; booked on 76 minutes. Dayot Upamecano, 7.0. Commanding in the air and hit the crossbar. Aleksandar Pavlović, 6.5. Aggressive without the ball, occasionally careless with it. Michael Olise, 6.5. Quieter than usual, yet the match's best pass efficiency in the league's data. Jonas Urbig, 6.5. Little to do after replacing Neuer; beaten only by the stoppage-time header. Alphonso Davies, 6.5. Fastest player on the pitch at 34.26 km/h; had a late shot cleared off the line. Nathaniel Brown, 6.0. Bright start on the left, faded after the interval. Tom Bischof, 6.0. Tidy in around 25 minutes as a substitute. Jonathan Tah, 5.5. Steady for long spells but lost the aerial duel for Tietz's goal. Josip Stanišić, 5.5. Sloppy in possession and missed a chance before half-time. Manuel Neuer, 4.0. Shaky punch early, flapped at the cross for the disallowed goal, then went off injured. Bayern's starting XI: Neuer; Laimer, Upamecano, Tah, Stanišić; Kimmich, Pavlović; Olise, Karl, Brown; Kane. Urbig replaced Neuer shortly before half-time; Davies and Bischof came on at 67 minutes for Stanišić and Karl; Boey and Ito came on at 86. Scouting the Next Opponent Scouting Köln: a side that cannot win on the road René Wagner's team arrive at the Allianz Arena 15th, without a league win in four and without an away league win in more than a year. 1. FC Köln are 15th on 9 points (two wins, three draws, four defeats, goals 10:14), a place above the relegation play-off spot. Their last league outing was a 2-1 home defeat by Leverkusen on November 8, per ZDF , their first home league loss of the season. The away record is the headline: 17 Bundesliga away games without a win, the last on October 3, 2025. Their form line, newest first, reads L 1-2 Leverkusen, D 1-1 at Union, W 5-0 Union in the Pokal, D 0-0 Schalke, L 0-1 at Frankfurt. Who to stop Said El Mala is the danger: a Germany youngster now in the No. 10 shirt, he scored late against Leverkusen. His older brother Malek El Mala scored on debut at Union. Captain and goalkeeper Marvin Schwäbe is in strong form, and Linton Maina was decisive in the cup rout of Union. Coach René Wagner , who replaced Lukas Kwasniok in the spring, is under growing pressure. Striker Ragnar Ache has a thigh problem, but Wagner expects him back for Munich, per Fox Sports . We could not verify Köln's preferred formation, so we leave it out. Where Bayern can hurt them: discipline and set pieces. Köln took six of the eleven yellow cards against Leverkusen and conceded from a seventh-minute free kick. They do create chances (1.59 expected goals at Union), so this is not a side that will only sit deep. Köln at a glance Position: 15th, 9 pts, goals 10:14 Coach: René Wagner Last five (newest first): L, D, W (cup), D, L Away: no Bundesliga away win in 17 games Doubt: Ragnar Ache (thigh), expected back Recent meetings: Bayern 5-1 Köln (May 2026); Köln 1-3 Bayern (Jan 2026); Köln 1-4 Bayern, DFB-Pokal (Oct 2025) Transfer News The left-wing hunt: summer targets, no January rush Bayern are scouting wide forwards for 2027, but Eberl says the injury list is not yet a reason to buy in winter. Bayern officially plan no winter signings, Sky reported on November 2, but they are watching the left-wing market. Before Mainz, Max Eberl said Musiala and Díaz return after the break, and any thoughts on winter would come then, including doing nothing at all . Ngumoha: the summer favourite Bild's Christian Falk reports Bayern were ready to pay about 70 million euros for Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha last summer, and that talks with the player's camp have continued. SI notes Liverpool called him not for sale, his deal runs to 2028, and his agent is discussing a new one. Certainty: concrete interest, no club-to-club talks. Pietuszewski, Nusa and Mohya Porto's Oskar Pietuszewski (18) has a reported 60 million euro release clause. Bayern sought accreditation to scout him, but A Bola says Porto have had no approach. Certainty: scouting interest. Eberl admires Leipzig's Antonio Nusa , but Sky's Florian Plettenberg calls a move very, very unrealistic: Leipzig will not sell in January and want 70 to 90 million euros in summer, per a Yahoo summary of his report . Gladbach's Wael Mohya (17) is being monitored, Eberl confirmed . Certainty: interest only. Barcelona ask about Tah; a centre-back is on the 2027 list Bayern have no intention of selling, but the defensive picture could shift in summer. Barcelona enquired about a winter move for Jonathan Tah , Sky reported on November 9 . Bayern see no reason to sell and Tah, under contract to 2029, does not want to leave. Certainty: enquiry. Falk and colleague Julian Agardi say Bayern want a centre-back next summer, naming Benfica's Tomás Araújo , valued at 35 to 40 million euros, via FCBinside's summary of their podcast . That likely depends on Kim Min-jae or Hiroki Ito leaving. Certainty: concrete interest, single-sourced. Olise is next on the contract list With Kane done, the club's most coveted attacker is the priority. Michael Olise is tied to 2029, and Dreesen said on November 5 that the club would sit down at the appropriate time. Romano reports Bayern rebuffed a summer approach from Real Madrid. No formal talks are confirmed this week. Ins & Outs: summer 2026 and this week In: Ismael Saibari (PSV, reported 50 to 55 million euros, Sky); Nathaniel Brown (Eintracht Frankfurt, reported about 55 million euros) Out: Leon Goretzka (Aston Villa, free); João Palhinha (Benfica, reported 14 million euros fixed, Sport1); Alexander Nübel (Beşiktaş); Jonah Kusi-Asare (Fulham, reported about 6 million euros, Bild) Out on loan: Ibrahimović, Zaragoza, Javi Fernández, Ofli, Chávez, Dalpiaz, Meier, Yanda ( club Loan Watch ) This week: Harry Kane extended to June 2029 (official, November 5) The Rumour Mill • Martin Ødegaard (Arsenal): denied. Falk: not true. • Désiré Doué (PSG): denied. Falk: PSG will not sell. • Jadon Sancho: denied. Falk cites wage concerns. • Alejandro Balde (Barcelona): rumour. Mundo Deportivo says he is open to leaving; no talks with Bayern. • Eli Junior Kroupi (Bournemouth): rumour, fading; no longer a priority per 90min citing Bild. • Nick Woltemade: no current move, per Falk. The Squad Kompany back at Säbener Straße; Musiala and Díaz close in The head coach is recovering on site, but nobody will put a date on his return to the bench. Vincent Kompany has been back at the training ground since the start of this week, the club said in a statement quoted by FCBinside . He collapsed on October 23 and was treated in hospital for meningeal irritation until late October. Whether he coaches against Köln remains open. Honorary president Uli Hoeneß told BR on November 8 he expected Kompany back in two or three weeks . Until then Aaron Danks stays in charge. At Mainz he made two changes from the Atlético win, bringing in Pavlović and Brown for Bischof and Davies. Returns and absentees Jamal Musiala joined part of team training on November 5, Bild reported , after a torn muscle fibre in his thigh. Danks hopes he and Luis Díaz can fully rejoin training after the break . Ismael Saibari had ankle surgery and is out for about three months; Serge Gnabry is expected out until around Christmas. Availability Manuel Neuer: partial tendon tear, right foot. No timeline. Ismael Saibari: torn ankle syndesmosis, surgery. About three months. Serge Gnabry: thigh muscle injury. Around Christmas. Jamal Musiala: muscle-fibre tear, thigh. Targeting return after the break. Luis Díaz: hamstring. Targeting return after the break. Vincent Kompany (coach): recovering at the training ground; return date open. Hoeneß stirs the dressing room The same BR appearance caused a stir. Hoeneß called Musiala's situation a dilemma and publicly doubted whether he would regain his old level after the health problems he has disclosed. Sky's Kerry Hau wrote that the comments harm team unity. Hoeneß also said Karl, 18, lacks humility, after the teenager's dismissive celebration against Atlético, per dpa . Karl answered on the pitch with his second goal in two games. Form lines Michael Olise leads the squad with six Bundesliga goals and four assists, joint third in the league scoring chart behind Niclas Füllkrug (nine) and Patrik Schick (eight), per Ligainsider . Kimmich, back since the BVB game after missing three matches following his father's death, scored his first goal of the season at Mainz. The Campus Assomo's double keeps Bayern II rolling; the U19s stay top Dante's reserves are nine league games unbeaten, and Leonhard Haas's U19s are already through to the next stage. FC Bayern II beat SpVgg Bayreuth 3-1 at the Grünwalder Stadion on November 7. Bastian Assomo scored twice and David Santos Daiber added a stoppage-time third, per the BFV . Dante's side are eighth in the Regionalliga Bayern on 24 points. Saturday's game at Ansbach has been called off, the club says. The Lead Five Clear, Seven Clean Sheets, One Winger Missing Arsenal reach the last international break of the year on top of the Premier League, with the division's meanest defence and without their best winger. The numbers behind the title defence, and why the sixteen days after November 21 will decide its shape. T here is a particular kind of quiet that settles over Arsenal when things are going well. Not the giddy quiet of a club that has just found something. The flat, administrative quiet of a club that has decided what it is. Ten Premier League games into the defence of their title, Mikel Arteta's side have won nine, lost one, scored fifteen and conceded five. They sit five points clear. Nobody at the Emirates sounds especially excited about it. They should not, because the football has not been exciting. It has been correct. The 1-0 win over Hull City on November 7, the last act before the players scattered to their national teams, was the purest expression of the method yet: 67 per cent of the ball, 21 shots to seven, ten on target to two, and a single goal, scrambled in on 72 minutes by Martin Odegaard after Konstantinos Tzolakis had parried Noni Madueke 's low drive into his path. It was Odegaard's fifth of the season and Arsenal's 34th Premier League 1-0 win under Arteta, more than any other side has managed since his first game in December 2019, according to Sky Sports . Hull's goalkeeper made nine saves. Arsenal's made two. The expected goals read 1.08 to 0.34. Reduced to its bones, this is a team that creates a great deal, converts a little of it, and then simply refuses to let anything back. The defence is doing something historically rare The clean sheet against Hull was the seventh in ten league games and the tenth in sixteen matches across all competitions. Arsenal arrived at the break on a run of 444 minutes without conceding a Premier League goal, by Sky Sports' count. They have also won their last ten home games in all competitions, seven of them in the league. Arteta's longest such run remains twelve, set in November 2022. Five goals conceded in ten games is the number that should frighten the rest of the division, and it has been achieved with a centre-back pairing nobody would have predicted in August. Ezri Konsa , signed from Aston Villa for an initial 51 million pounds, has slotted in beside Gabriel Magalhaes and against Hull won all seven of the duels he contested while completing 51 of 53 passes. William Saliba , Arsenal's best defender for three seasons, has not played a competitive minute this season. "We need to praise our players for the way they go about every game." Mikel Arteta, after the Hull City win The one defeat still explains the season The single blemish came at the Amex on September 19, where Brighton won 3-0. It remains the only time Arsenal have conceded more than once in the league, and it is also the reason the table looks the way it does: Brighton's goal difference of plus nineteen is the best in the division, and the gap at the top is five rather than eight. Arsenal have the points. Brighton have the goals. Arteta's answer has been to lean further into control rather than chase the arithmetic. Bruno Guimaraes , bought from Newcastle United for 75 million pounds in August and now the man who goes back to face his old club on November 21, has taken over as the metronome in a 4-2-3-1 that asks very little of its full-backs in transition. Against Hull, Arsenal completed 490 of 569 passes. There was no counter-attacking to speak of because there was nothing to counter. Saka's absence is the live problem Bukayo Saka injured a thigh muscle in the 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich on October 21 and has now missed five matches. Arteta's only timeframe has been a flat "weeks", with a further note that Saka will "start hitting the pitch" after the international break. There is no date. There has been no club bulletin. The vice-captain was not in England's squad, and Arsenal have won four of the five games since he limped off, drawing the other at Fleetwood Town. That last fact is the trap. Madueke has been outstanding in his place, to the point where Arteta told Sky Sports he "has become a different player", and Christos Tzolis , the 34 million pound arrival from Club Brugge , has had a run of starts on the left. But neither has Saka's capacity to decide a game that has gone flat, and Arsenal's margins are thin by design. Six of their nine league wins have come by a single goal. Why the sixteen days after the break matter most Arsenal come back on Saturday November 21 at St James' Park. Three days later they host Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, where they lie third in the league phase on ten points from four unbeaten games. Five days after that, Manchester City come to the Emirates. Then Brentford away on December 2, and Tottenham away on December 6. That is five matches in sixteen days against two of the three best teams in England, one of the best in Germany, and a derby. There is at least no Carabao Cup to navigate, because Fleetwood Town knocked Arsenal out on penalties on October 27. Arteta spent the week before the break publicly playing down the schedule and privately managing Declan Rice , who came off on 63 minutes against Hull and about whom the manager said: "We are really looking after him more than any other season." The title defence is in excellent order. It is also being run with a very small number of spare parts, in a month where the fixture list stops being kind. Saliba's return, now genuinely close, may be the most valuable thing to happen to Arsenal in November. Barcelona, the Camp Nou, and the Hardest Night of Renee Slegers' Reign Arsenal Women go to the Spotify Camp Nou on Thursday sitting sixth in the Women's Super League, missing five forwards, and eighteen months removed from beating the same opponent in a European final. Eighteen months ago Arsenal beat Barcelona 1-0 in Lisbon to win the Women's Champions League. On Thursday evening they walk out at the Spotify Camp Nou for the first time in the club's history, for the first meeting between the two sides since that final, and almost nothing about their situation is the same. Arsenal are sixth in the WSL on thirteen points from nine games, with three wins, four draws and two defeats and a goal difference of exactly zero. Manchester City are twelve points ahead of them. Renee Slegers , who took the team to that trophy, has had the kind of autumn in which a manager's name starts appearing in sentences it did not use to appear in. The 2-1 win at Anfield on November 8 was a genuine reprieve, and a tactically interesting one. Alessia Russo scored both goals, the first from a low Emily Fox cross and the second from a Lisa Baum delivery. Both came from the right. Liverpool set up to force Arsenal down their left, and Arsenal went the other way instead. Slegers said afterwards that Liverpool "wanted to have us on our left side". Fox was the story. Playing, in her own description, "more of a free role", she was advanced inside twenty-five seconds, created four chances, and carried the ball some forty yards on one occasion. Arseblog called it possibly the best individual Arsenal performance of the season. It is worth noting that she signed a contract extension in late September. The injury list going into Barcelona is brutal. Stina Blackstenius , who scored the goal in Lisbon, is out with an Achilles problem. Mariona Caldentey has a hamstring injury, Michelle Agyemang a knee, Katie Reid an ankle and Selina Cerci a knee. Chloe Kelly is back on grass but not fit. Daphne van Domselaar is not on the Champions League squad list. Barcelona, who beat Lyon 4-0 in the 2026 final in Oslo, have lost Alexia Putellas and Mapi Leon to London City Lionesses and Salma Paralluelo to Lyon, and have Aitana Bonmati back from a knee injury. Claudia Pina and Ewa Pajor remain. Slegers has been candid about what Thursday will involve. "We will have to suffer," she said, adding that Arsenal will need to "put bodies on the lines" and be "really disciplined". Around a thousand supporters are travelling from London. The match was moved from Wednesday to Thursday because of a general strike in Spain. Arsenal are fifth in the league phase on seven points from three, by arseblog's count, having beaten HB Koge 1-0, drawn 2-2 at Paris FC and beaten Benfica 3-0. A top-four finish avoids the knockout play-off round, and the games that decide it are this one and Lyon at home on November 19. It is, as arseblog put it, a make-or-break week. Transfer News Zubimendi Says No. Spain Keeps Saying Yes. Down to 100 Premier League minutes and linked with Atletico Madrid by three Spanish outlets inside three days, Arsenal's 2025 signing from Real Sociedad went to Marca and shut the door. The reporting has not stopped. The story broke in Spain, as these stories usually do. RNE Deportes reported that Martin Zubimendi was close to a move to Atletico Madrid . Relevo followed with the detail that did the damage: that the midfielder's relationship with Mikel Arteta had gone "cold" after "friction towards the end of last season". AS added that Arsenal would want to recoup the roughly 50 million pounds they paid. What he actually said Zubimendi answered it himself, on Spain duty, in an interview with Marca published on November 10. The quotations below are the English renderings carried by Arseblog and ESPN. "There's absolutely nothing to it, and I'm not close to anything," he said. He added that he had not "wasted any energy on it" and had not "got in touch with anyone", and that he was "busy enough trying to earn a place, get playing time, and fight to win this Premier League". Asked directly whether he would see out the season at Arsenal: "Yes, I hope so. I'm happy there. I'm happy in London." He was also unusually frank about why he has fallen out of the side. "I played an enormous number of minutes last season, and, to be honest, I was tired," he told Marca, and said he had thought about psychological help without going down that path. The minutes are the real story The reporting exists because the selection record is extraordinary for a player who started all 38 league games a year ago. Zubimendi has 100 Premier League minutes this season across seven appearances, and 380 minutes in total across twelve. In the Hull City match he came on in the 89th minute. Ahead of him in league minutes: Martin Odegaard on 830, Declan Rice on 827, Myles Lewis-Skelly on 432, Bruno Guimaraes on 390 and Mikel Merino on 203. His contract runs to June 2030, which is the single most important fact in the file. Arsenal are not under pressure. FourFourTwo's own understanding is that the club would rather sell in the summer than in January, if at all. Where it sits Concrete interest, reported in Spain, publicly denied by the player, with no bid, no named Tier-1 journalist attached and no word from either club. Real Madrid and Chelsea have also been linked, more loosely. Treat the "close to leaving" framing with care: the English coverage of it is an aggregation of Spanish radio and a Spanish website, not an Ornstein or Romano report . Sources: RNE Deportes (original), Relevo, AS. No named reporter in the English coverage. Player's position: denied, on the record, to Marca on November 10. Scouting the Next Opponent Newcastle United, away, Saturday November 21 A 100 million pound sale, a 75 million pound sale to Arsenal, a new German head coach and twelfth place. St James' Park is still St James' Park. Newcastle United have had the strangest summer of any club in the division and the table shows it. They sit twelfth on twelve points from ten games, with three wins, three draws and four defeats, thirteen goals scored and sixteen conceded. Their recent league form reads draw, defeat, win, defeat, defeat. The most recent game was a 1-1 draw at Fulham on November 7, preceded by a 1-0 home defeat by Everton on November 2. The upheaval was structural. Eddie Howe stepped down on July 31 and Matthias Jaissle was appointed six days later. Then the squad was dismantled at the top end: Sandro Tonali to Tottenham for 100 million pounds, Anthony Gordon to Barcelona for 69.3 million, and Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal for 75 million on August 8. That is 244 million pounds of midfield and attack sold in five weeks. Kieran Trippier left on a free. Roughly 214 million pounds went back in, spread wide rather than deep: Nico Gonzalez from Manchester City for 47 million, Bazoumana Toure from Hoffenheim for 42.8 million, Amar Dedic from Benfica for 30.7 million, Aladji Bamba from Monaco for 30 million, Sean Steur from Ajax for 19.6 million, and two goalkeepers. Three of those signings play in central midfield. None of them is Bruno Guimaraes. Who Arsenal have to stop Anthony Elanga was Newcastle's leading league scorer in the early weeks and Harvey Barnes has been the other reliable source of goals. The two names worth more attention, though, are Jacob Murphy , who leads the squad for big chances created with three, and Toure, who leads it for shots on target per match at 1.5. With sixteen conceded in ten, Newcastle have been as leaky as they have been blunt, which argues for Arsenal taking the ball and squeezing, exactly as they did at Anfield and at Slavia Prague. Availability Joelinton is carrying a knock with a return flagged for late November and Ewen Jaouen has a hamstring injury flagged for early December. Jacob Ramsey was sent off for a second yellow card against Everton. Newcastle have no European football this season, which means a clear fortnight to prepare for this, where Arsenal will have come straight back from ten different senior international camps. William Saliba aggravated a back problem on France duty at the World Cup and has been out of the Arsenal side ever since. He avoided surgery. He played 45 minutes behind closed doors, then 45 minutes for the under-21s against Aston Villa on November 8, and he was an unused substitute at Slavia Prague on November 4. Arteta's language has moved from cautious to warm: "He's in a really good place," he said before the Hull match. "His evolution has been as expected, which is not always the case. He feels really comfortable." And yet Zinedine Zidane left him out of France's squad for this window, which is probably the right call for a player four months into a back problem and ten days from a run of five games in sixteen. Saliba has spent the fortnight at the training ground with the other senior players left behind: Noni Madueke , Kepa Arrizabalaga and Illan Meslier . The problem is that Konsa has been excellent Ezri Konsa arrived in August for an initial 51 million pounds and was widely read as a squad upgrade rather than a starter. Instead he has formed a centre-back pairing with Gabriel that has conceded five league goals in ten games. Against Hull he won seven duels out of seven and misplaced two passes in 53. Saka, and the honest version of the timeline Bukayo Saka 's thigh injury, sustained at Bayern Munich on October 21, has cost him five matches. Arteta has given two useful sentences and no date. Neither is an Arsenal statement, and the Digest is not going to pretend otherwise. Load management is now a visible policy The most revealing thing Arteta said all week was about Declan Rice , withdrawn on 63 minutes with no sign of a problem: "We are really looking after him more than any other season." Ezri Konsa was taken off at Slavia Prague purely as a precaution, with Arteta explaining that he had "played a lot, so many games in the last few weeks". This is a squad being driven with the handbrake half on, by a manager who has worked out that the title is won in April and lost in December. The Lead Eight in a row, and Mourinho's Madrid have found a shape Two away wins in four days sent Real Madrid into the international break as the form team in Spain. The questions now are about who plays, not whether it works. N obody at Valdebebas will say it out loud, but the week ended with José Mourinho 's team looking like a finished product. A 3-2 win in Athens on Wednesday was chaotic and late. A 3-0 win at Mestalla on Saturday was controlled from the first whistle. Together they made it eight straight wins in all competitions . The table explains why the run matters. Madrid sit second in La Liga on 30 points, three behind Barcelona and two clear of Atlético Madrid , per the standings after matchday 12 . In the Champions League league phase they have 12 points from 12, second only to PSG on goal difference. The only league defeats came at Betis in September and at Atlético on September 20. Athens: the game Madrid should have lost For 20 minutes at AEK, Madrid were ragged. AEK Athens led through Koita after 12 minutes, and Sports Illustrated's verdict was that without Thibaut Courtois Madrid could have been three down early. Jude Bellingham back-heeled an equaliser from Marc Cucurella's cross on 32 minutes, after an earlier effort was ruled out for offside. AEK went ahead again on 75 minutes when Pilios's shot squirmed through Courtois. Mbappé levelled three minutes later from Denzel Dumfries's cross, his sixth straight Champions League appearance with a goal. Then, in stoppage time, substitute Federico Valverde hit a 25-yard winner. Madrid finished with 70 per cent of the ball and an expected-goals tally of 3.35 to 0.86, per ESPN's match data . “At 2-2, we did not accept the draw. We decided to take a risk to win.” José Mourinho, after AEK Athens 2-3 Real Madrid Mourinho's line afterwards, reported by AfricaSoccer , was that these are matches "only Real Madrid can win in the final minutes." It was also a warning. Antonio Rüdiger struggled with Luka Jović, and Dumfries was exposed on the right. Three days later, Mourinho changed the back line. Mestalla: the version Mourinho wants At Valencia , Valverde started at right-back with the captain's armband, Ibrahima Konaté and Dean Huijsen paired in the middle, and Arda Güler returned to the attacking line. Valverde opened the scoring from about 22 yards just before the half hour, Güler finished first-time on 36 minutes, and Mbappé ran onto Güler's ball over the top to round the goalkeeper on 75, per beIN Sports . The numbers were lopsided: 68 per cent possession, 19 shots to four and an expected-goals count of 2.20 to 0.16, according to Sports Illustrated's match data . Valencia finished with ten men after José Luis Gayà's late red card. "This team smells good," Mourinho told reporters, before adding that his players were in "extreme fatigue" and that he hoped nobody came back injured from the break. The shape that is emerging Three selection calls now look settled. Valverde is the right-back, ahead of both Trent Alexander-Arnold and Dumfries. Güler and Bernardo Silva are the creators in midfield, with Valverde and Aurélien Tchouaméni no longer paired as the holding duo. And Yan Diomande, signed in the summer for a reported 140 million euros, has taken the left wing. That last call is the one with consequences. Vinícius Júnior has one goal all season and no goal involvement in seven games, per Sports Illustrated . He was suspended for the Valencia win, the last of a four-match domestic ban for pulling a Villarreal player's hair in October. He is available against Celta Vigo on November 21, and Mourinho will have to choose. Mourinho has managed the issue in public with care. He described his handling of Vinícius as "80 per cent soft hand, 20 per cent firm" and insisted the Brazilian "didn't provoke anything" when Diomande moved to the left. Valverde and Éder Militão have both backed their teammate. But Diomande has four goals to Vinícius's one, and the numbers are hard to argue with. What the break means The international window takes 18 first-team players away, per RPP and EFE , leaving Mourinho with a handful of fit seniors and academy players at Valdebebas. Madrid then play three home games in eight days: Celta on November 21, PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League on November 24, and Alavés on November 28. Barcelona and Atlético meet the same weekend Madrid face Celta, so the title picture could tighten quickly. Champions League: four wins from four (Inter, Roma, RB Leipzig, AEK). Kylian Mbappé: 17 goals in all competitions (13 in La Liga, 4 in Europe). The Boardroom Nadal joins the board as Pérez prepares a record budget The tennis great's appointment and a reported 1.4 billion euro budget both go to a members' vote on November 21. The board approved Rafael Nadal as a director at its meeting on November 3, and Real Madrid announced it the next day, according to Reuters, via Al Jazeera . The club cited his 92 singles titles and two Olympic golds, and said his values "form part of Real Madrid's identity." Nadal said he had accepted "with great enthusiasm, keen to learn and to contribute as much as I can." Reuters noted that Nadal has been talked about as a possible successor to Florentino Pérez , a suggestion he has played down. Pérez, 79, won a new four-year term in June in the club's first contested election in two decades, beating Enrique Riquelme by roughly 65 per cent to 35 per cent of votes cast, per Wikipedia's election record . The November 21 assembly The club has called its ordinary and extraordinary general assemblies of member delegates for Saturday, November 21, the same day Madrid host Celta, per the official notice . The agenda covers the 2025/26 accounts, the 2026/27 budget, next season's membership fees and Nadal's ratification. Nothing on the agenda concerns statute changes or outside investment. Marca's reported figures for the budget, relayed by Bernabéu Digital , are records across the board: revenue of about 1.405 billion euros, a sporting budget of 707 million euros covering wages and amortisation, and 154.8 million euros expected from player sales. The club's audited 2025/26 revenue was 1.221 billion euros excluding transfers, with a 26.3 million euro profit. On Tuesday the club added Hotels.com as an official sponsor, with Emilio Butragueño signing at Valdebebas, per realmadrid.com . The club did not give a length; trade outlet 2Playbook reports the deal runs to 2029. The Lead La Liga, Matchday 12 Fermín's double at the Metropolitano sends Barça into the break three points clear Atlético were the better side for half an hour. Then Pedri found Fermín, Lamine Yamal found him again, and Hansi Flick's leaders passed the hardest test of their season. F or half an hour on Sunday night, Barcelona were second best at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano. Atlético Madrid led inside ten minutes, hit the crossbar and made Barça's goalkeeper work twice. Then the game turned on one deflected shot, and by the final whistle Barça were going into the international break three points clear at the top of La Liga. The opener came on ten minutes: Giuliano Simeone scored from Julián Álvarez 's cross, and Pubill headed against the bar soon after. ESPN's Sam Marsden called Atlético "the better side in the first half", and Joan García needed a one-on-one save from Álvarez as early as the sixth minute. Hansi Flick admitted afterwards that his side had been too far from their opponents in the first half to press. It showed. Barça used four different back lines over the evening, according to ESPN, and the right side, where academy graduate Brian Fariñas was playing out of position at full-back, was where Atlético kept coming. “We have the quality to win these matches.” Hansi Flick, after the 2-1 win at Atlético (ESPN) The turn The equaliser arrived on the stroke of half-time. Pedri found Fermín López , whose shot took a deflection off Pubill and went in. Flick's verdict was blunt: "The 1-1 was very important before the break." Barça did not trail again. At half-time Flick took Fariñas off and sent on Frenkie de Jong at right-back. Vavel rated his 45 minutes a 7.5, the best mark of any substitute, and Barça took hold of the ball. Andreas Christensen, back from injury, replaced João Cancelo after an hour, with Gerard Martín moving to left-back. The winner, after 66 minutes, was a Lamine Yamal special: a through ball that sent Fermín clear, and a first-time finish. "That pass was half a goal," Fermín said afterwards . It was his second of the night, his eighth of the season in all competitions and it came in his 100th La Liga appearance. Referee: Alberola Rojas Sources: club report , EFE , ESPN What it means The table tells the story. Barça have 33 points from 12 games, three more than Real Madrid and five more than Atlético. They have scored 48 and conceded 13, and the only league defeat is still the 2-1 Clásico loss at Spotify Camp Nou on October 25. Asked to rate the run into the break, Flick said "a 10" out of 10. There were warnings, too. Álvarez lobbed over the bar when clean through early in the second half, and Yamal could not connect with Anthony Gordon's cross for a third late on. Cancelo, so good against Aston Villa five days earlier, lost Giuliano Simeone for the opener, per ESPN. The club's search for a January defender did not come from nowhere. Diego Simeone said his side were "not as clinical" as usual. Fermín went further: "Last year they beat us in the Cup and the Champions League," he told reporters . This time Barça won the duel that mattered, without the injured Rodri, Jules Koundé and Dani Olmo, and with four academy players called up to train with the first team beforehand. The money A €3m to €4m margin and a €60m choice La Liga has set Barça's salary limit at €582.7m, against a budget of €636m for squad wages and amortisation, and the club sits under the 1:1 rule, so it can spend one euro for every euro it saves or earns. Crónica Global puts the spare margin at about €3m to €4m and reports that Deco is slowing some renewals to protect it ( Crónica Global, Nov 10 ). That leaves three routes for a January defender: a free agent, a loan with wages covered, or a sale. Sport has also reported, via Barça Universal in September, that the club holds about €60m of allowance it can either use in January or carry into 2027-28, when Camp Nou roof works are expected to cost matchday income ( Barça Universal ). The request to carry it over must be made before the window opens. Outgoing Balde accepts he must leave Alejandro Balde , 23, has accepted that he must move on, according to The Athletic ( via Sports Mole ). He had five appearances and no starts when that was reported, and was unused at the Metropolitano. Manchester United have been interested since the summer. Romano says a January exit is "not something that we have to rule out 100 percent". Status: club open to a sale ; no fee reported. k: Back-to-back home defeats to Bayern and Barcelona ended a seven-game league winning run and exposed the gap Simeone admits still exists.
x: STOPPAGE TIME The Weekly Atlético Madrid Digest Everything rojiblanco, every week Edition of Tuesday, November 10, 2026 · Season 2026-27 La Liga: 3rd, 28 pts, 5 behind Barcelona · Last ten (oldest to newest) W 4-0 OSA W 2-1 RMA W 2-1 ALA W 2-0 MUN W 1-0 ESP D 1-1 STU W 1-0 DEP W 2-0 LEV L 0-2 BAY L 1-2 BAR Next: Getafe (A), La Liga, Sun Nov 22, 12:00 PM PT In this edition The Lead · Player Ratings · Scouting the Next Opponent · Transfer News · The Squad · The Academy · Atlético Femenino · Players Away · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch Collapse all If you read nothing else Atlético lost 0-2 at home to Bayern and 1-2 to Barcelona, ending a seven-game La Liga winning run; they sit third, five points off top. RNE, Relevo and AS report concrete Atlético interest in Arsenal's Martín Zubimendi for January; no bid has been reported. Atlético are 23rd in the Champions League table with 4 points, and next play Getafe away on November 22 at 12:00 PM Pacific. Next match Opponent: Getafe (away) Competition: La Liga, Matchday 13 Date: Sunday, November 22, 2026 Kickoff: 12:00 PM Pacific (21:00 in Madrid) Venue: Coliseum, Getafe Watch in the US: ESPN+ and ESPN Deportes, per ESPN's fixture listing The Lead Two Nights at the Metropolitano, One Hard Lesson Bayern punished one mistake, Barcelona punished two. In five days a seven-game league run ended, the Champions League table turned awkward and Simeone admitted what everyone could see: the elite are still a step ahead. F or seven weeks Atlético had looked like a side built for more than third place. Seven straight La Liga wins, a 2-1 derby victory over Real Madrid and a 2-0 Champions League win over Manchester United had made the new-look squad feel finished. Then came the two biggest home nights of the autumn, and two defeats. On Tuesday Bayern won 2-0 at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano. On Sunday Barcelona won 2-1 at the same ground, with Fermín López scoring either side of the break after Giuliano Simeone had put Atlético ahead. The international break now arrives with Atlético third on 28 points, five behind the leaders. Bayern: control without a cutting edge Simeone said his side had Bayern exactly where they wanted them. For 53 minutes that was arguable. Atlético sat in a compact 4-4-2 with Sørloth a surprise starter beside Julián Álvarez , and Bayern, led from the touchline by assistant Aaron Danks with Vincent Kompany absent on medical grounds, were kept largely in front of the block ( ESPN ). The game turned on one moment. Le Normand was slow on the ball in his own area, Lennart Karl nipped in and lifted it over Oblak on 54 minutes ( beIN ). Karl, 18, became only the fourth player to reach five Champions League goals before turning 19. Konrad Laimer added the second from a Harry Kane pass on 74. The numbers back up Simeone's reading of the first hour but not of the night. ESPN's data gave Bayern 1.77 expected goals to Atlético's 0.83, and 58 percent of the ball. Oblak made five saves, one of them tipping an Upamecano shot onto the bar. It was Atlético's first home defeat to Bayern in the Champions League ( MundoNow ). Key facts Bayern, Nov 3: Champions League MD4, Atlético 0-2 Bayern (Karl 54', Laimer 74'). xG 0.83 to 1.77; possession 42 to 58 percent. Barcelona, Nov 8: La Liga MD12, Atlético 1-2 Barcelona (Giuliano 10'; Fermín 45', 66'). xG 1.53 to 1.60; possession 37 to 63 percent. La Liga: 3rd, 28 points from 12 games, five behind Barcelona (33) and two behind Real Madrid (30). Champions League: 23rd of 36, 4 points (W1 D1 L2), knockout play-off zone. Season, all competitions: 16 played, 10 won, 2 drawn, 4 lost; 27 scored, 15 conceded. “Liverpool and Bayern are better than us, we have to get closer to them.” Diego Simeone after the Bayern defeat, via SoccerNews Barcelona: the better performance, the same result Sunday was different in feel. Simeone rehearsed the XI on Friday and made two changes, dropping Le Normand and Sørloth, moving Llorente to the right of a back four and pushing Lee Kang-in into a free role behind Álvarez ( Comuniate ). It worked early: Álvarez crossed and Giuliano scored on 10 minutes. Álvarez had already been played through one on one and denied by the Barcelona goalkeeper, and Pubill and Pedri both hit the crossbar before the break. Then Fermín equalised on 45 minutes, and on 66 Lamine Yamal slipped him through for the winner ( ESPN ). Atlético had 37 percent of the ball but matched Barcelona almost exactly on expected goals, 1.53 to 1.60. What the week actually tells us The common thread is not effort or shape. It is margins at both ends. Bayern needed one Atlético error; Barcelona needed two moments of quality. At the other end Atlético created enough against Barcelona to win and finished like a side that had stopped expecting to. Álvarez, to the disgruntlement of some home fans, missed the one-on-one and lobbed over on 55 minutes ( ESPN ). Simeone backed him without hedging. "Le queremos y para llegar donde queremos necesitamos al mejor Julián Álvarez. Si no, no vamos a llegar," he said ( El Gol Digital ). He called his side a team "en construcción" and said he was proud of the players. That is the honest frame: a squad rebuilt with roughly €123m of summer signings (El Desmarque's tally) is good enough to beat most of La Liga, not yet to beat Europe's best on a bad night. The European picture is the real concern. Atlético are 23rd of 36 on four points, inside the knockout play-off places but well short of the top eight that sporting director Mateu Alemany named as the target before the Bayern game ( Esto es Atleti ). Viking at home on November 25 is now close to a must-win. The break comes at the right time. Valdano put the week down to the physical and emotional cost of two huge games in five days ( Esto es Atleti ). Cuti Romero is targeting the Getafe trip, and Getafe, Viking and Elche come before the December 2 return to Barcelona. Nine points from those three would make this week look like a blip. Simeone, Aragonés and the Next Contract The record that slipped away on Sunday matters less than the deal being drawn up for 2029. The 2-0 win at Levante on October 31 put Simeone level with Luis Aragonés on La Liga coaching wins for the club ( Football España ). Beating Barcelona would have given him the record outright. It waits now for Getafe on November 22. The bigger story is the next contract. Simeone's deal runs to June 2027. Onda Cero's Edu Pidal reported on November 9 that the board has decided to extend it by two seasons, to June 2029 ( El Gol Digital ). Nothing is signed or announced. Esto es Atleti added on November 10, without naming a source, that Simeone does not want a three or four year deal and would prefer to go season by season ( Esto es Atleti ). Treat both reports as direction of travel, not done deals. Scouting the Next Opponent Getafe: Unbeatable at Home, Toothless Away Bordalás's side have not lost at the Coliseum this season and have not scored on the road. Atlético go there first after the break. Getafe are 15th on 12 points with a goal difference of minus 10, two points above the relegation places ( LaLiga ). The split is extreme: three wins and three draws at home (8 scored, 4 conceded) and six defeats from six away, with no goals scored and 14 conceded. Atlético visit the half of that record that works. José Bordalás is still in charge and the identity is familiar: duels, set pieces and a compact, deep block. At Villarreal last weekend he picked Soria; Carvajal, Boselli, Djené, Mojica; Mangala, Gudelj, Andrés García, Mario Martín; Satriano, Ünal, and lost 2-0 to two late goals ( LaGrada ). The players to stop Martín Satriano leads the team in both goals (3) and assists (2) in the league. Enes Ünal has two goals and an assist but is nursing an ankle problem. David Soria is in goal, and Bordalás has admitted his side struggle to string passes together ( Al Cabo de la Calle ). Getafe will be without Nemanja Gudelj, suspended after his fifth yellow card ( FútbolFantasy ). Uche (knee ligaments, out until May 2027) and Juanmi are out, Zaid Romero is a doubt with a quadriceps issue and Borja Mayoral is available again after illness. Where Atlético can hurt them Only eight league goals in 12 games suggests Getafe are poorly built to chase a game. An early goal, the thing Atlético managed against Barcelona, changes the whole shape of this fixture. Without Gudelj, their most experienced holding midfielder, there should be more room for Barrios and Koke to turn. Doubtful: Zaid Romero, Ünal Recent meetings: Atlético 1-0 Getafe (Mar 14, 2026); Getafe 0-1 Atlético (Nov 23, 2025); Getafe 2-1 Atlético (Mar 9, 2025) Transfer News Zubimendi Moves to the Top of the January List Three outlets report concrete interest in the Arsenal midfielder, and two Atlético players have gone public with their approval. The newest and biggest thread of the week is Martín Zubimendi . RNE's Silvia Barba reported on November 9 that the Arsenal midfielder is "close" to Atlético and could arrive in the winter window. Relevo's Marcos Durán and AS followed on November 10, both confirming the interest ( Sport Witness , Yahoo ). The logic is simple. With Barrios and Cardoso both carrying knocks and Koke on a one-year deal, a senior midfielder is the most widely reported need. Durán described Zubimendi's relationship with Mikel Arteta as "cold". AS says Arsenal would want back what they paid, put at €60m; El Desmarque says €70m. No bid, fee structure or loan proposal has been reported. A swap involving Julián Álvarez appears only as El Desmarque speculation. Certainty: concrete interest, three outlets. The dressing room has already voted. Álex Baena told Cadena SER "Me encantaría que viniera" ( Sport Witness ), and Pablo Barrios told RNE "Martín es un jugadorazo" ( Esto es Atleti ). A left-back to push Grimaldo Marca reported on November 10 that Villarreal's Sergi Cardona , 27, is the main option to compete with Grimaldo ( El Desmarque ). His contract ends in June 2027, which would keep the price modest. The position has been thin since a late move for Tagliafico was dropped and reserve centre-back Dani Martínez was converted to cover. Certainty: link, single origin (Marca); no contact with Villarreal reported. Sørloth, Juventus and the outgoing column Juventus are considering a fresh January approach for Alexander Sørloth , per Gazzetta dello Sport as relayed by ESPN . Atlético reportedly wanted around €40m in the summer, and Esto es Atleti says only a "considerable" offer would be entertained ( Esto es Atleti ). With no goals yet this season and a quiet hour against Barcelona, his case for staying is not getting stronger. Certainty: link. The club plans to reassess Michael Carrick's position over the international break; reports say no official contact has been made with other coaches. Matheus Cunha's double beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League, but his red card rules him out at Sporting CP. The Lead Carrick's reprieve runs into the international break A first win in ten against Roma bought Michael Carrick a week. A wild 4-4 with Aston Villa left United 18th, and the people who decide his future now have a fortnight to make up their minds. F or a few seconds on Sunday evening, Old Trafford believed again. Patrick Dorgu rose to head in Bruno Fernandes 's corner in the 96th minute, and United had drawn 4-4 with Villa after trailing by two goals twice. Then the table refreshed. United are 18th, eight league games without a win, with one victory from ten. That is the context for the fortnight ahead. The international break gives the club's hierarchy room to do what it did not do in late October: decide, calmly and without a match looming, whether Michael Carrick is the man to lead the climb. The next game is at Liverpool on November 22. A week of two faces The week began with relief. On Tuesday, Roma led 2-0 at Old Trafford inside 17 minutes in the Champions League, the second a penalty for handball. Fernandes scored a retaken penalty on 58 minutes. Matheus Cunha then struck twice late on, the winner coming on 86 minutes, to end a run of nine games without a win ( Sky Sports ). The numbers flattered nobody's doubts about effort. United's xG was 2.72 to Roma's 1.53, and Roma did not have a shot after half-time, according to Sports Illustrated . Cunha was then sent off for a second booking in stoppage time, his first yellow coming for celebrating shirtless in the crowd. Carrick refused to frame it as personal salvation. "I really 100% wasn't thinking about myself," he told ESPN . His captain went further: "We don't need to save anyone's job," Fernandes said to Sky Sports . Sunday's chaos, and what it exposed Villa scored after 59 seconds through Alysson , and Nicolas Jackson made it 2-0 after three minutes and 40 seconds, the earliest United have ever been two down in a Premier League game, according to Opta Analyst . Senne Lammens spilled the shot that led to the second. United came back through a Fernandes penalty and Youri Tielemans before half-time. Villa went ahead again through a John McGinn penalty, after Diogo Dalot fouled Alysson, and a Leon Goretzka finish on 53 minutes. Joshua Zirkzee and Dorgu, both substitutes, rescued a point in stoppage time ( ESPN ). “It's not going to happen, no.” Michael Carrick, asked after the Villa draw whether he would resign (via Goal) The record books noticed both halves. No Premier League side had come from two goals down twice to draw a game. But United also have no clean sheet in their first ten league games for the first time since 1986-87, and the 18th place is their lowest at this stage of a top-flight season since that same year ( Opta Analyst ). Inside the boardroom The decision sits with Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox , with Sir Jim Ratcliffe above them. After crisis talks in late October they gave Carrick more time. David Ornstein of The Athletic reported on November 5 that the club had issued a vote of confidence with a three-match assessment, and that a lack of an obvious replacement was a factor ( Football365 ). Since then United have lost at Chelsea, beaten Roma and drawn with Villa. Laurie Whitwell of The Athletic said on Sunday that a reassessment is planned around the break but there is no immediate urgency. Fabrizio Romano said United have made no official contact with other coaches and expect a decision before January ( Football365 ). If they do act, Sky Sports reported on November 5 that the club is unlikely to appoint another interim ( Sky Sports ). The same Sky report listed Julian Nagelsmann, Fabian Hurzeler and Eddie Howe among the names being weighed, and the Guardian reported in late October that Howe was Wilcox's preference ( Irish Examiner ). None of that is confirmed by the club. What to judge him on Carrick's case rests on credit earned last season, when he took over from Ruben Amorim in January, finished third ( Sports Mole ) and signed a deal to 2028 in May ( ESPN ). The case against is this autumn: a back line that concedes in clusters, a goalkeeper short of confidence, and one league win in ten. Before the Villa game he admitted the club had given him no assurances. "Whatever is going to happen is going to happen," he said ( Goal ). The next fortnight will tell us which way it goes. Anfield, on November 22, may be the first game of a new era or the first test of a renewed mandate. Scouting the Next Opponent Liverpool at Anfield: the worst possible fixture at the worst possible time Liverpool are fourth under a new head coach, but they are carrying injuries in midfield and United have won the last two meetings. United's first game after the break is at Liverpool on Sunday, November 22, moved by Sky Sports to a 4:30pm UK kickoff, which is 8:30am Pacific ( Sky Sports ). Liverpool are fourth with 18 points from ten games, ten clear of United, after a 3-1 win over Crystal Palace on Sunday in which Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak scored ( ESPN ). This is a new Liverpool. Andoni Iraola replaced Arne Slot in the summer. We could not confirm his preferred shape at Anfield, but his Bournemouth sides were built on an intense, high press, which is exactly the kind of pressure that has rattled United's build-up from the back this autumn. Their form has wobbled too: they lost 1-0 to Arsenal on November 1. History offers United a sliver of hope. k: Seven straight wins have turned into three defeats as Forest beat City 3-1, exposing structural flaws and new defensive injuries before a brutal run of fixtures.

The Lead Seven up, three down: what has gone wrong for Maresca's City A record-breaking start has curdled into the club's worst league run since 2004. The problems are structural, the injuries are mounting, and the fixtures after the break are brutal. S ix weeks ago Manchester City looked unstoppable. Enzo Maresca had won his first seven Premier League games, a record for a new manager in the competition. On Saturday his side lost 3-1 at Nottingham Forest, a third straight league defeat, and they go into the international break third, six points behind Arsenal. The run reads Aston Villa away (1-2), Brighton at home (0-1) and now Forest away (1-3). City have scored two goals in those three games and conceded six. According to The National , it is the club's worst league sequence since the autumn of 2004. The City Ground defeat was the bleakest of the three. City were 2-0 down inside 18 minutes, their earliest two-goal deficit in a league game since Liverpool in November 2019, according to GOAL . They then had 78 per cent of the ball, 665 accurate passes and 1.59 expected goals to Forest's 1.00 ( ESPN ), and still lost by two. How Forest pulled it apart The opener, after six minutes, came from the way City want to play. Forest pressed high, Jair Cunha took the ball off Joško Gvardiol in City's half, and finished. Liam Delap added the second on 18 minutes after a mix-up between Iliman Ndiaye and Elliot Anderson, then sealed it on the counter with 17 minutes left. Rayan Cherki's half-volley into the top corner on 52 minutes briefly offered a way back. Fernández had already headed wide from six yards and Jair cleared a Haaland effort off the line before the break ( ESPN ). ESPN's match data counts three big chances for City and none for Forest. We need to have balance. We won seven in a row. Now we have lost three in a row, so we need balance on that. Enzo Maresca, after the Forest defeat Maresca's own diagnosis was candid. "First one is a consequence of the way we want to play," he said. "Second and third goals quite similar: we lost the duel then concede on transition." He added: "We are conceding too many goals unfortunately," while insisting there was "no panic" ( BBC Sport via Yahoo ). The structural problem The sharpest reading came from Jonathan Wilson in The Guardian on Monday. His case: a high back four is being exposed in transition, and with Rodri sold to Barcelona the midfield lacks a natural screen. Enzo Fernández and Cherki are light defensively, so Anderson is doing the physical work of two players. The numbers support him. City have not kept a clean sheet in the eight games since the 3-0 win at Anfield on October 11, conceding 17 goals in that time. Gianluigi Donnarumma has also made costly errors, including at his near post in Leipzig on Wednesday. Wilson also raised a harder question: whether the guilty verdict on 114 of the Premier League's 115 charges, delivered in late September and now under appeal, is weighing on the dressing room. "The issue is tactical," he wrote, "but it may not only be tactical." Key facts Run W7 then L3 in the league; the first losing run of the Maresca era Position 3rd, 21 points from 10 games; Arsenal top on 27, Brighton 2nd on 22 Goals 21 scored, 13 conceded in the league (GD +8) Clean sheets None in eight games since October 11 Europe 7th in the Champions League league phase on 9 points (W3 L1) Next Fulham (H) Nov 21, Napoli (H) Nov 24, Arsenal (A) Nov 28 or 29 Injuries arrive at the worst time The defensive reshuffle will be forced, not chosen. Marc Guéhi went off at half-time with a hip problem, had a scan and has withdrawn from the England squad , with Dan Burn called up. Gvardiol also came off at the break; Maresca said he "had some issue already during the week." Both "asked for a change," Maresca said. Antoine Semenyo has been out since mid-October with a knee injury expected to keep him out until December, and Nico O'Reilly was left out of the England squad because he is not fully fit. What comes next The break could hardly arrive at a better moment, but what follows it is unforgiving. Fulham visit the Etihad on Saturday, November 21, Napoli follow on the Tuesday in the Champions League, and then comes the trip to Arsenal, the leaders, the following weekend. Lose at the Emirates and the gap could be nine points before December. Win the three and the narrative changes overnight. Maresca called his side "a work in progress" in Leipzig and "a learning journey" in Nottingham. The next fortnight will show how quickly it is learning. Haaland wears the armband and finds Leipzig again Wednesday's 3-2 win at RB Leipzig showed both sides of this team. City led through Castello Lukeba's own goal from O'Reilly's cross, were pegged back by Ridle Baku, went ahead through Fernández's header and were caught again by Antonio Nusa within three minutes ( Bundesliga.com ). Erling Haaland, captain for the first time this season, settled it on 78 minutes from Anderson's low cut-back. It was his 13th goal in nine games against Leipzig, the most he has scored against any club ( Sky Sports ). Leipzig had won all five home games before kick-off without conceding ( AFP ). Off the pitch: the appeal clock is ticking City lodged their appeal on October 1 against the commission's verdict that they breached 114 of the 115 charges, saying the decision contains "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact" ( Sky Sports ). No sanction has yet been set, and no hearing date has been announced ( ESPN ). The appeal rules allow 12 weeks for a hearing, which points to late December, though City may contest the timetable. The BBC's Dan Roan explained on November 5 that the league board argues for a sanction and a three-person commission decides it ( BBC via Yahoo ). Gary Neville spoke of an "obvious cloud" on Sky this week ( Sky Sports ). Elsewhere, Sheikh Mansour put a further £100m into City Football Group in October, lifting his stake to about 81 per cent ( Inside World Football ). On Saturday the club released a charity shirt with Manchester band Blossoms to mark 40 years of City in the Community ( Yahoo ). Scouting the Next Opponent Next up: Fulham (H), Saturday, November 21 Arbeloa's Fulham like the ball, and that may suit City Fifteenth and still finding their feet under a new coach, Fulham have tightened up lately. But their open style leaves space behind. Fulham sit 15th with 10 points from 10 games (W2 D4 L4), with 10 goals scored and 12 conceded. Álvaro Arbeloa , appointed in July to replace Marco Silva, failed to win any of his first six league games but is unbeaten in the four since (W2 D2). They drew 1-1 with Newcastle on Saturday, Rodrigo Muniz equalising three minutes after Jacob Murphy's opener ( theScore ). Before that came a 1-0 win over Hull, a 1-0 win at Coventry and a 1-1 draw at Aston Villa. System and style Arbeloa sets up in a 4-2-3-1 with Sander Berge anchoring a double pivot and Oscar Bobb, Josh King and Alex Iwobi behind Gonzalo García. Fulham average 58 per cent possession, fifth-highest in the league ( FotMob ). "We're not the best team in open games," Arbeloa admitted in late October ( beIN Sports ). The players to stop are King, the top scorer with two league goals; Iwobi, who takes the set pieces and leads the side in line-breaking passes; and García, whose 4.1 expected goals have not yet brought a league goal. Muniz is a dangerous option from the bench. Where City can hurt them Fulham often leave only three players behind the ball, and counter-attacks have punished them ( Fulhamish ). After five games they had allowed the most big chances in the league ( Fantasy Football Scout ). Set pieces are not a weakness, though: they have conceded only once from a dead ball. Tom Cairney has a knee problem but is expected back. The history favours City heavily: they have won the last five meetings, most recently 3-0 at the Etihad in February ( Ahram Online ). By 11v11's count City had won 19 straight meetings going into last December's 5-4 at Craven Cottage. Rayan Aït-Nouri: expected to leave The clearest story at City is an exit. The Athletic's Sam Lee reported on November 3 that Rayan Aït-Nouri is expected to leave in January if a suitable offer arrives (as cited by City Xtra ). The left-back, signed for £31m in 2025, has not played a league minute this season, behind Gvardiol and O'Reilly. Sky Germany's Florian Plettenberg reported that personal terms would not be an issue for Manchester United, with the relationship between the two clubs the main obstacle ( Football365 ). Juventus are preparing a loan with an option to buy, per The Athletic, and Sports Mole judges them the likelier destination. Certainty: concrete interest from other clubs, no bid reported. Aït-Nouri was also left out of Algeria's squad this month after a dispute over playing time in September ( Africa Soccer ). Who replaces him? The left-back question If Aït-Nouri goes, City may look for cover. Spanish daily Sport reported that agent Jorge Mendes has contacted City about Barcelona's Alejandro Balde , with Barça open to around €40m and Mendes preferring a loan with an option ( via City Xtra ). Certainty: rumour, single-sourced, and dependent on Aït-Nouri leaving. A striker for the future Italian daily La Stampa reported that City and Chelsea have asked Club Brugge about striker Nicolò Tresoldi , with a €50m starting price and Brugge reluctant to sell mid-season ( via Sport Witness ). Graeme Bailey also reported City tracking him ( Yahoo ). Certainty: concrete interest, two mid-tier sources. Grealish and Monga: loans under strain Jack Grealish has missed four games for Everton, including two after a breach of club discipline in late October. Reports split on what comes next: Football Insider says Everton could end the loan in January ( Yahoo ), while TEAMtalk says there are no such plans and he is targeting the Brentford game on November 23 ( TEAMtalk ). His City contract expires in June 2027. Swansea and City are negotiating to end Jeremy Monga's loan early, according to local reports relayed by The72 . The winger, signed from Leicester in the summer, has not played for Swansea. Certainty: advanced talks, local sources only. The Squad A defence in flux, and Anderson asked to do everything Maresca's rotation of full-backs is about to become a necessity, and the midfield balance is the debate of the break. City manager Enzo Maresca has used a 4-2-3-1 all season, rotating between two full-back pairings: Nunes and O'Reilly, or Khusanov and Gvardiol. At Forest, Rúben Dias wore the armband; at Leipzig, Haaland did. Phil Foden, scorer of a hat-trick against AEK Athens, started on the bench on Saturday. The midfield is the hot topic. With Fernández and Cherki both attack-minded, Elliot Anderson is being asked to cover as a holding midfielder and a box-to-box runner at once. He was City's best player at Leipzig and, by most ratings, their best midfielder at Forest. Availability Injuries and doubts Marc Guéhi Hip. Off at half-time at Forest; withdrew from England. If Guéhi and Gvardiol both miss Fulham, the likeliest pairing is Dias with Khusanov, who looked more comfortable after moving into the middle in the second half at Forest. Vitor Reis, on Brazil duty this week, is the other option. The Academy A first Youth League win, and Samba's debut still echoing City 's under-19s won 2-1 at RB Leipzig in the UEFA Youth League on Wednesday, their first win of this season's campaign, with goals from Teddie Lamb on 53 minutes and a Dexter Oliver penalty on 57 ( Foot Mercato ). Ryan McAidoo and Braithwaite, both registered with the first-team squad, started. The under-18s were knocked out of the U18 Premier League Cup by Burnley on Saturday, a week after beating the same opponents 2-1 in the league. The under-21s had no game this week and return to Premier League 2 against West Brom on November 27. City Women Shaw's perfect hat-trick puts City back on top A 5-0 rout of West Ham and a Chelsea slip return City to first place, just in time for the trip to Stamford Bridge. City Women beat West Ham 5-0 at the Joie Stadium on Saturday to return to the top of the WSL. Khadija Shaw scored a perfect hat-trick (header, left foot, right foot), taking her to 12 WSL goals in nine games ( ESPN ). Aoba Fujino and substitute Iman Beney scored their first league goals of the season. Lauren Hemp, who set up one of Shaw's goals, leads the WSL with six assists ( Opta Analyst ). It was City's biggest league win since February. With Chelsea held 1-1 by Everton, City return to the top on 25 points from nine games, two ahead of Chelsea and six ahead of London City Lionesses ( Dave ). They are unbeaten in the league, with eight wins and a draw. Injuries and a huge week The blow came before kick-off: Alex Greenwood (ankle) and goalkeeper Anna Moorhouse (foot) were hurt in training and are out until after the international break. "They will be out for a while," said head coach Andrée Jeglertz ( Hayters ). City are at Inter in the Women's Champions League on Tuesday, sitting 10th in the league phase after three draws (2-2 at Bayern, 1-1 with Real Madrid and PSG) ( Inter ). Then, on Saturday, it is first against second at Stamford Bridge, live on BBC One. Elliot Anderson is City 's only England player after Guéhi's withdrawal; England host Croatia, with Gvardiol and Kovačić, at Wembley on Thursday before visiting Spain on Sunday ( England Football ). The Lead Liverpool find an answer at Selhurst, but the set-piece leak still stings Two defeats in four days, then a composed 3-1 win at Crystal Palace. Iraola's side go into the break fourth, nine points off Arsenal, with one flaw still glaring. T en days ago Liverpool were a side still searching for a settled identity under Andoni Iraola . They still are, but the shape of the problem is clearer now. A 1-0 home defeat to Arsenal on November 1, a 3-2 loss at Fenerbahce on November 4, then a calm 3-1 win at Crystal Palace on Sunday: two steps back and one firm stride forward before the international break. Arsenal's win at Anfield, their first there since 2012, came from a short goal kick. Odegaard intercepted, Rice crossed and Havertz scored at the back post on 16 minutes. Liverpool did not manage a shot on target all afternoon, AP reported , and the defeat ended a five-match winning run. What went wrong in Istanbul Iraola made five changes at the Sukru Saracoglu, resting Isak, Wirtz and Gakpo and using Barcola as a makeshift striker in a front line with no No 9. Liverpool had 68 per cent of the ball, by FotMob's count, and led twice: through Trey Nyoni 's deflected volley on 25 minutes and Isak's header with his first touch on 69. They still lost, as liverpoolfc.com reported . All three Fenerbahce goals came from dead balls. Greenwood's free-kick deflected off Jacquet through the wall on 29 minutes. Archie Brown tapped in at the far post after a corner on 73. Vedat Muriqi, a substitute, rose above Jacquet to head in from a long throw on 79. Liverpool have now conceded 10 goals in four Champions League games, three in each of the last three. Cheap goals. Messy goals. Andoni Iraola after Fenerbahce 3-2 Liverpool "We conceded from a free-kick, a corner, a long throw and that has hurt us," Iraola told reporters, per the Irish Examiner . He added that the noise made it "almost impossible to communicate." Isak was blunter: "We had the lead twice and for us to then lose the game is not good enough," he told the club's website . The answer at Selhurst Park The reply at Selhurst Park turned the set-piece theme around. Alexis Mac Allister met Szoboszlai's free-kick at the near post on 40 minutes, his fifth league goal of the season. Florian Wirtz finished Barcola's cutback first time on 54 minutes, ending a 12-game league drought, and Isak sealed it on the counter on 89 before Nketiah's stoppage-time penalty, Sky Sports reported . It was not a dominant display. Palace had 19 shots to Liverpool's 20, ESPN's match stats showed. Alisson made six saves, including a double stop from Pino and Lerma on 77 minutes, and Pino hit the bar. "It was an important win for us before going into the international break," Iraola said. Where this leaves Iraola The win lifted Liverpool back to fourth on 18 points from ten games, nine behind Arsenal, four behind Brighton and three behind Manchester City. Their 13 away points are the most in the division. At home the story is weaker: five points from five games, with defeats to City and Arsenal. The break arrives at a useful moment for the medical staff and an anxious one for the manager. Szoboszlai went off at Selhurst with a knee problem, Gravenberch (heel) missed the trip, and Frimpong and Bradley are targeting the visit of Manchester United on November 22. United arrive 18th and without a league win since August: an opportunity, and a trap. Key facts The week: L 0-1 Arsenal (H, Nov 1); L 2-3 Fenerbahce (A, Nov 4, Champions League); W 3-1 Crystal Palace (A, Nov 8) Premier League: 4th, P10 W5 D3 L2, goals 14-10, 18 points Home and away: 13 away points, the most in the league; 5 home points from five games Champions League: 8th after four games, 9 points; 10 goals conceded Set pieces in Istanbul: all three Fenerbahce goals: a free-kick, a corner and a long throw Next: Manchester United (H), Sunday November 22, 8:30am Pacific Secondary feature The class of 2027: Liverpool's spine is running out of contract Van Dijk, Alisson and Gomez are all out of contract in June 2027, and Mac Allister has gone public about his own future. Behind the week's results runs a quieter question that will shape Iraola's first full year at Liverpool : how much of this team is still under contract in 2027? Captain Virgil van Dijk , goalkeeper Alisson and Joe Gomez all have deals that end in June 2027, according to TEAMtalk's reporting . On Van Dijk, TEAMtalk's Graeme Bailey reports that Iraola "really wants to keep him around", with talks expected in early 2027 (single-sourced) . Alisson told the Liverpool Echo's Paul Gorst: "My agent is talking with the club... my will is to stay," as relayed by Anfield Index . Fabrizio Romano has called an exit next summer "a serious possibility" given interest from several countries, per TEAMtalk . The most striking words came from Mac Allister, whose deal runs to June 2028. He told Argentine journalist Gastón Edul that "last season I was told that the club's idea was not to renew it, at least for now," calling it a "painful, unpleasant situation," Goal reported . Four days later he headed the opener at Selhurst Park. Add the Araujo decision, which both sides are reported to be deferring to the end of the season, and the spine of this side is in flux. That in-tray belongs to Julian Ward , who returned as sporting director in September after Richard Hughes left for Al-Hilal, according to LiveScore's report . Scouting the Next Opponent Manchester United: dangerous on the break, brittle everywhere else Michael Carrick's side arrive at Anfield 18th and under review, but they have shown they can come from behind. Manchester United visit Anfield on Sunday November 22 (4:30pm UK, 8:30am Pacific) sitting 18th on 8 points from 10 games (W1 D5 L4), one point above bottom-placed Palace and without a league win since August, Sky Sports noted . Michael Carrick 's position is to be reviewed during the break, and he stayed tight-lipped on his future after the Villa draw, TimesLIVE reported . Their last five: a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on November 8, rescued by Dorgu in the 96th minute; a 3-2 Champions League comeback against Roma on November 3; a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea; a 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth on October 25; and a 4-1 defeat at Como on October 21. System and the players to stop Without the ball United defend in a zonal 4-2-4 or 4-4-2, pressing in moments, with four players narrow and high waiting for turnovers, according to BBC Sport's analysis . Bryan Mbeumo has four league goals. Bruno Fernandes scored a penalty against Villa, and Matheus Cunha scored twice against Roma; his red card that night is a UEFA ban, so he should be available at Anfield. The weaknesses are plain. United conceded twice inside four minutes against Villa and Sky described theirs as the worst defence in Europe's top leagues across all competitions. Opta Analyst flagged errors by goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Leny Yoro. Carlos Baleba is out for "a number of weeks" with a hamstring injury (ESPN) , and Benjamin Šeško (shin) is out until at least January, The Athletic reported. That leaves no natural holding midfielder: exactly the gap Liverpool's counter-attacks exploited at Palace. History is less comforting. Liverpool have lost the last two meetings, 1-2 at Anfield in October 2025 and 3-2 at Old Trafford on May 3, 2026, per Sports Mole's record .
