Ronald Araujo joined Liverpool on a season-long loan from Barcelona with an option to buy reported at €55m (£47m). Spanish paper SPORT reports that club and player will both wait until the end of the season before deciding, as relayed by TEAMtalk . Status: option in the loan deal; decision deferred (reported) . His form makes the case. Araujo was voted the club's October Player of the Month (liverpoolfc.com) and has mostly started at right-back. TEAMtalk, citing SPORT, also claims Barcelona have floated a package with Alejandro Balde; treat that as an unconfirmed rumour . Bayern want Ngumoha. Ngumoha's deal runs to 2028, and TEAMtalk and SportBible report an extension could be signed during this break. He was named in the England squad for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. Finding Van Dijk's successor Two expensive names are being linked as the captain's contract runs down. TEAMtalk The Squad Szoboszlai's knee, Gravenberch's heel and a manager who wants more from referees Iraola rotates heavily in midweek and is still settling his best attack; the break brings an injury scare and some respite. Liverpool have mostly lined up as a back four with Alexander Isak through the middle and Wirtz, Barcola and Gakpo around him. Iraola makes "four or five" changes for midweek games, and after trying Barcola as a striker in Istanbul he said the Frenchman will "mainly" stay a winger. Van Dijk captains the side. Wirtz's first league goal was a relief. "Happy for him because I think he's been very unlucky in the Premier League," Iraola said, pointing to "a couple of goals disallowed," per Hayters . Isak scored in both games this week, sealing the Palace win on the counter on 89 minutes. The Szoboszlai scare Dominik Szoboszlai went off on 69 minutes at Selhurst. "I think he extended a little bit the knee, it was fine, but not 100 per cent, so he has to be careful to see if he can play with the national team or not," Iraola said. He was due medical tests on Monday, theScore reported ; no result had been published when this edition went to press. Iraola is also unhappy with officiating. He called his side "sometimes too honest" and, after the late penalty at Palace, said: "I am very upset because the ones in our box they are calling penalties and in the other box they are not," FotMob reported . ESPN cited Opta data showing 58 per cent of fouls in Liverpool's games are given against them, the highest ratio in the league . Kirkby Nyoni's breakthrough and a Will Wright hat-trick in Istanbul The academy had its best night of the week while the first team lost at Fenerbahce. Hours before the senior game, Liverpool 's Youth League side won 5-3 at Fenerbahce. Will Wright scored three, including a penalty, his second Youth League hat-trick of the season, with Josh Sonni-Lambie and Finn Inglethorpe also on target, liverpoolfc.com reported . Rob Page's side are unbeaten in the group (W2 D2) and visit Club Brugge on November 25. Wright has since earned a first England U19 call-up. In the first team, Nyoni scored with a deflected volley in Istanbul at 19, making him Liverpool's second-youngest Champions League scorer behind Trent Alexander-Arnold, the Irish Examiner noted. He then came off the bench at Palace and was named in the England U21 squad. The U21s, last seen drawing 2-2 at Chelsea on October 24 through Wright and Jayden Danns (liverpoolfc.com) , visit Huddersfield on Tuesday at 7pm UK (11am Pacific). Loan watch Harvey Elliott was an unused substitute as Valencia lost 3-0 at home to Real Madrid at the weekend; he had yet to start a game this season as of November 1, RotoWire reported. Kieran Morrison has 13 appearances and three assists at Sheffield Wednesday and is in the Northern Ireland squad. The Lead No striker, no spark: Chelsea stall at the Stadium of Light Enzo Le Fée's penalty sent Xabi Alonso's side into the international break fifth and 11 points off the top. The absence of João Pedro, and a habit of alternating wins with defeats, now defines their autumn. T here are defeats that tell you nothing and defeats that tell you everything. Chelsea 's 1-0 loss at Sunderland on Sunday belonged to the second group. A single penalty from Enzo Le Fée in the 36th minute was enough, and Xabi Alonso did not pretend otherwise. "I think that we didn't deserve more than probably one point," he said ( DAZN ). The penalty came from a familiar weakness. Levi Colwill, already booked, dragged down Brian Brobbey, and the Dutch forward had been getting the better of the centre-back for half an hour. Alonso withdrew Colwill at half-time to avoid a second yellow and moved Moisés Caicedo into the back line, where he handled Brobbey far more comfortably ( FotMob ; Evening Standard ). Chelsea had the ball, and very little else. They held about two-thirds of the ball and attempted 648 passes, yet their first shot on target arrived in the 45th minute. NBC's live coverage put their first-half expected goals at 0.19 against Sunderland's 1.71. "We missed a bit of patience and a bit of quality, creativity in the last third to create more chances." Xabi Alonso after the defeat at Sunderland The missing No 9 The root of the problem is not hard to find. João Pedro, Chelsea's joint top league scorer with five goals, is out with a thigh injury and has no firm return date. Without him Alonso asked Pedro Neto to play as a makeshift striker, a role for which, as the Standard put it, he lacks the physical presence. Chelsea have now scored once from open play in four matches: Morgan Rogers' strike against Manchester United is the only one, alongside penalties at Anfield and against United ( Sports Mole ). Two of the three league games since his injury have been lost. Alonso was candid about the squad's thinness. "We are shorter in options and we need to go through this time," he said. The injury list explains why: João Pedro, Reece James, Maxence Lacroix, Jorrel Hato and Jamie Gittens were all unavailable, Josh Acheampong felt a minor problem, and Emiliano Martínez was left out as he returns from jaw surgery ( Evening Standard ). Since back-to-back wins over Bournemouth and Everton in mid-October, Chelsea have gone loss, draw (lost on penalties), win, loss. Away from Stamford Bridge they have lost three of their five league games, at Arsenal, Brentford and now Sunderland ( results via VAVEL ). The margin for another alternating month is thin. There is some reassurance. Alonso's side have scored 19 league goals, the attack is far better with João Pedro and Palmer both fit, and Leeds, ninth, arrive at Stamford Bridge on November 21 having won once in five away league games. But Alonso's own diagnosis, a lack of "patience" and "creativity in the last third", is a fair summary of a team still finding its identity in his first autumn. Scouting the Next Opponent Leeds United: stubborn at home, short of goals, and back at the Bridge Daniel Farke's side arrive ninth and freshly buoyed by a late win over Tottenham. Leeds United come to Stamford Bridge on Saturday November 21 sitting ninth on 14 points, with three wins, five draws and two defeats ( BeSoccer ). Their defining number is 10: goals scored and goals conceded across 10 games add up to just 18, the profile of a side that keeps games tight. Their last outing was their best in weeks. Substitute Noah Okafor scored with his third touch, on 79 minutes, to beat Tottenham 1-0 at Elland Road on November 7, Leeds' first win since mid-September ( Leeds United ). How they play Daniel Farke switched to a back three with wing-backs partway through last season, and analysts describe Leeds as an aerial and set-piece threat with a goalkeeper, James Trafford , comfortable with the ball at his feet ( VAVEL ). That matters: one analyst counts Chelsea as having conceded six set-piece goals in nine games, the most in the league (single source, Substack analysis ). The men to stop are Dominic Calvert-Lewin , Leeds' top league scorer with four, and left-sided defender Tarik Muharemović , who has two assists and scored in the cup tie at Stamford Bridge ( FotMob ). Gabriel Gudmundsson went off at half-time against Spurs with a hamstring problem and Farke only "hopes" he will be fit; Anton Stach has been a doubt with a broken toe ( LiveScore ; Sports Mole ). The vulnerability is away form and finishing: Leeds have won once in five away league games, and Farke admitted after Spurs that the "finishing pass wasn't there" for long spells. Chelsea also have recent history on their side, winning 6-3 in the EFL Cup in September and 1-0 in last season's FA Cup semi-final ( Leeds United ; AP via KSL ). The table says Barcelona lead La Liga. The form says something less settled. Atlético Madrid have won seven consecutive league matches, sit two points back, and host the leaders on Sunday evening in Madrid. Win it and Diego Simeone 's side go top for the first time this season. Barcelona's numbers are still the division's most arresting. Eleven games, ten wins, 46 goals scored, a goal difference of plus 34 that is sixteen better than anybody else's. Their only league defeat came at home to Real Madrid on October 25. Atlético's case is built differently: 22 scored, eight conceded. The 2-0 win at Levante last Saturday, through Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone , was a controlled away performance of the kind Simeone has spent two seasons trying to restore. And then there is the third party. Real Madrid have won all three league games since Vinícius Júnior 's red card against Villarreal, including that win at Camp Nou, and go to Valencia on Saturday looking for an eighth straight victory in all competitions. They are three points off the top. Our objective is not to beat Barcelona in one match. Our objective is to win a championship. José Mourinho, Real Madrid manager, October 31 The absences that shape it Barcelona arrive short. Rodri , signed from Manchester City in the summer, was withdrawn at half time at Aston Villa on Tuesday, and tests on Wednesday confirmed a hamstring injury. Fabrizio Romano reported he will be out for roughly a month, which rules him out of Sunday and of Spain duty. A workload argument has followed. Rodri had played 14 of Barcelona's first 15 matches and around 945 minutes, close to three quarters of everything available, including the full 90 against Alavés with the game long won. Broadcaster Josep Pedrerol was among those questioning the distribution. No medical link to Hansi Flick 's management has been established. Jules Koundé is also doubtful, having sprained his left ankle at Real Betis on October 17 and missed four games since. Dani Olmo , Andreas Christensen , Éric García and Roony Bardghji are all out, and Flick has said he will not force the recovery of his injured defenders. Atlético are not whole either. Cristian Romero has still not trained with the group and was released by Argentina. Johnny Cardoso returned to training on Thursday after a thigh problem but is expected to begin on the bench. Morten Hjulmand is available again after a European suspension. The tactical question Simeone's answer to this Barcelona has been to play through the first press quickly rather than try to out-pass it, which is what the Levante win rehearsed. Ronaldo ends his international career at 146 goals He announced it on Thursday in a video on Instagram, a month after walking out of the national squad and serving a 30-day suspension. Jorge Jesus says he asked him to stay and does not feel guilty. Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football . The announcement came on Thursday, and it closes a Portugal career of 146 goals in 234 caps, both national records, and both figures unlikely to be approached soon. The ending was not clean. Ronaldo left the national team during the previous international window after a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus over playing time, accusing him of breaking promises. x: Stoppage Time The Weekly Juventus Digest All Juventus, every week: Serie A, Europa League, Women, Next Gen Thursday edition · November 5, 2026 Serie A: 7th, 17 pts · 11 behind leaders Lazio · Europa League: 10 pts from four games W 5-0 NEC W 2-0 ATA D 1-1 CAG W 2-1 CEL L 0-3 LAZ D 2-2 REN W 2-0 LEC L 0-2 GEN W 2-0 NAP W 2-1 AZ Last ten competitive games, oldest first · Next: Fiorentina (a), Sun Nov 8, 11:45am PT Next match Opponent Fiorentina Competition Serie A, matchday 11 Date Sunday, November 8, 2026 Kickoff 11:45am Pacific (20:45 in Italy) Venue Away: Stadio Artemio Franchi, Florence Watch in the US Paramount+ and CBS Sports Golazo Network, per published US TV listings ; check Paramount+ on the day In this edition The Lead · Player Ratings · Scouting the Next Opponent · Transfer News · The Squad · Next Gen · Juventus Women · Players Away · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch Collapse all If you read nothing else Juventus won 2-1 at AZ Alkmaar on Thursday, four days after beating Napoli 2-0, and now have 10 Europa League points. Chief executive Giovanni Carnevali publicly backed Luciano Spalletti as shareholders approved a capital increase of up to €250m on Tuesday. Juventus are seventh in Serie A, 11 points behind Lazio, and visit 16th-placed Fiorentina on Sunday at 11:45am Pacific. The Lead Ten days on a knife edge: Spalletti's Juventus fight for air A defeat at Genoa, a retreat, a rare speech from the chief executive, then wins over Napoli and AZ Alkmaar. The reprieve is real, but it is thin. L uciano Spalletti wants the Allianz Stadium to become a fortress again. On Sunday night, with his own crowd jeering from the opening whistle and hundreds of ultras protesting outside the Curva Sud before kickoff, Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 on the club's 129th birthday. It was not a cure. It was oxygen, and the days that followed showed how little of it there is. The win came four days after the low point of the season: a 2-0 defeat at Genoa on October 28, with goals from Ehizibue and Baldanzi inside half an hour ( club report ). It was a third league loss in nine rounds. Juventus had 14 points, 11 behind leaders Lazio and six off fourth place, as Fanpage noted the next morning. The response was a mandatory retreat before Napoli and a stern dressing-room address from chief executive Giovanni Carnevali . "The most important speech was made by Carnevali, because they are not accustomed to hearing his voice," Spalletti said afterwards ( Football Italia ). His own message before the game was blunter: "Physical strength can fade, but mental strength cannot" ( Goal ). The noise around the bench Outside, the speculation ran hot. Mediaset reported on October 29 that Antonio Conte was Carnevali's first choice should a change be made; Conte said on Instagram there were no advanced talks. La Repubblica, as relayed by CalcioNapoli24 , named Stefano Pioli and Didier Deschamps as alternatives. Fabrizio Romano reported that the club was backing Spalletti, had contacted no other coach, and was nonetheless unhappy, with Napoli framed as the key game ( via L'Interista ). Mediaset called Napoli, AZ Alkmaar and Fiorentina "ten decisive days". How the Napoli game turned Spalletti returned to a back four: Vicario; Kalulu, Bremer, Lucumí, Cabal, with Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and McKennie in midfield behind Alajbegović, Woltemade and Kolo Muani ( club line-up ). Vicario's early reflex save from Lorenzo Lucca's diving header kept it level, and Cabal headed a corner against the post. The first half was thin, and Weston McKennie did not come out for the second, his adductor tightening. Federico Gatti replaced him and, as Football Italia saw it, Juventus shifted to three at the back. With a pure marker on him, Lucca faded. Edon Zhegrova replaced the whistled Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. Eleven minutes later he beat Rrahmani and found Kerim Alajbegović , whose left-footed shot from about 20 yards went in off the far post for his first Serie A goal. “You can say Spalletti's no good, that player's no good, get rid of everyone, but right now we need to be united, and this stadium must return to being our fortress.” Luciano Spalletti, after Napoli Napoli's Luca Marianucci was sent off on 75 minutes for a second booking, for stepping on Cabal's foot. Jérémie Boga , on for Alajbegović, cut inside and curled the second into the far corner on 87 minutes, set up by Andrea Cambiaso ( Football Italia ). Juventus finished with 18 shots to Napoli's seven, five on target to one, by Napoligrafia's count . Napoli were led from the bench by assistant Marco Landucci, with Massimiliano Allegri suspended. A squad of thirteen The win did not hide the arithmetic. "Lo dico eh, siamo in 13," Spalletti said: I'll say it, there are 13 of us ( SOS Fanta ). "All the substitutions I made were forced ones," he added, with Sarr out with a fever and McKennie, Cabal and Alajbegović all needing checks. On Tuesday, at the shareholders' meeting, Carnevali closed the question for now: "Spalletti è l'allenatore della Juventus e noi lo sosteniamo" (Spalletti is the Juventus coach and we support him), Calciomercato.com reported. Alkmaar: the second breath Thursday night in the Netherlands brought a second win in five days. With eight players unavailable, Juventus won 2-1 at AZ Alkmaar to reach 10 points from four Europa League games ( Juventus News 24 ). Spalletti went with three at the back: Vicario; Gatti, Lucumí, Kelly; Kalulu, Sarr, Koopmeiners, Cambiaso; Alajbegović and Woltemade behind Kolo Muani ( Football Italia line-ups ). Bremer and Douglas Luiz started on the bench. The man whistled off on Sunday decided it. On 19 minutes Randal Kolo Muani beat his man and cut the ball back from the byline for Teun Koopmeiners to finish past De Busser. On 37 minutes Kolo Muani played a one-two with Woltemade and volleyed in his fourth goal of the season ( Corriere dello Sport ). AZ pulled one back through Mexx Meerdink on 88 minutes, and in stoppage time Vicario saved Meerdink's header before De Wit's rebound was ruled out for offside ( Football Italia ). Jeff Ekhator made his first official appearance off the bench. Sunday in Florence is the last stop before the international break. Fiorentina are 16th but won 4-2 at Sassuolo on Monday, and Juventus have not beaten them in four meetings. The organised groups of the Curva Sud will not be there: they are boycotting the trip over ticketing ( Juve Oggi ). Off the pitch Exor's €250m lifeline comes with a warning attached Shareholders approve a €66m loss and a capital increase; Carnevali promises to buy "who we can" within UEFA's limits. The other big Juventus meeting of the week took place on Tuesday at the Allianz Stadium, and it was about money. Shareholders approved the 2025-26 accounts, a net loss of €66.0m against €58.1m a year earlier, with 91.8% of the vote ( Football Italia ). They also authorised the board to raise up to €250m in fresh capital, passed with 99.9%. Exor, which holds 65.4%, guarantees its share and any part other shareholders do not take up, and has already paid €60m in advance ( Di Marzio ). Roughly half of the money rebuilds equity; about €100m is earmarked for investment, mainly the first team and transfers, according to Calciomercato.com . No spree in January Carnevali said the UEFA settlement agreement still limits spending and that there would be no extraordinary outlays. "Compreremo chi potremo," he said: we will buy who we can ( Corriere dello Sport ). Chief financial officer Stefano Cerrato expects another loss this season because Europa League revenue is lower than the Champions League's. President Gianluca Ferrero described Tether as the second-largest shareholder at 11.5%, said the club was open to dialogue but had no joint initiatives, and ruled out delisting. He also floated a second, smaller stadium closer to the city for the women's team and Next Gen, while admitting there is no executive project ( Calcio e Finanza ). The floor was hostile. Small shareholders attacked John Elkann and called for club great Del Piero as president ( Calcio e Finanza ). Others criticised former chief executive Damien Comolli, and one called Randal Kolo Muani's fee excessive. Ferrero cut off one persistent critic mid-speech. Scouting the Next Opponent Fiorentina: dangerous going forward, leaky at the back Paolo Vanoli's side are 16th but scored four at Sassuolo on Monday, and Juventus have not beaten them since April 2024. Fiorentina sit 16th with 8 points from 10 games (W2 D2 L6), with 15 goals scored and 23 conceded ( Sky Sport table ). Fabio Grosso was sacked on September 6 after three straight league defeats in which his side scored once and conceded nine; Paolo Vanoli returned the next day ( Reuters via The Star ). Form has picked up. They won 4-2 at Sassuolo on Monday (Pellegrino, Njie, Mastantuono, Valdepeñas), drew 2-2 with Atalanta on October 29, and lost 2-1 at Inter on October 25 to goals in the 91st and 98th minutes. System and the men to stop Vanoli has used a 4-3-2-1 in the last two games: De Gea; Jiménez, Dragušin, Viery, João Mário; Ndour, Fagioli, Brescianini; Mastantuono, Njie; Pellegrino. Franco Mastantuono is the club's top scorer with at least four league goals and their highest-rated player. Mateo Pellegrino has at least three goals as the lone striker. Former Juventus midfielder Nicolò Fagioli sets the tempo, and David de Gea is in goal. Where they can be hurt Fiorentina concede 2.3 goals a game, joint third-worst in the league, and they average 397 passes a game (15th) against Juventus's 545 (4th), per theScore . But they also average 1.5 goals and 16.4 shots a game, slightly more than Juventus. Sottil, Atta, Pongračić, Parisi, Ranieri and Gosens were listed as injured, and Njie came off after 63 minutes at Sassuolo. No suspensions have been reported. Recent history is poor for Juventus: a 2-0 home defeat in May 2026, a 1-1 draw in Florence in November 2025, a 3-0 loss there in March 2025 and a 2-2 draw in December 2024. The last win was 1-0 in April 2024. The clearest thread in Turin this week is a centre-forward. Calciomercato.com, via Football Italia , reported on Wednesday that Juventus expect to invest in a striker in January. Monaco's Folarin Balogun , under contract to 2028, and Manchester United's injured Benjamin Šeško head the list. Sunderland's Brian Brobbey and Frankfurt's Ebnoutalib are also named. All are at the interest stage. No bid has been reported for any of them. Marco Conterio of TMW, reported via Tuttojuve , adds the catch: a striker arrives only if someone leaves first. His list includes Balogun, Atlético Madrid's Alexander Sørloth and free agent Mauro Icardi, with Jeff Ekhator a candidate for a loan exit. Conterio names Edon Zhegrova as the most likely sale. That report is single-sourced. The Kosovo winger has two league goals and set up the Napoli winner, yet he has not started a game all season and is not on the Europa League list. The list rule explains that last part: when Locatelli's injury opened a place, UEFA required a locally trained replacement, so Ekhator went in instead ( Goal Italia ). Carnevali's line on Tuesday, "we will buy who we can", suggests the January budget will be shaped by who leaves. Ins & Outs Window Closed. Reopens in January. The Squad Spalletti's thirteen: the injury list that shapes every choice Back four or back three, the coach is picking from a shrinking group, with the captain out until the new year. Luciano Spalletti began the season with a back four, mostly a 4-2-3-1, through to the 1-1 draw at Cagliari on October 11. Since then a back three has dominated: it has been used in all four Europa League games and in the league against Lazio, Lecce and Genoa. Against Napoli he went back to four, then to three when Gatti came on. The constant is personnel: Douglas Luiz, Kolo Muani, Lucumí, Bremer and Kalulu are the regulars, and Vicario has started every Serie A game, with Neto and Pinsoglio behind him. The captain's long absence Manuel Locatelli , the captain, had his right lateral meniscus repaired in September and is out until early 2027 ( Sky Sport ). Bremer wore the armband at Lecce. Kenan Yildiz broke the base of his left fifth metatarsal in the opener at Frosinone and had surgery. Quotidiano Sportivo expects him back in team training in early December, with Monza on December 14 or Roma on December 19 the targets. Conceição (shoulder), Nico González (calf) and Çelik (hamstring) are aimed at the Venezia game after the break, according to DAZN . McKennie stayed home from Alkmaar as a precaution and is targeting Fiorentina ( Corriere dello Sport ). Kolo Muani's test, and the cards to watch Kolo Muani was whistled off against Napoli. "He has to react to certain moments," Spalletti said, adding that the first step and the courage to dare must come from the player himself. He answered in Alkmaar with a goal and an assist, taking him to four goals in all competitions, one more than Woltemade. No player is suspended for Fiorentina. By the Digest's count from match reports, Lucumí has three Serie A bookings and Douglas Luiz two. Woltemade has taken and scored both of the team's penalties, against NEC and Rennes. Next Gen Next Gen stuck near the bottom as Durmiši knocks on the door A 1-1 draw with Pro Vercelli, a goalless derby for the Primavera, and a hard week for the loanees. Massimo Brambilla's Juventus Next Gen drew 1-1 with Pro Vercelli on Monday, Merola scoring on 31 minutes and Bertoli equalising after the break ( Juventus News 24 ). They are 17th of 20 in Serie C Group A with 11 points from 12 games, two wins, five draws and five defeats. The bright spot is Arman Durmiši , an Albanian striker born in 2008, who has three Serie C goals and got his first senior call-up for the trip to Genoa, alongside Pagnucco and Owusu ( Tuttosport ). With the first team stretched, Spalletti took four Next Gen players to Alkmaar ( Juvenews ). Primavera and the loanees The Primavera drew 0-0 in the derby at Torino on Sunday; Beydts was their best player and Ali Camara went off injured ( Mondo Primavera ). They are 14th in Primavera 1 with 10 points from nine games and host Empoli on Saturday. Among the loanees, Loïs Openda is still out at Lyon with a broken right fibula ( Sky Sport ), and Fabio Miretti is sidelined at Beşiktaş with a shoulder injury until early December. Vasilije Adžić started Sassuolo's 4-2 home defeat to Fiorentina on Monday and was taken off after 59 minutes; in the same game João Mário played 90 minutes at left-back for Fiorentina ( Goal Italia ). Michele Di Gregorio remains a cup goalkeeper at Bournemouth ( Football Italia ). Juventus Women Two away wins put Guerrero's Juventus Women back on track Four goals in Vienna, a first league win on the road in Florence, and Lyon on the horizon. Isaac Guerrero's Juventus Women answered three straight league defeats with two away wins. In the Women's Champions League on October 29 they won 4-1 at Austria Wien , with goals from Pavan, Redondo (a penalty after a VAR check), Sylla and Bartel ( Solo Calcio Femminile ). That took them to six points from three league-phase games, after a 2-1 home loss to Benfica and a 3-0 win at Häcken. On Monday they won 2-1 at Fiorentina's Viola Park in Serie A Women, Alba Redondo scoring on 28 minutes and Kysha Sylla adding her first league goal for the club on 56 before Severini's late reply ( FIGC ). It was their first away win of the league season. The Lead Stung by the derby, revived in Rotterdam: Inter face Como's test A first league defeat exposed old habits. Three days later a patched-up side won 3-0 in the Champions League. Sunday's visit of Fàbregas's Como will show which version is real. F or ten minutes on Saturday night, Inter looked like a team that had forgotten what a derby demands. Christian Pulisic headed in after four minutes and Adrien Rabiot scored from a short corner after ten, both set up by Diego Moreira . By half-time Milan led 3-1 and the unbeaten league start was gone. Inter's website carried Chivu's call afterward to “rediscover our humility.” The numbers made the result stranger. Inter had 57 percent of the ball, 19 shots to Milan's seven and an expected-goals tally of 1.68 against 0.62, according to FotMob . Alessandro Bastoni headed in a Calhanoglu corner after Akanji's flick, and a late penalty for a Gila handball was overturned by VAR. It was still Inter's eighth straight derby without a win. Cristian Chivu did not hide behind the data. “We had the wrong approach,” he told Sky Italia, adding that Pio Esposito had been unwell and Bonny “had a fever until 4.30pm,” forcing him to improvise up front with Lautaro already injured ( Football Italia ). Marcus Thuram later spoke of a senior players' meeting and the need for “a change of mentality.” The reply at De Kuip Rotterdam on Tuesday was the answer Chivu wanted. Without Bastoni (suspended), Lautaro, Curtis Jones, John Stones and Luis Henrique, Inter beat Feyenoord 3-0. Yann Bisseck pressed, turned between two defenders and scored after eight minutes, his first Champions League goal in his 27th appearance ( Football Italia ). Djed Spence crossed for Bisseck and then for Francesco Pio Esposito 's header on 34 minutes, becoming the first English player to score or assist for Inter in the Champions League, per beIN Sports . Piotr Zielinski curled the third in off the inside of the post after 54 minutes. It was the club's 87th Champions League win, level with Milan. “This performance gives us a lot of confidence and something to build on.” Cristian Chivu, after Feyenoord 0-3 Inter Key facts: the week in two matches Sat Oct 31, Serie A: Milan 3-1 Inter (Bastoni 22'). Shots 7-19, xG 0.62-1.68, attendance 77,691 Tue Nov 3, Champions League: Feyenoord 0-3 Inter (Bisseck 8', Esposito 34', Zielinski 54') Serie A: 2nd, 25 pts from 10 games (W8 D1 L1), 3 behind Lazio, 1 ahead of Roma Champions League: 15th of 36, 6 pts after four games; top eight go straight to the last 16 Out this week: Lautaro (hamstring), Luis Henrique; Bastoni suspended in Europe only What changed between Saturday and Tuesday The shape changed first. In the derby Chivu used Diouf and Sucic behind a lone Thuram; in Rotterdam he went back to a 3-5-2 with Esposito beside Thuram and Zielinski and Dimarco restored. Carlos Augusto moved to left centre-back for Bastoni. Feyenoord had more of the ball (53 percent), but Inter created the better chances, with expected goals of 1.19 to 0.73 per FotMob. The pressing changed too. Bisseck's goal came from a defender stepping out to win the ball high, the very aggression that was missing when Milan scored twice in ten minutes. Chivu's own warning stands, though: “Consistency brings results, confidence and belief, and that's what we're trying to find right now,” he told Inter TV . Why Como matters Sunday's opponent is the hardest possible check. Como sit fourth on 23 points, two behind Inter, and have won four straight league games. They share the best defence in Serie A with Lazio (eight conceded) and average 62.1 percent possession, second only to Inter's 62.4, per the club's opponent analysis . On Wednesday they won 9-1 at Lens. The stakes are plain. A win keeps Inter within touching distance of Lazio , who lead on 28, and opens a five-point gap on Como. A defeat would drop Inter to fourth if Roma also win. Inter were unbeaten in four meetings last season (three wins and a 0-0), including a 4-0 at San Siro in December, but this Como side is a different animal. The New Stadium A 71,500-seat future: the Generali Stadium is unveiled Inter and Milan presented the design for San Siro's successor, with a naming-rights deal reported as a record for Italy. On October 29, Inter and Milan presented the new stadium at the Castello Sforzesco. It will be called the Generali Stadium, designed by Foster + Partners with MANICA, and hold 71,500 spectators, according to Il Post . The two clubs bought the old San Siro and its land from the city for 197 million euros in November 2025. The money is large. Goal , citing Calcio e Finanza, puts the naming rights at about 650 million euros over 25 years, roughly 26 million a year split between the clubs. The build is estimated at around 1.2 billion euros; neither club has confirmed that figure. Timelines vary. Il Post reports construction starting in 2028 and the ground ready before summer 2031, in time for Euro 2032, while earlier reports pointed to a 2027 start. Thursday, November 5, was the deadline for the clubs' company, Stadio San Siro SpA, to file its feasibility project with the city after a three-month extension; this edition could not confirm the filing. Scouting the Next Opponent Como: Fàbregas's possession machine arrives on a 9-1 high Fourth in Serie A, winners of six straight and scoring for fun, Como bring the league's joint-meanest defence to San Siro. Como arrive in rare form. In his third full season in charge, Cesc Fàbregas has them fourth on 23 points (seven wins, two draws, one defeat, a 2-0 loss at Frosinone). They have won six in a row in all competitions; the last five: 4-1 against Manchester United and 9-1 at Lens in the Champions League, plus Sassuolo, Torino and Venezia in Serie A ( ESPN ). The system is a 4-2-3-1 with at least four attackers. Anastasios Douvikas scored a hat-trick at Lens and has five Serie A goals. Nico Paz is the creative hub after 12 goals and seven assists last season, with Martin Baturina and Lucas Da Cunha shooting from between the lines. Perrone, Milla and Caqueret rotate in the double pivot. Where Inter can hurt them Inter's own opponent analysis is candid about the risks: Como press high and have scored four goals from high turnovers. But they struggle against sides that press their build-up, as Torino and Feyenoord showed, and full-backs Yan Couto and Valle push so high that space opens behind them in transition. That suits Bisseck's aggression and Spence's running. Como are also short up front: Diao and Kean are out and Chalobah is unavailable, with Kempf partnering Jacobo Ramón at centre-back, per the club analysis and Fàbregas's own remarks . The Lead Nine at Bollaert: Como rewrite the Champions League record book A 9-1 win at Lens equalled the competition's biggest winning margin, made Tasos Douvikas Europe's top scorer and lifted Como to fourth. The harder question arrives on Sunday at San Siro. T he biggest night in Como 's 119-year history came on a Wednesday night in northern France. Cesc Fabregas's side won 9-1 at Lens in the Champions League, the fourth European Cup game the club has ever played, and turned a promising debut campaign into a story told across the continent. It was "a wonderful night for Como" , Fabregas said. The record books agreed. The numbers came fast and kept coming. Tasos Douvikas scored at 7, 32 and 57 minutes. Nico Paz , Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali and Martin Baturina joined in, and the 18-year-old academy midfielder Matteo Papaccioli rounded it off in stoppage time on his first-team debut. Lens managed one reply, a Ruben Aguilar volley from a corner at 65 minutes. The eight-goal margin equals the biggest win in Champions League history, alongside Liverpool's 8-0 over Besiktas in 2007 and Real Madrid's 8-0 over Malmo in 2015, beIN Sports noted . Como are only the second side to score nine in a Champions League game, after Bayern's 9-2 against Dinamo Zagreb in 2024. No Italian club had ever scored more than seven in the competition. Key facts Result: Lens 1-9 Como, Wednesday, November 4, Stade Bollaert-Delelis (Champions League, league phase matchday 4) Como scorers: Douvikas 7', 32', 57'; Paz 40'; Da Cunha 47'; Kempf 53'; Liberali 62'; Baturina 69'; Papaccioli 90+1' Lens scorer: Aguilar 65' Stats: possession 57-43; shots 18-11; on target 12-3 (ESPN); xG about 4.2 to 1.0 (FotMob) Records: equals the eight-goal Champions League record margin; most goals by an Italian club in a Champions League game Table: Como 4th of 36 on 9 points, goal difference +13 How it happened This was not a smash-and-grab. Como had 57 per cent of the ball, 18 shots to 11 and, per ESPN's numbers, 12 on target to Lens's three. FotMob's expected-goals model gave Como about 4.2 and Lens about one, so the finishing ran hot. But Fabregas's side created enough to win comfortably, and the clinical part followed from that. The shape was Fabregas's familiar 4-2-3-1: Jean Butez in goal; Yan Couto, Jacobo Ramon, Kempf and Alex Valle across the back; Maximo Perrone and Luis Milla in midfield; Da Cunha, Paz and Maxence Caqueret behind Douvikas. The opener came from a Perrone corner. Kempf headed in a Milla cross for 5-0. Paz's rifled shot made it 3-0 just before half-time, and he then set up Da Cunha for the fourth. There were two early warnings. Butez denied Florian Thauvin, and a Lens penalty for a Caqueret handball was overturned by VAR, according to VAVEL's live report. Had either gone the other way, this might have been a much tighter night. The bench made it a record Fabregas changed three players at 58 minutes, sending on Samuele Ricci, Liberali and Baturina, then Papaccioli for Douvikas three minutes later. Liberali scored within four minutes of arriving, and ESPN credited him with two assists as well. Baturina added the eighth. Papaccioli's goal, ruled onside after a review, completed the nine. That detail matters. Fabregas told Sky Sport on Tuesday, as reported by ANSA, that his Champions League list leaves him only 15 outfield players. Moise Kean, Assane Diao and Jesus Rodriguez are all injured. The players who came on this week were the young and the recently recovered, and they scored three times in half an hour. We must learn this now so we don't buy into our own hype or think that the job is already done. Cesc Fabregas, after the win at Lens (via ANI) Where it leaves Como, and what comes next Como are fourth in the 36-team league phase on nine points, three wins from four, with a goal difference of plus 13 (19 scored, six conceded). Only PSG, on 20, have scored more. The top eight go straight to the round of 16, and Como's next two games are at home to AEK Athens on November 24 and away to Real Betis. Douvikas has now scored in all four of Como's Champions League games, six goals in total, the most in the competition. Sky Sport Italia found only one precedent for an Italian side's player scoring in each of the first four, Alessandro Del Piero in 1995-96. He has 11 goals in all competitions and signed a new contract to 2031 in late October. Fabregas spent the post-match period trying to lower the temperature. He said he was "angry" about the goal conceded, because his substitutions had changed the defensive structure, and that he had been telling the players to slow the tempo with another game coming. He also called PSG and Barcelona "two teams who are of a superior level to the rest." The real test is Sunday. Como have won six in a row in all competitions, but they visit Inter, the one club Fabregas has never beaten as Como coach. In four meetings since December 2025 Inter have won three and drawn one, including the Coppa Italia semi-final in April, when Como led 2-0 at San Siro and lost 3-2. Beating Lens 9-1 proves this side can be ruthless. Winning at San Siro would show it can compete for the title. Also this week Suwarso: the selling will come, and the stadium plan is ready In a wide-ranging interview, the club president prepared fans for future sales and said the revised Sinigaglia project is ready to file. Speaking to La Provincia di Como on Tuesday, president Mirwan Suwarso was unusually direct about the club's model. "Sooner or later, more sooner than later, we will be forced to sell some pieces of our collection," he said, as reported by Gianluca Di Marzio . He named Atalanta as the model. The books explain why. An independent analysis of UK filings published on The Esk this week put the 2024-25 net loss at 105.1 million euros and owner funding at 297.4 million euros by November 2025. On the stadium, Suwarso said the revised Sinigaglia project, rewritten to answer earlier objections, is ready to be filed with the Comune; he gave no date, according to La Provincia di Como . He also clarified his old "Disneyland" remark about the city. The ground already got a new home end this summer, taking capacity to 12,370 for Serie A and 10,875 for UEFA games, per Calcio e Finanza . On Fabregas, the message was calm: "An excellent relationship, very clear, very transparent... the day he wants something else, he'll tell us in time." Player Ratings The Digest's marks: Lens and Venezia Two wins in four days, one of them historic. These are the Digest's own ratings out of 10, informed by the match reports and data cited. Players who featured for under 10 minutes are not rated. Lens 1-9 Como (Champions League, November 4) Lineup per FotMob and ESPN . FotMob's own algorithm made Douvikas player of the match at 9.8, with Paz at 9.2 and Liberali at 8.9. Butez 6.5 Couto 6.5 Ramon 7.5 Kempf 7.5 Valle 7 Perrone 7 Milla 7 Da Cunha 8 Paz 8.5 Caqueret 7 Douvikas 9.5 Ricci 6 Liberali 8.5 Baturina 7.5 Papaccioli 7.5 Smolcic 6 Chart: the Digest's marks for Lens 1-9 Como. Every mark is also listed in the ratings below. Butez 6.5 Early save from Thauvin set the tone; barely tested after that. Couto 6.5 Steady at right back on a night when attack mattered more. Ramon 7.5 Composed on the ball and in control of the box; FotMob had him among the best. Kempf 7.5 Headed in Milla's cross for 5-0; replaced at 72 minutes after a knock to the head. Valle 7 Got forward willingly from left back. Perrone 7 His corner led to the opener; tidy in the first hour. Milla 7 Crossed for Kempf's goal and kept the ball moving. Da Cunha 8 Scored the fourth from Paz's pass and was a constant outlet. Paz 8.5 Rifled in the third and set up the fourth. Caqueret 7 Lively on his start; the VAR-overturned handball the only blemish. Douvikas 9.5 Hat-trick inside an hour; six Champions League goals from four games. Ricci 6 On at 58 minutes; quiet but tidy. Liberali 8.5 Scored within four minutes of coming on and added two assists, per ESPN. Baturina 7.5 Came on at 58 minutes and scored the eighth. Papaccioli 7.5 Scored in stoppage time on his first-team debut at 18. Smolcic 6 Replaced Kempf at 72 minutes; a calm finish to the night. Como 1-0 Venezia (Serie A, November 1) Lineup per Calciomercato.com . A narrow, contested win: Como had 66 per cent of the ball and 19 shots to seven, but only four on target. Fabregas admitted afterwards, "we were lucky" with the penalty decision. Smolcic (82 minutes) and Valle (85) came on too late to be rated. Butez 6 Barely called upon; only Yeboah troubled him. Couto 6.5 Busy on the right and curled one effort just wide. Kempf 6.5 Solid; also tried his luck from about 25 metres. Ramon 6.5 Calm in a back line that conceded one shot on target. Kaiki 6 Booked at 86 minutes; sound otherwise. Ricci 6 Kept the ball circulating as Como held 66 per cent possession. Milla 6 Flashscore's man of the match, but his handball nearly gave Venezia a penalty before VAR intervened. Da Cunha 7 Scored the 43rd-minute penalty that decided it, despite constant double-marking. Paz 6 Heavily marked and kept quiet by Venezia's deep block. Baturina 6.5 His solo run around 51 minutes forced a save from Stankovic. Douvikas 6.5 Won the penalty; had a close-range volley parried. Liberali 6 On at 73 minutes to see the game out. Caqueret 6 On at 73 minutes; helped manage the closing stages. Perrone 6 On at 73 minutes; steady in midfield. Scouting the Next Opponent Inter: wounded, rotated and still second Cristian Chivu's side lost the derby last weekend but answered with a 3-0 win in Rotterdam. Without Lautaro Martinez, they are beatable. History says Como have not managed it yet. Inter sit second on 25 points from 10 games (eight wins, one draw, one loss), two clear of Como . Their only league defeat came last Saturday, a 3-1 derby loss to Milan in which they conceded twice in the first 10 minutes, once from a corner, and a third from a direct free kick. They responded with a 3-0 win at Feyenoord on Tuesday, through Bisseck, Pio Esposito and Zielinski, per beIN Sports . Chivu has used a 3-5-2. Marcus Thuram leads the scoring with five league goals, and Hakan Calhanoglu runs the set pieces; he made five key passes in the derby. Piotr Zielinski scored against Fiorentina and Feyenoord, and Carlos Augusto has chipped in from wing back. In Europe, Inter are only 15th on six points after defeats to Real Madrid and Club Brugge. Team news and weak spots Lautaro Martinez is out with a muscle strain and is aiming for the Atalanta game after the break, per L'Interista . Luis Henrique (adductor) is also missing. John Stones and Curtis Jones are back in partial training and could make the bench, Benjamin Pavard is fit again, and Alessandro Bastoni, who scored in the derby, is available after serving a Champions League suspension. The vulnerabilities are recent and specific: slow starts (the derby), a habit of leaving it late (they needed stoppage-time goals to beat Fiorentina 2-1), and set pieces against. Como's quick wide combinations and Douvikas's movement are built to test exactly that. The head-to-head is the worry. Inter won 4-0 at San Siro in December 2025, won 4-3 at the Sinigaglia in April and came from 2-0 down to beat Como 3-2 in the Coppa Italia semi-final second leg. The only result Como took was a 0-0 in the first leg. Soccerway also recalls that Inter wanted Fabregas as their coach in June 2025, and Como said no. Inter at a glance Position: 2nd, 25 points (W8 D1 L1) Coach and system: Cristian Chivu, 3-5-2 Last five: W 1-0 Shakhtar; W 2-1 Fiorentina; W 2-0 Venezia; L 1-3 Milan; W 3-0 Feyenoord Players to stop: Thuram (5 league goals), Calhanoglu (set pieces), Zielinski Out: Lautaro Martinez, Luis Henrique. Back: Pavard, Bastoni; Stones and Jones in partial training Recent meetings: Inter 4-0 Como (Dec 2025); Como 0-0 Inter (Mar 2026, cup); Como 3-4 Inter (Apr 2026); Inter 3-2 Como (Apr 2026, cup) Transfer News Nico Paz: Como's line is firm, but the clause hangs over everything Premier League clubs are circling Como's playmaker. Real Madrid hold the real power, and nothing can happen until July. The structure was set in June. Real Madrid triggered their buy-back on Nico Paz , Como then bought him back for 60 million euros, and Madrid kept a new 80 million euro buy-back clause, as Fabrizio Romano reported . ESPN's Alex Kirkland described Madrid's option as one-sided and for the 2027-28 season. Spanish outlet Fichajes, citing AS, says the clause can be triggered from July 1 to 15, 2027. That is single-sourced and worth treating as a report, not a fact. TEAMtalk, via The Hard Tackle, says Chelsea, Manchester United and Arsenal are monitoring him and that Como will not entertain January bids. Certainty: rumour . Paz has already scored twice against United this season. Jacobo Ramon draws the same suitors CaughtOffside, citing the Daily Mail, links Arsenal, Manchester United and Chelsea with the young centre back Jacobo Ramon , and says Real Madrid retain a buy-back and sell-on interest; no figures were given. Certainty: rumour . Marca reports he is in contention for a first senior Spain call-up when the squad is named on Friday. Camello the name for January The only named incoming target this week is Rayo Vallecano striker Sergio Camello . Marco Conterio of TuttoMercatoWeb wrote on October 30 that Como admire him, that his contract ends in June 2027, that a January move would cost about 10 million euros, and that Atletico Madrid hold a buy-back "until the winter". Certainty: concrete interest . With Kean, Diao and Rodriguez all injured, a forward makes sense. Sky Italia reported in September that the winter window opens early, in December. Douvikas is going nowhere The one piece of official business: Tasos Douvikas extended his contract to 2031 in late October, per Calciomercato.com . TMW's Simone Bernabei argued on Thursday that he is now worth more than 50 million euros and that Como would refuse even huge offers. That is opinion, but the contract makes it a strong position. Ins & Outs Official (late October): Douvikas renews to 2031 Window: closed; Sky Italia reports it reopens early, in December Summer arrivals now in the squad: Trevoh Chalobah (Chelsea, about 30m euros); Moise Kean (Fiorentina, loan with obligation); Robert Sanchez (loan, Chelsea); Yan Couto (loan, Dortmund); Luis Milla (Getafe); Samuele Ricci (loan, Milan); Mattia Liberali (Catanzaro) Key summer exits: Yannik Engelhardt (Freiburg), Stefan Posch (Mainz), Alvaro Morata (loan, Leganes), Nicolas Kuhn (loan, Gladbach) The Rumour Mill Nico Paz to the Premier League: rumour (TEAMtalk). Como say no January sale; Real Madrid's 80m euro clause comes first. Jacobo Ramon to Arsenal, United or Chelsea: rumour (CaughtOffside, citing the Daily Mail). Sergio Camello to Como: concrete interest (TMW, Marco Conterio). About 10m euros in January. Assane Diao renewal to 2031: unconfirmed, from an aggregator only. Treat with caution. Fabregas release clause: AS, via Sports Mole, says his contract runs to 2028 with a fixed clause for Arsenal, Chelsea or Barcelona. Unconfirmed; the fee is not public. The Squad Fabregas's emergency up front, and how he is managing it Three forwards are out, one centre back is a doubt, and the Champions League list is short. It has not stopped the winning. Cesc Fabregas has stuck with a 4-2-3-1 through the injuries. Against Venezia the XI was Butez; Couto, Kempf, Ramon, Kaiki; Ricci, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas. Against Lens he rotated: Valle for Kaiki at left back, Perrone for Ricci and Caqueret for Baturina. After Lens he said he is "only thinking about getting back the many players we're missing, especially up front", per Corriere dello Sport . Douvikas has carried the attack, with 11 goals in all competitions (five in Serie A, six in Europe). Paz has six goals and leads Como's Serie A assists with three. Butez has started the big games, though Fabregas called the Butez and Robert Sanchez question "still open" in October. The availability list Who's fit Trevoh Chalobah: muscle problem since October 18; missed Lens. Fabregas: "we'll see for Inter". Moise Kean: bruised tibia from the October break, treated in Barcelona; about five weeks out from October 29 ( Sky Italia ). Misses Italy's games. Assane Diao: grade-one left hamstring tear against Feyenoord; expected back after the international break. Jesus Rodriguez: out more than 60 days after a training injury on October 20; Caqueret replaced him on the UEFA list. Jayden Addai: new muscle problem against Torino, soon after returning from an Achilles rupture; being assessed. Marc-Oliver Kempf: came off at Lens after a blow to the head; no update yet. Back: Mattia Liberali, after an October shin scare, scored at Lens. Squad-list squeeze UEFA allows one injury replacement before the knockout phase, goalkeepers apart, and Como have used it on Caqueret. "We're penalised by the Champions list: we have 15 outfield players," Fabregas told ANSA on Tuesday, citing his comments to Sky Sport. That is why academy players such as Papaccioli are getting minutes in Europe. The Academy Papaccioli's night, and a Primavera finding its feet An 18-year-old from the academy scored on his debut in the Champions League. The Primavera, new to the top youth division, sits mid-table. Matteo Papaccioli was born on May 9, 2008. He is a left-footed Italian-Brazilian midfielder who grew up in Brazil, playing for Taubate and futsal until he was 10, joined Como in 2022 and signed his first professional contract in October 2024, per TuttoMercatoWeb . He has 11 caps and three goals for Italy's under-16s and under-17s. At Lens he came on for Douvikas at 61 minutes and scored in stoppage time. Primavera Como's Primavera are in Primavera 1 for the first time after promotion, coached by Gianluca Falsini , formerly of Roma's academy. They are 12th on 12 points after nine rounds (three wins, three draws, three defeats), six behind leaders Parma and Inter, per MondoPrimavera . Their latest league game was a 2-1 home win over Atalanta. In the UEFA Youth League they lost 2-1 at Lens, with Riccardo Cassano scoring. Sportitalia reports Cassano has been named in Italy's senior squad this week (see Players Away). Next: Fiorentina away on Sunday. Loan watch Noel Tornqvist (Monza): now first-choice goalkeeper; Ivan Juric called him "fantastic" in a 4-0 win over Cagliari. Alieu Fadera (Cagliari): assisted against Lazio on November 1, then went off with a hamstring strain; expected back around November 21. Ivan Azon (Getafe): one goal and one assist in seven La Liga games. Emil Audero (Rayo Vallecano): seven appearances, starting each of his last five. Ignace Van der Brempt (Sassuolo): three Serie A starts, but unused in the last two games. Nicolas Kuhn (Gladbach): two substitute appearances; now out one to two weeks with a muscle injury. Alessandro Gabrielloni (Palermo): eight appearances off the bench, one assist. Alvaro Morata (Leganes): still without a goal and suspended after a red card off the bench against Cordoba. Also out on loan: Fellipe Jack (Cremonese), Andrea Le Borgne (Verona), Federico Chinetti (Mantova). Women's Team Como 1907 Women, unbeaten newcomers, host leaders Roma In their first Serie A season, Selena Mazzantini's side are third and unbeaten. Saturday brings the leaders to town, and the city derby follows a week later. A note first: two clubs from the city play in Serie A Women this season. Como 1907 's own team, coached by Selena Mazzantini with Patrizia Panico as her assistant, won Serie B last season. Como Women, in black and white, is a separate club owned by Mercury13, as Il Post explains . This section follows Como 1907's team. They are third on 11 points after five games (three wins, two draws, goals 13 to seven), four behind leaders Roma, per DAZN . Last Saturday they drew 1-1 at Ternana: Bonfantini scored after 25 minutes from Moraca's pass, and Strode equalised at 76. A statement start The results so far: 4-1 against Milan, 2-1 at Napoli with Xhemaili scoring in the 95th minute, a 4-2 win at Juventus with two from Agnese Bonfantini, and a 2-2 draw with Sassuolo (Valentina Giacinti scored, and Tessa Wullaert rescued a point with a 93rd-minute penalty). Wullaert, signed from Inter, leads the scoring with four; Bonfantini has three and Emilie Haavi two. Next up is Roma, top on 15 points, at home on Saturday (3:30 a.m. Pacific, DAZN). The derby against Como Women, fourth on eight points after beating Milan 1-0 last weekend, follows on Sunday, November 15, according to the FIGC schedule. Players Away Seven called up so far, with Spain still to come The November window starts next week. Here is who is going where. Argentina: Nico Paz and Maximo Perrone are in Lionel Scaloni's squad, his first since Lionel Messi's international retirement, per Ambito . Argentina play Uruguay at La Bombonera on November 13 and Costa Rica in Cordoba on November 17. One Argentine report says Paz may be handed the No. 10 shirt; that is unconfirmed. Italy: Roberto Mancini has picked Samuele Ricci and, for the first time, Mattia Liberali , for Nations League games against France at San Siro (November 12) and Belgium in Brussels (November 15), per Sportitalia . The Primavera's Riccardo Cassano is also reported in the squad; check the official FIGC list. Moise Kean is injured and misses out. Croatia: Martin Baturina and Ivan Smolcic are in the preliminary 32 for England at Wembley (November 12) and the Czech Republic in Osijek (November 15). Still to come: Spain name their squad on Friday, with Marca tipping Jacobo Ramon for a first senior call-up. Lists for Greece (Douvikas), Senegal (Diao), France (Butez, Da Cunha) and England (Chalobah) had not been published when this edition went out. On loan in Europe: Ivan Azon's Getafe host Brighton in the Conference League on Thursday night; the result was not in when this edition went out. Numbers of the Week The week in four figures 9 Goals at Lens, the most an Italian club has scored in a Champions League game. The previous best was Juventus's 7-0 against Olympiacos in 2003. 11 Goals in all competitions for Tasos Douvikas, including six in four Champions League games. 6 Straight wins in all competitions, starting with 3-1 at Fiorentina on October 18. 15 Outfield players on Como's Champions League list, according to Fabregas. In Brief Quick hits New third kit: Revolut Business features on Como's new third shirt for the league, announced on October 26; no fee was disclosed. Late restart fine: the Serie A disciplinary judge fined Como 8,000 euros on October 20, as repeat offenders, for starting a second half four minutes late. Sanchez on loan: Robert Sanchez is at Como on a season-long loan from Chelsea, competing with Jean Butez for the gloves. Venezia penalty row: Suwarso said Milla's handball against Venezia was a penalty against Como, adding that "episodes even out over time". Remembering Hartono: this is Como's first season since co-owner Michael Bambang Hartono died in March, aged 86. Robert Budi Hartono remains the controlling owner. t: The Weekly AC Milan Digest: November 5, 2026
k: Milan beat Inter 3-1 to climb to fifth in Serie A, but sit 24th in the Europa League and must beat unbeaten Ferencváros tonight at San Siro.
x: STOPPAGE TIME The Weekly AC Milan Digest Everything rossonero, every week Thursday, November 5, 2026 · Weekly edition Season tracker · Serie A: 5th, 21 pts, 7 behind Lazio D 2-2 LAZ L 0-2 BEN W 3-0 LEC D 1-1 SAS W 4-0 SAL W 3-2 ATA L 0-3 BOU W 2-0 UDI L 2-4 BOL W 3-1 INT Last ten competitive games, oldest left. Next: Ferencváros (H), Europa League, Thu Nov 5, 9:45 AM PT. Next match Opponent: Ferencváros Competition: Europa League, league phase, matchday 4 Date: Thursday, Nov 5, 2026 Kickoff: 9:45 AM Pacific (18:45 in Italy) Venue: Home: San Siro, Milan Watch in the US: Paramount+ (English); TUDN and ViX (Spanish), per published US listings In this edition The Lead · Off the Pitch · Transfer News · Player Ratings · Scouting the Next Opponent · The Squad · The Academy · Women's Team · Players Away · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch If you read nothing else Milan beat Inter 3-1 on Oct 31, with Diego Moreira scoring once and assisting twice, to climb to fifth in Serie A on 21 points. Milan, 24th in the Europa League with three points, host unbeaten Ferencváros tonight at 9:45 AM Pacific with Maignan suspended. Markus Krösche has agreed to become Milan's head of football, per Gianluca Di Marzio; the club has not announced it yet. The Lead After the derby, the night that decides Milan's European autumn Rúben Amorim's side beat Inter 3-1 to climb to fifth in Serie A. Tonight they must turn that energy into points against an unbeaten Ferencváros, because in the Europa League they are 24th of 36. T here are wins that change a table and wins that change a mood. Milan 's 3-1 victory over Inter at San Siro on Saturday did a little of the first and a great deal of the second. It handed Cristian Chivu's side their first league defeat of the season and lifted Amorim's team to fifth on 21 points, seven behind leaders Lazio and two off the top four. It also came three days after the worst night of the new regime: a 4-2 home defeat by Bologna in which Milan led 2-1 at half-time and then collapsed under a Mbangula hat-trick . The derby was the reply. Now comes the harder question: can this team carry it into Europe, where three matchdays have produced one win, two defeats and a red card? How Amorim won the derby The game was settled inside 43 minutes, and almost everything ran through Diego Moreira . The €50m summer signing from Strasbourg crossed for Christian Pulisic to head in after four minutes, then delivered the corner that Adrien Rabiot turned in on ten. After Alessandro Bastoni headed Inter back into it from a corner, Moreira curled a left-footed free kick over the wall just before the break. Moreira became only the second Milan player in 20 years with three goal involvements in a derby, after Rafael Leão in 2022. It was Milan's fourth straight derby win and, per Opta Analyst , their third in a row in Serie A for the first time since 2002 to 2004. Their unbeaten run against Inter now stands at eight. The second half was about survival. Inter finished with 19 shots to Milan's seven and roughly 1.68 expected goals to 0.62, per the single stats feed we could find ( AllFootball ), so treat those numbers with care. On 75 minutes referee Marco Guida gave Inter a penalty for a Mario Gila handball, then overturned it after a VAR review showed the ball had struck his midriff. It was not an amazing game, but it's an amazing night for our fans. That is part of the process. Rúben Amorim to DAZN, Oct 31 Amorim, speaking to DAZN, was candid about it. Inter were "very strong in the air", he said, so Milan "changed the way we addressed the game", and in the second half "we maintained the ball", a credit he directed at Luka Modrić ( SoccerNews ). He also named the three players who had just returned from injury: "Gila, Moreira and Rabiot made a big difference." Why tonight matters more The Europa League table is unforgiving. Milan opened with a 2-0 home defeat by Benfica , then won 4-0 in Salzburg behind an Alphadjo Cissé hat-trick, then lost 3-0 at Bournemouth after Mike Maignan was sent off. Three points from three games leaves them 24th, the last of the play-off places, with four games left. Ferencváros arrive with nine points from nine and, per TuttoMercatoWeb , a 20-match unbeaten run. A defeat would leave Milan looking over their shoulder at elimination before the Olympiacos trip on Nov 26. A win would cut the gap to the Hungarians to three points. Amorim framed it bluntly at his press conference on Wednesday. "We need to forget about Inter; there's a new competition," he said, adding: "This is the most important game, but we'll need to rotate, all players are ready" ( Goal ). To Sky Sport Italia he called it "a crucial game" in which Milan must "stay humble and attentive to details". The selection puzzle Rotation is unavoidable with Genoa away on Sunday. Maignan serves his one-match ban, so Lorenzo Torriani is expected to make his first start of the season. Strahinja Pavlović has been left out to rest, not through injury, per TMW . Football Italia 's probable XI has Torriani behind a back four of Filippo Terracciano, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Davide Bartesaghi; Omari Hutchinson, Ardon Jashari, Yunus Musah and Cissé across midfield; Rabiot behind Gonçalo Ramos. Modrić and Pulisic would start on the bench. Sources disagree on whether Diawara plays centrally or wide. The key battle is in central midfield. Without Modrić's tempo, Jashari and Musah must stop Ferencváros's 4-2-3-1 finding Kristoffer Zachariassen between the lines. Up front, the night is another chance for Ramos, the €74m club-record signing, whose slow start has become a talking point. Key facts Derby Milan 3-1 Inter, Sat Oct 31, San Siro. Milan 's shareholders approved the 2025/26 accounts on Oct 29, and they show the cost of a season without European football. The club reported a net loss of €23.7m , the first loss under RedBird, after profits of about €3m the previous year ( Calcio e Finanza ). The value of production fell 6.1 percent to €464.6m. Net financial debt rose from €92m to €145m, per Pianeta Milan . There were brighter lines: sponsorship passed €100m for the first time, and average attendance topped 72,000, the best in Serie A for a second straight year. RedBird paid in €53m toward a future capital increase on Aug 19, per the club's figures reported by MilanPress . The Generali Stadium The same day, Milan and Inter unveiled the design of their new home. Designed by Foster + Partners and MANICA, it will hold about 71,500 in two tiers. Work is due to start in 2028, with a first match targeted for the 2031/32 season, subject to approvals. ANSA puts the whole development at about €1.2bn. Generali's naming-rights deal is worth about €650m over 25 years, per Adnkronos , roughly €13m a year for each club. Adidas, and Cardinale's message Gazzetta reports that Milan have agreed to return to Adidas from 2028/29 in a deal worth €500m over ten years, about €50m a season, roughly double what Puma pays now ( Calcio e Finanza ). It is not yet official. Owner Gerry Cardinale , speaking to Gazzetta on the eve of the derby, said Amorim "is absolutely not in danger", that the rebuild is only about a quarter done, and that Milan will be "aggressive and opportunistic" in January ( via Pianeta Milan ). Transfer News Krösche agreed as head of football, with a January shopping list waiting Milan's new football chief is lined up, a centre-back is the priority and Cardinale has fallen for a striker Club Brugge will not sell. Markus Krösche: agreement reached, announcement pending Milan have found the man to run their football operation. Gianluca Di Marzio reported on Oct 31 that an agreement had been reached with Markus Krösche , 46, who has been released by Eintracht Frankfurt at his own request. Certainty: agreement reached, not yet official. The timing is still moving. Di Marzio expects an announcement by Dec 1 and Calciomercato.com in December; Bild and Sky Germany say by Jan 1, 2027. Matteo Moretto reported on Nov 5 that the move is finalised and that he starts in January. Compensation to Frankfurt is reported variously: about €4m (Bild, via 90min ), €5m (Sky Germany) and a €7m clause that Milan may not pay in full (Calciomercato.com). His Frankfurt record is the selling point: Randal Kolo Muani and Omar Marmoush arrived free and left for €95m and €75m. The role matters because of what Cardinale told Gazzetta: he will never again hand "the keys" to a sporting director. Krösche will run things day to day at Milanello and work alongside the owner, not above him. The centre-back hunt: Inácio first, Sylla as the alternative Injuries have made defence the January priority. Matteo Gabbia is out until early 2027 with a hamstring tear, and Fikayo Tomori is out for about a month ( Calciomercato.com ). The favourite since June, per Fabrizio Romano, is Gonçalo Inácio , Sporting's 25-year-old left-footed centre-back and a former Amorim player. His release clause is €60m; Sporting's asking price is reported at €40m to €45m ( Virgilio ). The summer move stalled because Sporting wanted a replacement first. Certainty: concrete interest, no talks confirmed. The cheaper option is Massiré Sylla , Union Saint-Gilloise's 21-year-old, 1.96m Senegalese centre-back, contracted to 2030. Moretto reported scouting, and Pianeta Milan says exploratory contacts have been made. Certainty: monitoring, single-sourced on contacts. Romano expects "at least one, probably two" January signings. Cardinale, per Gazzetta, was won over by Nicolò Tresoldi when the 22-year-old scored a Champions League hat-trick against Inter on Oct 13. Club Brugge turned down €50m bids in the summer and will not sell in January ( Goal ). Certainty: owner's interest, club refusing. Endrick remains a background thread. Gazzetta reported in October that he would choose Milan if Real Madrid let him go on loan, but José Mourinho said anyone who wants him in January "will have to go over me" ( DAZN ). It was a tenth straight competitive win: PSG top Ligue 1 by two points and the Champions League table with 12 points. David Boly, 17, scored on his Champions League debut, and RMC reports PSG want him on a five-year first professional contract. The Lead Champions League · Villarreal 0-6 PSG Six goals, ten wins, no Dembélé: PSG's understudies run riot in Villarreal Without four injured stars, Luis Enrique's reshuffled side scored four times in 17 minutes, set a Champions League record and made a statement about the depth of this squad. T here was a version of Tuesday night in which Paris Saint-Germain looked short. Ousmane Dembélé , Khvicha Kvaratskhelia , Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes were all missing at the Estadio de la Cerámica, and Villarreal had a new coach and a home crowd. Instead the champions produced their most complete European display of the autumn and won 6-0 . The damage was done almost before the hosts had settled. João Neves headed in at nine minutes after Pacho flicked on Doué's corner. Doué scored at 12, Senny Mayulu volleyed in at 13 and Fabián Ruiz finished Akliouche's cut-back at 17. Four goals in eight minutes of play between the first and the fourth; the tie was over. Ruiz added a lovely fifth five minutes after the break, cutting past Veiga and lifting the ball through Gulácsi's legs. Then, at 78 minutes, the substitute David Boly, a 17-year-old right-back from the academy, scored with a deflected shot from Neves's pass on his Champions League debut. Ruiz, with the second brace of his career, was named man of the match. According to Playmakerstats , PSG's 20 goals across the first four league-phase games is a Champions League record, beating the 17 Bayern Munich managed in 2021-22. PSG have now gone 14 Champions League games unbeaten , equalling Lyon's French record from 2004 to 2006, and sit top of the 36-team table with 12 points and a goal difference of plus 15. Key facts Result: Villarreal 0-6 PSG, UCL league phase matchday 4, Tue Nov 3 Scorers: Neves 9', Doué 12', Mayulu 13', Ruiz 17', 50', Boly 78' Stats (Fotmob): Possession 71% to 29%; shots 22 to 14; xG 2.69 to 0.66 UCL table: PSG 1st, 12 pts, GD +15; Barcelona 2nd, 9 pts (after Tuesday's games) Record: 20 goals in four league-phase games; previous best 17 (Bayern, 2021-22) Unbeaten: 14 UCL games, equalling Lyon's French record (2004 to 2006) Missing: Dembélé, Kvaratskhelia, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes (all injured) How the reshuffle worked The interesting part is how Luis Enrique replaced his missing attackers. He did not hand the No. 9 role to the summer signing Ferran Torres. He started Mayulu centrally between Maghnes Akliouche and Désiré Doué, a front three with no fixed target man, and left Torres on the bench until the hour. It suited the night. PSG had 71 per cent of the ball, 22 shots to 14 and 43 touches in the Villarreal box to 10 , with an expected-goals count of 2.69 against 0.66 (Fotmob figures). Akliouche, who set up two of the first four goals, earned an 8 from L'Équipe ( as compiled by Canal Supporters ), level with Hakimi and Neves and behind only Ruiz's 9. Set pieces mattered again too. Neves's opener was his eighth PSG goal from a dead ball out of 15 in total, per Opta via the club , and since 2024-25 PSG have scored 19 Champions League goals inside the first 15 minutes of games, more than any other club. The early-strike habit is no accident; it is how this team breaks a block before it sets. "We are not champions yet, nor in the final in Madrid. None of that is a given." Luis Enrique after the 6-0 win, as quoted by Foot Mercato (translated from French) The coach refuses to celebrate Luis Enrique was almost apologetic afterwards. "I am not very happy to see my opponent in that kind of difficulty," he said, according to Foot Mercato , before adding that after 3-0 "there are few teams that can overcome that". His message to the squad was clear: four wins guarantee nothing in a format where the top eight go straight to the last 16. Lucas Hernández said the same thing in plainer terms: PSG are "only halfway there" and, "as things stand, we haven't qualified yet" ( club reaction ). The remaining league-phase games are Roma at home on November 25, Aston Villa away on December 8, then Como away and Galatasaray at home in January. Barcelona, beaten 4-2 in Paris on October 20, were second with nine points after Tuesday's games. What the night really showed is the strength of the squad. With four regular starters in the treatment room, PSG still beat a Champions League side by six. The question for January is not whether they can cope without Kvaratskhelia, who is out for months, but whether they want one more winger anyway. More on that in Transfer News. Ligue 1 · Le Havre 1-5 PSG Hakimi at Le Havre: the right-back who keeps scoring like a forward Three goals and two assists in a 5-1 win on Friday gave Achraf Hakimi a night no defender had produced in Ligue 1's Opta era. Four days before Villarreal, Luis Enrique rested several regulars for the trip to Le Havre , and PSG still won 5-1 at the Stade Océane on Friday, October 30. Josh Maja put the hosts ahead at 18 minutes. Mika Godts equalised at 26, and then Achraf Hakimi took over: a goal at 28 after a VAR check for offside, a direct free kick at 55 and a third at 69. By the count beIN Sports reported from Opta , Hakimi was directly involved in five goals, three scored and two assisted. He is only the seventh player to manage that in a Ligue 1 match since 2006-07, and the first defender. In his previous 135 Ligue 1 appearances he had never been involved in more than two in a game. "No, it's not the match of my life," he said. His coach called him "the best right-back in the world" and "clearly an attacker when we have the ball", yet also told him off for arguing with the linesman during the VAR check. That balance is typical of Luis Enrique: praise for the output, and a reminder that the standards do not move. The win kept PSG top of Ligue 1 on 20 points, two clear of Lille. Scouting the Next Opponent Troyes at the Parc: a promoted side with the league's bluntest attack Stéphane Dumont's newcomers just climbed out of the bottom three. They have not beaten PSG since 2001. Troyes (ESTAC) arrive at the Parc des Princes on Saturday as the 16th-placed side in Ligue 1, on eight points from nine games (two wins, two draws, five defeats, seven scored and 16 conceded). They sealed promotion as Ligue 2 leaders in April, two years after dropping to the third tier on the pitch and being reinstated to Ligue 2 by administrative decision. Their coach, Stéphane Dumont , sets up with a back four, shown as a 4-2-3-1 at Lorient and a 4-3-3 elsewhere. Goals are spread thin: no Troyes player has more than one in the league. The names to watch are the veteran forward and penalty taker Renaud Ripart, the midfielder Antoine Mille (a goal and an assist) and Timothé Nkada, who set up the opener against Le Mans. The form line is improving. Last Saturday's 2-0 home win over Le Mans , through Diop and Boura, lifted them out of the relegation zone, and they drew 0-0 at Toulouse the week before. Before that came five straight defeats, starting with a 6-2 home thrashing by Strasbourg in September and ending with a 3-1 home loss to Lens. Where Troyes can be hurt The vulnerabilities are obvious. Before Le Mans, Sports Mole noted they had the league's lowest goal tally and the joint-fewest big chances created. Their seven goals are still the joint-lowest in Ligue 1, and they have one away win in four. Against a PSG side that has scored 11 times in its last two games, sitting deep and hoping is a plan with a short life expectancy. History is no comfort for the visitors either. The last time they met in Paris, in October 2022, PSG won 4-3 with Messi, Neymar and Mbappé all scoring; the last meeting, in Troyes in May 2023, ended 3-1 to PSG. Troyes have not beaten PSG since November 2001. Troyes at a glance Opponent: ESTAC Troyes, 16th in Ligue 1, 8 pts (W2 D2 L5, GF 7 GA 16) Coach / system: Stéphane Dumont; back four, 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3 Last five: W 2-0 Le Mans, D 0-0 Toulouse (a), L 1-3 Lens, L 0-2 Marseille, L 0-2 Angers (a) Players to stop: Renaud Ripart, Antoine Mille, Timothé Nkada Team news: Before Le Mans, Ouzenadji (ankle) was likely out, Koné (knee) a doubt and Titi carrying a leg problem; no newer update found Recent H2H: PSG 4-3 Troyes (Oct 2022), Troyes 1-3 PSG (May 2023) Transfer News The Kvaratskhelia gap: PSG weigh a January winger The Georgian's torn ACL has turned a vague wish list into a live search. Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza is the most concrete name. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured the cruciate ligament in his right knee in the 4-2 win over Barcelona on October 20 and is expected to miss more than six months. L'Équipe had reported, via Culturap , that PSG were already looking for a winger for January before the injury. The injury has made it urgent. Luis Enrique has been careful in public. "No injury means you have to sign new players," he said on October 24, according to VIPSG , "but we remain open to opportunities." Luis Campos has said nothing new on the record since August, when he told Ligue 1+ the window was not finished. The most solid lead is Ibrahim Maza , the 20-year-old Bayer Leverkusen playmaker under contract to 2030. Sky Germany's Florian Plettenberg reports concrete interest, with Maza on PSG's shortlist as a possible Kvaratskhelia replacement. Maza himself told RTL and Sky that PSG "would be a huge dream" , while also naming Real Madrid, Barcelona and Arsenal. Certainty: concrete interest. A claimed first offer comes only from a fan account and is unverified. Chelsea's Estêvão has also been linked with a loan, with TEAMtalk reporting three Chelsea conditions . Fabrizio Romano has played it down : no transfer alert, and a January exit is not a Chelsea priority. Certainty: rumour. Nico Williams, meanwhile, said on October 26 that he had turned down offers from clubs including PSG and Arsenal. That thread is dead. Ferran Torres: a World Cup hero on the bench The €50m summer signing has gone five games without a goal. Spanish reports of regret are thinly sourced. Ferran Torres joined from Barcelona on August 15 for about €50m on a contract to 2031, weeks after scoring Spain's extra-time winner in the World Cup final. He scored seven in his first six PSG games. Since the 2-1 win in Marseille on September 20 he has not scored, a run of five games by Foot01's count. At Villarreal, with Dembélé and Kvaratskhelia out, he still started on the bench. Foot01 framed that as Luis Enrique losing patience, citing unnamed Spanish press; that is opinion, not reporting. L'Équipe's line, relayed by Foot01 on October 30, was the opposite: the coach is "very satisfied" and the dip is "a logical phase". The "wants to go back to Barcelona" story, picked up by Foot Sur 7 from ElNacional.cat, names no sources, and even Foot Sur 7 calls an exit within six months hard to imagine. Certainty: low-grade rumour. The more useful reading is tactical: with Mayulu thriving centrally, Torres's route back may be on the left, where Kvaratskhelia's absence leaves minutes. Contracts: Doué's big offer, and the academy pair PSG want to lock down RMC says talks have opened with Quentin Ndjantou, while David Boly is in line for a first professional deal in January. RMC Sport's Fabrice Hawkins reports, via Maxifoot , that PSG have opened talks with Quentin Ndjantou , 19, on a five-year deal to 2031; his current contract runs to 2028. The same report says PSG want to give David Boly a five-year first professional contract once he turns 18 on January 22, and that the player wants to stay. Certainty: talks opened. Désiré Doué (contract to 2029) received a first verbal offer in late October for a deal to 2031 or 2032 with a large raise, RMC reported, as relayed by VIPSG . No agreement yet. PSG also still intend to extend Kvaratskhelia to 2032 despite the injury, per RMC via Foot01. Ousmane Dembélé 's extension remains unsigned. An agreement in principle to 2030 was reported on August 31, but the player said on September 2 that "nothing is signed yet" ( ParisUnited ); there has been no announcement since. Already official since September 4: Luis Enrique to 2030; Pacho, Neves, Beraldo and Mayulu to 2031; Fabián Ruiz to 2028 ( psg.fr ).
