The Squad Rotation, a new front three and an armband on the move Luis Enrique made five changes between Le Havre and Villarreal and won both games by a combined 11-1. The selection pattern this week was striking. At Le Havre, Vitinha, Neves, Ruiz, Pacho and Doué did not start; four days later all five did. Safonov, Hakimi, Zabarnyi, Hernández, Akliouche and Mayulu started both. Luis Enrique said before Villarreal that if his side thought results so far would win the game, "we are mistaken" , and he picked accordingly. The coach has been open about trusting youth. "I'm sure they have the level, Senny Mayulu in particular," he said, per Planète PSG . Mayulu has now scored against Lyon, Le Havre and Villarreal in successive games, and has played centrally as well as wide. Dro, Beraldo, Ndjantou and Boly all had real minutes this week. Captaincy, goalkeepers and the injury list With Marquinhos out, Achraf Hakimi has worn the armband, handing it to Warren Zaïre-Emery when he was substituted at Le Havre. In goal, Matvey Safonov is clearly first choice; "I play every match," he said in September ( Footeo ). The third goalkeeper Alessandro Longoni returned to the squad for Villarreal. The injury list is unchanged and none of the four is expected back for Troyes. The Academy Boly's night, Mayulu's run, and a hard lesson for the U19s The academy delivered two goals in the first team's record win, on the same day the youth side lost 3-0 at Villarreal. David Boly , born in Colombes in January 2009, has been at the PSG academy since 2022 and made his senior debut in the Coupe de France last December. On Tuesday he came on for Hakimi at 74 minutes and scored four minutes later. At 17 years and 285 days he is PSG's second-youngest scorer in Europe , five days older than Zaïre-Emery was. "Making my Champions League debut in a match like that was an incredible feeling," Boly told the club afterwards. Sports Mole , citing L'Équipe, reports that his academy deal runs to 2027 and that he has a large first-professional-contract offer he has not yet signed. With RMC adding that PSG plan a five-year deal once he turns 18, the club's intent looks clear. Senny Mayulu , 20, who scored in the 2025 Champions League final, has become a starter in all but name during the injury crisis. Quentin Ndjantou , 19, made two substitute appearances this week and was booked for time-wasting at Villarreal; his own contract talks are covered in Transfer News. U19s and loanees The UEFA Youth League side had a rougher Tuesday, losing 3-0 to Villarreal U19 , with the hosts scoring in the first minute. PSG U19 are 12th on seven points from four games (a 6-1 win over Slovan, 2-0 at Man City, 1-1 with Barcelona and this defeat). Next is Roma U19 on November 25. On loan, the goalkeeper Renato Marin played 90 minutes for Nacional in a 1-0 defeat at Arouca on November 1, after keeping a clean sheet against Braga the week before. Gabriel Moscardo has six La Liga appearances for Espanyol, two of them starts. Khalil Ayari is on loan at Dunkerque in Ligue 2; we found no recent match data for him. PSG Féminine Two late-drama draws, and Bayern next at the Parc PSG rescued a point at Manchester City, then shared the Paris derby. A big Champions League night follows on Tuesday. PSG Féminine travelled to Manchester City for the third Women's Champions League league-phase game last Thursday and looked beaten when Khadija Shaw scored a penalty at 85 minutes, after a foul by Griedge Mbock. Three minutes later Tara Elimbi Gilbert equalised , and goalkeeper Oliwia Peda's saves had kept PSG in it. The detailed report is from one outlet; the score is confirmed elsewhere. Sunday's derby at Charléty against Paris FC also finished 1-1 . Clara Matéo put Paris FC ahead at 11 minutes, PSG levelled at 29, and Evelyne Viens had a stoppage-time winner ruled out for offside. Sources disagree on who is credited with PSG's equaliser, so we have left it unnamed. Where they stand PSG are second in the Première Ligue on 16 points from seven games, five behind OL Lyonnes on 21 (Fotmob). Earlier in October they beat Fleury 3-1 and Montpellier 1-0 but lost 4-0 to OL Lyonnes. In Europe, PSG have five points from three games (1-1 at Real Madrid, 5-0 against OH Leuven, 1-1 at City). The top four go straight to the quarter-finals, which makes Tuesday's visit of Bayern Munich to the Parc des Princes the biggest night of their autumn. The international window comes next: France's coach Zinédine Zidane names his squad on Friday at 6:00 PM in Paris (9:00 AM Pacific). France lead Nations League group A1 with 10 points from four games and play Italy in Milan on November 12 and Turkey in Bordeaux on November 15 . Dembélé, a regular in recent squads, is injured. Other federations had not published November lists for PSG's internationals (including Portugal, Spain, Morocco, Ecuador and Ukraine) by the time we went to press. k: Dortmund drew 2-2 at Bayern after Niko Kovac switched to a back four, and now host unbeaten Real Betis in the Champions League tonight.
x: STOPPAGE TIME The Weekly Borussia Dortmund Digest Black, yellow and every story in between Weekly edition · Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Bundesliga: 2nd, 18 pts (level with leaders Bayern on points, behind on goal difference) · Last ten, oldest first W 3-2 VIL W 3-0 SCP W 1-0 VFB D 2-2 SVW L 0-1 BOD D 0-0 FCU W 2-1 SAB W 1-0 SGE W 3-2 SVW D 2-2 FCB Next: Real Betis (H), Champions League, today 12:00 PM PT Next match Opponent: Real Betis Competition: UEFA Champions League, league phase, matchday 4 Date: Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Kickoff: 12:00 PM Pacific (9:00 PM in Dortmund) Venue: Home, Signal Iduna Park (sold out) Where to watch in the US: Paramount+ ( listing ) In this edition The Lead · Player Ratings · Scouting the Next Opponent · Transfer News · The Squad · The Academy · Women's Team · Players Away · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch If you read nothing else Dortmund drew 2-2 at Bayern on Saturday through Guirassy and an 89th-minute Fábio Silva goal, and sit level on 18 points. Kovac switched to a back four in Munich, with Joane Gadou at right-back for the first time, and may use it again. Unbeaten Real Betis visit Signal Iduna Park tonight at 12:00 PM Pacific; Dortmund are 13th in the Champions League on six points. The Lead The back four that held Munich now meets Betis and their perfect record Niko Kovac's surprise reshuffle earned a point at the Allianz Arena. Tonight's Champions League visit of Real Betis will test whether it was a one-night trick or a new way of playing. N obody in Munich saw it coming, and that was the point. The team sheet Borussia Dortmund handed in at the Allianz Arena on Saturday looked like the usual three-man defence. It was not. "That was not it, we played with a back four from the start," Niko Kovac explained afterwards, as reported by Sport1 . The result was a 2-2 draw that kept Dortmund level with Bayern Munich on 18 points after eight unbeaten games, Bayern staying top only on goal difference. Serhou Guirassy cancelled out Konrad Laimer 's 38th-minute opener on the hour, Dayot Upamecano restored Bayern's lead six minutes later, and substitute Fábio Silva drove in an 89th-minute equaliser, per the official match report . The detail that matters for tonight is how Kovac got there. According to captain Nico Schlotterbeck , the coach called him and Waldemar Anton in beforehand and asked how they felt about a back four, a shape Schlotterbeck said Dortmund had not used in about a year and a half. Joane Gadou played right-back for the first time, facing Serge Gnabry and then Alphonso Davies. “Niko had a brilliant chess move with the back four.” Gregor Kobel, after the Klassiker, via Sport1 Why it worked, and what it cost Kovac's reasoning was about pressing, not caution. "We attacked Bayern much higher, and that gave us an extra player in midfield," he said. Joey Veerman sat alone at the base, which freed Jobe Bellingham and Carney Chukwuemeka to jump onto Bayern's build-up. The equaliser came straight from that plan: Schlotterbeck won the ball high, Chukwuemeka found Guirassy, and the striker finished low. It was not a smash-and-grab without risk. Bayern created far more: ESPN puts the expected-goals count at 4.18 to 0.63, and the hosts hit the frame several times. The worst moment was Dortmund's own: Felix Nmecha handled a Harry Kane shot in the 56th minute, and Kane's penalty came back off the crossbar. Kobel, given Dortmund's best mark by the Ruhr Nachrichten , made the saves that kept it close. Key facts: Bayern 2-2 Dortmund When: Saturday, October 31, Allianz Arena, Bundesliga matchday 8 Goals: Laimer 38', Guirassy 60', Upamecano 66', Silva 89' Missed penalty: Kane, 56', off the crossbar after Nmecha's handball Expected goals (ESPN): Bayern 4.18, Dortmund 0.63 Booked (Dortmund): Bellingham Table: both on 18 points from 8 games; Bayern top on goal difference From Munich to Betis Analysis at BVB-WLD argues the new shape has a future because it spreads players more evenly across the wide areas and stops Maximilian Beier being stretched as a wing-back. Kovac himself is keeping his options open. "It is not definite that we will always do it this way, but it is not definite that we won't try it again," he said before tonight's game, as quoted by Mucho Deporte . That is the selection question against Real Betis . Manuel Pellegrini's side like the ball, and Kovac's instruction was blunt: "We have to do exactly the opposite of what they want us to do." A high-pressing back four would ask the same question of Betis's double pivot that it asked of Joshua Kimmich and Aleksandar Pavlovic. The predicted line-ups at The Hard Tackle and FútbolFantasy , though, still show the familiar back three with Julian Ryerson and Daniel Svensson as wing-backs. The stakes are real. Dortmund are 13th in the league phase on six points after beating Villarreal and Sabah and losing in Bodø. Betis have nine from nine. A home win would lift Dortmund level with them and well into the top-eight conversation before trips to Arsenal and Aston Villa. "Tomorrow there is only one direction: we want to win this thing," Kovac told the club ticker . Secondary feature: the cup tie that nearly got away Four days before Munich, Dortmund needed a 93rd-minute free kick from Marcel Sabitzer to beat Werder Bremen 3-2 in the DFB-Pokal second round. Guirassy and Chukwuemeka had them 2-0 up, before former Dortmund striker Niclas Füllkrug scored twice in three minutes, the first a penalty. Kovac was reported to be unhappy with how his side managed the lead, per All Football . The reward came on Sunday night: a last-16 trip to Eintracht Frankfurt , drawn at the football museum in Dortmund and scheduled for December 1 or 2, according to ran.de . Sabitzer's winner was the club's first direct free-kick goal since November 2024. Player Ratings Bayern 2-2 Dortmund: how every Dortmund player rated The Digest's own marks out of 10, informed by the Goal Germany and Ruhr Nachrichten player grades and the match reports. Inácio and Ryerson came on in the 87th minute and are not rated. Scouting the Next Opponent Real Betis: nine from nine, and a coach who has been here before Pellegrini's side arrive in their second ever Champions League campaign having won every game, and with an old Dortmund defender at the heart of it. Real Betis have never won three straight Champions League matches before this season, according to El Gol Digital . They won 3-2 at Lille, 3-2 at home to Porto and 1-0 against Feyenoord, and arrive fourth in La Liga after beating Málaga 2-1 on Saturday through Marc Bartra and Pablo Fornals. The Hard Tackle counts ten wins from their last 14 since late August. Manuel Pellegrini , 73, will take charge of his 70th Champions League match. He has history here: Dortmund knocked his Málaga side out in the 2012-13 quarter-finals. "If they had told us we would collect nine points from three games, it would have been a feat," he said on Tuesday, per ElDesmarque . Kovac called his longevity on the touchline "admirable". The players to stop Isco is the playmaker and has faced Dortmund with three clubs; Abde Ezzalzouli carries the threat from the left; and Marc Bartra , who played for Dortmund from 2016 to 2018, has been scoring from defence. The Brazilian has not scored in 13 games this season, and Pellegrini said a big performance "would do him a lot of good". Expect a 4-2-3-1 built on Fornals and Marc Roca as a double pivot, with Héctor Bellerín and Fran García pushing on from full-back, per FútbolFantasy . Where Dortmund can hurt them Betis can be got at: Barcelona put five past them in a 5-2 league defeat in Seville this autumn, and both Lille and Porto scored twice against them in Europe. Their full-backs push high, which leaves room behind for Guirassy and Silva to run into. Dortmund have also won their last four UEFA home games against Spanish clubs. In this edition The Lead · Kane's New Deal · Player Ratings · Scouting Mainz · Transfer News · The Squad · The Campus · FC Bayern Women · Players Away · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch If you read nothing else • Bayern won 2-0 at Atlético Madrid on Tuesday through Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer, with Aaron Danks still deputising for Vincent Kompany. • Fabio Silva's 89th-minute equaliser earned Dortmund a 2-2 draw in Munich, leaving both clubs level on 18 points at the top. • Max Eberl says Ismael Saibari faces three to four months out after ankle surgery and Serge Gnabry will miss the rest of 2026. The Lead In Kompany's absence, Bayern find another gear Twelve days after their head coach collapsed at the training ground, an injury-ravaged Bayern under Aaron Danks are unbeaten, top of the Bundesliga and fresh from their best European night of the season. N obody at Säbener Strasse planned for this. On Friday, October 23, Bayern head coach Vincent Kompany collapsed while watching a reserve-team session and was taken to hospital, ESPN reported . He had been fighting a viral infection that affected his legs, and had pushed through it to sit on the bench for the 2-2 draw with Arsenal two days earlier. The diagnosis came on October 28, the day he was discharged. "It's a meningeal irritation that caused this incident on Friday," board member for sport Max Eberl told reporters . Kompany is resting and taking medication, and there is no return date. On November 2 Eberl said the recovery was going well and "there are no complications," but "it'll take a little while longer" ( FCBinside ). Into the gap stepped Aaron Danks , Kompany's assistant, who had already taken training and media duties on the Tuesday before the collapse. His record since: four games, three wins, one draw, 13 goals scored and four conceded. That run includes a 3-1 win at Freiburg , a 6-1 cup rout of Magdeburg , the Klassiker and Tuesday's 2-0 at the Metropolitano. Key facts Kompany Collapsed Oct 23; meningeal irritation; discharged Oct 28; no return date Danks record P4 W3 D1, goals 13-4 Bundesliga 1st, 18 pts after 8, level with Dortmund Europe 8 pts from 4 games, unbeaten Out Musiala, Díaz (after break); Gnabry (rest of 2026); Saibari (3 to 4 months) The numbers flatter nobody, because the squad Danks inherited is shredded. Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz were already out with thigh muscle injuries. Then, inside three first-half minutes against Dortmund , Ismael Saibari tore ankle ligaments in a collision with Gregor Kobel and Serge Gnabry pulled up with a hamstring problem ( Bundesliga.com ). Eberl's latest timelines are stark: Saibari three to four months after surgery, Gnabry out for the rest of the year, Musiala and Díaz back only after the November international break ( Yahoo Sports ). Manuel Neuer missed three games with a foot tendon problem, Michael Olise played through a knock and Aleksandar Pavlović was withdrawn before kickoff in Madrid. Three ways Danks has adapted So how has Danks kept the machine running? The clearest answer is Alphonso Davies. With wide forwards falling, Danks pushed the Canadian from left-back to the left wing, a move he said had been a good option in recent weeks ( FCBinside ). Against Atlético , Davies started high on the left, with Tom Bischof deputising for Pavlović in midfield ( AZ ). The second answer is Konrad Laimer. Nominally the right-back, he scored the opener against Dortmund and the clincher in Madrid, a left-footed finish into the top corner from Harry Kane's pass on 74 minutes. He was named player of the match both times. "We have great belief in our squad and in the players we have," he said ( FC Bayern ). The third is the press. Tuesday's breakthrough on 54 minutes came when Lennart Karl hunted down a slow Robin Le Normand clearance and lifted the ball over Jan Oblak ( Bundesliga.com ). It ended Atlético's 16-game home unbeaten run against Bundesliga clubs, a record stretching back to a 1996/97 defeat to Dortmund ( AZ ). "That was total domination from the first to the 93rd minute." Manuel Neuer, after the 2-0 at Atlético What the Klassiker still says None of that hides the Klassiker. Bayern produced 4.83 expected goals to Dortmund's 0.70, hit the woodwork four times and saw Kane's 57th-minute penalty crash off the bar ( Bundesliga.com ). Silva's 89th-minute equaliser, after Konstantinos Karetsas charged down a Pavlović clearance, cost them the chance to go three points clear at the top. The stakes now are about sequencing. Bayern have 18 points from eight league games and 8 from four in Europe, enough to sit on course for the top eight that avoids February's play-off round ( AZ ). One more fixture, at Mainz on Saturday, stands before an international break that should return Musiala and Díaz to training. The danger is depth. With Saibari and Gnabry gone, Karl, Davies and Nathaniel Brown carry the wide burden, and Danks cannot rotate the way Kompany did in October. Bild reports chairman Jan-Christian Dreesen ruled out a January signing with a simple "I don't think so" ( GOAL ). For now, the Danks interregnum is less a stopgap than a stress test, and Bayern are passing it. Secondary Feature Kane's new deal is "a matter of days" away The Ballon d'Or winner says the big points are settled on an extension to 2029. The paperwork is the last step. Bayern are on the brink of keeping their Ballon d'Or winner. Before Tuesday's trip to Madrid, Harry Kane said a contract extension was "more a matter of days" away. "There were good talks over the weekend. I know I keep saying we're close, but now we're really extremely close," he said, adding that many of the bigger points were settled ( SPORT1/SID ). His current deal runs to the end of this season. Sky Germany first reported a preliminary agreement to 2029 in early October, with salary agreed in principle and the final paperwork outstanding ( GOAL ). Nothing has been signed or announced by the club as of Wednesday morning, so the status remains terms agreed in principle, awaiting signature. The timing sharpens the point. Kane was crowned the 2026 Ballon d'Or winner in London on October 26, the first Englishman to win it since Michael Owen in 2001, after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season ( Sky Sports ). Bayern honoured him before the Klassiker. On the pitch the week was mixed. He missed a penalty for only the second time in 27 Bundesliga attempts, had six shots against Dortmund without hitting the target, then set up Laimer in Madrid. Mats Hummels described his deep role as "the Toni Kroos position of the centre-forward" and said Bayern need him in the box more often ( LiveScore roundup ). Chart: Digest ratings out of 10 for the cup tie. Olise top at 8.5. Scouting the Next Opponent Mainz: dangerous on the road, fragile at home Urs Fischer's side press high and leave gaps. Bayern's patched-up attack should find them. Mainz 05 host Bayern on Saturday ninth in the table on 10 points from eight games: three wins, one draw, four defeats, 17 goals scored and 17 conceded ( ESPN ). The split is stark. They have won three times away, including 5-0 at Hamburg, but taken one point from four home games ( Hessenschau ). Form is poor. Mainz lost 3-2 at home to Werder Bremen, were knocked out of the DFB-Pokal in the second round by second-tier Bochum, and then lost 4-1 at Elversberg last Friday, their first league away defeat since March ( Bundesliga.com ). Sporting director Nico Bungert called the cup display a complete mess ( Wochenblatt ). Unlike his old Union sides, this Mainz team presses high and attacks quickly, but Get German Football News notes it is prone to defensive errors and leaves space behind a high line. That is exactly the territory Laimer, Davies and Karl have exploited all autumn. The players to stop: captain Nadiem Amiri, the creative hub, who missed the Bochum tie with a knee problem; Kaishu Sano in midfield; and Lee Jae-sung, a goal threat from midfield. Up front, Phillip Tietz does the link-up work. Dominik Kohr and Silas are listed out until January ( FotMob ). The last meeting, at the MEWA Arena in April, finished 4-3 to Bayern ( ESPN ). Bayern arrive unbeaten in 23 league games, according to Bundesliga.com. Expect Danks to weigh Neuer's minutes and Olise's knock against the international break. Transfer News January: the line holds, the market whispers Bayern's bosses rule out a winter signing. Their scouts are still watching wingers. The official line is clear. Asked about January reinforcements after the Saibari and Gnabry injuries, chairman Jan-Christian Dreesen replied, "I don't think so," Bild reported. Bayern expect everyone but Saibari back for the first game after the winter break, against Gladbach on the weekend of January 9 ( GOAL, citing Bild ). The briefings beneath it are less tidy. Bild's Christian Falk wrote in October that Bayern would move only for a "perfect opportunity" that is good, available and affordable, and named a left winger to cover Luis Díaz as the most likely addition ( FussballTransfers ). A Bavarian Football Works piece this week says the club is quietly examining loans and early arrivals, without naming a source ( Yahoo Sports ). Certainty: low. Ngumoha joins the winger shortlist The one new name this week is Rio Ngumoha , Liverpool's 18-year-old winger. Bild reports Bayern are eyeing him as competition for Díaz, FourFourTwo relayed on Wednesday ( FourFourTwo ). Transfermarkt values him at 50 million euros. No bid, no talks and no comment from either club are reported. Context matters here: Bayern lost out on Bradley Barcola in the summer partly over PSG's price, and The Athletic reported he joined Liverpool for 106 million pounds plus add-ons. Certainty on Ngumoha: rumour, single-sourced to Bild. Olise: the extension that has gone quiet Bild reported on September 30 that Bayern were preparing a new contract for Michael Olise to 2032, with a substantial pay rise, replacing his current deal to 2029 ( Yahoo Sports/GFFN ). There has been no signing or announcement since, and no fresh development this week. Status: the club's intention is reported, not agreed. Ins and Outs In (this week) None. The window is shut until January. Out (this week) None. The Squad How Danks has rebuilt the side on the fly A winger at left-back, a full-back in the box and a teenager with something to prove. Aaron Danks has settled on a 4-2-3-1 that bends to the injury list. Davies has become a left winger in all but name, Laimer a right-back who arrives in the box, and Bischof the holding midfielder when Pavlović is unavailable. Danks made five changes for Madrid, recalling Neuer, Tah, Stanišić, Karl and Bischof ( Bundesliga.com ). Real Madrid play AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday at 9:45am Pacific; Güler and Tchouaméni were left out of the travelling squad. Three Chinese brands ended deals with Mbappé over a Mao Zedong remark; both the player and the club have apologised. The Lead Mourinho's Madrid take a six-game charge to Athens Three points off the top, perfect in Europe and ready to rotate, Real Madrid face AEK with a squad that has learned to win ugly as well as pretty. S ix straight wins, a Clásico taken at the Camp Nou and a clean sheet at El Sardinero: Real Madrid arrive in Athens looking more like a José Mourinho side every week. Sunday's 3-0 at Racing Santander ( ESPN report ) was not vintage, but it was controlled, and it kept Madrid three points behind leaders Barcelona after 11 league games. Wednesday's opponent, AEK Athens , sit 29th in the Champions League's league phase on three points; Madrid are fourth on nine, level with four other sides ( NBC Sports table ). On paper this is the softest European away trip of the autumn. Mourinho's squad list says he believes it, too: Arda Güler and Aurélien Tchouaméni stayed in Madrid ( official squad ). How the machine works The shape is a 4-2-3-1 on the team sheet ( ESPN lineup ) but the identity is in the midfield. Mourinho has moved Federico Valverde to right-back in recent weeks and handed the creative controls to Güler and Bernardo Silva, with Tchouaméni as the screen. Mourinho has called himself "not a stubborn coach" and credited the tweak ( LiveScore roundup ). The results since the change are striking: 4-1 against Sevilla, 4-1 against RB Leipzig, 2-1 in Barcelona and 3-0 at Racing. Against Racing, ESPN's numbers had Madrid on 22 shots to 10, seven on target to one, and 3.45 expected goals to 1.15. That is not a side scraping by. The Clásico was the proof of resilience. With Vinícius suspended and Courtois ill, Andriy Lunin started in goal and Kylian Mbappé scored twice, the second from Eduardo Camavinga's pass three minutes from time ( match report ). Courtois said afterwards that Lunin "won us El Clásico". "Que futbolistas de ataque hagan ese esfuerzo defensivo transmite un mensaje inmejorable a todo el vestuario." (Attacking players making that defensive effort sends the best possible message to the whole dressing room.) José Mourinho, after Racing 0-3 Real Madrid, via Récord The Diomande effect The other quiet revolution is on the left. Yan Diomande, the 19-year-old signed from Leipzig for a club-record fee in August ( Al Jazeera ), has kept Vinícius out of the conversation during his four-match league ban. Diomande has at least four goals, including the first-time strike into the top corner at Racing, and created Mbappé's opener at the Camp Nou. Vinícius is eligible again in Europe and travels to Athens, but he still has to serve the last game of his league ban at Valencia on Saturday ( Al Jazeera ). That gives Mourinho a selection headache he has clearly enjoyed creating: the most expensive teenager in the club's history against its vice-captain. Key facts Run: Six straight wins in all competitions; 9 wins and 2 defeats in La Liga. League: 3rd on 27 points, three behind Barcelona (30) and one behind Atlético (28). Europe: 4th in the league phase on 9 points from 3 wins; AEK are 29th on 3. Top scorer: Mbappé, 15 in all competitions by the Digest's count (12 in La Liga, per LaLiga). Out for Athens: Güler and Tchouaméni (rested), Rodrygo and Asencio (injured), Mendy (not registered). Kickoff: Wednesday 9:45am Pacific, Paramount+. Rotation, and a warning Mourinho was blunt on Sunday about the schedule. "Tchouaméni isn't playing on Wednesday. So he plays 90 minutes today," he said ( Yahoo Sports ), and he sarcastically thanked LaLiga for the "gift" of a Sunday game followed by a Saturday one ( Récord ). Madrid Universal expects three or four changes in Athens, with Camavinga, Dumfries, Carreras, Rüdiger, Endrick and Brahim in contention (single-sourced). The warning sign is defensive. Madrid conceded three in Rome and needed three corners in the last eight minutes to win 4-3 ( theScore ). AEK have lost four of their last five games in all competitions, but The Hard Tackle reports seven straight home wins with 30 goals scored and one conceded (single-sourced). A raucous Allwyn Arena is no place for a half-hearted second string. Mourinho is also asking for more than goals. "Attacking players making that defensive effort sends the best possible message to the whole dressing room," he said after Racing. If Madrid take three points in Athens, they will be on 12 with four games to play in the league phase, and well placed for a top-eight finish. The title race 1. Barcelona 30 pts, GD +34 2. Atlético Madrid 28 pts, GD +14 3. Real Madrid 27 pts, GD +18 Next for the top three: Real Madrid visit Valencia (19th) on Saturday. Secondary Feature The Mbappé meme that cost a market A throwaway line about Mao Zedong has cost Mbappé three Chinese sponsors, taken La Liga off Chinese state television and brought an apology from the club itself. It began with a meme. In a French podcast video, since taken down, Kylian Mbappé discussed an image that put his face on pictures of Mao Zedong and referred to "some guy, I think he's a Chinese dictator" ( Khaleej Times/AFP ). The reaction in China was swift. Drinks company Dongpeng and dairy firms Mengniu and Milkground ended their partnerships with the player, and CMG, which oversees state broadcaster CCTV, suspended La Liga broadcasts ( Kuwait Times/AFP ). Mbappé apologised. Real Madrid then issued its own statement, saying it "wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people" and "maintains a deep respect for China, its history, its culture and its citizens". China's foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said on October 28: "We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made." LaLiga apologised too ( Inside World Football ), and president Javier Tebas said on November 2 that he is talking to Chinese authorities "both in Madrid and in Beijing" and will wait ( El Informador ). Why it matters China is one of the club's biggest overseas fan bases and a key commercial market. On the pitch Mbappé has been unaffected: he scored twice in the Clásico and converted the penalty at Racing. Off it, he has lost three sponsors, and La Liga's presence on Chinese state television depends on how Beijing judges the apologies. Scouting the Next Opponent AEK Athens: loud at home, leaking in Europe Marko Nikolić's side have one Champions League win and a striker Madrid know well. AEK Athens are coached by Marko Nikolić and usually line up with two strikers; previews disagree on whether it is a 4-4-2 or a 4-1-3-2 ( Goal , The Hard Tackle ). Their European campaign so far reads 1-0 against LASK, 3-1 defeat at Shakhtar and a 5-1 loss to Manchester City: eight conceded in two games. Domestic form has dipped. They lost 3-1 to PAOK in the cup and 2-0 to Panathinaikos in the league, their first league defeat of the season, before beating Panetolikos 5-0. At home, though, The Hard Tackle reports seven straight wins (single-sourced). Who to stop Barnabás Varga is the top scorer with nine goals in 13 games ( Sports Mole ). Alongside him is Luka Jović , Madrid's former striker, with seven in 15. Lovro Majer is the creator between the lines and João Mário provides the running from midfield. Goalkeeper Thomas Strakosha is out with a hand injury, so Brignoli is expected to start; João Mário and Lazaros Rota are doubtful with illness. The vulnerability is obvious: a two-striker side that has shipped eight goals in two European games should leave space for Mbappé and Diomande to run into. Transfer News JJ Gabriel edges closer as Madrid shut the January door No senior signings planned this winter, a 16-year-old prodigy in the pipeline and a Liverpool approach for Trent that Fabrizio Romano says never really happened. JJ Gabriel: advanced talks, not yet official Real Madrid are pushing to sign JJ Gabriel , the 16-year-old Manchester United academy forward ( profile ). Fabrizio Romano reported on October 14 that Madrid had made direct contact with United ( via CaughtOffside ). Barcelona daily Sport reported that Madrid accepted the terms set by the player's camp, a package reported at €10m or more over three years ( Football365 ), and on November 1 that Gabriel had turned down an improved PSG offer ( Football365 ). TEAMtalk says Madrid are confident of a January deal but that "important discussions remain", with Barcelona, Bayern and Dortmund still circling ( TEAMtalk ). Certainty: advanced talks, with reported agreement on personal terms. Nothing is signed and United have not agreed a deal. No January signings, and an Endrick question AS reported over the weekend that the board plans no January signings, trusting the squad after the Clásico win and Bernardo Silva's form ( Goal México, citing AS ). Any departure would need both the player's request and Mourinho's approval, which AS calls unlikely. The one name that could test that is Endrick , who has made only one league start this season. TEAMtalk reports Arsenal want a loan with an option to buy, while Milan and Roma offer straight loans ( TEAMtalk exclusive , single-sourced for Arsenal). Matteo Moretto has also linked Roma. Madrid prefer a straight loan if he goes at all, and Mourinho wants him to stay. Certainty: concrete interest from other clubs. Trent: a Liverpool loan story denied Cadena SER reported on October 29 that Liverpool had asked about taking Trent Alexander-Arnold back on loan. Romano said on November 2 that Liverpool "never started any kind of concrete or serious conversation" and that player and club are aligned on him staying at least to the end of the season ( Football365 ). Certainty: rumour, denied. Planning for 2027 The longer view is a defensive midfielder and a centre-back to replace Antonio Rüdiger, whose one-year extension runs to June 2027 ( El Español ). Rodri chose Barcelona in August, and ESPN's Rodra says Mourinho wanted a more physical profile anyway ( Defensa Central ). Romano has said a midfielder is wanted in 2027, most likely in the summer. AS adds that no decision on buy-back options for Jacobo Ramón, Nico Paz, Rafa Marín or Víctor Muñoz will be made until spring ( ESPN ). Moretto says Ramón could return for about €8m to €9m ( Defensa Central ); Como confirmed in June that Paz stays this season with Madrid retaining an option ( Goal ). x: STOPPAGE TIME The Weekly Barcelona Digest Every Barça story, every week: first team, La Masia, Femení Weekly edition · Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Season tracker LaLiga: 1st, 30 pts, 2 clear of Atlético Last ten competitive results, oldest to newest: W 5-1 FEY W 4-2 LEV W 7-2 RAC W 3-1 SEV W 3-0 GET W 4-1 GAL W 5-2 BET L 2-4 PSG L 1-2 RMA W 6-1 ALA Next: Aston Villa (H), UCL, today 12:00 PM PT Next match Opponent: Aston Villa Competition: UEFA Champions League, league phase, matchday 4 Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Kickoff: 12:00 PM Pacific (21:00 CET) Venue: Home: Spotify Camp Nou, Barcelona Watch in the US: Paramount+ (as listed on FC Barcelona's official where-to-watch page; TUDN also listed) In this edition The Lead · Player Ratings · Scouting · Transfer News · The Squad · La Masia · Femení · Players Away · Numbers · In Brief · What to Watch If you read nothing else Barça host Aston Villa in the Champions League tonight at 12:00 PM PT, sitting 8th on 6 points while Villa are 2nd on 9. Sunday's trip to Atlético is first against second: Barça lead LaLiga on 30 points, two ahead of Simeone's side. Flick has confirmed a centre-back is wanted after four defenders went down, with Lisandro Martínez and Natan the most concrete names. The Lead Villa at the Camp Nou: a patched-up Barça defence meets Europe's form side Four defenders are out, the top eight is the target, and Unai Emery arrives unbeaten in the Champions League. Here is how tonight is likely to be decided. T wo weeks ago Barcelona were a team that could not stop winning. Eleven straight victories in all competitions ended in Paris, where PSG won 4-2, and then Kylian Mbappé scored twice in a 2-1 Clásico defeat at the Camp Nou. Saturday's 6-1 rout of Alavés steadied the ship. Tonight's visit of Aston Villa tells us whether it is properly back on course. The table explains the urgency. Barça are 8th in the Champions League league phase on 6 points, the last automatic place in the round of 16, according to NBC Sports' standings . Villa are 2nd on 9 points, level with leaders PSG, having won all three of their games with 12 goals scored and 3 conceded. Hansi Flick did not hide the target. "We want to be among the top eight," he said on Monday, in remarks carried by the club . He also refused to read too much into the two defeats: "Against Real Madrid the result could have been different, and the same against PSG. I think we played at the same level." The back four problem The hardest question is in defence. Jules Koundé , Eric García , Andreas Christensen and Xavi Espart are all out, with Dani Olmo and Roony Bardghji also unavailable. "We've got four players out in defence, quality players, and it's not easy to manage that," Flick said, as reported by Barça Universal . Against Alavés the answer was improvisation. Frenkie de Jong played at centre-back beside Pau Cubarsí, and the academy midfielder Brian Fariñas made his debut at right-back. Flick said Fariñas "is an option for tomorrow, but there are others", and that Gerard Martín "can play as a centre-back or a left-back". “We can make history. To win La Liga and the Champions League.” Hansi Flick, Monday's press conference Heavy's projected line-up has Gerard Martín alongside Cubarsí, with João Cancelo at right-back and Alejandro Balde at left-back, behind a 4-2-3-1 built on Rodri and Pedri. That is a projection, not a confirmed team, and Flick's weekend choices suggest Fariñas and De Jong remain live options. Jackson against the high line Villa's danger man is Nicolas Jackson , who has 8 goals in his first 12 games for the club, 3 of them in this competition, per the club's preview . He scored both goals when Villa ended Manchester City's perfect start 2-1 on October 24. Flick: "Jackson is performing at an incredible level." That matters because Barça defend high, and whichever centre-back pairing Flick picks will be a makeshift one. Jackson's runs in behind will test Cubarsí's reading of the game and his partner's pace. One misjudged step and Villa have exactly the counter-attacking weapon to punish it. The flip side is Villa's own record on the road. They have conceded 8 goals in their last five away games, according to Goal's results page , including three at Bournemouth in the Carabao Cup last week. They are 10th in the Premier League on 12 points. Barça have scored 46 times in 11 league games. Where the game is won On Barça's right, Lamine Yamal is likely to meet Ian Maatsen , who starts at left-back in Heavy's projected Villa XI. Yamal has 13 Champions League goals, level with Mbappé's record for goals in the competition before turning 20, per Heavy . One more tonight would make the record his alone. In midfield, Rodri and Pedri face Boubacar Kamara and João Gomes , with John McGinn and Emiliano Buendía drifting inside. Unai Emery usually sets up 4-2-3-1 but shifts shape to the opponent. He is without Amadou Onana, Matteo Ruggeri and Aaron Wan-Bissaka. There is a personal angle too. Anthony Gordon , signed from Newcastle in the summer, faces Premier League opposition tonight and told Mundo Deportivo that competing for every trophy is "good pressure". He scored his second league goal for the club on Saturday, a chipped finish off the bench. The verdict: a win would lift Barça to 9 points and keep the top-eight target firmly in their hands before the trip to Baku on November 25. A defeat, with Atlético away on Sunday, would turn a bad fortnight into a genuine wobble. Key Facts: Barça v Aston Villa Kickoff: 12:00 PM PT (21:00 CET), Spotify Camp Nou US TV: Paramount+ Barça: 8th in the league phase, 6 points (W2 L1, 11 scored, 6 conceded) Villa: 2nd, 9 points (W3, 12 scored, 3 conceded) Out for Barça: Koundé, Eric García, Christensen, Espart, Olmo, Bardghji Out for Villa: Onana, Ruggeri, Wan-Bissaka Head-to-head: Barça won the 1977-78 UEFA Cup quarter-final 4-3 on aggregate; Villa won the 1982 Super Cup 3-1 on aggregate Then the Metropolitano: first against second Sunday's league trip to Atlético could hand Simeone an all-time record or give Barça a five-point cushion. Win or lose tonight, the week's second test is bigger domestically. Barcelona go to Atlético Madrid on Sunday, November 8, at 12:00 PM PT (21:00 CET), leading LaLiga on 30 points to Atlético's 28, with Real Madrid on 27, per Goal's table . Atlético have won seven league games in a row and have the best defence in the division, 8 goals conceded. Their latest was a 2-0 win at Levante on Saturday, through Álex Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone , although beIN Sports noted Atlético's xG was just 0.58 to Levante's 1.25. Diego Simeone sits on 344 LaLiga wins, level with Luis Aragonés for the all-time record, according to Yahoo Sports . Beating Barça would make the record his. Grimaldo has 4 goals and 2 assists, the most goal contributions of any LaLiga defender, and Álex Baena has 5 goals and 3 assists. Recent history is mixed. Atlético won 4-0 in last season's Copa del Rey semi-final first leg and knocked Barça out of the Champions League quarter-finals 3-2 on aggregate in April. Barça won both league meetings, 3-1 at home and 2-1 at the Metropolitano, per Sports Mole . Player Ratings Barça 6-1 Alavés: Fermín runs the show LaLiga matchday 11, Saturday, October 31, Spotify Camp Nou. The only first-team match in the last seven days. Barcelona had 77 per cent of the ball, completed 771 passes at 93 per cent and created 3.19 expected goals to Alavés's 0.62, per ESPN . Raphinha scored twice, Lamine Yamal twice, Fermín López once and Anthony Gordon once; Mariano Díaz replied late for Alavés. The club's match report says the result was Flick's 100th win as Barça coach and ended a two-game losing run. The goals came at 8, 23, 41, 45+1, 64 and 81 minutes. Pedri and Cancelo were booked, per FutbolFantasy . The Digest's own ratings, informed by the club, ESPN, FutbolFantasy and ElDesmarque reports. Starters plus substitutes with at least 10 minutes. Scouting the Next Opponent Aston Villa: perfect in Europe, patchy in England Emery's side have won all three European games but have wobbled domestically. Aston Villa have beaten Club Brugge 3-2 away, Fenerbahçe 6-0 and Viking 3-1 in this season's Champions League. Domestically they are 10th in the Premier League on 12 points, after a start that included a 4-0 defeat at Brighton, per Goal . Their last five: a 1-1 draw with Fulham on Saturday, a 3-0 Carabao Cup defeat at Bournemouth, a 2-1 win over Manchester City, the 3-1 win over Viking and a 1-0 win at Newcastle. Unai Emery usually plays 4-2-3-1 and adapts it to the opponent. The three to stop: Nicolas Jackson (8 goals in 12 games for Villa), Ross Barkley (3 Champions League goals) and Emiliano Buendía (2). Pau Torres and Victor Lindelöf are expected at centre-back. Johan Manzambi, a reported Barcelona target, is likely in the attacking midfield line. Vulnerabilities: eight goals conceded in their last five away games, with over 2.5 goals in four of them, per Goal . That is the opening for a Barça attack averaging more than four league goals a game. The two clubs have not met in a competitive match for more than four decades. Whether it can afford to act in January is another matter. The clearest signal came from the coach. Asked about a centre-back on October 30, Hansi Flick said the subject had been discussed with Deco and Bojan : "Si podemos, quizá lo haremos" ("If we can, maybe we will"), per Mundo Deportivo as relayed by Fichajes.net . Mundo Deportivo has reported that Barcelona 's technical committee agrees a centre-back should be signed, in January or in the summer, and has a four-man shortlist, as summarised by Sports Mole . Certainty: concrete interest, with no bid reported. Lisandro Martínez: the cheap-if-possible option Lisandro Martínez of Manchester United is the most concrete name. Sport reported the interest on November 1 and 2, and The Athletic's Laurie Whitwell has described it as genuine but price-dependent, per Goal . His deal runs to June 2027, with United holding a one-year option. That contract is the whole story. Barça will only move in January if the fee is small; otherwise they could wait and approach him as a free agent next summer. Mundo Deportivo said talks with his agents would begin in the first half of November. Atlético are also watching. Status: concrete interest. Natan: Betis say not now Spanish reports put Natan of Real Betis on Barça's list at around €30 million plus add-ons. Betis do not want to sell mid-season and value him at a minimum of €35 million, up to €40 million with add-ons, per Fichajes.net . His release clause is €80 million and his contract runs to 2030. Status: concrete interest. The bigger names, and the money Alessandro Bastoni of Inter was linked by Mundo Deportivo, but Italian outlet TMW says a mid-season exit is hard to imagine. Joško Gvardiol has been called a "dream" target, per The Hard Tackle , realistic only in 2027. Both are rumours. The money is tight. LaLiga set Barça's squad-cost limit at €582.76 million in September and says the club is inside the 1:1 rule, per EFE . But summer arrivals cost roughly what departures freed, and treasurer Ferran Olivé has said sales are needed before any winter signing, per Crónica Global . Balde: a January exit is now a real possibility The left-back has fallen behind Cancelo, and Premier League clubs are circling. Alejandro Balde has lost his place to João Cancelo. Fabrizio Romano reported that a January move is a "strong possibility" if a good offer arrives and that the decision rests with the player, per TEAMtalk , which names Manchester United, Liverpool and AC Milan as interested clubs. Spanish reports put Barça's asking price at €40 million to €45 million or more, per Fichajes.net ; that figure is not confirmed by the club. A swap involving Lisandro Martínez has been floated in the press. Status: concrete interest. Flick was protective on Monday. "When you don't play often, you lack confidence. João Cancelo is in great form. I'll help him regain his confidence," he said, calling Balde "a great person and a hard worker". Araújo at Liverpool: what exactly is the deal? Reports disagree on whether Liverpool hold an option to buy. Ronald Araújo joined Liverpool on loan on August 10. ESPN reported a €55 million option to make it permanent; Romano later said there is no buy option at all, per Barça Universal . The Digest cannot resolve the conflict. The Lead Bayern come to the Metropolitano with Atlético's midfield stretched thin No Romero, no Hjulmand, no Cardoso, a captain back from five games out and the reigning Ballon d'Or winner arriving. Then Barcelona on Sunday. Simeone's strangest strength this autumn has been a defence that barely concedes; this week tests whether it survives a depleted spine. T here are weeks that shape a season and weeks that merely fill one. This is the first kind. Atlético host Bayern Munich at the Metropolitano on Tuesday night in the Champions League, then welcome Barcelona on Sunday with first place in La Liga available to whoever wins. Two home games in five days, against two of the most powerful clubs in Europe. Diego Simeone arrives at it on a seven-game winning run in the league and with the thinnest midfield he has had all autumn. The squad list confirmed on Tuesday morning had no Cristian Romero , no Morten Hjulmand and no Johnny Cardoso . Captain Koke is back after five matches out with a muscle injury. That is the story of the night before a ball is kicked. ( beIN Sports , ABC Color ) Who plays in the middle Hjulmand serves a suspension for the straight red card he took at Stuttgart, a studs-up challenge on Angelo Stiller that Simeone himself called fair. Cardoso has a low-grade thigh problem and misses a third straight game. That leaves Pablo Barrios , whose workload the staff are managing carefully, plus Koke, Rodrigo Mendoza and Obed Vargas . ( SportsAdda , El Gol Digital ) Forbes' preview expects a 4-2-3-1 with Barrios and Koke as the pivot behind Giuliano Simeone, Kang-in Lee and Alex Baena, and Julián Álvarez up front. World Soccer Talk projects a flatter 4-4-2 with Mendoza beside Barrios. Either way, the central pairing is the least experienced or least fit combination Simeone has fielded in a big European night this season. ( Forbes , World Soccer Talk ) At centre-back the question is simpler. Romero was on the bench at Levante without playing, then did not train on Sunday or Monday. Marc Pubill , who has partnered David Hancko through Romero's adductor injury, should start again. The pair kept a clean sheet in Valencia, and Pubill's form has been one of the quieter good news stories of October. “We're playing at home, and that's where we're strong.” Diego Simeone, before Bayern (as quoted in FC Bayern's preview) The matchup Bayern will have the ball. They lead the Bundesliga on goal difference and have scored ten goals in three Champions League games. But they have also drawn their last two in Europe, 3-3 at Viking and 2-2 at home to Arsenal, conceding five. Without Jamal Musiala , Luis Díaz , Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari , and with Vincent Kompany ill, they are not at full strength either. ( FC Bayern ) Atlético's case rests on the numbers since the September defeat at Liverpool: nine games unbeaten, three goals conceded, six clean sheets. Simeone's side are compact without the ball and quick to break, and Harry Kane said as much on Monday: "We know how dangerous they are in attack and on the counter-attack." The key battle is Kane dropping between the lines against whichever pivot Simeone trusts. There is one warning sign. At Levante, Atlético allowed 20 shots, 14 from inside the box, and lost the expected-goals count 1.33 to 0.63. Jan Oblak saved all four on target. A side with Kane and Kimmich will not be as wasteful as Levante, who put only four of 20 shots on target. ( SNA ) The stakes Atlético sit 16th of 36 on four points, a point behind 14th-placed Bayern; the top eight skip the play-off round. After Bayern come Viking, PSV, Bodø/Glimt and Fenerbahçe, a run that looks kinder on paper. Win on Tuesday and the top eight becomes a realistic target. Lose, and the margin for error in the last four rounds disappears. History helps: Bayern have never won a competitive game at Atlético's home, and Atlético are unbeaten in 16 home European games against German sides. ( Infobae , FC Bayern ) Key Facts Atlético in Europe: L 1-2 at Liverpool, W 2-0 v Manchester United, D 1-1 at Stuttgart. 4 points, 16th. Bayern in Europe: W 5-0 v Bodø/Glimt, D 3-3 at Viking, D 2-2 v Arsenal. 5 points, 14th. Unavailable for Atlético: Romero (not fit), Hjulmand (suspended), Cardoso (thigh). Unavailable for Bayern: Musiala, Díaz, Gnabry, Saibari, Ndiaye. Neuer and Olise checked on matchday. Head-to-head in Madrid: Atlético 1-0 (2015-16), 1-0 (2016-17), 1-1 (2020-21). Last nine games: 8 wins, 1 draw, 3 goals conceded, 6 clean sheets. Sunday's summit: win and Atlético go top Barcelona arrive with 30 points and the league's top scorer. Simeone arrives one win from owning the La Liga record outright. Atlético are second on 28 points after 11 games, two behind Barcelona and one ahead of Real Madrid . The two leaders meet at the Metropolitano on Sunday, November 8, at 21:00 in Madrid, which is 12:00 p.m. Pacific. A home win would put Atlético top. Atlético's best league scorer is Alex Baena with five. The contrast is plain: Barcelona win by scoring, Atlético by not conceding. Atlético have conceded eight league goals in eleven games. Saturday's win made Diego Simeone the joint holder of La Liga's record for wins by a coach, 344, level with Luis Aragonés, who needed 192 more matches to get there. Simeone has done it all with one club. "Without that moment we would not have got here," he said of the backing he received from chief executive Miguel Ángel Gil Marín. Win on Sunday and the record is his alone. ( Diario Río Negro ) Hjulmand's ban is a UEFA one, so he should be available again on Sunday. Romero and Cardoso are the two to watch in Thursday and Friday training. Bayern Munich top the Bundesliga on goal difference, level on 18 points with Dortmund after eight games. Saturday's 2-2 draw with Dortmund was typical of their recent games: dominant, then careless. Konrad Laimer (37') and Dayot Upamecano (66', from close range after Kane's knock-down) scored, but Guirassy equalised and Fabio Silva struck late after Bayern failed to clear a corner. Bayern conceded three at Viking and two at home to Arsenal, and Dortmund's equaliser came from a corner. Atlético are at their best in exactly those moments. William Saliba is back in full training and in the squad at Slavia Prague after three months out; Bukayo Saka's thigh injury still has no return date. Mikel Arteta says a new Declan Rice contract is "a matter of time," with reports putting the deal at £350,000 a week. The Lead Fourteen Years, One Goal, And A Defensive Masterclass At Anfield Arsenal did not out-play Liverpool on Sunday. They out-organised them, and in the process they took the league lead and confirmed the identity that will decide their season. T he goal that ended fourteen years of waiting was not a work of art. Arsenal pressed the ball high, Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker misplaced a pass to Jérémy Jacquet , and the ball squirted loose. Noni Madueke and Declan Rice worked it down the right, Rice overlapped and drove a low cross through the six-yard box, and Kai Havertz tapped it in at the far post. Sixteen minutes gone. It was the only goal Arsenal needed, and the only goal they got. The bare facts undersell what followed. Mikel Arteta 's side had not won a league match at Anfield since 2012. They had lost a League Cup tie at League Two Fleetwood Town four days earlier, on penalties, with a sixteen-year-old sent off in the closing minutes. The response was a performance of almost pathological discipline: 74 minutes of a compact back four, a shrinking pitch, and a Liverpool side that finished the match without registering a single shot on target. Liverpool had 56 per cent of the ball and 17 shots to Arsenal's 10. The expected-goals numbers were almost level, 1.05 to 0.98. The number that matters is 52 against 24: touches in the opposition box, Liverpool's figure double Arsenal's. The hosts got into the area constantly and found nothing there. Florian Wirtz struck the crossbar from a free-kick. Alexis Mac Allister headed over. David Raya did not make a save of consequence until he held Víctor Muñoz 's late header. The back four is the project now Five goals conceded in nine Premier League matches is the best record in the division. Two conceded in three Champions League games is jointly the best in that competition. Arsenal have done this without William Saliba , who has not played for the club since the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May. Ezri Konsa , the £55m summer signing from Aston Villa , has instead formed a partnership with Gabriel Magalhães that Arteta has had no reason to break up. On Sunday that pair were flanked by Jurriën Timber and Riccardo Calafiori , with Rice and Bruno Guimarães screening in front. Arteta was candid afterwards that this was not the plan. Liverpool's verticality, he said, forced Arsenal into defending far more than they wanted, and he admitted "we had an element of luck as well." "I don't think there is a better team in world football that defends quite like Arsenal defend." Alan Shearer, on Match of the Day Havertz keeps answering the question Havertz's finish was his 46th Premier League goal, which took him past Ilkay Gündogan as the competition's highest-scoring German. It is the kind of record that tends to be filed under trivia, but it speaks to something Arsenal have relied on heavily this autumn. With Saka injured and Viktor Gyökeres yet to start a league game, Havertz has led the line in all nine Premier League matches and is the club's joint-top scorer. Around him, the summer rebuild is bedding in at different speeds. Rice now has four league assists, more than any Arsenal player. Christos Tzolis , back from a hamstring problem, drew Alisson's best save of the afternoon with a first-time shot. Bruno Guimarães, the £75m arrival from Newcastle United , curled an effort just wide and otherwise did the unglamorous work of holding the middle of the pitch for 62 minutes. What it was worth Arsenal arrived at Anfield level on points with Manchester City. They left three clear, because City lost to Brighton & Hove Albion the same day. Twenty-four points after nine games is a total Arsenal have bettered at this stage only twice in Premier League history, in 2004/05 and 2007/08. Arteta, asked about the title, said what managers say: "it's too early." He then named the thing actually in front of him, "another big, big, big fight in Prague." There is a case that this was the single most instructive 90 minutes of Arsenal's season. Last year's title was won on control. Sunday was won on something harder to coach and easier to lose: the willingness of eleven players to defend a one-goal lead at Anfield for 74 minutes without panicking. Gary Neville called it "a defensive masterclass." Theo Walcott , watching, said the quiet part out loud: "They are going to be difficult to stop this year." The caveats are real. Arsenal were fortunate that VAR did not look again at Alexander Isak 's shirt being tugged by Timber in the first half, an incident Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said would have been a penalty "100 per cent" had Isak gone down. Rice's own verdict on the Anfield atmosphere, "It's nothing I've ever seen before," hints at how close it ran. But the table does not record hints. Saliba Walks Back Into A Side That Learned To Live Without Him After a three-month absence, the centre-back is back in training and in the squad in Prague. Arteta's problem is now a pleasant one. William Saliba has not played for Arsenal since they lost the Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties in May. A back problem he had been managing late last season worsened at the World Cup, where he was substituted in France 's semi-final defeat to Spain . On Tuesday, Mikel Arteta confirmed he had completed full first-team training and travelled to Prague. "He played 45 minutes in closed door last week, and he feels ready to go," Arteta said. "He's in a really good place." Pressed on whether he would actually use him, the manager was deliberately non-committal: "Whether we use him or not is now a matter of what the team needs." That line matters, because the team does not obviously need him. Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhães have conceded five league goals between them. What Arsenal need is bodies: ten matches are scheduled between the coming international break and the end of the year, including Manchester City on November 29, Tottenham Hotspur on December 6 and Real Madrid in the Champions League on December 9. Arteta framed the return in exactly those terms. "He's built the capacity that we needed, and now it's about giving him minutes," he said, noting that "a centre-back normally has to be able to play 90 minutes." The useful detail is positional flexibility: Konsa can fill in at either full-back, and Saliba has played on both sides of a back four for club and country. Four senior centre-backs for ten games in eight weeks is not a luxury. It is the minimum. Transfer News Rice Is About To Become The Best-Paid Player In Arsenal's History Arteta says a new deal is "a matter of time." The reported figure is £350,000 a week, and the timing is not accidental. The most consequential piece of Arsenal business this winter may not involve a signing at all. Declan Rice is in the final two years of the contract he signed on joining from West Ham United in 2023, and Mikel Arteta used his pre-Liverpool press conference to confirm that an extension is coming. "Yes, my feeling is that he is very happy here," Arteta said when asked whether he expected an agreement. "Every conversation I have with him, he wants to continue here for the long term. It will be a matter of time when we resolve that." The numbers, with the usual caution Rice's current deal runs to the summer of 2028, with a reported club option for a further twelve months. He is one of nine Arsenal players whose contracts expire that summer. Capology estimates his present salary at around £260,000 a week. The new terms being reported are £350,000 a week, which would move him past Bukayo Saka , on a reported £300,000, as the club's highest earner. Two caveats are worth holding on to. First, the only wage figures in the public domain are estimates and reports, not confirmed terms. Second, the £350,000 benchmark has been reached at Arsenal before, by Mesut Özil and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang , and in both cases the headline number reportedly included performance add-ons. Certainty tier: advanced talks. Fabrizio Romano reported in October that Arsenal were closing in; Arteta has now effectively confirmed the direction. Nothing is signed. Why it is the right player to pay Rice has started all nine Premier League games and leads the squad with four league assists, including the cross for Kai Havertz 's winner at Anfield. Jamie Carragher described him as "world class" after Sunday's match. For a club whose defensive record is now its main competitive asset, paying a record wage to the player who anchors the midfield in front of that defence is an easier sell than most record wages are. Sources: Arseblog News , Sports Mole . Gyökeres Has Not Started A League Game, And His Camp Has Noticed Last season's 21-goal striker is a substitute in the title race he helped win. January is the obvious pressure point. Viktor Gyökeres scored 21 goals in all competitions last season as Arsenal won the league. This season he has not started a single Premier League match. Kai Havertz has played all nine as the centre-forward, and Gyökeres has come off the bench, including for the final six minutes plus stoppage time at Anfield. TEAMtalk reported in mid-October that the Swede is prepared to push for a move in January, with his frustration centred specifically on the absence of league starts rather than on his overall minutes. Atlético Madrid are described as retaining their interest, with unnamed clubs in Italy, Germany and the Premier League monitoring. Certainty tier: concrete interest, with no bid reported and no fee in the public domain. This is a single-sourced report at origin, picked up widely since. The complicating factor Arsenal's own reported interest in Atlético's Julián Álvarez has, according to the same reporting, hardened doubts in Gyökeres's camp about his long-term role. That is the sort of circular transfer logic that often precedes nothing at all. It is also exactly the kind of signal worth logging in early November, because it is the shape a January saga takes before it becomes one. The counter-argument is simple arithmetic. Arsenal have ten fixtures between the international break and New Year's Day, Saka has no return date, and Havertz has started every league game. Selling a proven 21-goal striker in the middle of that run would require a replacement Arsenal are not obviously positioned to buy. Gyökeres did start the Fleetwood tie, and scored. Sources: CaughtOffside , reporting TEAMtalk; ESPN . The January Attacker Question, And What Arsenal Can Actually Afford David Ornstein's read is that Arsenal left themselves room in the summer. The financial trackers suggest the room is real but not unlimited. The structural case for an Arsenal forward signing in January was made in the summer, by omission. Gabriel Martinelli left for Al Hilal and was not replaced. Gabriel Jesus joined Barcelona and was not replaced. Christos Tzolis arrived from Club Brugge , but principally as cover for the departed Leandro Trossard . Ethan Nwaneri went to Borussia Dortmund on loan, with a recall option written in. David Ornstein , in an Athletic question-and-answer session, put it this way: Arsenal "have given themselves the opportunity to" sign an attacker, and "I could see something happening because they wanted to." He also said he knew of nothing "brewing," and that on current evidence the squad "doesn't look like they need it." His stated condition was blunt: "the key for them is to keep people fit." The financial ceiling Ornstein's note of caution was that Arsenal are "close to UEFA's financial rules" and "have got to be very careful on the financial side of things." The independent Bean Counter tracker, whose figures are estimates rather than official numbers, puts Arsenal's UEFA squad-cost ratio for calendar 2026 at 58.4 per cent against the 70 per cent limit, which it reads as roughly £95.8m a year of squad-cost headroom after the Martinelli sale. On Premier League PSR it estimates Arsenal have used close to none of the £105m three-year loss allowance, with the final assessment due in January 2027. In plain terms: the constraint on a January signing is not a hard ceiling. It is the recurring annual wage bill, which is the number squad-cost ratios actually measure, and which a record Rice contract will push upward. That is the trade-off Arsenal are managing, and it is why "we could, if we wanted to" is a more accurate summary of the position than "we will." Scouting the Next Opponent Slavia Prague: Champions At Home, Cursed In Europe One win in 23 Champions League matches, and the record for the longest winless run is now within reach. Arsenal arrive on Wednesday. Slavia Prague are the most comfortable team in Czech football and the least comfortable in this competition. They lead the Czech First League by seven points, having won their last two domestic matches. In the Champions League they have one point from three games and sit 32nd of 36. The longer record is stranger still. Slavia have won one of their 23 Champions League matches, a debut victory over Steaua Bucharest in September 2007. Since then: eight draws and 14 defeats across four campaigns. AEK Athens hold the competition record of 24 games without a win, set between 1992 and 2006. Slavia's current run is 22, so two more without a victory would match it. Jindřich Trpišovský has managed the club since 2017 and was candid about what the streak does to him. The longer it runs, he said, "the more unpleasant it is," and he admitted he broods over it more than he used to. His assessment of Wednesday was unsentimental: everything would need to go Slavia's way, and the team must give 100 per cent to have a chance. Who Arsenal must stop, and where Slavia leak The principal attacking threat is David Moses . Behind him, defender David Zima has set the tone publicly, calling the competition "a football university" and arguing the team cannot stress about needing a result now. Tomáš Chorý is not expected to play for the club again. Lukáš Provod and Ange N'Guessan are doubts, and Ivan Schranz is recovering from a long illness. Previews put Slavia's absentees at five first-team regulars through injury or suspension. The vulnerability is straightforward: Slavia have conceded seven goals in three European games. They were reduced to ten men against Lens and led 2-1 in the 89th minute before losing 3-2. They then lost 2-0 at Sabah in Baku, a result Vladimír Šmicer , the former Slavia striker and 2005 Champions League winner, singled out as the real failure. Losing to Arsenal and Bayern Munich , Šmicer argued, is not the problem. Losing in Baku is. The head-to-head offers Slavia nothing. Arsenal won 3-0 in Prague in last season's league phase and 7-0 in London in 2007, a result that remains among Arsenal's largest European wins. Slavia have not beaten them. The one genuine risk is the one Mikel Arteta named himself: a trip to Prague four days after Anfield, with rotation likely, against a side with a record to break and a crowd that will treat it as a final. Slavia Prague, at a glance Manager: Jindřich Trpišovský, in charge since 2017 Domestic: top of the Czech First League, seven points clear Champions League: 32nd of 36, one point from three games, goal difference minus three League-phase results: lost 3-2 at home to Lens, lost 2-0 at Sabah, drew 2-2 at Fenerbahçe European record: one win in 23 Champions League matches Out or doubtful: Tomáš Chorý (not expected to play for the club again), Lukáš Provod, Ange N'Guessan, Ivan Schranz Key man: David Moses Head-to-head: Arsenal have won every meeting, including 3-0 in Prague last season and 7-0 in London in 2007 Sources: Reuters via Malay Mail , Sports Mole , NBC Sports . The Saka problem has no timeline Bukayo Saka picked up a thigh injury in the Champions League draw at Bayern Munich on October 21. Arsenal have never graded it publicly. A second MRI was required two days later because of fluid around the injury, and Mikel Arteta described the signs then as "not good." By October 30 the manager said Saka was "feeling much better than he was a few days ago," but had not been cleared, and that a further scan was needed to see how the fluid was resolving and whether the tendon was involved. "Afterwards we'll know more about it," he said. As of this edition, no result and no return date have been published. One injury tracker places a possible return at the Brentford game on December 2. Asked whether Saka would miss England's November internationals, Arteta said: "Looks like it, but we'll have to wait and see next week." Saka has three goals in seven league appearances this season and remains the squad's only genuine right-sided specialist, which is why Noni Madueke has started the last two matches there. Arsenal Women Seventh, Twelve Points Back, And Conceding To The First Shot Again Arsenal are flying in Europe and sinking in the league. The gap between those two things is now the whole story of Renée Slegers' season. Another late rescue, another two points dropped Arsenal drew 1-1 with Aston Villa at the Emirates on Sunday. Lucia Kendall released Chasity Grant on 25 minutes, Grant's shot deflected off Steph Catley and looped over Misa Rodríguez , and that was Villa's only shot of the match. Alessia Russo headed in Stina Blackstenius ' cross off the left post on 85 minutes. It was the second consecutive Women's Super League match in which Arsenal conceded from the opponent's first shot. They are seventh with 10 points, twelve behind leaders Chelsea , and have won one of their last five league games. Arsenal have now trailed 1-0 in three consecutive home league games for the first time since 2015. The diagnosis is no longer about the low block Arsenal dominated the ball and the shot count against Villa and created almost nothing of quality. Tim Stillman's analysis described a "horseshoe" attacking shape around a deep defence: volume without incision. Opta logged one big chance from a high shot count, a ratio that has become the season's signature. Daily Cannon's tactical read found the more alarming pattern at the other end. In three of Arsenal's four home games, the opposition have had one shot on target and scored from it. The Villa goal came from a long pass over a six-player press, a quick switch wide, and a simple pass that left defenders isolated one against one. The selection question, and the manager Renée Slegers had built new partnerships before the October international break: Taylor Hinds and Caitlin Foord left, Riola Reuteler and Ona Batlle right, Russo behind Olivia Smith . A double half-time substitution broke them up, removing Hinds and Reuteler, the two players who had only recently begun earning minutes. Blackstenius did not come on until the 82nd minute. Stillman's conclusion is the sharpest thing written about Arsenal Women this season: managers reveal who they trust under pressure, and Slegers' circle of trust is shrinking even as her squad grows. Victoria Pelova is in limited-trust limbo. Batlle, signed largely as a left-back, had not played there since the Birmingham game. Slegers was visibly frustrated at the final whistle, which is out of character. Daily Cannon suggests a decision on the manager could come around the end of November, during the international break. Jurriën Timber pulled Alexander Isak 's shirt in the first half and VAR did not intervene. Andoni Iraola said it would have been given "100 per cent" had Isak gone down. Virgil van Dijk 's verdict was more resigned: "In the end, it wasn't given and we lose the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal." No major Emirates expansion. Following an Advisory Board meeting attended by co-chair Josh Kroenke and chief executive Richard Garlick , Arsenal confirmed in early October that they will pursue "continued evolution of Emirates Stadium" rather than a large-scale rebuild. Current capacity is 60,704. A working group had reportedly examined an increase toward 80,000, which would have required moving home games during construction. Safe standing, in phases. The Clock End gets safe standing this season and the North Bank in 2027/28. Arsenal have said neither will increase capacity. Legends Global became official caterer for 2026/27 under a new "1886 by Arsenal" food and beverage identity. The financial position, per the trackers. Independent estimates put Arsenal's UEFA squad-cost ratio at 58.4 per cent against a 70 per cent limit, with roughly £95.8m a year of headroom, and close to zero of the £105m Premier League PSR allowance used. These are estimates, not club figures, and the final PSR assessment falls in January 2027. Bayern are watching Ødegaard. Sky Germany reported that Bayern Munich have kept contact with the Arsenal captain's representatives. Martin Ødegaard 's contract runs to 2028 and early, informal extension talks have taken place. No move is reported to be imminent. Arsenal's remaining European draw. After Prague come Borussia Dortmund on November 24, Real Madrid on December 9, Real Betis on January 20 and Sabah on January 27.
