k: Michael Carrick faces Roma at Old Trafford with United 17th, winless in nine and his position set to be assessed at the international break.
x: STOPPAGE TIME The Weekly Manchester United Digest All United, every week Weekly edition · Monday, November 2, 2026 Premier League: 17th, 7 pts · 17 behind leaders Arsenal · Next: Roma (H), Tue Nov 3 Last ten, oldest to newest W 4-0 SAB L 0-1 MCI L 2-3 BHA D 1-1 FUL D 1-1 TOT L 0-2 ATM D 1-1 LEE L 1-4 COM L 0-3 BOU L 0-2 CHE Next match Opponent: AS Roma Competition: Champions League, league phase, matchday 4 Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026 Kickoff: 12:00 PM Pacific (8:00 PM UK) Venue: Home, Old Trafford Where to watch in the US: Paramount+ ( official listing ) In this edition The Lead · Player Ratings · Scouting the Next Opponent · Transfer News · The Squad · Carrington · United Women · Players Away · Off the Pitch · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch Collapse all If you read nothing else • United are 17th on seven points after a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, their ninth game without a win in all competitions. • The Athletic reports the club will assess Michael Carrick's position at the start of the international break, after Sunday's Aston Villa game. • Benjamin Šeško is expected to be out until at least January with a shin problem, according to The Athletic. The Lead Champions League preview and analysis Carrick's Roma reckoning: one night to change the story United are 17th and winless in nine after defeat at Stamford Bridge. Gian Piero Gasperini's unbeaten Roma arrive at Old Trafford with the head coach's future set to be weighed within a week. T he arithmetic is stark. Manchester United have taken seven points from nine Premier League games, sit 17th on goal difference alone above Crystal Palace , and have not won in nine matches in any competition. Sky Sports calls it the club's longest winless run since September 1984. Into that comes Roma , unbeaten in Serie A, on Tuesday night. Saturday's 2-0 defeat at Chelsea followed a familiar arc. United were the better side before half-time: Matheus Cunha had a goal ruled out for offside, Bruno Fernandes skied a clear chance and Mike Penders saved twice from Amad. Five minutes after the restart Morgan Rogers ran through the middle and scored. ESPN and Sky both put the second half down to unravelling rather than bad luck. The unravelling had a name. Lisandro Martínez , whom Sky judged at fault for the opener, was booked for fouling Rogers and then shown a second yellow after a VAR check for raising an arm to Wesley Fofana's face at a corner. Cole Palmer scored the penalty. United had 41 per cent of the ball and an expected-goals figure of 1.17, per ESPN match data . Where the decision sits Carrick told TNT Sports he expected to be in charge against Roma, answering simply: "Yeah." The Athletic's Laurie Whitwell, as relayed by Football365 , reported that United will keep him until an assessment at the start of the November international break, after crisis talks last week. Sunday's home game with Aston Villa is the last before that break. Fabrizio Romano went further on Monday. According to TEAMtalk , he said the feeling inside the club is that Carrick has "very good chances" of surviving, with a final call likely during the break. The away end, for its part, sang Carrick's name at full-time on Saturday, with only a smattering of boos (Sky Sports). “I can't look into the future, you never know what's going to happen.” Michael Carrick, Monday's pre-Roma press conference Key facts: United v Roma Kickoff: Tuesday, November 3, 12:00 PM PT (8:00 PM UK), Old Trafford Watch in the US: Paramount+ ( Paramount+ listing ) United form: nine without a win in all competitions (D3 L6); last win 4-0 v Sabah, 10 September Roma form: 3rd in Serie A on 24 points, unbeaten in ten league games (W7 D3) League phase so far: United 3 pts (W1 L2); Roma 4 pts (W1 D1 L1) Head-to-head: eight meetings; United W5 D1 L2, including 7-1 (2007) and 6-2 (2021) The names already being floated are big ones. Romano told DAZN that Villa's Unai Emery is "a manager they love" but "a very difficult target" ( Football365 ). TEAMtalk reports that Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are the two main contenders, with Nagelsmann closely behind and backed by recruitment director Christopher Vivell ( TEAMtalk ). Treat all of it as reporting, not process: no approach has been confirmed. The tactical question Roma pose The irony of Tuesday is the opponent's method. Gasperini's sides are built on aggressive, man-for-man pressing across the pitch, which is precisely what Fernandes said United should have done in Como. "It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man," he said after the 4-1 defeat there, as quoted by Sky Sports . Roma will force United to answer that argument with the ball. Roma's likely 3-4-2-1 puts width on the wing-backs and asks the two number tens to find space between the lines. With Luke Shaw ruled out this week and Patrick Dorgu not involved after one day back in training, United have no recognised senior left-back. That flank is where Roma's right wing-back will aim, and where United's back line was stretched in the second half at Chelsea. Martínez is available. His second-booking dismissal carries a domestic ban, not a European one, so he can play Roma but will miss Villa. Carrick said on Monday he had "no concerns about commitment at all" ( full press conference ). Amad's fitness after he went off at Chelsea and Marcus Rashford's day-to-day progress are the other selection questions. What a result would change In the Champions League, United's three points from three games left them around 20th after matchday three, inside the play-off band ( league-phase table ). A home win would lift them toward the top 16 with Sporting, Villarreal, Bayern and Leipzig still to come. A defeat would leave them chasing points in Lisbon on 25 November with a new coach possibly in the dugout. Carrick chose to recall the 7-1 against Roma in 2007, in which he scored twice, as "a magical night." He needs something far smaller: a first win since 10 September, a performance that lasts 90 minutes, and a reason for the club to keep holding its nerve. Secondary feature: the captain, the coach and the clear-the-air talks The week before Chelsea was dominated by Bruno Fernandes . After the defeat in Como he said the decision not to press man to man was "on the manager and on the staff to see it, it's not on me" ( Sky Sports ). Carrick left him out against Bournemouth , calling it "pure football," and Harry Maguire captained the side ( ESPN ). United lost that game 3-0 at home. Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson scored, the second after a Leny Yoro slip and the third after Senne Lammens came off his line, per NBC Sports . A "Standards" banner appeared in the Stretford End. Carrick and Fernandes then met face to face at Carrington on Tuesday, October 27, and Sky Sports reported that the coach was satisfied the animosity was over. An all-squad meeting followed, with an acknowledgement of underperformance across the group. Fernandes started at Stamford Bridge with the armband. The relationship is repaired, for now; the results are not. Player Ratings Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United: the Digest's ratings Saturday, October 31, Stamford Bridge. Rogers 50', Palmer pen 64'. Martínez sent off 63'. These are the Digest's own marks, informed by the reports from Sky Sports , ESPN and NBC Sports , and the line-up and statistics on ESPN . Manchester United started in a 4-2-3-1. Joshua Zirkzee, the fourth substitute, came on late for Amad and is not rated because ESPN's timing does not confirm he played ten minutes. Martínez's 2 is the only mark below 5. Ratings in full (out of 10) Senne Lammens 5 : Beaten by Rogers's solo run and Palmer's penalty; a full-stretch stop from Estêvão kept the score at two. Diogo Dalot 5 : Part of a back four that held through a strong first half, then came apart after the break. Harry Maguire 5 : Solid enough before half-time; could not stop the rot once Rogers broke through. Lisandro Martínez 2 : Sky Sports judged him at fault for the opener; two bookings within minutes, the second also conceding the penalty. Leny Yoro 5 : Played through the tendon problem Carrick later described; no clear error, little control either. Amad Diallo 6 : United's sharpest outlet: twice denied by Penders before going off in apparent discomfort. Andrey Santos 5 : Busy in a midfield that won the first half on territory; withdrawn after 66 minutes. Carlos Baleba 5 : Shared the screening job without imposing himself; replaced by Mainoo. Bruno Fernandes 5 : Back in the side and wearing the armband, but skied the clearest chance of the first half from Mbeumo's cross. Matheus Cunha 6 : Had a first-half goal chalked off by VAR for offside and gave the press its bite before he went off. Bryan Mbeumo 6 : Kept probing, was inches from converting a Fernandes cross and hit the bar in stoppage time off Penders's fingertips. Kobbie Mainoo 5 : Brought on as United chased the game; could not change its shape. Ayden Heaven 5 : Sent on to shore up the defence after the red card; little to defend or attack. Mason Mount 5 : Came on with United a man down and two behind; no real openings. Scouting the Next Opponent Roma: Gasperini's unbeaten machine Third in Serie A, unbeaten in ten league games, and coming off a 5-2 win over Udinese. Roma arrive in form. ESPN's Serie A table has them third on 24 points from ten games (W7 D3 L0), behind Lazio and Inter and one point ahead of Como. Their last five matches read W-W-D-W-W, per Khel Now , and they scored five at Udinese on Saturday ( dave.sport ). Europe has been patchier. Roma drew 1-1 with Fenerbahçe, lost 4-3 at home to Real Madrid and then beat Slovan Bratislava 4-0, which gives them four points from three games ( Paramount+ preview ). Five goals conceded in three European games is the one soft spot in their numbers. The men to stop Donyell Malen is the danger. Signed in the summer for a reported €25m, he has three Champions League goals, per Paramount+ , and leads Roma's scoring. Khel Now's predicted XI has Matías Soulé and Rodrigo Mora as the two tens in a 3-4-2-1, with Nahuel Molina and Wesley as wing-backs. Roma have absentees of their own. Goalkeeper Mile Svilar and midfielder Manu Koné are out, and Khel Now also lists Lorenzo Pellegrini; Pierluigi Gollini is expected in goal. Paulo Dybala's availability is uncertain after a return to training. Where United can hurt them Gasperini's man-marking leaves space behind when a press is beaten. United's best moments at Chelsea came from quick wide combinations involving Amad and Mbeumo, and with Svilar out, testing Gollini early makes sense. The history is kind too: United have won five of the eight meetings, losing two and drawing one. Roma at a glance Manager: Gian Piero Gasperini; system 3-4-2-1 Serie A: 3rd, 24 pts from 10 (W7 D3 L0) Champions League: D 1-1 Fenerbahçe, L 3-4 Real Madrid, W 4-0 Slovan Bratislava Key man: Donyell Malen, 3 Champions League goals Out: Svilar, Koné, Pellegrini (per Khel Now); Dybala doubtful Head-to-head: United W5 D1 L2; last meeting a 3-2 Roma win in the 2021 Europa League semi-final second leg Transfer News The Martínez standoff A contract that runs out next summer, a row with the hierarchy and now a red card. Talks are due. Lisandro Martínez 's deal at Manchester United runs to June 2027, with a club option for a further year. Renewal talks were paused in mid-October after he criticised the club's hierarchy following the defeat in Madrid, according to Football Insider as reported by The Hard Tackle . On Monday Fabrizio Romano said "there will be direct contacts between Lisandro Martínez's camp and Manchester United" ( CaughtOffside ). Carrick, asked about the contract, said the club would let people know "when anything's finalised." Certainty: talks expected (Romano). A claim from the fan site utdreport that he has agreed terms with Atlético for 2027 is unconfirmed and single-sourced. The striker gap Benjamin Šeško is expected to be out until at least January with a shin problem that first flared after a collision late last season, The Athletic's Laurie Whitwell reported on October 28 ( via The Peoples Person ). With Rasmus Højlund sold to Napoli in the summer, Joshua Zirkzee is the only other senior centre-forward. That makes January a striker window whoever is in charge. FootballTransfers and TEAMtalk report that Folarin Balogun has been offered to United and other clubs ( LiveScore round-up ). Certainty: player offered, no confirmed interest. The captain's contract Bruno Fernandes 's renewal talks have stalled, and Sports Witness reports that Al-Hilal are ready to offer about €55m in January. Carrick said there was "nothing any further to update" on either his or Martínez's contract. Certainty: rumour, single-sourced. TEAMtalk adds that few bidders outside Saudi Arabia would pay £60m. Ins & Outs: summer 2026 (window now closed) In: Carlos Baleba (Brighton, reported £65m plus £5m add-ons); Andrey Santos (Chelsea, reported £48m); Youri Tielemans (Aston Villa, reported £35m); Cristian Orozco (Fortaleza); Tynan Thompson (Tottenham); Kit Margetson (Swansea); Karl Darlow (Leeds, free) Out: Rasmus Højlund (Napoli, permanent); Toby Collyer (West Brom); Casemiro, Jadon Sancho and Tyrell Malacia released Notable loans out: André Onana (Trabzonspor), Altay Bayındır (Celta Vigo), Chido Obi (Willem II), Dan Gore (Luton) Next window: January. Source: season record The Rumour Mill Alejandro Balde (Barcelona): CaughtOffside says United are considering a January loan for the left-back. With Shaw injured and Dorgu just back, the need is real. Rumour. Lennart Karl (Bayern Munich): CaughtOffside reports an enquiry for the 18-year-old, whom Bayern value at €60m and want to keep. Rumour; early interest at most. JJ Gabriel (outgoing): Real Madrid are growing confident of signing the 16-year-old academy forward, per TEAMtalk via CaughtOffside . More in Carrington below. Concrete interest, multiple clubs. The dugout: Emery, Howe, Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte have all been linked with Carrick's job. Romano calls Emery a "very difficult target" because Villa want him to stay. Speculation; no approach confirmed. The Squad Availability: no left-back, no Šeško, questions over Amad Carrick's options are thinning at the worst moment. Carrick's Monday update was blunt. "Luke definitely won't be around this week," he said of Luke Shaw . Patrick Dorgu , back in training on Monday after a hamstring injury picked up with Denmark in September, "won't be involved tomorrow" ( The Peoples Person ). Leny Yoro is managing a tendon issue that Carrick said "comes and goes." Marcus Rashford, who returned from his Barcelona loan in the summer, missed training and will be assessed "day by day." Amad went off at Chelsea in apparent discomfort and is a doubt, per dave.sport . Availability for Roma Out: Benjamin Šeško (shin, until at least January); Luke Shaw (this week) Not involved: Patrick Dorgu (first day back in training) Doubtful: Marcus Rashford (day by day); Amad (knock at Chelsea) Managing: Leny Yoro (tendon) Suspended domestically: Lisandro Martínez misses Aston Villa; available for Roma Selection and shape At Chelsea United lined up 4-2-3-1 with Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba as the pair in front of the defence, Fernandes behind Mbeumo and Cunha and Amad wide. The two summer midfielders were both withdrawn, Baleba for Kobbie Mainoo and Santos for Ayden Heaven. How Carrick balances legs and control in midfield against Roma's press is the call to watch. The deeper problem is late-game control. United were the better side in the first half at Stamford Bridge and still lost; against Bournemouth they conceded twice in four first-half minutes. Gary Neville said on Sky Sports that United are "stuck in a rut" ( LiveScore round-up ). The captaincy Maguire wore the armband against Bournemouth; Fernandes took it back at Chelsea after the clear-the-air meeting. Mainoo sat alongside Carrick at Monday's press conference. Carrington JJ Gabriel and the fight to keep Carrington's best The academy's brightest teenager wants out, and Spain's giants are circling. JJ Gabriel , 16, formally asked to leave Manchester United in September, and the club has so far failed to change his mind, according to TEAMtalk as relayed by CaughtOffside on November 1. Real Madrid are said to be increasingly confident after positive talks with his camp; Barcelona, PSG and Bayern have also been linked. Fabrizio Romano put the odds bluntly last month: "95% is for JJ Gabriel to go," probably to La Liga ( Yahoo Sports ). Any move is subject to FIFA rules on young players, and reports point at a deal around the January window. Certainty: concrete interest; nothing agreed. Graduates and debutants Shea Lacey scored in the 3-2 EFL Cup defeat by Brighton in September, the season's clearest first-team academy moment so far. Ayden Heaven came off the bench at Stamford Bridge. Tynan Thompson, signed from Tottenham in July, was in England's under-19 squad in September. Loan watch André Onana's Trabzonspor won their last three Süper Lig games, beating Gaziantep 2-0 on Sunday, Rizespor 4-3 and Beşiktaş 2-0, per his ESPN match log . Detailed weekend performances for the wider group of loanees (Ethan Wheatley at Lincoln, Jack Moorhouse at Dundee, Jacob Devaney at Hibernian and others) could not be verified this week, so they are not graded here. United Women Olid's side stall at Everton but stay in the hunt Unbeaten in ten since mid-September, fourth in the WSL and through four cup games with four wins. Manchester United Women drew 0-0 at Everton on Saturday, and head coach Eva Olid did not hide her frustration. "For me it was a bad match," she said, adding that "we need to have a conversation because this cannot happen" ( Yahoo Sports ). The context is better than the mood. United are fourth in the WSL, one place off the Champions League spots and four points behind London City Lionesses, who have a game in hand. They had gone nine games unbeaten since the 5-0 defeat by Chelsea on September 13 before Saturday's draw, per The Peoples Person . Cup run and returns Wednesday's 3-0 Players' Cup win over Burnley made it four from four in the competition ( The Peoples Person ). Ellen Wangerheim scored her first goal for the club and Lea Schüller added two. Jayde Riviere returned from injury and Celin Bizet made her first appearance since giving birth earlier this year, two welcome additions to a squad reshaped in the summer under Olid, who replaced Marc Skinner in August ( season record ). Next up United visit Aston Villa at Villa Park on Sunday, November 8, at 12:00 PM UK time (4:00 AM Pacific), then host Crystal Palace on November 14 ( fixture list ). Players Away European nights and a break that could decide everything This week's away duty is European. Manchester United host Roma on Tuesday in the Champions League, and the November international window opens after Sunday's Villa game. England name their squads on Friday, November 6 ( England Football ). Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford were in the senior squad in September; Rashford's fitness makes his place uncertain. England host Croatia at Wembley on November 12 and visit Spain on November 15 in the Nations League. Dorgu's hamstring injury came on Denmark duty against Wales in September ( Evening Standard via AOL ), a reminder of what international weeks can cost. Among the loanees, Onana kept a clean sheet in Trabzonspor's 2-0 win over Gaziantep on Sunday. Off the Pitch Boardroom pressure and the cost of a bad season The chants at Stamford Bridge were aimed upward rather than at the bench: at Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers, per AOL . BBC Sport sources, as reported by The Peoples Person , have suggested Ratcliffe could be considering a wider overhaul of senior staff. Anonymous sourcing; nothing confirmed. The money explains the nerves. An analysis of the club's filings by The ESK puts 2025-26 revenue at £677.6m and notes that lenders require adjusted EBITDA of at least £125m over every rolling 12 months. The same analysis says adidas can halve its payment in any season United spend outside the Premier League. Relegation is not the base case for anyone. But a club this indebted cannot afford a long stay in the bottom half, which is why the Roma and Villa results matter beyond the dugout. x: STOPPAGE TIME The Weekly Manchester City Digest Everything Manchester City, every week Weekly edition · Monday, November 2, 2026 Season tracker Premier League: 2nd, 21 points from 9 , three behind leaders Arsenal, two ahead of Brighton. Last ten competitive games, oldest first (the Brighton cup draw was won 4-3 on penalties): W 1-0 MUN W 5-0 NOR W 5-3 SUN W 3-0 LIV L 2-4 PSG W 3-2 IPS W 5-1 AEK L 1-2 AVL D 2-2 BHA L 0-1 BHA Next: RB Leipzig (away), Champions League, Wednesday, November 4. Next match Opponent: RB Leipzig Competition: Champions League, league phase, matchday 4 Date: Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Kickoff: 12:00 p.m. Pacific (8:00 p.m. UK) Venue: Away: Red Bull Arena, Leipzig Where to watch in the US: Paramount+ ( listing ) In this edition The Lead Player Ratings Scouting the Next Opponent Transfer News The Squad The Academy Women's Team Players Away Numbers of the Week In Brief What to Watch If you read nothing else • Brighton won 1-0 at the Etihad on Saturday, City's second straight league defeat, and Arsenal's win at Anfield sent them three points clear. • City beat Brighton 4-3 on penalties after a 2-2 draw in the Carabao Cup; Rulli saved twice and League One Bradford await in December. • Manchester City Women won 2-1 at London City Lionesses and sit level on 22 points with WSL leaders Chelsea, behind on goal difference. The Lead Maresca's first real test: two defeats, a lost lead and a trip to Leipzig Seven straight league wins built a cushion; a week of errors at the back has spent it. What has gone wrong, and what changes before Wednesday. F or seven weekends Manchester City looked as though the handover from Pep Guardiola had been seamless. Enzo Maresca won his first seven Premier League games, including a 3-0 win at Anfield. Then came a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa , and on Saturday a 1-0 loss at home to Brighton . It is the first time City have lost consecutive league games in 14 months, according to BBC Sport . The table punished it within a day. Arsenal won 1-0 at Liverpool on Sunday, their first win at Anfield in 14 years, and moved to 24 points. City are second on 21, and Brighton, winners of five of their last six league games, are only two points further back on 19 ( NBC Sports table ). The goals City keep giving away The pattern is not a lack of chances. It is avoidable goals. Brighton's winner came in the 11th minute, when Matheus Nunes missed a low ball, it struck Maxim De Cuyper and Yasin Ayari finished from close range ( Sky Sports ). A week earlier at Villa Park, Nicolas Jackson scored twice, the second going under Gianluigi Donnarumma ( ESPN ). BBC Sport counted the individual errors: Marc Guéhi at Villa (he was dropped for Brighton), Donnarumma at Villa, Nunes against Brighton. City have conceded 10 league goals in nine games, double Arsenal's total, and have kept only one clean sheet in their last eight matches in all competitions. We are conceding silly goals and we can avoid that. Enzo Maresca, after the Brighton defeat Maresca has backed his goalkeeper. He said Donnarumma remains first choice and treated the mistakes as part of football. The harder question is structure. With Rodri and Bernardo Silva gone, the club spent roughly £327 million rebuilding midfield, and against Brighton Maresca started all three new arrivals. Muscle in midfield, and nobody to unlock the door Enzo Fernández (£125m, a joint Premier League record), Elliot Anderson (£116m) and Ayyoub Bouaddi (£86m, the most expensive teenager in English top-flight history) were picked as what Maresca called a physical unit. Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden began on the bench, with the plan to bring them on later. It did not work. Bouaddi was withdrawn after 55 minutes and Fernández after 64. City had 62 per cent of the ball, 21 shots and an expected-goals figure of 1.92 to Brighton's 1.00, yet only six efforts hit the target ( SI, using FotMob data ). Bart Verbruggen made seven saves. Ndiaye hit the bar, and O'Reilly headed wide in stoppage time. Across the last two league games City have scored once from nine big chances, BBC Sport noted, and the Brighton result ended a run of 23 top-flight games with a goal. Haaland, scorer in each of his previous four league meetings with Brighton, had about a dozen touches in the first half. Why Leipzig matters more than usual Wednesday's trip to RB Leipzig is the obvious place to reset. City are 10th in the 36-team Champions League table with six points from three games, after wins over Porto and AEK Athens and a 4-2 home defeat by PSG. A win would put them back in the automatic top-eight places; another loss would leave them chasing in November. Expect changes. Sports Mole expects Cherki to return in the No. 10 role and Guéhi to push for a recall, with Foden in contention too. The bigger tell will be whether Maresca keeps all three new midfielders together; the evidence of Saturday argues for a playmaker between the lines. None of this is a crisis yet. City remain the league's second-highest scorers with 20 goals, Haaland leads the Golden Boot race with nine, and Saturday brings a trip to Nottingham Forest, who are 19th. But the margin for loose goals has gone, and the next two games will say a lot about how quickly Maresca learns. Key facts Result: Manchester City 0-1 Brighton, Etihad Stadium, Saturday, October 31. Ayari 11'. Shots 21 to 7; on target 6 to 3; possession 62% to 38%; xG 1.92 to 1.00 (SI/FotMob). Verbruggen saves: 7. Brighton's first win at the Etihad (Sky Sports). City league record: 7 wins, 0 draws, 2 losses; 20 scored, 10 conceded. Gap: Arsenal 24 points, City 21, Brighton 19. Next league game: Nottingham Forest (away), Saturday, November 7, 9:30 a.m. PT. Waiting on the appeal: the verdict hangs over the season City were found guilty of most of the 115 charges in late September. The appeal clock is running, and Haaland's father has now spoken. The football has been played under a cloud since an independent commission found Manchester City guilty of most of the Premier League financial charges covering 2009-10 to 2017-18. The club lodged what it called a comprehensive appeal at 7pm on Thursday, October 1, and maintains it is innocent ( Sky Sports ). Sanctions have not been set. The same three-person panel will decide them, and that hearing can run alongside the appeal. Under the league's newer rules the appeal should be heard within 12 weeks of being lodged, which points to mid-December, with a verdict due within 30 days of the hearing ending. City may argue those rules do not apply to a case charged in 2023. David Kogan , chair of the Independent Football Regulator, told Times Radio he expected clarity early next year ( via Yahoo Sports ). Nothing new on the timetable emerged this week. What did emerge was a careful comment from Alf-Inge Haaland . Asked whether his son's contract contains a relegation exit clause, he said: "I can't comment on player contracts or Erling's contract." He added that Erling concentrates on playing and that "those of us outside the pitch" think about it more ( beIN Sports ). No talks with any club have been reported. Scouting the Next Opponent RB Leipzig: fourth in Germany, short of points in Europe Martín Demichelis's side won at Schalke on Saturday and need a result; City have the history but not the form. RB Leipzig appointed Martín Demichelis in June, and the former City defender has them fourth in the Bundesliga after a 2-0 win over Schalke on Saturday, three points behind Bayern Munich ( Yahoo Sports ; Sports Mole ). Across all competitions they have won eight and lost five of 13. Europe has been harder. Leipzig have three points from three league-phase games and sit 29th of 36, so this is close to a must-win for them, which should make for an open game. Sports Mole notes the last six meetings between the clubs averaged five goals. Who to stop Antonio Nusa scored a penalty at Schalke and is the direct threat from the left. Rômulo won that penalty and scored the second on a counterattack. Brajan Gruda , on loan from Brighton, is the creator from the right with one Champions League goal this season ( Khel Now ). Christopher Nkunku's fitness is uncertain. The way Leipzig scored the second goal at Schalke, a quick break from a long Benjamin Henrichs pass, is exactly the kind of transition City have struggled to stop. Maresca's full-backs push high; whoever plays there will need help. Leipzig are without Assan Ouédraogo (shoulder, out until around late December) and Marc Guiu (muscle), while Maxime Estève is doubtful with a knock. City's only absentee is Antoine Semenyo. The Lead No shot on target, no answer: Arsenal expose Liverpool's Anfield problem An Alisson error decided it, but the bigger story is a home attack that has scored four league goals in five games and could not make David Raya work once. F or sixteen minutes on Sunday, Liverpool looked like a side still finding the temperature of the game. Then Alisson Becker played a loose pass towards Jérémy Jacquet , Arsenal won it, Noni Madueke and Declan Rice combined down the right, and Kai Havertz tapped in at the far post. It was the only goal, and it was enough ( ESPN ). What followed was the story of Liverpool's autumn in miniature. They had more of the ball (56 per cent) and more shots (17 to 10), and they hit the woodwork through a Florian Wirtz free-kick. They did not, however, make David Raya work once. It was the first Anfield league game without a Liverpool shot on target since records began in 2003, a run of 442 matches ( LBC ). The result leaves Liverpool fifth on 15 points from nine games, nine behind the leaders and the reigning champions, Arsenal, who have now won all five league games this season in which they scored first. It was also Arsenal's first league win at Anfield since 2012 ( NBC Sports table ; LBC ). Key facts Result: Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal, Premier League, Sunday, November 1, Anfield (attendance 60,406) Goal: Kai Havertz 16', from Declan Rice's low cross Shots: Liverpool 17, Arsenal 10; on target 0 to 3 Possession: Liverpool 56% Officials: Referee Andy Madley; VAR Stuart Attwell Record: First Anfield league game without a Liverpool shot on target since 2003 (442 matches) An Anfield problem, not a form problem The scoreline flatters nobody, but the pattern is the worry. Liverpool have scored four league goals in five home games, which Sports Mole says equals their worst Anfield return ( via LiveScore ). Away from home they have looked freer: wins at Ipswich, Bournemouth and Brentford, and six goals in Linz in the Champions League. At Anfield, opponents have been content to sit in a low block and let Liverpool cross. Against Arsenal the chances came from set pieces and wide deliveries: Mac Allister heading an unmarked chance over from Milos Kerkez's cross, Isak just failing to reach Bradley Barcola's inswinger, and a late Víctor Muñoz header that lacked the power to trouble Raya ( liverpoolfc.com ). Andoni Iraola made one change from the 2-0 win over Brighton, handing Trey Nyoni his first Premier League start ahead of Ryan Gravenberch. The 19-year-old was replaced by Dominik Szoboszlai after 58 minutes, Rio Ngumoha came on for Cody Gakpo at 67, and a triple change at 82 brought on Kostas Tsimikas, Lewis Koumas and Muñoz ( liverpoolfc.com ). “From 1-0, I loved the reaction of the team.” Andoni Iraola, after the defeat (PA) The penalty that wasn't, and the dive debate Iraola was candid about where the game was lost. “I think we have to blame the start of the game,” he said, adding that until the goal his side were not “at the level of the rest of the game” ( PA via AOL ). The louder line came on VAR. Replays showed Jurrien Timber pulling Alexander Isak's shirt as he rose for a header, and neither referee Andy Madley nor VAR Stuart Attwell intervened. “You have to dive, if you don't dive they won't call it,” Iraola told the BBC ( Dragon Football ). Virgil van Dijk was blunter still: “Everyone has seen it... In the end it wasn't given and we lose” ( SB Nation via Yahoo ). Those remarks will keep the incident alive this week, and a manager publicly telling his players to go down invites scrutiny. No response from the referees' body had been reported by Monday morning. The goalkeeper question and the week ahead The other conversation is in goal. Alisson's error was the decisive moment, though he later tipped a low Christos Tzolis shot around the post and saved from Rice. His contract runs to 2027, and Football Insider reported in September that no new deal is planned ( Football365 ). Giorgi Mamardashvili started Wednesday's cup tie. Iraola has resisted big statements all autumn; on Friday he said it was “too early to start looking at the standings” ( ESPN ). Sunday's result makes that caution look wise. The next eight days bring a trip to Istanbul and a Sunday visit to Crystal Palace, who are 18th, before the international break. Three points at Selhurst Park and a positive result in Turkey would reset the mood. The race after Week 9 1. Arsenal: 24 pts 2. Manchester City: 21 pts 3. Brighton: 19 pts 4. Chelsea: 16 pts 5. Liverpool: 15 pts, nine off the top, one off the top four Secondary feature Shootout nerve sends a much-changed Liverpool past Chelsea A much-changed side drew 1-1 and won 6-5 on penalties, setting up a quarter-final with Iraola's old club. Midweek brought the relief. Against Chelsea in the Carabao Cup fourth round, Iraola made seven changes and Liverpool still found a way through: 1-1 after 90 minutes, then 6-5 on penalties ( ESPN ). Morgan Rogers put Chelsea ahead from the spot on 40 minutes and Cody Gakpo levelled with a penalty three minutes later. The underlying numbers favoured Liverpool (xG 2.10 to 1.82, per ESPN), and the academy pair of Nyoni and Ngumoha started alongside James McConnell and Lewis Koumas. “The players have done a very big effort today and at least we get the reward of being in the quarter-finals,” Iraola said ( liverpoolfc.com ). The draw then handed him the one tie he did not want: his former club Bournemouth at Anfield. “The only team that I don't want is Bournemouth,” he admitted ( ESPN ). Scouting the Next Opponent Kuyt's homecoming, Fenerbahçe's crisis A club in turmoil hands its first Champions League night under an interim coach to a Liverpool legend. Few fixtures this season carry a better story for Liverpool . Fenerbahçe accepted İsmail Kartal 's resignation on October 27 after a chaotic run that included a 2-1 derby defeat at Galatasaray and a 6-0 humiliation at Aston Villa in this competition. Their caretaker is Dirk Kuyt , six seasons a Liverpool forward and a scorer in the 2007 Champions League final ( ESPN/AP ). Kuyt, who also played for Fenerbahçe from 2012 to 2015, had joined as Kartal's assistant in pre-season. His first game in charge went badly: a 2-1 home defeat by Göztepe on Saturday. FotMob lists Fenerbahçe sixth in the Süper Lig, on 16 points from ten games ( FotMob ; Goal ). System and danger men Expect a 4-2-3-1, with N'Golo Kanté and Matteo Guendouzi among the midfield options and Vedat Muriqi (seven league goals) leading the line. Mason Greenwood , who missed the Göztepe game through illness, has trained fully and is available, per Turkish broadcaster NTV ( NTV ). Romelu Lukaku is also in the squad. The weakness is plain: a team that has won none of its three league-phase games and shipped six at Villa Park. They also go into the game without defender Kojo Oppong and Nathan Aké, according to NTV. For Liverpool, the opportunity is to turn Sunday's sterile possession into chances against a side low on confidence. A win would take Iraola's side to 12 points with four league-phase games left: Club Brugge away, Porto at home, Inter away and Lens at home ( UEFA ; NBC Sports ). The biggest Liverpool transfer story of the week surfaced on Monday: Italian outlet Tuttomercatoweb reported that Liverpool have a €50m (about £42m) offer ready for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara , with the aim of agreeing a deal before the window opens ( Football365 ). Certainty: rumour. No bid has been confirmed, and the figure is single-sourced. The interest itself is better grounded. Fabrizio Romano said on October 20 that Liverpool are tracking the 22-year-old and would act only for “the right opportunity”, in January or the summer, adding that midfield is a 2027 focus ( TEAMtalk ). Romano has also said Bournemouth's Alex Scott could leave in January for a big proposal, with a price above £100m ( TEAMtalk ). Against that, David Lynch reports midfield is not a January priority and that a large mid-season fee would surprise him ( Anfield Index via Yahoo ). Certainty for both: monitoring. The context is a single-sourced report from Sky Sports Switzerland that the club is leaning towards selling Alexis Mac Allister next summer, despite his wish to stay; his contract runs to 2028 ( Goal ). Right-back cover with Frimpong out Jeremie Frimpong's muscle injury, picked up at Brentford, has revived interest in Chelsea full-back Malo Gusto . Liverpool tried a deadline-day loan in September; Chelsea wanted a permanent sale. Dean Jones says Chelsea's €80m summer valuation is being re-evaluated ( TEAMtalk ). Certainty: monitoring. Conor Bradley's return, possibly for Sunderland on December 2, may ease the need ( Evening Standard via Yahoo ). Alisson and Virgil van Dijk are both out of contract in 2027, and no new deal has been agreed for either. On loan at Valencia , Harvey Elliott has played 152 La Liga minutes off the bench and was sent off against Villarreal on October 24. The Daily Mail's Julian Burgos says Valencia could end the loan in January ( Roundtable via Yahoo ). Certainty: speculation. Liverpool knocked Chelsea out of the Carabao Cup 6-5 on penalties at Anfield on Wednesday after a 1-1 draw; Wesley Fofana missed the decisive kick. Chelsea Women won 6-0 at Charlton to stay top of the WSL on goal difference, but Lauren James went off with a suspected hamstring injury. The Lead Analysis Lavia, Rogers and a rare clean sheet: how Alonso steadied a lurching week Three days after a shootout exit at Anfield and a week after Spurs won at the Bridge, Chelsea out-thought a ten-man United. The question now is whether a thinned squad can carry it to Sunderland. F or the first 45 minutes on Saturday, Chelsea looked like a team still carrying the week. Their run had read: a 2-0 home defeat to Tottenham , then a Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool on penalties. Against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge the first half was even and nervy. Then Morgan Rogers took the game away from everyone. Five minutes after the restart Rogers picked the ball up, ran at Harry Maguire and finished a solo goal that Sports Illustrated called stunning. The assist came from Roméo Lavia , and that detail matters more than the finish. Lavia, in his best afternoon in blue, made 23 defensive contributions according to FotMob figures cited by SI. The second goal arrived out of United's temper. Lisandro Martínez , already booked, barged Wesley Fofana at a corner and was shown a second yellow after VAR intervened, with a penalty awarded. Cole Palmer , back from a one-match ban, sent it home for his 50th Chelsea goal, as the Sutton and Croydon Guardian report noted. Key facts Result: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United, Premier League, Stamford Bridge, Saturday October 31 Goals: Morgan Rogers (about 50 min), Cole Palmer (penalty) Red card: Lisandro Martínez (Man United), second yellow Possession: 59% to 41% · Shots: 18 to 12 (9 to 5 on target) Expected goals: 2.67 to 1.17 (FotMob, via SI) Table after nine games: 4th, 16 pts, W5 D1 L3, goals 19-15 The shape that worked Xabi Alonso went 4-2-3-1 with Pedro Neto as a makeshift centre-forward because João Pedro is out with a thigh injury. Neto struggled against Maguire. The fix came from elsewhere: Lavia and Moisés Caicedo owned the middle, and Estêvão , starting at last, kept pulling Diogo Dalot wide on the right. The numbers back the eye test. Chelsea had 59 per cent of the ball, 18 shots to 12 and an expected-goals total of 2.67 against 1.17. United produced just 0.08 xG after half-time while Chelsea built 2.39 in that period. Estêvão had two goals ruled out for offside, one by what the Guardian report described as about an inch. “It's very important; it's the second in three Premier League games and we need many more.” Xabi Alonso on the clean sheet That quote is the real story. Alonso's side have scored freely all season: 19 league goals in nine games, the third-best total of the top four. They have also conceded 15, more than anyone in the top six. Against United, Mike Penders , a week after punching a Spurs corner into his own net, made the saves that mattered and kept a clean sheet. The week that framed it Context makes Saturday more impressive. Against Spurs on October 24, Penders' own goal in the 77th minute and a late Mathys Tel solo run handed Roberto De Zerbi 's side their first win at the Bridge since 2018. Palmer was sent off for a second yellow, the first red of his career, as Alonso pointed out. At Anfield on Wednesday Chelsea fielded something close to their strongest team. Rogers scored a penalty, Cody Gakpo levelled from the spot after Fofana raised an arm, and the shootout went to sudden death. Valentín Barco , Emmanuel Emegha and Fofana missed. Liverpool won 6-5 and Chelsea lost Maxence Lacroix to a hamstring injury before half-time. What it means for the table The win lifts Chelsea to fourth on 16 points, eight behind Arsenal and one ahead of Liverpool. That is the last Champions League place. With the November international break starting on the 9th, the trip to bottom club Sunderland on Sunday is the last chance to bank points before a two-week pause. Sunderland beat Chelsea twice last season. The risk is depth. Alonso is without his captain Reece James , his first-choice goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez , his main striker and now Lacroix. The calls he made on Saturday, trusting Lavia for 90 minutes and finally starting Estêvão, suggest he has found a midfield and a right side that work. Sunderland will test whether they work twice in eight days. Secondary feature Estêvão finally gets his start, and makes Alonso's point for him Two starts in all competitions before Saturday, one unused-substitute night at Anfield, and the loudest cheer at the team announcement. Estêvão 's minutes have been the running argument of Chelsea 's autumn. Before United he had started only two matches in all competitions, according to Reuters . Xabi Alonso dismissed talk of a January loan: “No discussions about that.” He also said, “I have to take the responsibility for that.” On Saturday the 19-year-old Brazilian repeatedly beat Diogo Dalot and had two goals chalked off for offside. Reports on Monday, carried by The Chelsea Chronicle and unconfirmed by the club, suggest Alonso still wants more from him in training. The club's stance on his future is clearer: Spanish outlet AS, via FootballTransfers , reports renewal talks and a pay rise, with no sale planned despite interest from Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona . Scouting the Next Opponent Sunderland (A), Sunday Sunderland: bottom, stretched by Europe, and Chelsea's tormentors from last season Le Bris's side sit 20th and have not won a league game since August 30. They also beat Chelsea home and away in 2025-26. Sunderland have five points from nine games (one win, two draws, six defeats), with seven goals scored and 17 conceded, per the ESPN table . Their last outing was a 3-1 defeat at Coventry on Saturday. Enzo Le Fée 's penalty there was their first Premier League goal since September 20, as Sky Sports noted. Europe explains much of it. Last season's final-day win over Chelsea took Régis Le Bris 's team into the Europa League, and the league phase has gone well: a home win over AZ Alkmaar, a stoppage-time win at Torreense and a 1-1 draw at Lech Poznań, per Dave Sport . They host Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday, which is why this game moved to Sunday. Who to stop Brian Brobbey is their leading scorer and the focal point. Le Fée is the set-piece and penalty taker. Noah Sadiki scored the late winner in Portugal, and goalkeeper Robin Roefs has kept them in games. Trai Hume , whose volley opened the scoring against Chelsea in May, is worth watching on the right. There is one certain absence: centre-back Omar Alderete was sent off for a second yellow card in stoppage time at Coventry, so he is due to serve a one-match ban. Dan Ballard, Wilson Isidor and Thomas Meunier have all missed games this autumn; their status for Sunday was not confirmed by Monday. Where Chelsea can hurt them Sunderland's finishing has been the problem, and the defence has leaked under pressure. Sky's analysis had their non-penalty xG at Coventry at 0.80, slightly above the hosts, yet they lost by two. A Chelsea midfield that dominated United should be able to pin them back; the danger is the counter if Alonso's full-backs push high. History is a warning. Sunderland won 2-1 at Stamford Bridge in October 2025 through a stoppage-time winner from Chemsdine Talbi, then won 2-1 on the final day in May 2026 to take the European place Chelsea wanted, as Flashscore reported. x: Stoppage Time The Weekly Soccer Digest World football, every Friday, for the weekend ahead Friday, October 30, 2026 · The weekend preview · Arsenal covered separately In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch If you read nothing else Bayern Munich host Borussia Dortmund on Saturday level on 17 points, both unbeaten, with Vincent Kompany at home recovering from meningeal irritation. Manchester United have one league win in nine games and sit 17th, with Michael Carrick confirmed only for Saturday's trip to Chelsea. Kylian Mbappe's joke about a Chinese leader cost him two sponsors and prompted apologies from Real Madrid and LaLiga. This weekend, in Pacific time Chelsea v Manchester United Premier League Sat 5:30am Manchester City v Brighton Premier League Sat 8:00am Bayern Munich v Borussia Dortmund Bundesliga Sat 10:30am AC Milan v Inter Serie A Sat 12:45pm Barcelona v Alaves LaLiga Sat 1:00pm Liverpool v Arsenal Premier League Sun 8:30am Juventus v Napoli Serie A Sun 11:45am New England v Inter Miami MLS Sun 4:00pm The Lead Der Klassiker arrives level, and without the man who built Bayern's season Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund meet on Saturday tied on points, both unbeaten, and separated by almost nothing except the way they score. The one certainty is that Vincent Kompany will not be in the dugout. There is a version of this fixture that arrives every autumn as a formality, Bayern a dozen points clear and Dortmund playing for third. This is not that version. After seven matchdays the two clubs are identical on the only line that matters: played seven, won five, drawn two, lost none, seventeen points. They are the only unbeaten teams left in Germany. Saturday at the Allianz Arena is first against second in the literal sense. What separates them is style, and the gap there is enormous. Bayern have scored 25 goals, more than anyone in the division and five more than the next best. Dortmund have scored 12, a total that eight other clubs have bettered, and have conceded four. Four, in seven games. Nobody in Germany has conceded fewer, and only Bayern, on six, are anywhere near. So the match has an unusually clean shape to it. Bayern are a team that overwhelms; Dortmund are a team that refuses. One of those propositions is going to look foolish by Saturday evening. The absence that frames everything Bayern's week has not been about football. On Friday 23 October, Vincent Kompany collapsed while watching the club's second team train and was taken to hospital. He had been unwell for some time, carrying a viral infection that affected his legs, sitting through the 6-1 league win over RB Leipzig on 17 October and missing training and a press conference in the days before. He was discharged on Wednesday 28 October. Sporting director Max Eberl told ARD that the diagnosis was an irritation of the meninges, the membranes around the brain and spinal cord, and that it had caused the collapse. Eberl was careful to separate it from the job. "This is a condition that could strike any one of us," he said. "This has nothing to do with the pressure associated with the Bundesliga." Kompany will not be at the Klassiker. He is not on the bench and, by the club's account, is being kept away from football conversations entirely. Assistant Aaron Danks takes the team, as he did for the 3-1 win at Freiburg and the 6-1 cup win over Magdeburg. Danks has been pointedly undramatic about it. "No big changes, no big differences for us," he said on Friday. "We want the players to go out and show who they are." Kane, Guirassy and the two theories of attack Monday night in London, Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or. He beat Kylian Mbappe into second and Lamine Yamal into third, and he mentioned Kompany from the stage. Kompany had phoned him that morning to wish him luck. Kane has four league goals this season, fewer than you might expect from a Ballon d'Or winner, because Bayern's goals are spread everywhere: Michael Olise has six, Luis Diaz four, and the 3-1 at Freiburg included Serge Gnabry 's 100th Bundesliga goal and an Olise winner in stoppage time. Dortmund's attack is one man and a prayer. Serhou Guirassy has seven goals in all competitions, and Bundesliga's own preview has framed Saturday as Kane against Guirassy. The supporting evidence is thinner. Against Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, Dortmund took 18 shots, Guirassy missed two clear chances, and the game was settled on 80 minutes by Maximilian Beier off a Jobe Bellingham pass. Three days later, 2-0 up on Werder Bremen in the cup, they were pegged back to 2-2 by a Niclas Fullkrug brace and rescued by a Marcel Sabitzer free kick in stoppage time. That is the Dortmund pattern under Niko Kovac , whose contract was extended to June 2029 earlier this month, two years ahead of schedule. They do not score early and they do not concede. They win late. It is not thrilling and it has them level with Bayern. Bayern are the pinnacle not only in Germany but in Europe. There is no team in the world that dominates the opponent for 90 minutes. Niko Kovac, Borussia Dortmund head coach, speaking to dpa on 29 October Who is missing Bayern are without Manuel Neuer , whose foot injury is still painful enough that Danks ruled him out on Friday, leaving Jonas Urbig in goal. Jamal Musiala has not returned to full training since the September international break. Luis Diaz is out too. Joshua Kimmich has resumed individual training following the death of his father and may feature. "Life is different for him now and we don't need to hide that," Eberl said. Dortmund are missing Emre Can and Giannis Konstantelias , both with knee problems. Konstantinos Karetsas , injured at Union Berlin in mid October, trained partly with the squad on Thursday and will be assessed. Kovac said the side that played the last match is otherwise fit. The weight of recent history Dortmund have not beaten Bayern since March 2024. Club adviser Matthias Sammer was asked about Saturday and gave an answer that sounded less like a prediction than a confession: Bayern alone, he told Sky, will decide whether they win this game. It drew criticism in Germany as defeatism from a man who used to embody the opposite. There is a counter-argument, and it is sitting in the Bayern treatment room. A side missing its goalkeeper, its most creative attacker and its manager is a side playing on structure and habit. Dortmund's entire season has been built on being the team that is still standing at minute 85. If they are ever going to end the run, a week like this one is the week. Der Klassiker: key facts Kickoff. Saturday 31 October, 10:30am Pacific, 18:30 in Munich, Allianz Arena. At stake. First place. Both clubs have 17 points from seven games and are the division's only unbeaten sides. Bayern lead on goal difference, plus 19 to plus 8. The contrast. Bayern have scored 25 goals, the most in the Bundesliga. Dortmund have conceded 4, the fewest. The dugouts. Aaron Danks stands in for Vincent Kompany, discharged from hospital on 28 October. Niko Kovac signed a contract to 2029 on 13 October. The run. Dortmund's last win over Bayern came in March 2024. Form. Bayern won 3-1 at Freiburg and 6-1 against Magdeburg in the cup. Dortmund won 1-0 against Frankfurt and 3-2 against Werder Bremen in the cup. Transfer News Bayern say the Kane deal is all but done, and only the lawyers are left The Ballon d'Or winner's contract expires at the end of this season. Bayern's chief executive says the hard part was settled before the ceremony. The most consequential piece of contract business in European football is being conducted almost in public. Harry Kane 's Bayern deal runs out at the end of 2026-27. On Wednesday 28 October, after the 6-1 cup win over Magdeburg, chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen spoke to Kicker in terms that left very little room. "We had already discussed and negotiated all the important issues before the Ballon d'Or ceremony," Dreesen said. The remaining work is detail, which "simply takes a few days." And then the line that matters: "But we both know that we want to extend this arrangement for as long as possible." Dreesen described repeated conversations with Kane's father and brother. Certainty: personal terms agreed in substance, not signed and not announced. Nothing has been filed and Bayern have made no formal statement. Dreesen is the club's chief executive speaking on the record to Germany's most authoritative football title, which is about as strong as an unannounced deal gets, but it is not an announcement. The timing is not accidental. Kane won the Ballon d'Or in London on Monday 26 October, ahead of Mbappe and Lamine Yamal, and also took the Gerd Muller award. A player who has just been named the best in the world and whose contract expires in eight months is, in theory, the most available footballer alive. Bayern appear to have closed that window before it opened. Milan tie down Pulisic and open a January list A renewal to 2031 confirmed on Friday, and an owner saying out loud that the summer window left the squad short. AC Milan announced on Friday 30 October that Christian Pulisic has extended his contract to 30 June 2031. The club cited 44 goals in 141 appearances since July 2023 and framed the renewal as confirming a shared path. Tuttomercatoweb 's Simone Lorini had the financial terms in advance, reporting a salary of 6.5 million euros net per season, a figure that does not appear in the club statement. Certainty: OFFICIAL. Announced by the club and carried by the ANSA wire. The renewal landed the same day Gerry Cardinale , whose RedBird Capital owns the club, gave a long interview conceding that the summer had fallen short. "We have to keep improving the squad because in the summer I did not manage to do everything I wanted," he said, promising high-level reinforcements in January. The names being worked on, per Tuttomercatoweb and Gazzetta dello Sport , are mostly defenders, which is what you would expect from a club that just lost its best centre-back for a month. Goncalo Inacio of Sporting is described as the front-runner. Tiago Gabriel at Lecce is a longer-standing target. Kim Min-jae is said to be open to a Serie A return from Bayern. Further forward, Endrick is considered a possible loan from Real Madrid, with Roma also interested. Alex Scott of Bournemouth is on the list but a reported 100 million euro valuation makes January unrealistic. Certainty: concrete interest, no bids reported. Cardinale's quote is on the record; the target list is reporting, not confirmation. Milan also published their 2025-26 accounts on Thursday: revenue of 464.6 million euros, a net loss of around 24 million, sponsorship above 100 million, and average attendance over 72,000 despite a season with no European football. Chairman Paolo Scaroni called the figures evidence of "the resilience of our business model in a challenging season." Dortmund have a renewal queue, and Guirassy is not at the front of it Four key players are out of contract in 2028. Bild's BVB correspondent has laid out the order, and it says something about how the club values its only reliable scorer. Four of Borussia Dortmund 's most important players run out of contract in summer 2028: goalkeeper Gregor Kobel , full-back Julian Ryerson , centre-back Waldemar Anton and striker Serhou Guirassy . On Friday, Bild 's Dortmund correspondent Sebastian Wessling set out the club's priority order on the paper's "Dortmund Insider" podcast. Anton is first, with talks already under way. Kobel is second, and the club would ideally like him signed this calendar year. Ryerson follows. Guirassy is last, and talks are not expected to start before spring 2027. Wessling's phrasing was that Guirassy "is not quite at the front of the queue," which for a player with seven goals and two assists this season is a pointed piece of information. Certainty: advanced talks for Anton, stated intent for Kobel, deliberate deferral for Guirassy. Sky Germany first reported the Anton negotiations on 8 October. Manchester United have been linked with Anton, which is at the rumour tier and has no reported bid behind it. Head of sport Rouven Schroder was unrestrained: "The way he dribbles forward, the audacity with which he sets up the goal. Hats off." Certainty: advanced talks. Around the Leagues Premier League A title race that has barely moved, a Manchester United collapse that keeps moving, and a weekend that could reshape both. Matchweek nine broke the pattern at the top. Aston Villa beat Manchester City 2-1 at Villa Park on Saturday, City's second defeat of the season and enough to drop them from first to second. Liverpool beat Brighton 2-0 at Anfield to move third on 18 points, their best run of the Andoni Iraola era, which is a sentence that would have read strangely in May. The Lead Kane's Crown, and the Klassiker That Follows Harry Kane collected the Ballon d'Or at the Palladium Theatre on Monday night. On Saturday he walks into the Allianz Arena for a first-against-second Klassiker, with Bayern Munich 's head coach in hospital, their best creator in a brace and Borussia Dortmund carrying the meanest defence in Germany. The Lead · Munich The two facts sit oddly together. On Monday night in London, Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or , an award built on the 73 goals in 65 games he scored for club and country across 2025-26. On Wednesday morning in Munich, the official Bayern Munich line on his head coach was that a diagnosis is still pending. Somewhere between those two sentences is the strangest week this club has had in years, and at the end of it comes Borussia Dortmund . Start with the collapse, because everything else at Bayern is downstream of it. On Friday Vincent Kompany was watching the second team train when he went down. He was taken to hospital and kept there. Sporting director Max Eberl said his condition was stable and the headaches had stopped, but that doctors had not finished their work. Sport Bild reports heart attack and stroke ruled out, with the medical focus on a head problem. Assistant Aaron Danks took the team to Freiburg the next day and won 3-1. Kompany is not expected on the bench on Saturday. What Bayern did in the 48 hours after that is why they are still top. At Freiburg they played without Luis Diaz (a muscle tear from the Arsenal draw), Jamal Musiala , Manuel Neuer , Aleksandar Pavlovic , and captain Joshua Kimmich , who is away from the squad after the death of his father. Dayot Upamecano headed in a Michael Olise cross, Serge Gnabry scored his 100th Bundesliga goal in his first league start of the season, and Olise finished it in stoppage time. Bayern's own numbers put them at 2.99 expected goals to 1.05. Eberl was unusually candid afterwards. "I don't think we really understand what we've achieved this week," he said. "The win means three points, but it was a bigger win than just three points." Danks , asked about his absent manager's message to the squad, reported it verbatim: "Brilliant. Now get some rest." Bayern are 22 Bundesliga games unbeaten and lead the division for goals, shots, possession and distance covered. Not burning yourself out in those circumstances is a special skill. Lars Ricken , Borussia Dortmund sporting managing director, on the demands on a head coach, via Get German Football News The most generous words of the week came from the opposition boardroom. Borussia Dortmund 's sporting managing director Lars Ricken wished Kompany "all the best and a speedy recovery" and then talked about the job itself: the match every three days, the 200-plus press conferences a season that Niko Kovac gets through. Chief executive Carsten Cramer went further. "I thought the way FC Bayern handled the situation was exemplary," he said, before noting that a head coach has at least ten difficult conversations with non-starters before every match. It is not often that Klassiker week opens with the two clubs agreeing about anything. On the pitch this is the league's best attack against its best defence, and the gap in style is enormous. A Stay of Execution at Old Trafford Manchester United are 16th, winless in eight and were beaten 3-0 at home by Bournemouth with their captain dropped. Michael Carrick kept his job on Monday for one reason: the club has not settled on who replaces him. The sequence is now familiar enough to be a genre. On Wednesday Manchester United lost 4-1 at Como in the Champions League, in a 10,000-seat stadium, to a club playing its first European campaign at this level. On Thursday their captain gave an interview to Sky Sport Italia. On Sunday they lost 3-0 at home to Bournemouth , with that captain sitting on the bench for 90 minutes. On Monday the executives met and decided to keep the manager anyway. Bruno Fernandes said this, among other things, to Sky Sport Italia's Pierluigi Bagnulo : "At this club, we focus too much on what was achieved in the past, but we are no longer the same." And, on the run itself: "Unfortunately, it's one of those moments where it seems like we can't get out of it." Gary Neville on Sky Sports called it "a direct attack on the manager." Carrick left him out against Bournemouth and gave no public reason. What followed was one of the bleaker afternoons Old Trafford has staged. Rayan scored at the far post from a Justin Kluivert free kick on 38 minutes, Marcus Tavernier added a second on 43 after a Leny Yoro slip, and Evanilson beat Senne Lammens to the ball on 71. The Stretford End turned its anger on the Glazer family, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and director of football Jason Wilcox , then sang Carrick 's name as he walked off. Marco Rose , whose Bournemouth side have won four in a row, said simply: "We were just Bournemouth today." Opta records seven points from eight games as United's worst start to a league season since 1986-87. They have also suffered seven home defeats by three goals or more in all competitions since 2023-24, more than any other Premier League club. Chelsea Move First, and Alone, on Alex Scott The most advanced January deal in Europe is also the least priced. Bournemouth 's owner has admitted on the record that his midfielder has turned down the chance to become the club's highest earner. The published findings describe sham commercial contracts, schemes that inflated revenues and reduced costs by more than 900 million pounds, and a club that, in the commission's words, "clearly intended to circumvent the PL Rules." Chief executive Richard Masters called it the most significant case in Premier League history. x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest One club, every beat, every Tuesday Edition No. 11 · Tuesday, October 27, 2026 · North London Season tracker 2nd in the Premier League · 21 points from 8 · level with Manchester City , behind on goal difference (+8 to +11) Last ten, oldest first W 2-1 CHE W 1-0 NAP W 2-0 SUN W 4-2 IPS L 0-3 BHA W 2-1 LEE W 3-0 LIL W 1-0 NFO D 2-2 BAY W 2-0 EVE Next: Fleetwood Town away, Carabao Cup fourth round, today at 1:00pm Pacific In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · Player Ratings · Scouting the Next Opponent · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch If you read nothing else 1. Bukayo Saka tore a quad at Bayern Munich and will be out for weeks, with a rescan due around the start of November. 2. Arsenal beat Everton 2-0 while Manchester City lost at Aston Villa , leaving the two level on 21 points. 3. Sunday brings Liverpool away, a side on four straight wins under Andoni Iraola and unbeaten by Arsenal since 2024. The Lead Anfield, Without Him Arsenal arrive on Merseyside on Sunday level on points with Manchester City and shorn of the player who has started almost every important afternoon of the Arteta era. What follows is a test of whether the champions are a system or a supporting cast. T here were about ten minutes on the clock at the Allianz Arena last Wednesday when Bukayo Saka played a simple pass, reached for the back of his upper leg and stopped running. He did not go down theatrically. He did not wave at the bench. He simply walked, slowly, towards the touchline with the expression of a man who already knew. Eberechi Eze came on. Twenty-five minutes later Eze put Arsenal in front in Munich, and by the end Declan Rice had rescued a 2-2 from a game Bayern Munich had begun to control. The night was a credit to the squad. It was also the moment this season changed shape. Mikel Arteta was immediately blunt. "It doesn't look good at all but we have to wait and see," he said in Germany, and by Friday he had hardened it: "It will be weeks." A second scan was ordered because of fluid in the area, and the club expects to rescan again a week to ten days from now before fixing a return date. Several national outlets have put the window at six to eight weeks, which would take the vice-captain past the Champions League league phase and into the back half of December. That figure is not Arteta's, and the Digest treats it as unconfirmed; what is confirmed is that Saka will not play at Anfield, and that Arsenal are now asking a reshaped front line to go to the venue where their season most often curdles. Key facts: Liverpool v Arsenal WHEN Sunday, November 1, 8:30am Pacific. Anfield. Kick-off 4:30pm in the United Kingdom. FORM Liverpool 4th, 15 points, four straight wins in all competitions. Arsenal 2nd, 21 points, one defeat in thirteen. THE RUN Arsenal have not beaten Liverpool since February 2024. The last four meetings: three draws and a 1-0 defeat at Anfield in August 2025. MISSING Saka (quad) and Saliba (back) for Arsenal. Szoboszlai and Wirtz are doubts for Liverpool, with Frimpong and Ekitike out. The Iraola problem Begin with the tactical shape of it, because this is not the Liverpool anyone scouted a year ago. Andoni Iraola replaced Arne Slot on a two-year contract in June and has spent four months dismantling the idea that Anfield must be a possession fortress. Against Brighton on Sunday his side won 2-0 with 35.6 per cent of the ball, which Opta logged as Liverpool's second-lowest possession share in a Premier League home win since 2003-04. Brighton had 64 per cent and one shot on target. That is the Iraola signature transplanted from Bournemouth: a high, aggressive, man-oriented press, an invitation to play out, and then four players arriving in the box within six seconds of the turnover. Which sets up the key battle, and it is not the one the television build-up will choose. Liverpool's press is designed to force the ball into the full-back channels and then trap it there. Arsenal's build-up this season has leaned harder than ever on Myles Lewis-Skelly stepping inside from left-back and on Ben White holding width on the right, because William Saliba has not played a minute all season and Jurriën Timber has been in and out. With Riccardo Calafiori only just cleared and Piero Hincapié freshly back from an ankle problem, the back four that walks out at Anfield may be the fourth or fifth distinct combination Arteta has used in thirteen games. Against a side that hunts exactly those players, composure in the first fifteen minutes will decide more than any substitution. "It will be weeks." Mikel Arteta on Bukayo Saka, October 23 Who plays wide, and who scores The selection questions multiply from there. Noni Madueke has taken the right wing and done it well, scoring the only goal at Nottingham Forest and starting on the left in Munich before drifting back to his natural side. He is not Saka and Arteta has sensibly stopped asking him to be: where Saka manufactured chances by holding the touchline and inverting late, Madueke is at his best attacking a defender who is already moving. That suits a transition game, which is precisely what Sunday will be. Eze , meanwhile, has two goals in his last three appearances and looks liberated by a role that lets him begin wide and finish central. The uncomfortable question is the centre forward. Viktor Gyökeres has not scored for Arsenal this season. Not in the Premier League, not in Europe, not in the Carabao Cup. He assisted Ezri Konsa 's opener against Everton and played the one-two that set up Rice in Munich, and Arteta's defence of him has been consistent rather than grudging: "He was unlucky two or three moments. He's in front of goal, he's won the position to both centre-backs," the manager said on Monday, adding that the ball simply does not arrive. The data broadly agrees that Arsenal's open-play threat is up on last season. It does not change the fact that a title race in which your striker has nothing is a title race fought with a hand behind your back, and that Kai Havertz , three goals already, is the man Arteta has turned to when the game needs a goal rather than a structure. Title race tracker, after eight matches 1. Manchester City 21 pts (+11) 2. Arsenal 21 pts (+8) 3. Brighton & Hove Albion 16 pts 4. Liverpool 15 pts 5. Chelsea 13 pts City lost 2-1 at Aston Villa on Saturday while Arsenal were beating Everton. Arsenal have conceded five goals in eight league games and kept five clean sheets. What is actually at stake The stakes are plainer than usual, because the table has closed up in Arsenal's favour at exactly the moment their squad has thinned. Manchester City went to Villa Park on Saturday and lost 2-1; Arsenal beat Everton and drew level on 21 points, second only on goal difference. In other words the champions have been handed the initiative in the week they lost their most reliable attacker. Win at Anfield and they go top with the hardest away day of the autumn behind them. Lose and the narrative writes itself: a title defence that survives on set-piece margins and a goalkeeper, with no striker and no Saka. Which is unfair, but not entirely. The record at least is suggestive. Arsenal have not beaten Liverpool in any competition since February 2024, a run of three draws and one defeat that spans the whole of their rise from nearly-men to champions. They drew 0-0 at the Emirates last January and lost 1-0 at Anfield the previous August, both games in which they controlled possession and found no way through. Iraola's version of Liverpool will offer them far more of the ball and far less space. On the evidence of Munich, where Arsenal were second best for forty minutes and still left with a point, that may suit them better than anyone expects. Before any of that there is tonight: League Two Fleetwood Town , in the last sixteen of the Carabao Cup for the first time in their history, with no VAR and penalties straight after ninety minutes. Arteta has made nine changes and handed debuts to Illan Meslier and the 18-year-old Ceadach O'Neill . "We know the risk," he said. "Show them the Arsenal shirt and what we represent and that's it." It is the right instinct. It is also, this week, the second story. The Set-Piece Machine Went Quiet for 153 Days Arsenal scored nineteen Premier League goals from corners last season, a competition record. Before Ezri Konsa's header on Saturday they had scored none at all this season. The numbers say this is mostly not a conspiracy. Konsa 's seventh-minute finish from Martin Ødegaard 's corner against Everton ended a run of thirteen competitive games and 153 days without a goal from a corner or free kick. The previous one came from Madueke 's delivery against Crystal Palace on the final day of last season, in May. For a team whose set plays accounted for 26.8 per cent of their goals in a title-winning campaign, the highest share any Premier League champion has recorded, that is a genuine structural absence rather than a quirk. The Opta Analyst breakdown published on Saturday is worth reading in full, because it argues against the simplest explanations. Arsenal are still whipping in almost as many crosses from corners (84.9 per cent this season against 86.6 per cent last) and every single crossed corner has been an inswinger. They are actually winning first contact far more often: 42.9 per cent, second highest in the league, against 28.3 per cent last season. What has fallen is the quality of what follows. Shots from corners are down from 2.8 a game to 2.1, expected goals from corners down from 0.36 a game to 0.22, and the conversion rate from a league-best 8.8 per cent of corners to nothing at all. Arsenal are 1.55 goals below their corner expected goals, the second-largest shortfall in the division behind Liverpool. The corner, season by season Per Premier League game, 2025-26 against 2026-27. Each pair is drawn to its own scale by the Digest, from the Opta Analyst figures cited below. Shots from corners, 2025-26 2.8 per game Shots from corners, 2026-27 2.1 per game Expected goals from corners, 2025-26 0.36 per game Expected goals from corners, 2026-27 0.22 per game Goals from corners, 2025-26 (19 in all) 0.50 per game Goals from corners, 2026-27 (none in the league) 0.00 per game Three explanations have real weight. The first is personnel: Saliba has missed the entire season and Timber , one of last year's most dangerous near-post runners, has been intermittent. Havertz now leads Arsenal for first contacts from attacking corners with four; Gabriel , the totem of the whole operation, has one. The second explanation is placement. Arsenal have cut central six-yard-box deliveries by nearly eight percentage points and added almost exactly that volume to the near post, chasing flick-on routines that die on the first defender when the delivery is a fraction flat. The third explanation is simply the league: corners have produced 9.8 per cent of Premier League goals this season against 18.0 per cent last, and referees are awarding defending teams free kicks from four per cent of corners, the highest rate in seven seasons. Grappling is being policed. Nicolas Jover 's choreography depended on it being tolerated. The consoling counterpoint is that Arsenal have not needed it. Open-play expected goals are up roughly seventeen per cent, from 1.06 a game to 1.24, and the team is second in the table having conceded five league goals. A side that has swapped a dead-ball edge for a live-ball one has traded sideways, not down. But dead-ball goals are the ones you can still manufacture at Anfield when a press has pinned you in your own half for an hour, and that is the context in which Konsa's header mattered more than its timing suggested. Transfer News Brugge Draw a Line in the Sand Over Tresoldi Arsenal's interest in the Italian striker is real and reported by Sky. The selling club's answer, delivered through the Belgian press this week, was about as flat a no as a board can give. The most substantial live thread of Arsenal's autumn runs through Belgium. Nicolò Tresoldi , 22, has twelve goals in fourteen games for Club Brugge this season, four of them in three Champions League matches including one against Aston Villa , and sixteen in twenty-seven for the Germany under-21s. Sky Sports Germany reported this week that Arsenal are seriously interested and had him on their radar over the summer, while judging a January move unlikely and a summer approach the likelier route. The Belgian outlet Nieuwsblad went further, reporting that Arsenal are weighing a January bid with Barcelona also interested. Status: concrete interest, no bid, two independent reports. Brugge's response was unusually direct. A board member told Nieuwsblad that "there is no price for Nicolò, and there never will be," adding that any January offer would be "completely irrelevant" to them. The club rejected €35m from AS Roma in the summer, Tresoldi is contracted to 2029, and the stated position is that they expect to sell him eventually but want a marquee exit rather than a mid-season one. Read that as a price being set by refusing to set one. The strategic logic is obvious, and it is also why the Digest urges patience with it. Arsenal's centre forward has not scored this season. Havertz is 27 and has never been a volume striker. On the Here We Go podcast in September Fabrizio Romano described Arsenal's striker search as neither "imminent or urgent," said the club were "very happy with the strikers they have," and pointed to summer 2027 rather than January, with Eli Junior Kroupi of Bournemouth named as a player they may revisit. Romano also flagged right-back as the position to watch. Nothing reported since has contradicted that framing. A Tresoldi deal in January would be a reaction to Saka's injury as much as to Gyökeres's drought, and Arsenal's recruitment under Andrea Berta has not been a reactive operation. Calafiori, and the Price of Being Indispensable Chelsea have not gone away. Real Madrid have been mentioned. The eye-catching valuation attached to all of it comes from an aggregator, not a tier-one source. Riccardo Calafiori scored twenty-three seconds into the Community Shield and equalised against Leeds United on October 10, and has become the kind of left-sided defender who starts conversations. Chelsea retain interest after a bid Arsenal rejected, Real Madrid have been linked, and the figure circulating is a €100m asking price that would be a world record for a defender. That number originates with CaughtOffside and has not been stood up by a tier-one reporter, so treat it as mood music rather than a valuation. Status: rumour, single-sourced on the fee. What is harder to dismiss is the squad arithmetic. With Saliba absent all season and Timber and Hincapié both carrying knocks, Calafiori is simultaneously Arsenal's most valuable asset in that part of the pitch and their least dispensable one. Any serious January bid would land in the middle of an injury crisis. It is not a coincidence that reporting on an Arsenal interest in Xavi Espart , the 19-year-old Barcelona full-back, has been framed as insurance against losing him.
