Arteta singled out the cameo as a turning point. Scouting the Next Opponent Liverpool, Rebuilt From the Press Up Andoni Iraola has spent four months turning Anfield into a counterattacking ground. Arsenal visit a side that no longer wants the ball and is suddenly very good at not having it. Liverpool sacked Arne Slot and appointed Andoni Iraola on a two-year contract on June 4, then spent more than £200m rebuilding around him: Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain for a reported £106m, Jérémy Jacquet from Rennes for £55m, Víctor Muñoz from Osasuna for £34.5m and Ronald Araújo on loan from Barcelona with a purchase option. On the other side of the ledger, Mohamed Salah , Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konaté all left on free transfers and Curtis Jones went to Inter Milan . It is a different club, and for six weeks it looked like a confused one. It is not confused now. After a 0-3 home humiliation by Manchester City on October 11, Liverpool have won four in a row in all competitions, including 2-1 at Brentford and 2-0 at home to Brighton . They sit fourth on fifteen points from eight, one behind Brighton, and third in the Champions League league phase on nine points. Alexander Isak has six league goals, three in his last three league games, and Barcola has assisted him in each of the past two. Cody Gakpo has been impressive from the left. Florian Wirtz manufactured the opener against Brighton with the shot Pascal Groß turned into his own net. The three Arsenal must stop are therefore clear. Isak is the finisher and the first press trigger, dropping into the left channel to drag a centre-back out. Barcola is the width and the cut-back, switched to the right against Brighton and immediately decisive from there, which puts him directly into whichever of Lewis-Skelly or Calafiori plays left-back. x: World football, every Wednesday · Arsenal covered separately The Weekly Soccer Digest Wednesday Edition · October 21, 2026 · Vol. 1 In this edition The Lead · Como's Night · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Mourinho Walks Back Into the Camp Nou Thirteen years after he left Spain, Jose Mourinho returns to Barcelona as Real Madrid's manager, six points adrift of a side that had won eleven straight until Tuesday, and without the two wingers who were supposed to win him the game. T here is no gentle way to walk into the Spotify Camp Nou, and Jose Mourinho has never looked for one. On Sunday evening, at 1 p.m. Pacific, he takes Real Madrid back to the ground where he spent three seasons in open warfare with the institution he is about to visit, and he does it as the underdog. Barcelona have won nine from nine in La Liga. They have 27 points. Real Madrid have 21, and are third, behind Atletico Madrid as well. A Barcelona win on Sunday makes the gap nine points before Halloween. What makes the fixture genuinely hard to call is that both sides arrive bruised in different places. Barcelona's winning run, eleven matches across all competitions, ended on Tuesday night at the Parc des Princes, where Paris Saint-Germain beat them 4-2 in the best game of the Champions League season so far. It was not a collapse. It was something more worrying for Hansi Flick : two individual errors, one from Lamine Yamal inside his own half for Desire Doue 's opener, one from Warren Zaire-Emery 's opponent under a high ball, and a midfield that could not hold the ball when Vitinha decided to take the game. Barcelona equalised twice, through Xavi Espart and then Yamal himself, and still lost by two. Real Madrid, meanwhile, will play the biggest match of their season so far without Vinicius Junior , who is suspended, and without Rodrygo , who has a cruciate ligament injury. That is a Clasico without either of the wingers who have carried Madrid's transitions for the better part of five years. Kylian Mbappe has nine La Liga goals and will almost certainly start centrally. Beyond him, Mourinho is short of the specific thing his teams have always been built to do, which is run at a high line with pace in the wide areas. Ferland Mendy is back in training. Raul Asencio is not available. Madrid at least arrive in form: they beat RB Leipzig 4-1 at the Bernabeu on Wednesday night, Mbappe and Arda Guler among the scorers, a third straight Champions League win. El Clasico: Key Facts Kickoff Sunday October 25, 1:00 p.m. Pacific (9:00 p.m. in Barcelona) Venue Spotify Camp Nou, La Liga matchday 10 Managers Hansi Flick (Barcelona), Jose Mourinho (Real Madrid) League Barcelona 1st, 27 pts from 9. Real Madrid 3rd, 21 pts from 9 Barcelona out Olmo, Christensen, Eric Garcia, Kounde, Bardghji, de Jong Real Madrid out Vinicius Junior (suspended), Rodrygo, Asencio. Mendy back in training Head to head Barcelona 29 wins, Real Madrid 21, 10 draws Which leaves the tactical question of the week: does Mourinho try to win this game, or does he try to stop Barcelona winning it? His record at the Camp Nou in his first spell suggests he is perfectly willing to do the latter and absorb the criticism, and there is a reasonable argument that 21 points from nine games is not a platform from which to gamble. Barcelona's shape under Flick is still the most aggressive in Europe's top five leagues, a high line that invites exactly the ball in behind that Mbappe has spent his career running onto. PSG hurt Barcelona by playing through them rather than over them. Madrid, without Vinicius and Rodrygo , may not have that option. Barcelona's own absentee list is longer. Dani Olmo came off injured in Paris. Andreas Christensen and Eric Garcia have thigh problems, Jules Kounde a sprained ankle. Roony Bardghji ruptured a cruciate ligament in training in August and Frenkie de Jong has been out since tearing the medial collateral ligament in his right knee at the World Cup. The absence that matters most tactically is at centre back: with Christensen out, Ronald Araujo on loan at Liverpool and Kounde injured, Gerard Martin is Flick 's only natural left-sided option. Catalan reporting this month names a left-footed centre back as Barcelona's clearest squad need, and the club cannot address it in January without selling first. More on that below. The two squads were rebuilt around each other over the summer, which gives Sunday an extra edge. Barcelona spent roughly 174 million euros on seven players, headlined by Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United for 70 million plus up to 10 million in variables and Rodri from Manchester City for 60 million plus up to 15 million, with Karim Adeyemi arriving from Borussia Dortmund and Joao Cancelo back on a free. Robert Lewandowski left at the end of his contract. Ferran Torres was sold to PSG for 48.5 million euros, which is why he was on the pitch in Paris on Tuesday in the other shirt, and why he hit the post against the club that made him. "I don't care about [the favourites tag] because I don't see PSG as the favourite. This match isn't decisive. The decisive month will be in April." Luis Enrique, after PSG 4-2 Barcelona The individual duel to watch is Raphinha against whichever full back Mourinho trusts. Raphinha leads the Pichichi race with twelve goals, three clear of Mbappe , and is the one Barcelona attacker whose form has not wobbled. Yamal has eight in La Liga and nine goals with ten assists across eleven appearances in all competitions, and Joan Laporta chose the week of the PSG tie to tell L'Equipe that he is going nowhere. "He's a Barca fan and came through La Masia," Laporta said, in beIN Sports' English rendering of the French interview. "All of that helps when it comes to renewing a contract. We're not worried." Raphinha Barcelona 12 Kylian Mbappe Real Madrid 9 Lamine Yamal Barcelona 8 Sergio Camello Rayo Vallecano 7 Ante Budimir Osasuna 7 The head-to-head record in the fixture's modern run reads 29 wins to Barcelona, 21 to Real Madrid, ten draws. None of that will matter much by Sunday evening. What will matter is whether Mourinho , who built his reputation on exactly this kind of night, can produce one more of them with half his attack missing, and whether a Barcelona side that has not lost a league game all season can absorb the first real test of its nerve. The tie is at 1 p.m. Pacific, 9 p.m. in Barcelona. Spain's clocks go back that morning, so the local time reads the same as it did in September while the Pacific conversion shifts. Como's Night Como 4, Manchester United 1 A club playing its first Champions League campaign took Manchester United apart on the shore of Lake Como, and the questions about Michael Carrick are now the loudest in English football. Nico Paz scored inside two minutes. By the time Anastasios Douvikas made it two early in the second half, Manchester United had managed no shots on target at all in the first half, had committed nine fouls to Como 's two, and had seen 62 per cent of the ball go the other way. Michael Carrick made two substitutions at the interval, sending on Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba for Matheus Cunha and Andrey Santos . It did not help. Como finished 4-1 winners, with Paz scoring twice and assisting another, and Douvikas and Ramon also on the scoresheet, according to Corriere dello Sport . It was Como's first home match in the competition. Como are fifth in Serie A on 14 points, have won four of seven, and beat Fiorentina 3-1 away on Sunday. Cesc Fabregas , whose contract runs to June 2028, has built something that now has to be taken seriously rather than enjoyed as a curiosity. His line after the match, to Gianluca Di Marzio , was about the next one rather than this one: "Crediamo tanto in Baturina. Vogliamo diventare una realta solida." We believe a great deal in Baturina. We want to become a solid reality. United's position is harder to describe charitably. They are 13th in the Premier League on seven points from seven games, with one win, and drew 1-1 at Leeds United on Sunday. They have now lost to Atletico Madrid and Como in successive Champions League matchdays after opening with a 4-0 win over Sabah . Carrick used his press conference last weekend to talk about January, telling Sky Sports : "When the next transfer window comes, you want to plan and you want to make the best of it. Whatever that looks like at this stage, we don't quite know. But without doubt, there's opportunity because the transfer window is open." Sky reported centre back and left back as the priorities. With Luke Shaw injured, United currently have no senior left back. The commercial irony is sharp. In late September the club reported record revenue of 677 million pounds achieved without European football. It now has European football and a 4-1 defeat to a club that was in Serie B three years ago. Across the rest of matchday 3 on Wednesday night, nine matches produced 34 goals and exactly one draw. Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4-1, Aston Villa made it three wins from three by seeing off Viking 3-1, Club Brugge beat Lens 3-0 and Inter Milan edged Shakhtar Donetsk 1-0 with ten men after Alessandro Bastoni was sent off. Real Betis beat Feyenoord 1-0 through an Isco penalty, Galatasaray came from 2-1 down to win 4-2 at Lille with Victor Osimhen scoring, and Bayern Munich were held 2-2 at home by Arsenal. The shock was in Lisbon, where LASK , pointless after two matchdays, won 3-2 at Sporting CP . Transfer News Europe's summer window closed on September 1, so nothing below is a completed transfer. What is moving instead is the thing that always moves in late October: the January pre-contract clock, which starts on New Year's Day and turns every player whose deal expires in June 2027 into either an asset to be sold now or a free agent to be lost later. Certainty tiers are stated for every item. The January 1 Clock Is Already Driving the Market Every contract expiring in June 2027 becomes a pre-contract target on New Year's Day. That single date explains most of this week's reporting. Under FIFA rules a player inside the final six months of a contract can agree a pre-contract with a club in another country. From January 1 that applies to the whole June 2027 cohort, and clubs with sellable players and no signatures are suddenly motivated. The cleanest illustration is at Bournemouth , where Rob Dorsett and Mark McAdam of Sky Sports News reported on October 16 that the club will consider offers in excess of 80 million pounds plus add-ons in January for Alex Scott , who has refused a new contract reported to be the best the club has ever offered. Status: concrete interest with a club valuation set, no bid on the table. Fabrizio Romano corroborated it four days later, saying Chelsea are "definitely there" and have had several contacts with Scott's representatives after a rejected summer bid, and that Liverpool made calls in late June and early July without ever bidding. Scott is 23, an England international, currently injured, and has a little over 18 months left. Marco Rose was blunt when asked: "I told you that Alex Scott was going to stay in the summer. He's a player of our club and now he's injured. If he is back, he's playing for Bournemouth." The same mechanism is producing stories everywhere. Jean-Philippe Mateta is out of contract in June 2027 at Crystal Palace and, per talkSPORT material carried in Sky's Paper Talk on October 20, is showing no inclination to extend, with Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur both linked. Graeme Bailey of TEAMtalk reported in late September that United's director of football Jason Wilcox rates his Premier League goals record. Status: concrete interest plus reported player willingness, no talks between clubs. Mateta has made two appearances this season with a hamstring problem, which is the obvious complication. In Spain the same clock is ticking loudest at Sevilla . Javier Merino of JaviSFC reported on October 21 that centre back Andres Castrin , out of contract on June 30 2027, agreed terms in early October on a three-year extension with a significant rise and a 50 million euro release clause, and that the club is still waiting for a formal response from his agency. From January 1 he can sign elsewhere for nothing. Bayer Leverkusen are following closely; Valencia , Real Sociedad , Leeds United and Espanyol are named as interested. This is a Sevilla-specialist outlet rather than a national one, so treat the detail as single-sourced, though the structural facts are not in dispute. Garcia Plaza said in late September: "Ojala renueve, ojala." Liverpool Have Three Midfielders on One List Alex Scott, Lamine Camara and Adam Wharton are all live Liverpool links inside ten days. Barcelona Have About One Million Euros of Room A detailed look at the club's fair-play position concludes that any January signing must be preceded by a sale. The renewals are eating the margin. Artur Lopez published the single hardest number in this week's European reporting. Writing for Cronica Global on October 11, he set out Barcelona 's position under La Liga's salary rules: the club's limit has risen from 432 million euros to 582 million, and its sporting costs have risen 115 million to 581 million. Nico Paz, Chelsea, and Real Madrid's 80 Million Euro Button Como own him outright. Madrid can buy him back next summer for a fixed price. Chelsea have been watching, and Como's number starts with a one. The most interesting contractual object in European football right now sits on the shore of Lake Como. Marco Conterio of TUTTOmercatoWEB reported on October 21 that Chelsea staff have watched Nico Paz in recent Serie A and Champions League matches and are not deterred by the price. The sequencing is the story: if Madrid press the button at 80 million, they buy a 22-year-old playmaker for less than Como could get on the open market, and Como's upside evaporates. x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest One club, every front, every Tuesday No. 10 · Season 2026/27 Tuesday, October 20, 2026 Read this edition on the web In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Back to Munich, Carrying a Different Kind of Problem Arsenal arrive at the Allianz Arena as champions of England, unbeaten in Europe and yet to concede a Champions League goal. They have also scored eleven times in seven league games. Wednesday night asks the question this season keeps asking: can a team this good at not losing find a way to actually win something bigger? T here is a version of this week that writes itself. Arsenal go to Bayern Munich on Wednesday with fourteen consecutive Champions League league-phase wins behind them, two clean sheets from two this season, a Premier League title in the cabinet for the first time since 2004 and a manager who has just signed on until 2030. They are second in the table, three points behind Manchester City , and they have lost once all season. By any ordinary accounting, this is a club in rude health walking into the most glamorous fixture on its calendar. Then you look at Sunday afternoon. Arsenal went to the City Ground, held seventy-four per cent of the ball, played 629 passes at ninety per cent accuracy, and registered precisely one shot on target. It went in, because Noni Madueke drove inside from the left on eighty minutes and the ball glanced off Jair Cunha and past Matz Sels . Without that deflection this is a goalless afternoon against a side that had not scored at home in the league all season, and the conversation this morning is very different. It reaches you five days late and stands as the record of that day. The lead previews a match that has since been played: Manchester City lost 4-2 at home to Paris Saint-Germain , and in Rome Real Madrid came from 3-1 down to beat Roma 4-3, Antonio Rudiger scoring the winner inside a seven-minute collapse. Everything below stands as written that evening, and the fixtures under What to Watch begin on 15 October. The Lead The champions of Europe walk into the one place nobody is losing Paris Saint-Germain have won the last two Champions Leagues. Manchester City have won all eight games of Enzo Maresca’s reign. Wednesday night at the Etihad is the first evening this season that asks one of those sentences to give way. T here is a particular kind of fixture that the league phase was invented to produce, and this is it. Manchester City against Paris Saint-Germain , in the middle of October, with nothing eliminated and everything implied. The Etihad is sold out. The visitors are the holders of the European Cup, and the holders of the one before that. The hosts have not lost a match since the summer, under a manager who was appointed on the last Monday of June and has not yet found out what a bad week feels like. Start with Enzo Maresca , because his start is the statistical story of the European autumn. Six Premier League games, six wins, sixteen goals scored and five conceded, eighteen points and a three-point cushion at the top. City’s own records department notes that this equals the best opening run by a new manager in Premier League history, matching Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea in 2009/10 and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer ’s caretaker spell at Manchester United in December 2018. Win at home to Ipswich Town on Saturday and it becomes a record outright. Add the Champions League and the domestic cup and the number is eight from eight, per the club . The win that changed the temperature was Sunday’s. City went to Anfield and won 3-0, a scoreline that flatters nobody and settles nothing, because it arrived on the back of a red card. Liverpool were level and comfortable when Ryan Gravenberch collected a second yellow on 62 minutes; Erling Haaland scored two minutes and 37 seconds later, Jeremy Doku followed on 68 and Rayan Cherki finished it on 78. Jamie Carragher called the first booking “a shocking decision” and Gary Neville called the second “very soft”. Andoni Iraola , whose side had not lost all season, said the first foul “should never have been a yellow”. None of that changes the ladder. Liverpool are ninth and nine points back. Route and key facts Manchester City v Paris Saint-Germain City’s season Eight wins from eight in all competitions. Six from six in the Premier League: 16 scored, 5 conceded, 18 points, three clear. Beat Porto 2-0 away on matchday one. PSG’s season Champions League holders, and winners in 2025 and 2026, having beaten Arsenal 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in Budapest on 30 May. Sixth in Ligue 1 on 11 points. Beat Slovan Bratislava 6-1 on matchday one. The benches Enzo Maresca, appointed 29 June 2026, succeeding Pep Guardiola. Luis Enrique, in a fourth season that has already brought two European Cups. The occasion Etihad Stadium, sold out. Kick-off noon Pacific on Wednesday 14 October. Guardiola expected in attendance. Next up Matchday three, Tuesday 20 October: PSG host Barcelona , City host AEK Athens . So City arrive in rude health. The interesting half of this fixture is the other one. PSG are not the team that beat Arsenal on penalties in Budapest at the end of May, because three of that night’s forwards have gone. Bradley Barcola is at Liverpool, and scored his first hat-trick for them in Austria on Wednesday afternoon. Randal Kolo Muani is at Juventus . Goncalo Ramos is at Milan , and Lee Kang-in is at Atletico Madrid . In their place Luis Enrique has Ferran Torres , bought from Barcelona for a reported fee around 41.5m pounds eleven days after he scored the goal that won Spain the World Cup, and Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco for around 43m, and Mika Godts from Ajax for around 39m. That reconstruction has shown in the league. PSG are sixth in Ligue 1 on eleven points, three behind Monaco, having drawn their first two matches, lost at home to Monaco in early September and lost the Trophee des Champions to Lens in August. Three straight league wins have steadied it, the most recent a 3-1 over Le Mans in which Akliouche scored his first PSG goal and Desire Doue missed a late penalty. Luis Enrique called the afternoon “an almost perfect result” and then conceded the obvious qualifier: “We conceded a goal, and it was tough.” “As a football fan, I like to watch City play.” Luis Enrique , speaking before travelling to Manchester In Europe, though, the machine still looks like the machine. PSG opened with a 6-1 dismantling of Slovan Bratislava in which Ousmane Dembele scored twice inside 22 minutes and Torres helped himself to a hat-trick. Dembele and Nuno Mendes were rested against Le Mans specifically to be available on Wednesday, and both trained through the week. Senny Mayulu is the absentee, though reports of the problem range from a thigh injury picked up with France’s under-21s to a dead leg, so treat the length of it as unsettled. Matchday two, Tuesday night Thirty-two goals in nine matches Galatasaray 1-4 Barcelona Batrakov 28; Cancelo 43, Fermin Lopez 50, Gordon 53, Adeyemi 65. Lamine Yamal made two. Inter 3-4 Club Brugge Tresoldi 30 pen, 63, 74; Vermant 87. Lautaro Martinez 44, 81; Bonny 90+3. Inter had 31 shots. Viking 3-3 Bayern Munich Stensness 2, Christiansen 38, Haugen 90; Kane 54 pen, 60, Luis Diaz 71. Olise sent off. Atletico Madrid 2-0 Man Utd Barrios inside a minute, Lookman late. Leny Yoro sent off. Villarreal 3-1 Napoli Rrahmani 8; Mikautadze 23, Mourino 26, Oluwaseyi 86. Lens 0-2 Sporting CP Luis Suarez 22, Issa Doumbia 74. RB Leipzig 1-0 PSV Gruda 75. Vandevoordt saved Perisic ’s penalty. Sabah 2-0 Slavia Praha Parris 49, Mickels late. A first league-phase win. Arsenal 3-0 Lille Timber , Saka and Eze . Lille ’s second defeat in two. Tactically this is a collision of two high lines and two very fast front threes, which usually means it is decided in the five yards behind the full-backs. PSG’s great structural strength is the Vitinha and Joao Neves axis, which wins the second ball before anyone else arrives at it; their great structural risk is that Achraf Hakimi and Mendes push so high that the channels either side of Marquinhos and Willian Pacho become open country. City have spent six weeks showing they can run into exactly that. Doku and Cherki both scored at Anfield from positions nobody assigned them, and Haaland leads the Premier League scoring charts without having had a difficult afternoon yet. There is also the matter that will not be in the team sheet. This is City’s first European night since an independent commission found the club guilty of almost all of the financial charges brought against it by the Premier League , covering nine seasons to 2017/18, including what the league’s own statement called “sham” sponsorship arrangements used to inflate revenue by more than 900m pounds. City lodged an appeal on 1 October, to be heard within twelve weeks. Sanctions have not yet been set. Maresca was asked about it in the international break and said simply: “I completely trust the club.” Asked whether past titles were tainted, he answered: “Absolutely not.” And the last wrinkle is the sweetest. Pep Guardiola , who resigned in the summer after nine completed seasons, is expected in the stands. Maresca was asked whether that was awkward and declined the invitation: “He can come at any time he wants.” Nine years of City’s European identity were built by the man in the seat; the new one is unbeaten and has a European Cup holder to measure himself against. Kick-off was noon Pacific on the day this was written, which is to say that the edition and the football match were meant to reach the world at the same moment. Matchday three gives the loser no rest either: PSG host Barcelona next Tuesday, and City go again on the same night. Mourinho goes back to Rome with his own October on the line Four months into the Real Madrid job, Jose Mourinho returns to the club he managed for two and a half years, without Vinicius Junior and with four defenders in the treatment room. The symmetry was always going to be too good to leave alone. Jose Mourinho was appointed Real Madrid manager in June on a three-year deal to 2029, his second spell at the club and his first since 2013. His first October in charge has handed him a trip to the Roma he managed from 2021 to 2024, and with whom he won the inaugural Conference League in 2022. He is still sung about in that stadium. He is also, four months in, being written about in Madrid in the way Madrid managers get written about. The numbers behind the noise are not catastrophic and not comfortable. Madrid are fourth in La Liga on 18 points from eight, six wins and two defeats, beaten by Atletico Madrid and by Real Betis . Infobae noted this week that the tally is three points worse than Xabi Alonso ’s side managed at the same stage, and framed a five-game October in fifteen days as the stretch that could shape Mourinho’s future. Saturday’s 1-0 over Villarreal was won by Diomande , the 140m euro summer signing, with his first Madrid goal, assisted by Fede Valverde . Kylian Mbappe hit a post, was twice denied, and was whistled by some of his own supporters. The afternoon’s lasting damage was not the performance. Vinicius Junior , a substitute, had a goal disallowed and was then sent off after a VAR review showed him pulling the hair of Villarreal ’s Nathan Saliba . On Wednesday the Spanish federation’s disciplinary committee handed down four matches: two for violent conduct away from the ball and two for protesting to the referee. Madrid’s claim of a “manifest material error” was rejected. He misses Sevilla on Sunday and, more to the point, he misses the Clasico at Barcelona on 25 October. His own public response was short: “The joy continues. My apologies to my team and the fans.” Mourinho skipped his post-match press conference entirely after Villarreal, giving no reason, having himself been booked for protesting. That followed a September in which he produced a printed sheet of disputed refereeing decisions after the derby defeat to Atletico, prompting league president Javier Tebas to reject any suggestion of a conspiracy and Madrid to reply that Tebas is “not the owner of the competition”. Four defenders were unavailable for the flight to Rome: Ferland Mendy , Eder Militao , Rodrygo and Raul Asencio , whose prognosis the club lists as pending. Roma, by contrast, have rarely looked more organised. Gian Piero Gasperini ’s side are third in Serie A on 14 points with the best goal difference in the division and the best defence in it, three goals conceded in six games. They drew 1-1 at Fenerbahce on matchday one and held Como to the league’s first goalless draw on Sunday, a night that cost them Donyell Malen to the first red card of his career. Malen leads Serie A’s scoring charts with six and serves his domestic ban against Genoa on Saturday, which means he was free to play against Madrid. Mourinho, of all people, will have noted that. Erling Haaland to Barcelona , which traces to an unverified social account. Carvajal’s long wait ends in the unlikeliest place A Champions League winner with Real Madrid, out of contract since June, has agreed terms with a club 14th in La Liga. The only remaining obstacle is a spreadsheet. Dani Carvajal is 34 and has been a free agent since 30 June, when a Real Madrid contract that spanned six European Cups expired without renewal. This week it became clear where he is going, and it is not where anyone would have guessed: Getafe , fourteenth in La Liga on eight points, managed by Jose Bordalas , playing in a 17,000-seat stadium on the southern edge of Madrid. The paper trail is unusually clean. Getafe ’s interest was first reported by ABC. Marca reported on 6 October that an agreement had been reached, subject to La Liga approving the club’s squad-cost position. Getafe’s president Angel Torres confirmed as much on DAZN, saying Carvajal had passed a medical and that the move is a free transfer: “If I can reach an agreement with La Liga, he will most likely join us.” By 8 October the deal was still being described as at risk on exactly that point. Fabrizio Romano now reports the salary has been cleared and that only the official announcement remains. Where it stands Agreement reached, announcement pending. Reported by Fabrizio Romano, after Marca on 6 October and confirmation on camera from Getafe ’s own president. The lesson is less about Carvajal than about the mechanism. Getafe are operating under a La Liga squad-cost limit that is a rounding error next to the clubs Carvajal spent his career beating. Real Madrid’s 2026/27 limit was set at 832.78m euros, Barcelona’s at 582.76m, Atletico’s at 361.27m and Sevilla ’s at 20.16m, the lowest in the division. In that world, a free transfer is not a bargain. It is a negotiation with a regulator. Madrid quietly solve their biggest 2027 problem Thibaut Courtois was on every list of players whose contracts expire next June. He will not be on the next one. Thibaut Courtois has agreed a new Real Madrid contract to June 2028, according to Fabrizio Romano , who describes it as done with only the club’s statement outstanding. AS had reported on 13 September that the two sides were close to an extension on those exact terms. Madrid have not yet announced it. Where it stands Agreed, announcement pending. Romano, with AS reporting the same terms a month ago. It matters more than a goalkeeper renewal usually does, because Madrid’s summer 2027 exposure is real. Antonio Rudiger and Brahim Diaz are also into the final year of their deals, and the club has already spent heavily at the other end of the pitch, including the 140m euros on Diomande . The one piece of long-term certainty they did buy themselves came in August, when Vinicius Junior signed through to June 2032, a deal that looks rather different in a week when he has been banned for four matches. Kane leaves the door open, and takes a step back from England Bayern’s captain says there have been no talks about a new contract. He also says the idea of going home has faded. Harry Kane ’s Bayern Munich contract runs to 2027, with a release clause reported at around 67m euros. Speaking to Reuters this month, he said he is open to extending beyond it, that no talks have taken place yet, and, most notably, that his desire to return to the Premier League has “decreased”. Where it stands No negotiation under way. The player is publicly receptive, and the release clause is reported rather than confirmed by the club. The timing is interesting because Kane’s own form is not the issue and Bayern’s is. He became the fastest player to 100 Bundesliga goals, reaching the mark in 98 appearances in September’s 7-0 against Union Berlin . He has now scored in nine consecutive Champions League matches, including both of Bayern’s goals from open play and the penalty in Tuesday’s extraordinary 3-3 at Viking in Stavanger. He also provided both assists in the 2-2 at Augsburg on Saturday without scoring, after which he told DAZN it “feels more like a defeat”. Bayern are third, eleven points from five, and have not won in four weeks. A club that has historically let contracts run until the player’s leverage has evaporated is dealing with a 33-year-old centre-forward who is the only reason several of those results were not worse. Expect this one to be settled quietly and in Bayern’s favour, and expect the Premier League clubs who have been waiting for the clause to become usable to read the word “decreased” several more times. Manchester United keep answering a different question The club insists Michael Carrick is safe. Everyone briefing about January is briefing about a left-back. Neither of those is the problem. Six points from six league games is Manchester United ’s worst start since 1986/87. On Tuesday they lost 2-0 at Atletico Madrid , conceding inside a minute to Pablo Barrios and finishing with ten men after Leny Yoro was dismissed. Fabrizio Romano reported on 13 October that the club is “still giving time and confidence” to Michael Carrick , that the players remain with him, and that the results are “not acceptable”. A day later he added that no last-minute change is expected and that United have not contacted any other manager. Where it stands Carrick is backed, for now. Two tier-one reporters arrive at the same answer from opposite directions, and no successor has been approached. David Ornstein landed in the same place from the other direction: he knows of no desire to remove Carrick, but said the manager “needs to improve things” and pointed the rest of the blame at recruitment, executives and owners. He singled out Sunday’s trip to Leeds United as “massive”. Nicolo Schira has gone further, naming Leeds, Como and Bournemouth as the decisive run. Reports linking Eddie Howe and Fabian Hurzeler to the job trace back to unnamed accounts and should be treated as speculation. Antonio Conte is a different case: Romano says he would be open to a mid-season move to a historical club and would not want the Middle East, while explicitly refuting a claim that he was reaching an agreement with INEOS. On the squad, Romano says January is “too early to say” and depends on conditions he did not specify, but that a left-back would not be “crazy money”. The name that keeps recurring is Adrien Truffert of Bournemouth , whom Ornstein valued at around 60m pounds last month while suggesting a deal was more likely in the summer of 2027. Bournemouth are expected to reject January offers. United wanted Newcastle United ’s Lewis Hall in August; Hall has since signed a new contract there. Milan and Inter spend the autumn protecting what they have Two clubs with no money to spend in January are doing the next best thing, which is making sure nobody can take anything for free in June. Inter have opened renewal talks with Federico Dimarco aimed at a contract to 2030, Gazzetta dello Sport reported on 12 October. The club holds a unilateral option to 2028, so there is no cliff edge, and no agreement has been reached. At Milan , Gazzetta reported in late September that Adrien Rabiot is close to a renewal through 2030 with an option year. Nothing is official on either. Where it stands Talks opened at Inter , reported progress at Milan . Neither club has announced anything, and both reports originate with Gazzetta dello Sport. Milan’s more pressing problem is structural. Matteo Gabbia tore a left hamstring with partial tendon involvement at Sassuolo on Sunday and is out for months, with a specialist deciding between surgery and conservative treatment. A club that drew 1-1 that afternoon and sits fifth now has a January window in which a centre-back is close to compulsory. Links to specific names have circulated without attribution and are not worth printing yet. Juventus , meanwhile, are reported by Tuttosport to be considering a striker in January to support Randal Kolo Muani , whose 81st-minute header at Cagliari rescued a point and was his first Serie A goal of the season. They have the balance sheet to think about it: the board approved accounts carrying a forecast 66m euro loss on 29 September and proposed a delegation for a capital increase of up to 250m euros, with Exor confirming an advance. The Rumour Mill Everything else that is moving, and how much of it is real Everything simmering, with the reliability stated plainly. Several of this week’s loudest stories are the thinnest. Advanced, or close to it Marc Bernal ’s Barcelona extension, from 2029 to 2031 with a 500m euro clause, was reported by El Gol Digital on 12 October as closed but unsigned. One non-tier-one source, no club confirmation, and worth watching rather than believing. Barcelona’s last official announcement on the midfielder was a renewal to 2029 a year ago. Certainty: single-sourced report of an agreement. Concrete interest, with a club saying no Alex Scott is the window’s clearest example of a selling club getting its answer in first. Bournemouth have told Chelsea and Real Madrid that the midfielder is not leaving in January, per talkSPORT as relayed on 7 October. Chelsea bid more than 60m pounds in the summer and were refused. Reports of a nine-figure valuation are the writers’ estimates rather than anyone’s quoted number, and the two best accounts of his contract length contradict each other, one saying a single year remains and one saying 2028. Rumour, and treat it that way A 70m euro January bid from Liverpool for Barcelona ’s Jules Kounde was reported on 14 October by TheHardTackle, attributing it to the Spanish site Fichajes, with the admission that no formal talks have happened. That is a low-reliability chain and nothing more. The same applies to Pedro Porro to Real Madrid and to the various claims about Florian Wirtz ’s future, both of which currently live on aggregator sites rather than with any reporter who would put a name to them. The loudest of the lot deserves a flat warning. The widely circulated story that Erling Haaland will leave Manchester City for Barcelona in 2027, with a figure around 130m pounds attached, traces back to an unverified social-media account and has been repeated by outlets that did not check it. There is no statement from either club or from the player, and Spanish reporting indicates there is no relegation release clause of the kind the story depends on. Certainty: noise. It is included here only because readers will have seen it everywhere else. Stated needs, which is where real deals start Paris Saint-Germain were reported by L’Equipe in early September to want two things in January: a right-footed centre-back to understudy Marquinhos , and an attacker. Juventus want a striker. Milan need a centre-back. Manchester United want a left-back. Those four sentences are more predictive of what actually happens on 1 January than any name currently trending, and three of the four needs were created by injuries or exits that happened in the last six weeks. Most goals: Brighton. Most goal involvements: Joao Pedro, 8. One team has turned the Premier League into an arithmetic problem. Manchester City have won all six, and the gap at the top is three points over Arsenal with Brighton a further two back. The chasing has been done in near silence: Enzo Maresca inherited a squad that was supposed to need rebuilding and instead has 16 goals and five conceded, and the 3-0 at Anfield on Sunday was his first genuinely hostile away afternoon. Joao Pedro of Chelsea leads the division for goal involvements with eight, five goals and three assists, per BBC Sport , which tells you how open the rest of it is. Behind City, the most convincing football is being played in two places nobody is shouting about. Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite Rodrigo Bentancur being sent off for a headbutting motion at Luke Shaw , a dismissal that triggered a touchline brawl and still was not enough; Dominic Solanke equalised in stoppage time for a Spurs side who have not won a league match since May despite spending over 300m pounds in the summer, and whose manager Roberto De Zerbi said last month he had “never seen a team like us, so fragile and inconsistent”. Germany is in the middle of the highest-scoring start in its history: 172 goals in the first five matchdays, beating the 170 of 1984/85, at 3.82 a game. On Saturday it produced a record that may never be beaten. Augsburg ’s Robin Fellhauer scored after 8.4 seconds, the fastest goal in Bundesliga history, when Manuel Neuer chipped the kick-off straight to him. Bayern Munich drew 2-2, Harry Kane assisting both goals without scoring, and Vincent Kompany defended his goalkeeper on the grounds that Neuer “has played football long enough”. The table has rearranged itself around that. SC Freiburg are top, level on 13 points with Borussia Dortmund and ahead on goal difference, after a 2-1 over Schalke 04 won with ten men, Ritsu Doan ’s compatriot Goto heading in a Vincenzo Grifo cross on 85. Bayern are third on eleven and have not won in four weeks. Frankfurt have conceded sixteen in five, and Adi Hutter substituted his captain Robin Koch at half-time of the Leipzig game, saying he expects more from a captain and that a signal was needed; Koch told Kicker that running away “is not an option” and will start and captain the side against Koln on Friday. Kompany was blunt. He called it “uberblod”, said the dismissal was “100 per cent his mistake”, and noted that Tripic had been the smarter man. Olise misses the home game against Arsenal on 21 October. Serie A Hide Leaders: Inter and Lazio, 16 points from 6. Best defence: Roma, 3 conceded. Capocannoniere: Malen, 6. Serie A has produced the most unlikely leader in Europe, and it is not even top on its own. Lazio are level with Inter on 16 points after five wins from six, the best start of the three-points era for the club, with the division’s second-best defence. Gennaro Gattuso beat Monza 3-1 on Sunday with goals from Nuno Tavares , who had not scored in three years, Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti . Roma are third with three goals conceded in six games. Cagliari are fourth. Juventus are sixth and Napoli , the reigning point of reference, eighth. Inter are the story, because Inter are two clubs at once. At home in Serie A they beat Parma 3-0 with Hakan Calhanoglu back from injury. In Europe they have no points and no answers: beaten 2-1 at Real Madrid on matchday one and then 4-3 at the San Siro by Club Brugge , who were given a hat-trick by Nicolo Tresoldi despite Inter having 31 shots. They have now lost seven of their last eight Champions League matches. Cristian Chivu took it on himself, telling Sky Sport Italia that two big chances went begging, “so a little frustration set in, we got frenetic, lost our balance”, and adding: “I take responsibility.” Gazzetta’s verdict was six words long: dominant in Italy, disastrous in Europe. Napoli are in the same hole and are being louder about it. Beaten 3-1 at Villarreal after Amir Rrahmani had put them ahead, they also have nothing from two matchdays, and Massimiliano Allegri used the aftermath to deliver the week’s most Allegri sentence: in Italy, knowing how to defend “has become almost a disgrace”. He also warned that if his players travel to Venezia on Saturday without humility, “we will come out with broken bones”. Venezia, for their part, sacked Giovanni Stroppa on Tuesday. Como lost their first ever Champions League match on Wednesday, 3-2 at Feyenoord , having led through Assane Diao , who then limped off on 23 minutes. The week’s administrative news was substantial. The Milan administrative court rejected five challenges to the sale of San Siro to Inter and Milan, clearing the way for the new stadium, while Serie A’s twenty clubs meet in Milan on Friday to consider a JPMorgan plan to create a media company and lift international television income from around 250m euros towards 500m. Two dismissals defined the weekend’s temper. At Cagliari, where Randal Kolo Muani rescued a 1-1 for Juventus, referee Marcenaro sent off both managers, Luciano Spalletti and Fabio Pisacane , after a post-match confrontation. Both were banned for a match, Spalletti missing Sunday’s visit of Lazio. Donyell Malen , Serie A’s leading scorer on six, serves a one-game ban for the red card he collected at Como. Ligue 1 Hide Leaders: Monaco, 14 points from 6, unbeaten. Top scorers: nine players on 4. France has the most genuinely open table of the six, and the club at the top of it is the one that sold its best young attacker to the champions. Monaco are unbeaten on 14 points under Filipe Luis , the former Brazil and Atletico left-back appointed in July, having drawn 2-2 at home with Toulouse after leading 2-0 at half-time. Lille are second on 13 under Davide Ancelotti , Rennes third on the same points, Lyon fourth, Paris FC fifth and Paris Saint-Germain sixth. Nine players share the top of the scoring charts on four goals apiece, among them Ferran Torres , Esteban Lepaul and Amine Gouiri . The week’s real subject, though, was tackling, and the Ligue 1 clubs are no longer being polite about it. Lyon lost Lois Openda , on loan from Juventus, to a fractured fibula in Friday’s 2-1 defeat at Lens , and issued a statement criticising referee Jeremy Stinat for the number of fouls he left unpunished. Openda is out until at least the November international window. Two days earlier Lille had gone public over Tiago Santos , whose knee was caught by Le Havre ’s Amir Richardson in a tackle that drew no card from referee Bastien Dechepy and no VAR intervention. Santos has a complete cruciate rupture and a meniscal lesion and will be out more than six months. Lille’s statement noted that “no sanction was pronounced, not even a warning”. Le Havre replied that both referee and VAR judged no sanction necessary and that a retroactive punishment would fall outside the rules. The rest: Marseille ended a run of five consecutive defeats in all competitions by winning 2-0 at Troyes through Amine Harit and a 98th-minute penalty from Himad Abdelli , which lifts Bruno Genesio ’s side to thirteenth and no higher. Lens beat Lyon for Yannick Cahuzac ’s first win since he replaced Dino Toppmoller , who was dismissed in September after six matches. And Lille settled 26.6m euros of stadium-related debt, which in the current French financial climate counts as a result. Major League Soccer Hide Leaders: Nashville SC, 63 points. Golden Boot: Messi, 23 goals. Decision Day: 7 November. The American season is five matchdays from its end and has one runaway and one record in play. Nashville SC lead the overall table on 63 points from 28 games, thirteen clear in the East, at a club-record 2.22 points a game; the league’s single-season record is the 74 Inter Miami posted in 2024, and as of the start of October Nashville needed fifteen points from their last seven to beat it. They won 4-1 at Austin FC on Saturday. Vancouver Whitecaps lead the West, and are the only side so far confirmed through. Decision Day is 7 November. Nine clubs qualify from each conference, the eighth and ninth seeds meeting in a single-game Wild Card on 18 November, with a best-of-three first round from 20 November and MLS Cup on Friday 18 December. Lionel Messi leads the Golden Boot with 23 goals and 13 assists, four clear of FC Dallas ’s Petar Musa on 19, with Rafael Navarro , Milan Iloski and Brian White on 17. Four days after his international farewell, a 3-0 win over Benin in Buenos Aires in which he scored his 126th Argentina goal from the penalty spot and cried at the end of it, he scored twice in Miami’s 4-0 against DC United , with Luis Suarez also scoring twice. He is contracted at Miami through 2028. Around that: Philadelphia Union beat Real Salt Lake 2-1 to extend a club-record unbeaten run to thirteen games, Iloski scoring his 17th. St. Louis City beat LA Galaxy 6-2 with a Magnus Holse hat-trick inside 21 minutes. LAFC , who dismissed Marc Dos Santos on 27 September and are being run on an interim basis by Xavi Tamarit , drew 1-1 with Vancouver despite the visitors losing a man in the seventh minute; Son Heung-min has 13 assists and six goals for them this season and Hugo Lloris has twelve clean sheets. And the structural news that will outlast all of it: this is the last full season of the spring-to-autumn calendar, with the league planning a shortened 14-match transitional season in early 2027 before moving to a summer-to-spring schedule. k: Arsenal followed Mikel Arteta's new contract to 2030 with a comeback win over Leeds and a 3-0 Champions League rout of Lille, in a week that ended with the death of Ken Friar.
x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest Everything Arsenal, every Tuesday No. 9 · Season 2026-27 Tuesday 13 October 2026 Catch-up edition, published October 26, 2026. In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Off the Pitch · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch Collapse all sections The Lead A new contract, two wins in four days, and the answer last month's defeat demanded Arsenal came back from the international break needing to prove the 3-0 defeat at Brighton was a blip. They signed their manager to 2030, came from behind to beat unbeaten Leeds United and then took Lille apart in seven second-half minutes. T he week began with paperwork. On Wednesday 7 October Arsenal confirmed that Mikel Arteta had signed a new contract, reported as a four-year deal running to 2030. His previous agreement was due to expire at the end of this season. It was the least surprising announcement of the autumn, and it was treated that way. Arteta , 44, is the longest-serving manager in the Premier League now that Pep Guardiola has left Manchester City . He arrived in December 2019, won the club's first league title in 22 years last season and took them to a Champions League final they lost to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties. “It's a privilege to commit my future to the club,” Arteta said in the club's announcement. “This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel.” He added that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together . The co-chairs, Stan Kroenke and Josh Kroenke , said: It has been an incredible journey so far and we are excited for what lies ahead. Two days later, in his press conference before the Leeds game, Arteta spoke more personally. He told reporters the thing he would remember was the moment of signing: looking around the room and seeing excitement in their eyes . He named Stan and Josh Kroenke , chief executive Richard Garlick , James King and sporting director Andrea Berta . Then he closed the subject: Now I have to earn the right every single day to continue at this level, and make the most of it. He did not have to wait long to start earning it. Saturday: a crowd that told them to wake up For fifty-five minutes on Saturday, the Brighton hangover looked real. Leeds United , unbeaten and with only three league goals conceded all season, came to the Emirates for the 12:30 kick-off and did exactly what Daniel Farke 's side had done to everyone else. They sat in shape, defended the box and waited. Arsenal had one meaningful chance in the first half, a Kai Havertz header straight at James Trafford . Gabriel Gudmundsson should have put the visitors ahead just before the break and was denied by a strong save from David Raya . According to the PA Media report, one supporter shouted Wake up as the players went down the tunnel at half-time. Ten minutes after the restart, Leeds scored. Gudmundsson drove a low cross into the six-yard box, Raya could not deal with it and James Justin blasted in from close range. It was the 55th minute. The equaliser came seven minutes later and changed the afternoon. Noni Madueke , starting on the left in place of the injured Christos Tzolis , crossed to the far post. Ben White nodded the ball back across goal and Riccardo Calafiori ran in to finish from close range. It was his first goal at the Emirates. A minute later Arteta sent on three players at once: Bruno Guimaraes for Myles Lewis-Skelly , Jurrien Timber for White and Viktor Gyokeres for Havertz . It took Guimaraes seven minutes to decide the match. A quickly taken free kick was flicked between several players, Declan Rice laid it into his path and the seventy-five million pound midfielder drove it into the bottom corner from just outside the box on 70 minutes. It was his first goal at the Emirates and his second for the club. This is the level for Arsenal , every week, every game, every minute, every action that you have to be at. Mikel Arteta , after Leeds Raya also turned an Ao Tanaka drive over the bar, and Arsenal saw it out. Arteta told TNT Sports the team had come in with something to prove. We weren’t pleased about what we did against Brighton , and today was an opportunity to prove that right , he said, and of the winner: The timing, I think, the connection and the execution of it, it was a beauty. The losing manager was gracious. Arsenal is the most consistent team in Europe, one of the best in the world , Farke said, before adding that he was heartbroken and gutted for players who had deserved to travel home with points. Justin , the scorer, put it more simply: Their mentality is unbelievable. Guimaraes had been told publicly that he was not at the level required at Brighton , where he had made his only league start and been withdrawn around the hour. His answer was a goal and a promise. I felt amazing and I can't wait to score more goals now , he said. We know how tight the Premier League is, so we're very happy with the win. For a little over twenty-four hours, Arsenal were level on points with Manchester City at the top. Then City went to Anfield on Sunday and won 3-0 after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for a second booking on 62 minutes, with Erling Haaland , Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scoring. City have won six from six. Arsenal are three points back. Tuesday: seven minutes of football The week ended under a cloud and in a blaze. On Tuesday the club announced the death of its life president, Ken Friar , at 92. That evening the Emirates stood to applaud him before kick-off against Lille , and then watched one of the best spells of football Arsenal have produced this season. Arteta made five changes from Saturday. Guimaraes got his first Emirates start, Eberechi Eze and Gyokeres started, and Bukayo Saka , Martin Odegaard and Havertz began on the bench. For an hour it was patient and not particularly sharp. Guimaraes fired wide from close range and had a deflected shot palmed away by Berke Ozer . Mikel Merino headed at the goalkeeper. Eze , arriving on the penalty spot, shot straight at him. Lille had a goal from Ayase Ueda ruled out for offside. Then it opened up. On 64 minutes Madueke slipped in Timber , and the Dutchman dinked a finish over Ozer . Timber said afterwards that his teammate had been screaming, ‘Shoot, shoot, shoot’ as he went through. A minute later Arteta made another triple substitution: Saka for Madueke , Odegaard for Merino , Havertz for Gyokeres . On 67 minutes Guimaraes found Saka , whose low cross was turned in by Eze with a slight deflection. On 71, Odegaard slid Havertz through, Havertz cut it back and Saka curled it into the far corner. Three goals in seven minutes, from three different scorers. Sky Sports' match page recorded that Lille did not manage a shot on target all night. It was a joy to watch, the three goals were unbelievable, the connections, the timings. Mikel Arteta , after Lille Arteta was candid about the first half. He said his side's technical quality wasn't good enough to deliver moments of real threat before a positional change at half-time lifted it. The more telling line was about the season as a whole: When other aspects aren't working, we need to make sure we have a variety of ways to win football matches. It is hard not to read that as a reference to set-pieces, which have not yet produced a single corner goal this season. Lille coach Davide Ancelotti , son of the Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti , told UEFA.com: I don't think the players deserve this scoreline. His side have no points after two games, having lost to Real Betis on matchday one. Arsenal have six, and share top spot in the league phase with Barcelona and Sporting CP . Not everything about the week was clean. The team that beat Leeds lost two players in a session after the final whistle, and the attack, for all the brilliance of Tuesday, is still not converting enough of what it creates. But Arsenal entered the week with questions about their nerve after Brighton . They leave it with a manager tied down, two wins, five goals across the two games and a bench that changed both matches. Key Facts: the week in two results Saturday 10 October Arsenal 2-1 Leeds United , Premier League, Emirates Stadium. Justin 55, Calafiori 62, Guimaraes 70. Tuesday 13 October Arsenal 3-0 Lille , Champions League league phase, matchday two, Emirates Stadium. Timber 64, Eze 67, Saka 71. League Second on 15 points from six, three behind Manchester City , who have won all six. Europe Six points from six, level at the top with Barcelona and Sporting CP . Tuesday stats Possession 58 per cent to 42. Shots 16 to 4. On target 8 to 0. Sources: PA Media and AP reports of Saturday's match , Al Jazeera on Tuesday , and Arseblog News for the match statistics. The bench that won the week Two triple substitutions, and two matches turned by the players who came off the bench. On Saturday Arteta sent on three players at 63 minutes, and one of them, Guimaraes , scored the winner seven minutes later. On Tuesday the three he sent on at 65 minutes were involved in both goals that followed inside six minutes, Saka with a goal and an assist and Havertz with an assist. Arteta called the timing of Tuesday's change instinctive. I felt it was the right moment to make the triple substitution with the way the game was panning out , he said, and he spread the credit: that's credit to the starters, and as well the ones who come in to create those moments. It is a striking contrast with the start of the season, and with Arsenal Women, whose problem this autumn has been exactly the opposite: games drifting away the moment the changes are made. For the men, at least this week, the bench was the weapon. Transfer News After the manager, the midfielder: Rice closes in on a new deal Within hours of Arteta 's extension, the BBC reported that Declan Rice was close to committing his long-term future too. The window is shut, so the business this week was about keeping people rather than buying them. On the evening of 7 October, BBC Sport reported that Rice was close to agreeing a new long-term contract. Talks, first reported by the BBC in March, were said to be at an advanced stage. Rice is 27 and joined from West Ham United in July 2023 for an initial one hundred million pounds, with five million more in add-ons. He has made 165 appearances for Arsenal . His current deal runs to 2028 with a club option for a further year. The BBC said he is reported to earn around two hundred and forty thousand pounds a week, and that the new contract would substantially raise that, bringing him level with Bukayo Saka , believed to earn about three hundred and fifty thousand. The following day Fabrizio Romano added his stamp. Arsenal are closing in on new deal for Declan Rice after Mikel Arteta, plan 100% confirmed , he posted, adding that Rice has already decided to stay and sign soon with final details of new deal now being discussed . No length or salary figure has been officially confirmed, and nothing had been signed by the end of the week. There was a footnote on fitness, too. Rice was left out of England's most recent camp, which Arteta described as load management . We have to manage him because he's had a few issues since he came back from the World Cup , the manager said on Friday. Rice then started both games this week and laid on Arsenal 's winner against Leeds . Arseblog News also noted that Martin Odegaard is reportedly in talks over new terms. That one remains a single line in the reporting rather than a story with detail. Nusa, again, and a door that stays shut The January left-winger search has a familiar name and a familiar obstacle. Last week's edition reported the claim that Antonio Nusa of RB Leipzig is Arsenal 's top January target. On 7 October FourFourTwo , citing the German outlet Fussball News, reported that Arsenal are working on formalising an offer for the Norway winger. That is the German-side corroboration this digest said it was waiting for. It came with a large caveat. The same report said Leipzig have no interest in letting one of their best players leave in the middle of the season. No fee has been reported. Transfermarkt values him at forty-five million euros. Stage: concrete interest, no bid. The logic has not changed. Arsenal sold Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard in the summer, Tzolis is injured again and Madueke was the left-sided starter against Leeds by default. He then set up the opener against Lille , which complicates last week's narrative about him drifting out of the picture. Contract Watch SIGNED Mikel Arteta , head coach, to 2030. Announced 7 October. His previous deal was due to expire in June. He has also extended in 2022 and 2024. CLOSE Declan Rice , midfielder. BBC Sport and Fabrizio Romano report a long-term deal is close. Current terms run to 2028 plus a club option. TALKS Martin Odegaard , captain. Reportedly in talks over new terms. No detail. PENDING Nicolas Jover , set-piece coach. Talks led by Andrea Berta , as reported last week. Nothing new this week. Compiled from BBC Sport, Arsenal.com and Arseblog News. Contract lengths are as reported unless announced by the club. The Rumour Mill A quiet week for January talk, which is how international breaks usually end. Antonio Nusa , RB Leipzig . As above. Stage: concrete interest, with the selling club publicly reluctant. And the sale question. Last week this digest said a Madueke sale funding a left-winger was the version of January that fitted the club's finances. A week later Madueke has started two games and assisted once. If he keeps doing that, the sale half of that equation gets harder, and the January budget gets tighter. The Squad Two ankles, one warm-down and a scene nobody had seen in seven years Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi were hurt in a small-sided game after the Leeds win. Hincapie 's looks the more serious. The injuries that cost Arsenal two players this week did not happen in a match. After Saturday's early kick-off, Arteta sent the substitutes and unused players back out for a session of small-sided games, a routine for players who had not had enough minutes. Hincapie , who had come on for Calafiori in the 82nd minute, and Zubimendi , an unused substitute, both hurt their ankles. Supporters filmed Hincapie in obvious distress. PA Media reported that he was carried off by the third-choice goalkeeper, Illan Meslier . Arteta confirmed both injuries on Monday. In two very unfortunate actions we lost two players. Not great , he said. Both ankles. They're both going to miss tomorrow's match for sure. Of Hincapie , he added: Piero's one looks a little bit more serious, but we have to wait and see. He also said: It has never happened in seven years that I have been here. The small-sided games, he explained, had been planned for the following day anyway. When you play these kinds of small-sided games, there is contact, and these things happen. After the Lille match he put a rough frame on the Hincapie absence: It will be a matter of weeks for him, we don't know exactly how many. For Hincapie it is another interruption. Sports Mole counted sixteen club and country matches missed since he arrived from Bayer Leverkusen , through two groin problems and two muscular ones. For Zubimendi it is a rarity: before Saturday he had not been injured in an Arsenal shirt. The returns: Havertz, Konsa and Rice all started The good news was that the break's walking wounded were fit. Kai Havertz , who had come off with what Arteta called a muscular injury on Germany duty, started against Leeds and assisted the third goal against Lille . Ezri Konsa , released by England with a quad problem, played every minute of both games. Arteta said on Friday that communication with the England camp had been good, and listed Hincapie , Cristhian Mosquera and Max Dowman as back from their own problems. Tzolis , injured with Greece, was the one who would miss a few weeks . Asked if his was the worst of the three, Arteta said: Yeah, he's not available. Saliba: back on the grass, still weeks away William Saliba trained individually on the grass at London Colney on Monday, the first public sighting of him outdoors since the back injury that he carried through the World Cup and aggravated in France's semi-final against Spain . In the next few weeks we can start to introduce him with the team , Arteta said. Asked whether that meant before or after the November international break, he answered: We're still talking about weeks. Set-pieces: none from a corner yet The most revealing number of the week came from the manager himself. Arsenal , whose corner routines set a Premier League record last season, have not scored from a corner in this one. Arteta said on Friday that his side had created better corner situations than last year and should have scored several. On the league's tighter refereeing of contact in the box, he said the team must adapt to what is now allowed, and that the change opens another window for different ways to score. On Monday he widened the point. He called the attacking output before the break better than any other year , but said: We need to be more clinical now to finish more actions. And on mentality, with Brighton in mind: We have to be emotionally dominant regardless of what the context is. Availability: end of the week OUT Piero Hincapie , ankle, a matter of weeks . Martin Zubimendi , ankle, scanned on Monday. Christos Tzolis , hamstring, a few weeks. William Saliba , back, individual work on grass. BACK Kai Havertz started against Leeds and came off the bench against Lille . Ezri Konsa played 180 minutes. Declan Rice started both. Cristhian Mosquera was on the bench against Lille . WATCH Max Dowman , fit again after his England under-19 knock, made a cameo from the 85th minute against Lille . Compiled from Arseblog News , Sports Mole and PA Media. He saw the men's team win twenty-five major honours under seven managers, the last of them in May. On Tuesday 13 October Arsenal announced the death of Ken Friar OBE. It is with profound sadness that we announce the death of Life President Ken Friar OBE , the club's statement began. It went on to say that no one has had an influence on the club quite like Mr Friar . His story is the kind that clubs no longer produce. He was born in Islington on 13 August 1934. In 1946, aged twelve, he was retrieving a ball outside Highbury when the manager, George Allison , noticed him. He was given a job running messages from the box office for half a crown a week, and joined the permanent staff in 1950. He became club secretary in 1973, succeeding Bob Wall , and managing director in 1983, appointed by Peter Hill-Wood . As managing director he handled player and manager contracts. With director Danny Fiszman , he was central to the move from Highbury to the Emirates, which opened in 2006. He received an OBE for services to football in 2000 and the freedom of Islington in 2004. He stepped down from the board in 2020, after seventy-four years of service, and became life president. The bridge that links the stadium with the surrounding streets is named after him, and a statue at its entrance shows him as a boy playing football outside Highbury. This week, scarves and flowers were laid there. It's a really sad day for everybody that loves Arsenal Football Club or anybody that has come across him. Afterwards Arteta said : I had the privilege, the honour to meet him, to spend time with him, to learn from him. Former players followed. Tony Adams called him the epitomisation of all that Arsenal stands for . David Seaman said: Ken Friar is an Arsenal icon and his achievements will never be forgotten. Charlie George , speaking to Arsenal.com, said: He knew everything and every person in the building. Supporters' groups joined in. The Arsenal Supporters' Trust said Ken's extraordinary lifetime of service to Arsenal speaks volumes about his loyalty, dedication and love for the club. A fuller tribute, arranged with his family, is planned for the home game against Everton on 24 October. The Lead The clock started at 7pm on Thursday Manchester City have appealed. The verdict stands until a new panel says otherwise, the punishment has not been set, and the timetable for both is now the most important document in English football. T he deadline was Friday. Manchester City did not wait for it. The club confirmed on Thursday 1 October that it had lodged its appeal at 7pm that evening, against the independent commission that found it guilty of serious breaches of Premier League financial rules across nine seasons, from 2009/10 to 2017/18. The appeal went to the Chair of the Premier League’s Judicial Panel, ITV News reported . The league says the Appeal Board hearing will stay private and confidential until its outcome can be published. City ’s statement repeated the line it has held since the verdict. The commission’s opinion, it said, contains “clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.” It added, without qualification: “The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League.” “This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history.” Richard Masters , Premier League chief executive What the appeal is actually about The commission found that sponsorship income booked by the club was, in large part, not paid by the sponsors at all. NBC Sports’ summary of the findings puts it at around 87 per cent of the reported commercial income over the period, supplied instead through the owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group. City ’s central argument, as ITV describes it, is that government funding through the Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Court helped sponsors meet their obligations. The commission rejected that account as a narrative built after the fact. That is the ground the appeal will be fought on: not whether money moved, but whose money it was. The timetable, and why it matters The Premier League handbook says an appeal hearing must finish within twelve weeks of being lodged. Counted from 1 October, that lands on Christmas Eve. The appeal panel then has 30 days to rule, which points to a decision in January. There are two catches. Sports Mole noted that it is unclear whether these fast-track rules apply to a case that began before they were introduced. And City ’s chief executive Ferran Soriano has warned that the process could take considerably longer. Route and key facts The Premier League v Manchester City The charges Serious breaches of financial rules over nine seasons, 2009/10 to 2017/18, plus charges of failing to co-operate with the investigation. The verdict Guilty of all the serious-breach charges and most of the co-operation charges. Communicated on 24 September, redacted decision published on 29 September. The appeal Lodged at 7pm on Thursday 1 October, a day inside the deadline. Heard in private by a fresh panel. The clock Hearing to finish within twelve weeks, around 24 December. Ruling within 30 days of the hearing, so likely January 2027. The sanction A separate hearing, with no date set. City can appeal any sanction too. Waiting in the wings Arsenal , Liverpool , Manchester United and Tottenham , who reserved the right to claim compensation in 2024. The Football Association is reviewing the findings. The punishment nobody has priced yet The sanction is a separate process, and nobody has said when it will be heard. Several Premier League clubs want it settled before the end of this season, according to The Sun as relayed by Sports Mole, and believe the new fast-track rules should apply. The precedents are small next to the scale of this case. Everton lost eight points across two profitability cases in 2023/24. Nottingham Forest lost four. Those were single-season accounting breaches; this is nine seasons and a finding of deliberate concealment. The Football Association has added another layer. It said it is reviewing the commission’s findings, that the decision has “significant implications for the integrity of the game”, and that it may act where appropriate. It will say nothing more while proceedings continue. The second front: money Four clubs preserved the right to sue back in 2024: Arsenal , Manchester United , Liverpool and Tottenham . The Independent has reported they are planning to act, with a combined claim of around 200m pounds discussed. The Times put the potential exposure to rival claims at more than 100m pounds. None of that can start yet. Legal action can only begin once the case and its appeals are finished, which is another reason the January date matters so much. And the football carries on Through all of this, City are top. Enzo Maresca ’s side have won all five league games and lead on fifteen points. Their first match back from the break is at Anfield on Sunday, against Liverpool . That is the strange shape of the autumn. The club playing the best football in England is also the club whose place in the league depends on a hearing held in private before Christmas. Every point City win between now and January is a point that may or may not count for anything. The bill for the longest break in memory Club football in Europe’s big leagues has been dark since 20 September. As it ends, the clubs are counting what four internationals in one window cost them. FIFA’s new calendar folded two international windows into one this autumn. National teams played up to four matches between 24 September and 6 October, and the big European leagues paused for three weekends. It returns this Friday. Niko Kovac spoke for a lot of coaches on Wednesday. “Those four games were definitely too many for me. The break was too long,” the Borussia Dortmund coach said, in comments carried by dpa . His point was not only about injuries. “We also had two and a half weeks with no rhythm at all,” he said. That matters for a side that won its first four league games and leads the Bundesliga. “When you have to play four games, there’s a lot of travel, and the squads are relatively small.” Niko Kovac , Borussia Dortmund coach Dortmund ’s own list shows why. Konstantinos Karetsas and Daniel Svensson came back with colds. Nico Schlotterbeck hurt an ankle in Germany training and is doubtful for Friday. Julian Ryerson is nursing a knock from a collision. In Barcelona the worry is Raphinha . He left the Brazil squad early with muscular swelling in his right thigh after the win over Australia . Early signs were not serious, but Marca reported that Hansi Flick will not rush him back. The reason is last season. Raphinha hurt the same thigh on Brazil duty in September 2025, his return was accelerated, and he broke down again. He then missed 58 days and 13 matches, Sports Mole recalled . Napoli had problems before the break and have more after it. Tuttomercatoweb reported on Wednesday that Antonio Vergara has a strain of the right soleus and will miss at least four or five matches. Mati Olivera came back from Uruguay with a groin problem. Costantino Favasuli , hurt with Italy ’s under-21s, is probably out until after the November break. They join a list that already included Alex Meret , Alessandro Buongiorno , Scott McTominay and Frank Anguissa . That leaves Massimiliano Allegri with nine matches between 10 October and 4 November, and a squad that is thinner than it has been all season. Elsewhere the damage had been done earlier in the window. Carvajal picks Getafe , if La Liga allows it A six-time European champion with Real Madrid has said yes to a club on the southern edge of the city. The last word belongs to the league’s accountants. Dani Carvajal is 34 and has been a free agent since his Real Madrid contract ended on 30 June. He has not played an official match since. This week he chose his next club, and it is Getafe . This week, Getafe president Angel Torres confirmed that Carvajal had passed a medical and that the agreement with the player was closed. Fabrizio Romano reported a verbal agreement too, citing ABC. Coach Jose Bordalas called the player himself to explain his role, and the response was positive. The terms of the contract, including its length, have not been published. The obstacle is the spending cap. Getafe operate with far less room than the clubs Carvajal spent his career with, and Bordalas admitted as much in September. Even a free transfer has to fit under the limit, and that is now a conversation between the club and the league. Bournemouth put up the closed sign for Scott Chelsea are expected to come back for Alex Scott . Bournemouth have already given their answer.
