k: Arsenal return from a three week international break second in the table with eight goals in five games and the sharpest question of their season still unanswered.
x: The Weekly Arsenal Digest Everything Arsenal, every Tuesday No. 8 · Season 2026-27 Tuesday 6 October 2026 In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Off the Pitch · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch Collapse all sections The Lead Twenty-one days to fix the thing nobody has fixed Arsenal come back from the longest break of their season second in the table and short of goals. Leeds United arrive at the Emirates on Saturday unbeaten, and the champions still cannot say where the next one is coming from. T he last competitive football Arsenal played was on 19 September, and it was awful. Brighton and Hove Albion pressed them man for man, watched them panic and won 3-0. Pascal Gross curled in from distance after half an hour. Charalampos Kostoulas struck fifteen seconds after Bukayo Saka had been denied at the other end. Chema Andres headed in a Gross corner nine minutes after the break. Mikel Arteta said his side did not respect the game and were extremely poor technically . Then the international calendar swallowed three weeks whole. The table says the damage was contained. Arsenal are second on twelve points from five, three behind Manchester City , who have won all five. Four goals conceded is championship-grade. The problem is at the other end. Eight scored is the lowest in the top seven and exactly half of Brighton 's sixteen. It is not hard to see why. Gabriel Martinelli went to Al Hilal for a club-record sixty million pounds in August, Leandro Trossard to Besiktas , Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona . Christos Tzolis , bought from Club Brugge for thirty-four million as Trossard 's replacement, is out with a hamstring strain. Kai Havertz pulled a hamstring for Germany and is a doubt. Noni Madueke has drifted so far out of the picture that Atletico Madrid and Juventus are watching. And Viktor Gyokeres , the centre-forward, has five Arsenal appearances and no goals. We have to make sure we learn the lesson because this can’t happen again. Mikel Arteta , after Brighton What Arsenal do have is the thing that won them the league. Nicolas Jover 's routines produced a Premier League record from corners last season, and the league responded over the summer with fresh instruction to referees to clamp down on holding and wrestling in the box at set-pieces. Five games in, the champions' first-choice route to goal is being refereed differently and their open-play alternative has been sold. That is why January already feels load-bearing. Saturday is harder than the names suggest. Leeds United are fifth and unbeaten, two wins and three draws, with three goals conceded in five matches. Only Brighton have a better defensive record. They are the opposite of the fixture Arsenal need: a low block with a tidy structure, against a side with no left winger and a striker without a goal. Arteta 's questions are not about shape. They are about who plays in front of Gyokeres , and whether Eberechi Eze or Dowman is trusted to unpick an organised defence. Behind that, the defence is a jigsaw. William Saliba has not played since July, when he came off in the first half of France's World Cup semi-final against Spain with a back problem he had carried for weeks. L'Equipe report he is targeting November. Ezri Konsa , the fifty-one million pound answer to that absence, was released by England with a quad complaint after ninety minutes against both Spain and Croatia . Gabriel Magalhaes and Piero Hincapie can cover, but a 12:30 kick-off on the first weekend back is exactly when a patched back four gets found out. Key Facts: Arsenal v Leeds United When Saturday 10 October, 12:30 in London. 4:30 a.m. Pacific . Emirates Stadium, matchweek six. Form Arsenal second, 12 points from 5 (W4 L1). Leeds United fifth, 9 from 5 (W2 D3), unbeaten. Goals Arsenal have scored 8 league goals, fewest in the top seven. Leeds United have conceded 3, second fewest in the division. Gap 21 days since Arsenal 's last match, the longest break of their season. Out Saliba (back), Tzolis (hamstring). Doubtful: Havertz (hamstring), Konsa (quad). Arsenal 's league season: 3-0 Coventry City , 1-0 at Aston Villa , 2-1 Chelsea , 2-0 Sunderland , 0-3 at Brighton . They also beat Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield, won 1-0 at Napoli and knocked out Ipswich Town 4-2 in the Carabao Cup. Top Scorers: all competitions 3 Bukayo Saka , Martin Odegaard 2 Max Dowman , both at Ipswich Town . Kai Havertz . 1 Bruno Guimaraes , Noni Madueke , Mikel Merino 0 Viktor Gyokeres , in five appearances Via Football Web Pages . The record-breaker who cannot score for Arsenal Viktor Gyokeres spent the break rewriting the Nations League record book. He returns to a club where he has not scored all season. Earlier this week in Bucharest he scored the only goal of a 1-0 win over Romania , pouncing on the rebound after Sebastian Nanasi 's shot came off the post. It was his seventh consecutive Nations League match with a goal, a competition record , past Aleksandar Mitrovic and Benjamin Sesko , and his twenty-fifth for Sweden, moving him ahead of Marcus Berg . He had scored against Bosnia and Herzegovina on 3 October too. Two columns tell the story: for Sweden four appearances and four goals, for Arsenal five appearances and none. Sofascore rated him 6.5 against Manchester City , 6.4 against Chelsea , 6.6 at Napoli , 6.2 at Ipswich Town , 6.5 at Brighton . The uncomfortable reading is that this is a supply problem rather than a finishing one: Arsenal , with Martinelli and Trossard sold and Saka carrying the width almost alone, give him possession and few crosses worth attacking. Transfer News The winger hunt is already on, and Leipzig is where it starts Arsenal did not sign a left-sided attacker in the summer. Five games into a title defence, the January search has a name attached to it. David Ornstein set the frame before the season began. Asked in a Q and A for The Athletic whether Arsenal would sign an attacker in January, he said: I could see something happening because they wanted to, I thought they needed to, in the summer and they didn't. He noted the club has money but operates close to UEFA's financial limits. Summer pursuits of Vinicius Junior , Julian Alvarez and Morgan Rogers all came to nothing. On Tuesday a name arrived. CaughtOffside's Ahad Shaukat reported , citing sources close to the agents industry, that Antonio Nusa of RB Leipzig is now Arsenal 's top January target, with Andrea Berta preparing a fresh approach after the club looked at him in the summer and moved on. Nusa is twenty-one, a Norway international, and exactly the profile Arsenal no longer have: a left-sided dribbler who can beat a man. Ole Werner , his coach at Leipzig , has said of him: He is a player who will be world class in the near future. Mind the certainty tier: a single-sourced report of concrete interest, not advanced talks, with no fee attached and no Leipzig -side corroboration in the German media yet, which is usually where a deal like this surfaces first. What makes it worth reporting is that it fits Arsenal 's stated need. The alternative on the same list, Kenan Yildiz of Juventus at around eighty-five million pounds, is a January fantasy rather than a January plan. Madueke is drifting, and Europe has noticed One goal, a shrinking role and two Champions League clubs watching. Noni Madueke is in the Arsenal Champions League squad and barely in the team. He has one goal and a role that has contracted as Arteta has leaned on Saka and Eze , and Sports Mole reported this week that Atletico Madrid and Juventus are both monitoring him ahead of January, with Arsenal braced for bids. Twelve clubs, one sixteen-year-old, and a decision Arteta keeps deferring Max Dowman scored twice at Ipswich Town , was called up by England and sent off by England under-19s inside three weeks. Dowman scored twice in the 4-2 Carabao Cup win at Ipswich Town, is the highest-rated player in the under-21 side and already has two senior goals, more than Gyokeres . Reporting in late September put loan enquiries into double figures, more than twelve approaches, with Arteta publicly open-minded about letting him go for regular minutes. He assisted and was then sent off for England under-19s against the United States on Friday, then withdrew with an impact injury, having been named in Thomas Tuchel 's senior England group before being released alongside Konsa . Where outlets differ the better-corroborated figure is used: Martinelli 's fee was reported at between 56m and 60m, with Sky Sports and ESPN both settling on 60m. The Rumour Mill Everything else simmering this week, with the certainty labelled. Most of it is early-stage gossip. Gilberto Mora, Club Tijuana. Arsenal have made contact over the teenage Mexico international, with a figure around nineteen million pounds discussed and a release clause reported at 18.7 million. Liverpool and Real Madrid are also circling. Stage: concrete interest, no bid lodged. Endrick, Real Madrid. Real Madrid are reported to have made their position clear amid Arsenal interest ahead of January. Single-sourced, no talks. Stage: link only. And the one to watch. Arsenal need a left-sided attacker, have an out-of-favour right-sided one, and are reportedly near their UEFA financial ceiling. A sale funding a purchase is the only version of January that fits all three. If Madueke 's situation hardens into a bid, expect the Nusa story to accelerate. The Squad A back four held together, and a manager committing to five more years The break cost Arsenal two forwards and returned four fit players. Meanwhile Arteta and his entire coaching staff are being tied to 2030. Arsenal lost Christos Tzolis to a hamstring strain inside twenty minutes of Greece's 2-2 draw with the Netherlands , reported at two to three weeks, which takes out Saturday, Lille and probably Nottingham Forest . They lost Kai Havertz to a hamstring problem in the 1-1 draw between the Netherlands and Germany, Jurgen Klopp 's first game in charge of the Germans, with the German federation calling it a muscle strain and Klopp hoping he would be relatively quickly available again . They also nearly lost the centre-back they bought to fix a centre-back problem. Ezri Konsa played ninety minutes against Spain and ninety against Croatia carrying a quad complaint and was sent home before Tuesday's game with Czechia . Thomas Tuchel put it plainly: He played versus Spain, which made it worse. He tried everything for Croatia and gave the green light. He got another hit on the quad, and it caused some light trauma. Against that, four returns: Ben White (groin), Piero Hincapie (muscular), Cristhian Mosquera (hamstring, out since late August) and Declan Rice , held out of the England squad and rested in Dubai. Selection: the shape of a thin attack If Havertz does not make it, the options for a 12:30 kick-off against the division's second-best defence are Gyokeres through the middle, Saka right, Eberechi Eze and Martin Odegaard in the creative positions, and a choice on the left between Noni Madueke , out of the picture, and Max Dowman , sixteen and coming off a red card and a knock. Mikel Merino is the hybrid who gives height in the box. Set-pieces, and the contracts that follow Arsenal 's dead-ball operation was the biggest competitive advantage in English football last season, producing a Premier League record from corners. Over the summer the league instructed officials to take a stricter line on holding and wrestling in the penalty area at set-pieces. Which makes the contract news interesting. Nicolas Jover is in talks over a new deal, and Daily Cannon reported on Tuesday that Andrea Berta is leading the negotiation personally. Arsenal's staff and players remain very much aligned on the value of set-pieces, and the club are willing to recognise that with a good contract , the report said. Above him, Mikel Arteta has agreed a four-year contract expected to run to June 2030, first reported by Sami Mokbel for the BBC in late September and corroborated by ESPN and the Irish Times, with Fabrizio Romano adding it carries a rise on his existing salary of around ten million pounds a year plus bonuses. The agreement remains verbal and formally unannounced. The Athletic reported the whole coaching staff will sign for the same four years: Albert Stuivenberg , Jover , Inaki Cana , Miguel Molina and, on enhanced terms, Gabriel Heinze . Christos Tzolis , hamstring, two to three weeks. DOUBT Kai Havertz , hamstring, scanned on return from Germany, weeks rather than months. Hale End A Golden Boy nomination, a red card and an under-21 side with no wins The academy is producing senior internationals faster than it is producing results. Myles Lewis-Skelly has been named on the twenty-five-man shortlist for the 2026 Golden Boy award , for the best under-21 player in Europe, alongside seven other Premier League players. He started for England against Czechia at Wembley on Tuesday night with Saka on the bench. Max Dowman compressed a career arc into three weeks: two goals in the 4-2 Carabao Cup win at Ipswich Town , a call-up to Tuchel 's senior England squad, an assist and then a red card for the under-19s against the United States, and a withdrawal with a knock. He is sixteen and has already scored more senior goals this season than the club's centre-forward. The draws came against Crystal Palace , Brighton and Birmingham City , the loss was 1-4 at Chelsea , and the one recent win was 2-1 against Leyton Orient in the EFL Trophy. Arsenal Women Tenth, four goals in five, and a manager insisting she still has the board Arsenal have surrendered leads in three of their last four matches. The expected-goals numbers say the problem starts the moment Renee Slegers makes a substitution. This is the second-worst start to a Women's Super League season in Arsenal 's history. They are not being outplayed. They are being out-finished and out-lasted. One win in five, two draws, two defeats, five points, four goals scored and six conceded, tenth in a fourteen-team league. Manchester City lead on fifteen. Sunday at the Etihad was the clearest version yet. Lisa Baum put Arsenal ahead on forty-three. Lauren Hemp equalised in first-half stoppage time. Alessia Russo curled Arsenal back in front five minutes after the break. Then Kika Casparaji levelled on sixty-three, Hemp scored again on seventy-two and Georgia Shaw added a fourth on eighty-four. Manchester City 4-2 Arsenal , from a position of control, for the second time in a week. The first time was in Paris. Arsenal led Paris FC 2-0 in the Champions League on 30 September and drew 2-2, with Leah Williamson conceding a penalty . Slegers did not attend the post-match press conference, later explaining that it was important to spend time with the players after the game . They get immediate effect when they make their changes. We haven’t had the same effect as last season. Renee Slegers , after Manchester City Tim Stillman 's analysis for Arseblog put numbers on it. Against Paris FC , Arsenal were 2-0 up having generated 1.3 expected goals; over the following forty minutes of substitutions that rose only to 1.7, and they conceded twice in the final eighteen minutes. Against HB Koge the xG line totally flatlined between the 65th and 85th minutes . The full piece is worth reading . Stillman 's diagnosis is a squad-profile problem. Geraldine Reuteler , signed from Eintracht Frankfurt after a year of pursuit, has barely been used. Selina Cerci has four appearances totalling fifty-nine minutes. Mariona Caldentey is played wide, which fields four midfielders and leaves Arsenal with nobody to stretch a low block. Some of this is the cost of the most aggressive overhaul in the club's modern history. Seven players arrived and thirteen left . In came Georgia Stanway from Bayern Munich , Ona Batlle from Barcelona , Misa Rodriguez from Real Madrid , Lisa Baum from RB Leipzig , Isabella Damm from Brondby , plus Reuteler and Cerci . Out went Beth Mead to Manchester City after nine years, Katie McCabe to Chelsea , Victoria Pelova to Tottenham Hotspur , Laia Codina to West Ham United and Manuela Zinsberger to Borussia Dortmund . That is a rebuild, not a refresh. Slegers was unambiguous about her position on Sunday. She told reporters there is a strong togetherness and I've really felt [the board's] support , naming Clare Wheatley , Richard Garlick , James King and Jodie Taylor , and added: I believe in the potential that we possess. She is the manager who won the Champions League in 2025 after taking over as interim. She has earned time. Europe is salvageable. A 1-0 win over HB Koge and the 2-2 in Paris leaves Arsenal unbeaten in the league phase, with Benfica at home on 28 October, Barcelona away on 11 November, OL Lyonnes at home on 19 November and Inter away in December. Off the Pitch Arsenal will not be building a bigger stadium After months of speculation about 80,000 seats and a temporary move to Wembley, the club has chosen renovation over reconstruction. Arteta was one of the voices against. Arsenal have ruled out a major expansion of Emirates Stadium. The decision was communicated at an Arsenal Advisory Board meeting, where co-chair Josh Kroenke and chief executive Richard Garlick said the club had shared a commitment to continued evolution of Emirates Stadium, rather than a huge scale masterplan . Arseblog News reported the detail and the decision was confirmed elsewhere the same week. The option on the table was a rebuild taking capacity to around eighty thousand, which would have required Arsenal to play home matches at Wembley during construction. Mikel Arteta opposed that, concerned about severing the connection between team and supporters at the moment the club had rebuilt it. Capacity stays at 60,704. x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World football, told properly Wednesday Edition · 30 September 2026 · Arsenal covered separately In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Guilty: the verdict that rewrites nine seasons of English football An independent commission has found Manchester City guilty of serious financial wrongdoing across nine seasons, ruling that the club inflated its revenues and cut its costs by more than £900 million through contracts it called commercial and the panel called sham. The sanction is still to come. Everything about the Premier League now bends around it. The document that landed on Tuesday afternoon runs to a redacted core decision and a conclusion that leaves almost no room to stand. An independent commission, appointed under Premier League rules, found Manchester City guilty of every charge relating to serious breaches of the league's financial regulations across nine seasons, from 2009/10 to 2017/18. It also upheld three of the four charges alleging that the club failed to co-operate with the investigation that produced them. In the panel's words, by its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the rules, and it made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the league's inquiry. The mechanism, as the commission describes it, was not a rounding error or an accounting disagreement. Commercial partners were required to pay only part of the sponsorship fees that appeared in the club's books, with the remainder funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment and Development, the ownership vehicle. Other arrangements allowed costs to be recorded at artificially low levels. Between them, the panel found, these structures inflated revenue and suppressed expenditure by more than £900 million, roughly $1.2 billion, across the period in question. Accounts were misstated. Auditors and regulators were kept from the real picture. Both Premier League and UEFA spending limits were breached, substantially. Premier League chief executive Richard Masters put the finding in a single sentence: the core decision, he said, details how the club systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade. That is the sort of language a regulator uses when it believes it has won. “By its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the PL Rules.” The independent commission, in the redacted core decision How the public came to know is its own story, and not a flattering one for the league. The commission's decision was communicated on Thursday 24 September. Club executives were briefed at a shareholders' meeting the same day and asked to sign non-disclosure agreements. Within about a day the substance was in The Guardian, The Athletic, the BBC, The Times and on Sky Sports. The Premier League then published its redacted core decision on Tuesday 29 September, five days after the parties who stand to claim compensation had already been told the outcome. Several outlets have characterised the ruling as 114 of 115 charges proven; the league's own statement simply says all charges of serious breach, plus three of four on co-operation. City's response was defiant and carefully lawyered. The club said it was disappointed and surprised, insisted a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence supports its positions, and declared that it would be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums. The opinion, it argued, contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe. It noted pointedly that it had respected due process for eight years on the understanding that the Premier League board would behave as an impartial regulator free from partisan influence. Chief executive Ferran Soriano took no questions. The Case: Route to the Verdict Origin Football Leaks documents obtained by Rui Pinto and published from 2018 triggered scrutiny of the club's sponsorship structures. UEFA A two-year European ban imposed in February 2020 was overturned at the Court of Arbitration for Sport, which left a €10 million fine in place. Charged February 2023, after a four-year Premier League investigation, with more than 100 alleged breaches. Hearing A closed hearing before an independent commission, held over a period of months. Verdict Communicated Thursday 24 September 2026. Reported publicly by Friday 25 September. Redacted core decision published Tuesday 29 September. Appeal window City have until Friday 2 October to appeal to a fresh three-person commission under Section W of the rules. There is no route to CAS, though a High Court challenge alleging procedural unfairness remains open. Sanction A separate hearing, still to be listed. The Times reports it is expected within weeks rather than months. Sources: Premier League statement, 29 September 2026; Sky Sports; The Times; Al Jazeera. Which brings us to the only question anyone in England is actually asking. What does it cost? The Premier League deliberately publishes no tariff, on the reasonable theory that a fixed price for cheating is simply a budget line. The commission has discretion to fine, to deduct points, to impose other sporting sanctions, and in theory to expel. Expulsion is the exotic option and worth understanding properly: it would not relegate City to the Championship. A club outside the league is outside the pyramid, and would have to apply to the Football Association to rejoin, entering the English Football League at League Two subject to a majority vote of EFL clubs. The Premier League would be left with nineteen teams and, most likely, two relegation places that season. The realistic range is a points deduction, and the precedent ledger is where the argument will be fought. Everton lost eight points in total in 2023/24 across two profitability cases, six of them after a successful appeal against an initial ten. Nottingham Forest lost four in the same season. Further down the pyramid, Derby County were docked 21 points in 2021/22 and Luton Town 30 in 2008/09. The football finance academic Kieran Maguire has suggested that a proportionate penalty here would sit between 40 and 60 points, which would have placed City eighteenth last season. Figures inside other clubs, according to The Times, want a deduction heavy enough to amount in practice to relegation. Precedent: points deductions in English football Luton Town, 2008/09 (agent payments and improper administration exit) 30 pts Derby County, 2021/22 (administration and financial irregularities) 21 pts Everton, 2023/24 (two profitability cases, combined) 8 pts Nottingham Forest, 2023/24 (profitability) 4 pts Chart built from published sanctions. No penalty has yet been set in the Manchester City case, and the commission is not bound by any of these figures. Then there is the second front, which may ultimately cost more than any deduction. Several Premier League clubs have already taken legal advice on compensation claims, the BBC reports, arguing that City's conduct affected their own league positions, European qualification or, in the worst case, their relegation. The template exists. In June, Burnley won a £35 million settlement from Everton on exactly that reasoning, a decision Everton are appealing. Multiply that logic across nine seasons and a dozen aggrieved clubs and the exposure becomes genuinely existential, whatever happens to the points column. The cruellest detail is the football. Manchester City go into October top of the Premier League with a perfect record: five wins from five, fifteen points, seven consecutive victories in all competitions under Enzo Maresca , who replaced Pep Guardiola in the summer and has lost only the Community Shield. Erling Haaland leads the division's scoring charts. Reports in Spain say there is no relegation release clause in Haaland's contract, which runs to 2034, though nobody at the Etihad pretends a severe sanction would leave the squad intact. Sponsors, the Mirror reports, are already examining their agreements against the possibility of a season without European football. Guardiola himself broke cover on Wednesday, posting that he wanted every City supporter to know he was there, more than ever, behind his club, his owner, his chairman, Ferran Soriano , the players, the staff, Maresca and the fans, and adding that they would get through it together. Maresca had been more oblique on Sunday, posting a line of Socrates on Instagram: the only thing I know is that I know nothing. Time to breathe, he added. Time to analyse. Time to learn. There is one more layer of irony, and it is not small. This is the first season of the Premier League's new financial architecture. Profitability and Sustainability Rules expired with 2025/26. In their place sits the Squad Cost Ratio, which caps on-pitch spending at 85 per cent of football revenue adjusted for player trading, with a multi-year allowance to exceed that by 30 percentage points at a financial cost, alongside a Sustainability and Systemic Resilience test of working capital, liquidity and positive equity. The league built a new rulebook and, in the same autumn, found that the old one had been dismantled from the inside for the better part of a decade. Whatever the sanction, that is the finding that will follow English football around. Secondary Feature The window that ate October: inside FIFA's first XL break Club football stopped on 20 September and does not restart until 10 October. In the gap, an experiment: four internationals instead of two, three weeks instead of one, and a Nations League that has already produced the result of the year. FIFA's answer to a crowded calendar was to consolidate rather than trim. The September window ran from 24 September to 6 October, national teams were handed up to four fixtures rather than the customary two, and the October break was abolished altogether. Add the buffer either side and the big five European leagues are dark from 20 September to 10 October. The stated logic is player welfare and travel: with the World Cup final falling on 19 July, the season started late and FIFA wanted two international windows a season rather than three. The remaining breaks are 9 to 17 November, 22 to 30 March and 7 to 15 June. UEFA slotted the Champions League league phase around it, with matchday one on 8 to 10 September and matchday two not until 13 and 14 October. The effect on the ground is strange and, for a European league fan, slightly disorienting. Three weekends without domestic football is not a pause, it is a mid-season break. Lower divisions in England kept playing. MLS took a fortnight off its own run-in. And the international game, handed the entire stage, has filled it. Start with the only story that can compete with Manchester for column inches. Greece have beaten Germany for the first time. Dimitris Kourbelis scored the goal, deflected, on 75 minutes in Augsburg on Sunday, and Jürgen Klopp lost his first match as Germany head coach on his home debut. Klopp took the blame without flinching: the line-up and the many changes, he said, were 100 per cent on him. He also insisted he would rather have a bad start than a bad ending. Captain Joshua Kimmich was blunter, describing a side that struggled against a deep block and was too static and not creative enough. Germany have one point from two; Greece have six and lead the group. Elsewhere the new managers are mostly thriving. Zinédine Zidane has won both with France , 1-0 in Türkiye through Kylian Mbappé and 1-0 in Belgium through a slaloming solo goal from Michael Olise two minutes from time. Jorge Jesus has won both with Portugal , with João Félix scoring in each. Xavi Hernández began at Netherlands with a 1-1 draw against Germany rescued by a Cody Gakpo volley in added time, then won 2-1 in Serbia through two goals from debutant Mexx Meerdink . Roberto Mancini 's Italy lost 2-0 at home to Belgium and then went to Türkiye and won 4-1, Pio Esposito and Michael Kayode among the scorers. And the world champions keep winning. Spain came to Wembley on Saturday and beat England 3-2, a result that will feel familiar to anyone who watched the last two finals these sides have contested. Lamine Yamal scored inside two minutes, Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane turned it around before half time, Kane struck the bar from the penalty spot on 54 minutes, and then Álex Baena equalised on 60 and Mikel Oyarzabal won it on 74. Three days later Spain hammered Croatia 4-1 in Seville with Yamal scoring twice. Thomas Tuchel 's England recovered by winning 2-0 in Czechia against ten men, Gordon and Kane again. Nations League A: after two matchdays Group A1 France 6 pts, Belgium 3, Italy 3, Türkiye 0. Group A2 Greece 6 pts, Netherlands 4, Germany 1, Serbia 0. Group A3 Spain 6 pts, England 3, Croatia 3, Czechia 0. Group A4 Portugal 6 pts, Denmark 3, Norway 3, Wales 0. Two teams qualify from each group for the quarter-finals. Matchday three runs 1 to 3 October, matchday four 4 to 6 October, with matchdays five and six on 12 to 17 November. England edge Croatia and Denmark edge Norway on goal difference. The bill for all this arrives at the training grounds. Mbappé suffered a hyperextension of the posterior capsule of his left knee in Türkiye and is expected to miss around two to three weeks, which for Real Madrid compounds a defensive injury list that already included Ibrahima Konaté and Fede Valverde . Jamal Musiala tore a muscle fibre in his right thigh. Gakpo went off with an ankle problem seventeen minutes into the Serbia game; Alexander Isak returned to Liverpool with a thigh complaint. Sunderland lost Brian Brobbey to a hamstring, Manchester United fear the same for Patrick Dorgu , and Barcelona had a scare with Eric García 's left knee before tests found nothing wrong. Four matches instead of two was always going to read like this. Also This Week The fight for FIFA reaches a Florida courtroom The other governance war escalated sharply. On Wednesday the Swiss Football Association withdrew its support for Gianni Infantino 's re-election as FIFA president, a remarkable rebuke from his home federation, which had pledged backing as recently as June. The Swiss cited two things: the secretive FIFA Forward Enterprise plan to sell stakes in World Cup commercial operations, revealed on 28 July and abandoned within days, and pressure from United States president Donald Trump not to impose a mandatory one-match ban on the USA forward Folarin Balogun after a red card against Belgium at the World Cup. Credibility, transparency, accountability and effective statutory bodies, the federation said, are essential to trust in the governance of the game. A day earlier, FIFA had filed a 21-page response through the law firm Linklaters in the Southern District of Florida, opposing UEFA's application to obtain documents and testimony for a planned criminal complaint in Switzerland. UEFA alleges the FFE proposal was developed with a small circle of advisers outside normal governance, that investors would have paid $4.2 billion for a stake in a business valued near $20 billion with no open auction or independent valuation, and that a $30 million commissioner role was earmarked for Infantino. FIFA calls the application bad faith and harassment, accuses UEFA of a misinformation campaign timed to influence the election, and argues it would have been a dereliction of duty not to evaluate such a project at all. Club football has taken a side. On 25 September the Premier League , LaLiga , Lega Serie A and the Bundesliga issued a rare joint statement calling for structural reform, arguing that the FIFA presidency should not combine unchecked regulatory, commercial and political power, and describing what had happened as one of the biggest abuses of power in FIFA's history. UEFA, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation had already written that leadership of the game should never be treated as personal property. Nominations close on 18 November and the vote is in Rabat on 18 March 2027. UEFA meets its 55 member federations in Berlin next week, still without a candidate. That is the thing to watch: not the filings, but whether a challenger emerges before the deadline. Transfer News The European windows are shut. That has never stopped the business, and with three weekends of empty fixtures the agents have had the floor to themselves. One story dominates, and it belongs to a boy who cannot legally sign a professional contract for another week. The boy who turns sixteen on 6 October Manchester United have a generational forward in their academy who has asked to leave, an Irish passport that lets him, and a birthday next Tuesday that makes it possible. Joseph Junior Andreou Gabriel , known to everyone in English football as JJ, was born in Enfield on 6 October 2010. He passed through the academies at Chelsea , Arsenal and West Ham before joining Manchester United in 2022. In April 2025, aged fourteen, he became the youngest player ever to appear for United's under-18s and scored twice on debut against Leeds United . In May 2026 he was named the under-18 Premier League player of the season. He has nine England youth caps across the under-15, under-16 and under-17 age groups. He wears the number 95 at Carrington. He has never played a senior minute, and he is already the most consequential transfer story in Europe. The reason is a passport. Gabriel holds Irish citizenship, which makes him eligible under FIFA's rules to move to a club inside the European Union from the age of sixteen rather than waiting until eighteen, as an English-only player moving abroad would have to. He turns sixteen next Tuesday. In mid-September he formally asked United to terminate his registration with immediate effect, stopped training, missed a Premier League 2 fixture against Brentford , and travelled to Barcelona. United refused to release him. Barcelona are the club most heavily linked, having first hosted him on a tour of the facilities in August 2024, when he met Lamine Yamal . Real Madrid are described by ESPN as monitoring the situation closely, with Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain also watching. One outlet, 101greatgoals, has gone further and reported that Gabriel will join Real Madrid on a free transfer on his sixteenth birthday; that claim is single-sourced and should be treated as such. Fabrizio Romano has pushed back on part of the narrative, stating that Gabriel did not hold direct talks with Barcelona in person and that it is his representatives who are speaking to several clubs. Romano's reading of United's position is that they are not giving up and still hope to keep him. United's head coach, Michael Carrick , has tried to lower the temperature, saying only that JJ is a young boy, that it is important nothing is played out in public, and that making sure he is all right is what matters. The hard-edged reality is simpler. If United retain his registration he cannot join an English club this season, which leaves a move to continental Europe as the only live route, and leaves United to argue about training compensation rather than a fee. For a player of this billing, that is the difference between a windfall and a rounding error. Certainty check: JJ Gabriel Where it sits Advanced interest and representative-level talks. No agreement reported with any club. Hard facts Turns 16 on 6 October. Has requested termination. Irish passport permits an EU move at 16. Best sourced ESPN (Barcelona and Real Madrid monitoring); Fabrizio Romano (no direct player-to-club talks; United still hopeful). Treat with care Reports of a done deal with Real Madrid on his birthday. Single-sourced. Bayern begin planning for life after Kane A contract running out in 2027, a Barcelona hovering, and a 6ft 6in Plan B currently playing in Turin. Harry Kane 's Bayern Munich contract expires in 2027, which means it is now inside its final nine months, which is precisely the point at which a striker with 152 goals in 154 appearances for the club becomes the most interesting man in Europe. He reached 100 Bundesliga goals faster than anyone in history, in 49 matches. Barcelona have been monitoring the situation for weeks. Kane himself addressed it on 25 September, telling Goal that talks are going well, that he is hoping something gets done, and that over the next month or so there should be some sort of decision. A separate strand of reporting claims he wants a release clause permitting a Premier League return. Bayern have announced nothing, so the correct reading is this: an extension is expected, it is not signed, and Barcelona are close enough to hear it if the talks stall. Behind that, Bayern are doing the sensible thing and building a list. Nick Woltemade is on it. The Germany forward moved to Newcastle United for a club record fee of around £69 million in 2025 and was loaned to Juventus on 1 September 2026 for a fee reported at about €4 million, with the Italian club covering his wages. Tuttosport, cited by Sport Witness, reported on 29 September that Bayern have held preliminary conversations with his representatives and that Newcastle would want in the region of €60 million to sell next summer. Nothing is imminent. Juventus, who are paying to watch him every week and would like to make the move permanent, are the immediate competition. Woltemade's own stated priority is more prosaic: get fully fit, play, score. Barcelona keep building the spine Rodri arrived for a package worth €76.5m. Since then the club has spent its energy locking down what it already has. The headline summer move in Spain was Rodri leaving Manchester City after seven years for Barcelona , with City accepting a package reported by Sky Sports and others at €76.5 million. The knock-on has been a burst of retention. Raphinha , who leads La Liga's scoring charts with nine goals, has extended to 2030 on improved terms. Xavi Espart has also signed to 2030, and the midfielder Marc Bernal has extended from 2029 to 2031. On top of that Barcelona have completed the signing of Dany Freire , a sixteen-year-old Portuguese attacking midfielder, on a three-year deal to 2029 after a successful trial. Romano calls that one done, and frames it as Barcelona moving early to head off rival interest, which is a familiar pattern and, given the JJ Gabriel saga, a pointed one. Chelsea sketch a January midfield Sell two senior midfielders in the summer, lose your remaining one to injury, and January arrives early. Chelsea sold Enzo Fernández to Manchester City and Andrey Santos to Manchester United over the summer, then watched Moises Caicedo manage fourteen minutes of football before injury intervened, which has forced Xabi Alonso to field right-backs in central midfield. The club's reporter Nizaar Kinsella , writing for BBC Sport, says Chelsea are open to signing a midfielder in January, while cautioning that they may prefer to wait until the summer for genuine quality rather than take a short-term option, depending on Caicedo's recovery and how the academy players develop. The primary target is Alex Scott of Bournemouth , who has so far been reluctant to sign an extension while the club tries to tie him down, possibly with a release clause attached. The alternatives named are Lamine Camara at Monaco , whose summer move collapsed, Manu Koné at Roma , Adam Wharton at Crystal Palace and Sander Berge at Fulham . Status: concrete interest, no negotiation. Juventus sign a goalkeeper out of season With Kamil Grabara injured and the window closed, Juventus went to the free-agent market and re-signed Neto , announced officially on 28 September on a deal running to June 2027. The Brazilian returns to Turin for a second spell as cover. It is a small piece of business with an unusual amount of romance attached to it, and a reminder that the closed window is not a sealed one: any club with a genuine emergency can still recruit an unattached player. Reported first by Nicolò Schira and confirmed by the club. The Rumour Mill Everything still simmering, with the certainty labelled. Around the Leagues Nobody in Europe's big five has kicked a competitive ball since 20 September, so this is a standings-and-consequences round rather than a results round. It is also, for once, a useful vantage point: five weeks of football is exactly enough to tell you which of the summer's many new managers have landed. ▾ Premier League Take the verdict out of the room for a moment and the sporting story is Enzo Maresca . Replacing Pep Guardiola after a decade should be one of the least survivable jobs in football. Instead Manchester City have won all five league games, sit top on fifteen points, and have taken seven straight victories in all competitions since losing the Community Shield. The manner is not Guardiola's. City beat Sunderland 5-3 on 20 September in a game that had Antoine Semenyo scoring twice, Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki adding to it, Erling Haaland leading the division's scoring charts, and Brian Brobbey becoming the first player since 2007 to score a Premier League hat-trick in a defeat. Maresca was unimpressed with the theatre of it. He said he would rather win 1-0 than 5-3, which is the most Marescan sentence available. At the other end the crisis is in north London and it is not subtle. Tottenham are twentieth with two points and two goals from five matches, already out of the EFL Cup at the hands of Liverpool , and beaten 3-2 at home by Aston Villa on 19 September in a game Roberto De Zerbi described with real anger. He said he was very disappointed, very sad and very frustrated, called the second goal conceded unbelievable, and told his squad that leaders need to be leaders, because football is like life and either you are stronger or you lose. He had warned them before kick-off that Villa were playing far more direct football this season. They were caught by exactly that. Romano reports that Spurs are not preparing to sack him, on the basis that they backed his ideas in the summer and understood this would be a process. Whether the stand holds through a fixture list that resumes with Manchester United away is a different question. Fulham , nineteenth on two points, would quite like the attention elsewhere. In between, the picture is genuinely strange. Xabi Alonso 's Chelsea have a minus goal difference and a set-piece problem that Brentford exposed in a 3-0 win on 18 September. Andoni Iraola 's Liverpool are unbeaten but have scored seven in five, with Alexander Isak responsible for most of the decisive moments, including both goals at Ipswich and the only goal at Bournemouth . Brighton have sixteen goals in five, more than anyone, including a 5-0 win at Coventry . And the promoted clubs are not drowning: Hull City are eighth, Ipswich Town have six points, and Coventry, for all their minus-nine goal difference, won at Nottingham Forest . Leeds United are fifth and put four past Newcastle . Manchester United , twelfth on five points, are the anomaly that keeps being an anomaly. In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Off the Pitch · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch Collapse all sections The Lead No match, no peace: Arteta signs up for four more years Arsenal did not kick a ball all week. In the space where the football should have been, their manager agreed to stay until 2030, their great rivals were found guilty, and the injury list kept growing. T he extended international break meant Arsenal 's men went from the 3-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion on 19 September to a blank calendar. Their next game is Leeds United at the Emirates on 10 October. That left the week to the people in suits, and they were busy. The big one had broken on the Tuesday before this week began. Sami Mokbel reported for the BBC that Mikel Arteta had agreed an improved contract, ending months of talks . His existing deal runs out at the end of this season. In May, co-chair Josh Kroenke had called securing the manager's future the club's priority. On Thursday the shape of the deal arrived. Fabrizio Romano reported that the agreement is valid for the next four years , which would presumably take Arteta to June 2030, and said the verbal agreement is done . Mokbel described a sharp pay increase on a current salary of around ten million pounds a year plus bonuses. No new figure has been published. It is not only the manager. David Ornstein of The Athletic reported that Arteta 's backroom staff are in the process of renewing their deals, and Romano said they will sign for the same four years. Ornstein did not name names. Arseblog News thought it reasonable to assume the group includes Albert Stuivenberg , set-piece coach Nicolas Jover , goalkeeping coach Inaki Cana and tactical assistant Miguel Molina , with Gabriel Heinze also in line for improved terms. There is one thing missing: an announcement. As of Tuesday night the club had confirmed nothing. Arseblog News reported the announcement was unlikely to come quickly because the club had yet to film the content that goes with it. For a manager who ended the long wait for a league title last season, after three straight second-place finishes, the paperwork feels like a formality. It is still paperwork. The verbal agreement is done. Fabrizio Romano , on Arteta ’s new deal The timing matters. Arsenal won their first four league games of the title defence and then were taken apart at Brighton . A contract signed in that light is a statement that the club sees one bad afternoon for what it was. It also gives Arteta security going into a stretch that, after the break, runs straight into Leeds United , Lille in the Champions League and a run of games every three or four days. The other contract news of the week was about Declan Rice . Romano reported on Thursday that a new deal is really, really close , with final details being sorted and paperwork going to lawyers before an announcement. His current contract runs to 2028, so the extension would land before it enters its final year. That good news came with a worry attached. Rice had withdrawn from the England squad on 21 September, with football.london reporting his workload was being managed. Then Thomas Tuchel confirmed on Saturday that he was carrying a problem. The England manager said he saw straight away on TV that something was off while watching Rice at Brighton , and that the player just confirmed that impression . After fifty-five games for Arsenal last season and seven of England's eight World Cup matches, the rest looks sensible rather than alarming. Key Facts: the week at a glance Played Nothing. Gyokeres speaks, and Sweden listens Viktor Gyokeres still has no goal for Arsenal this season. He scored twice for his country in four days, and talked frankly about the gap. On Friday he scored the winner in Sweden's 2-1 Nations League win over Romania , his goal arriving in the forty-third minute. Daily Cannon noted that he was named player of the match and looked fairly miserable celebrating. On Monday he volleyed in Patrik Walemark 's cross in the seventy-second minute of a 3-1 win over Poland in Solna. In between he spoke. I haven't played much, but I've had a few games , he said. It is clear that you want to play football. And, on the criticism: If you do well, you get accolades and if you don't score as a striker and perform as they expect, of course there will be criticism. x: World Football, Weekly The Weekly Soccer Digest Reporting, analysis and the transfer paper trail Wednesday, September 23, 2026 · No. 1 · Arsenal covered separately In This Edition The Lead · Transfer News · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Football's Cold War Reaches the Ballot Box Two months after Gianni Infantino tried to sell a fifth of the World Cup's commercial future to private capital, the withdrawal has not settled anything. A conciliatory letter landed on Monday. By Tuesday the German federation had called it a campaign stunt, and on Wednesday UEFA's president was talking about broken trust. The 2027 election has effectively begun. Governance · Analysis T he letter went out on Monday to all 211 of FIFA's member associations, and it was written in the register of a man who knows he has a problem. Gianni Infantino told the federations he was willing to put his own house under outside inspection. "First, I will ask the Council whether it wishes to commission an independent external review of FIFA's current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements," he wrote, in a passage reported by Reuters . Of the scheme that triggered the crisis, he was blunt: "It remained a proposal, not a decision, and was always subject to the necessary approvals of the Council and the Member Associations. It has now been withdrawn and will not proceed." The scheme was FIFA Forward Enterprise. Announced on 28 July, it would have moved World Cup and Club World Cup broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing rights into a commercial subsidiary valued at roughly $20bn, with Joshua Kushner 's Thrive Capital taking about 20 per cent for $4.2bn. The sweetener was aimed at the small federations who hold the votes: annual development funding would have climbed from $8m to $20m for the 2027 to 2030 cycle. For the confederations that generate the revenue, it was the sale of an asset FIFA holds in trust rather than owns. The revolt was faster than anyone at FIFA appears to have modelled. On 30 July all 55 UEFA associations voted unanimously to boycott future World Cups and FIFA competitions. CONCACAF and its 41 members rejected the plan. The Asian Confederation's Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa called it "totally unacceptable." Infantino withdrew it on 31 July, three days after announcing it. That is not a retreat. That is a rout. Gianni Infantino is definitely not the right person to lead a reform process. He has squandered all credibility. Bernd Neuendorf , president of the German Football Association, 22 September Withdrawal did not buy peace. On 27 August UEFA launched legal action against Infantino personally, alleging he had "fraudulently" offered the stake without proper FIFA authorisation at an "absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20bn," and describing the vehicle as a way for "Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA's most valuable assets." The boycott was suspended only once FIFA confirmed in writing that the plan was "irrevocably and permanently withdrawn" and would "not re-appear in any other shape, construction, name or form." UEFA added that the underlying crisis had not been resolved. Reporting differs on where the action was filed, so we are not naming a venue. ( Yahoo Sports ) Which brings us to this week, and to the reason Monday's letter did not land the way it was meant to. Within twenty-four hours Bernd Neuendorf , president of the German Football Association , went on the record with Reuters : "I regard Gianni Infantino's letter as a transparent ploy to secure his re-election next year." He added that Infantino "is definitely not the right person to lead a reform process" and "has squandered all credibility." Germany is not a peripheral federation lodging a protest. It is a four-time world champion, the host of the last European Championship, and one of the four or five associations whose position other federations read before settling their own. On Wednesday it escalated again. The Associated Press reported UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin speaking directly to the damage, framing the task ahead as repairing trust broken by Infantino's World Cup plan ( AP, 23 September ). The choice of word is deliberate. A governing body that has to litigate against its own president to establish what he is authorised to sell has a problem no external review can write away. The arithmetic, though, still favours the incumbent, and that is the uncomfortable part for the reformers. Reuters reports that Infantino stands for re-election in March 2027 and that sources believe he retains the votes to win, with opponents concentrating on limiting his powers rather than fielding a rival. FIFA's electorate is one association, one vote, which means Germany and Gibraltar count the same. The federations that were offered a tripling of their development grant in July are the same federations who will fill in the ballot in March, and Infantino's letter took care to promise that a federation's position on governance "would not affect their treatment by FIFA." It is a sentence that only needs writing if people were worried about the opposite. So the shape of the next six months is clear. Europe and CONCACAF have the money, the clubs and the lawyers. Infantino has the ballot box. Every reform proposal from here will be read by both camps as a vote count, and the confederations will keep the litigation running because discovery is the only mechanism capable of establishing what was actually promised in July and to whom. None of it is incidental to the football. The question underneath is who decides what the World Cup is for, and it will be settled by a show of hands in a conference hall. Spain Has Its Own Civil War, and It Is Not About Football Real Madrid lost a derby, the referees' committee conceded one of the three big calls, and within forty-eight hours the club had formally demanded the resignation of the league's president. Meanwhile Barcelona quietly went seven from seven. The match itself was tight and bad-tempered. Atletico Madrid beat Real Madrid 2-1 at the Metropolitano on Sunday. Dean Huijsen was dismissed after a VAR review, Alejandro Grimaldo converted the resulting penalty on fifty minutes, Jonathan David made it two on 59 and Antonio Rudiger headed a consolation on 89. Real Madrid's own match report, published on the club's website, carried the headline "Un pesimo arbitraje decide el derbi" : a dreadful refereeing performance decides the derby. Clubs do not usually put that on their own front page. On Monday and Tuesday the Spanish referees' technical committee published its review, and the outcome was genuinely split. The committee ruled that Lee Kang-in 's 44th-minute challenge on Fede Valverde was a clear and obvious error: it should have been a red card and VAR should have intervened. It also ruled that the earlier incident involving Cristian Romero and Jude Bellingham was correctly handled, and that Huijsen's red card and the penalty were correct ( via El Nacional ). Two right, one wrong. Madrid had a legitimate grievance and, in the committee's judgement, not the one they were shouting loudest about. Jose Mourinho , in his first Madrid derby since returning to the Bernabeu bench in June, did not wait for the review. "Son dos tarjetas rojas claras," he said, two clear red cards, before turning on the video official: "this gentleman has a very complete history as a VAR referee in Real Madrid matches" ( La Opinion ). It is the oldest script Mourinho owns, and at the Bernabeu it plays. Then the institutions took over. On Tuesday Real Madrid issued a formal statement calling it "intolerable that the LaLiga president uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking Real Madrid," and said the competition required "a leader capable of administering it with the essential duty of neutrality" ( EFE ). The trigger was Javier Tebas 's social-media reply to the refereeing row, in which he said that arguing referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy. Tebas answered the statement the same day and aimed straight at Florentino Perez : "The president of LaLiga is not the owner of the competition. Neither is the president of Real Madrid." And: "I am not the owner of LaLiga and I will not run it as though it belonged to a single club. Respect for everyone. Subordination to no one." ( beIN Sports ) Two things are worth holding onto. Tebas is also among the loudest voices calling for Gianni Infantino to resign, which made this a week in which Spanish football's most combative administrator fought on two fronts at once. And then there is the table. While all this went on, Barcelona won 3-1 at Sevilla to move to seven wins from seven. The First of January Is Closer Than It Looks Anyone whose contract expires in June 2027 can open talks with a foreign club on New Year's Day. The single biggest expiry in world football belongs to Harry Kane , who is in the final year of the deal he signed with Bayern Munich in 2023 and who on 18 September became the fastest player ever to 100 Bundesliga goals, reaching the mark in his 98th appearance. Bayern are not hiding. Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has said the club are "having productive discussions" and expects matters to wrap up after the international break; president Herbert Hainer has gone further: "We want to extend his contract further, and I also think that's what will happen" ( bundesliga.com ). Kane himself, on the night of the record: "All I can say is that I enjoy every minute of it. I'm extremely happy here. The talks are ongoing" ( beIN Sports ). Bild has reported a target of 2029, a broadly flat salary near €25m a year and an exit clause under discussion. Status: advanced, not signed. The renewal nobody is covering properly is Christian Pulisic 's. His Champions Get a Warning. The BBC reported on Tuesday morning that Arsenal and their manager have agreed terms on a new long-term contract. It lands three days after Brighton & Hove Albion pulled the champions apart on the south coast, and the sequence tells you a great deal about how this club now sees itself. T here is a particular kind of week that only happens to a club that has finally won something. Sami Mokbel of the BBC reported on Tuesday morning that Mikel Arteta has agreed a new long-term contract at Arsenal , with a significant rise on the roughly 10 million pounds a year he currently earns. No end date has been made public and no announcement has been issued. The old deal ran only to 2027, and for most of this year the absence of a new one has been the quiet hum underneath everything else at London Colney. That hum has now stopped. What has not stopped is the noise from Saturday evening, when Brighton & Hove Albion beat Arsenal 3-0 at the Amex and made it look less like an upset than an inevitability. Pascal Gross struck from distance on the half hour. Charalampos Kostoulas added a second on the stroke of half time, fifteen seconds after Bukayo Saka had tamely missed a chance to equalise. Chema Andres headed in a corner nine minutes into the second half. It was the first defeat of the season, the end of a seven-match winning run, and the first time since the title was won in May that anyone had been able to say out loud that this Arsenal side looked ordinary. The timing is coincidence rather than cause and effect. But put the two stories side by side and you get the truest picture of Arsenal in September 2026 that anyone is going to draw: a club that has decided the manager is the answer, and is now discovering that the squad still has a question in it. Start with the defeat, because it was more instructive than the scoreline. Brighton & Hove Albion pressed Arsenal from the first throw-in, which is close to the phrase Arteta reached for afterwards, and the champions had no coherent way through it. David Raya was imprecise with the ball at his feet and the nervousness travelled up the pitch from him. Gabriel Magalhaes gave Gross the yard he needed. The defending at the corner for the third was, in the view of even sympathetic Arsenal writers, not really defending at all. And when Arsenal did reach a promising area, there was no pace to run beyond anyone and no Plan B to reach for. That last point is the structural one, and it did not appear on Saturday. It has been there since the window shut on September 1. Gabriel Martinelli went to Al Hilal . Gabriel Jesus went to Barcelona . Leandro Trossard went to Besiktas . In came Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge , a fine footballer who has already started to build something with Kai Havertz and Riccardo Calafiori , but who arrived as a replacement for three departures rather than as an addition on top of them. “A very disappointing result and performance. They were another gear from us in the basics of the game.” Mikel Arteta, after the defeat at Brighton David Ornstein of The Athletic has been blunt about what that means. Arsenal wanted a player to raise the level of their attack this summer and did not get one. Vinicius Junior was the headline pursuit. Julian Alvarez was a long-standing admiration. Malick Fofana was looked at as an investment. Bradley Barcola and Morgan Rogers were explored and ruled out. None of them moved at a price Arsenal were willing to pay, so the money stayed in the building. The owners, Ornstein says, showed a willingness to fund a marquee signing. The club simply could not land one. The consequence is visible in a number that should trouble nobody and yet nags at everybody: eight goals in five Premier League matches, from around 6.8 expected goals. Arsenal are not failing to create. They are creating and then wasting, and they are doing it while scoring nothing at all from set pieces, the single most reliable source of goals in last season's title win. A team that took 19 league goals from corners in 2025-26, a competition record, has taken none from any dead ball in eight matches this term. THE SQUAD The Set-Piece Machine Has Stalled, and It May Not Be an Accident Nineteen corner goals last season, a Premier League record. None from any dead ball in eight matches this one. A rule change is hovering over the explanation. The most striking statistic about Arsenal 's start is not the eight goals or the one defeat. It is the zero. Eight matches into 2026-27, across the Community Shield, the Premier League, the Champions League and the Carabao Cup, Arsenal have not scored from a corner or a free kick. To understand why that is remarkable you have to remember what last season was. Arsenal scored 19 Premier League goals from corners, breaking a record that had stood since 1992-93. Add indirect free kicks, direct free kicks and long throws and the total reaches 25 non-penalty set-piece goals, the most in the division and around 35 per cent of their 71 goals. No champion had previously taken more than 30 per cent of its non-penalty goals from dead balls. At the other end they conceded only eight set-piece goals, a net swing of 17 and the best figure in the league. The architecture belongs to Nicolas Jover , who arrived from Manchester City in July 2021 and built a system around crowding the goalkeeper in the six-yard box and attacking the flick-on at the back post. Gabriel Magalhaes was the primary target, winning first contact on 13 crossed corners. Declan Rice became the principal taker with 95 corners, 87 from the left, producing seven goals and 6.9 expected goals, the best of any taker in the league. Bukayo Saka handled the right. Bars are scaled to the 19-goal record. So what has changed? One candidate is the refereeing guidance introduced for this season, which instructs officials to be stricter about holding, pulling and wrestling in the penalty area at set pieces, with penalties explicitly available as a sanction. The guidance retains a high bar for intervention, and the Premier League has not framed it as being about any one club. Observers have nonetheless nicknamed it the anti-Arsenal rule, because the screening that lets Arsenal 's runners get free is precisely the behaviour under review. The counter-view, argued at Arseblog, is that this is an anomaly rather than a problem. Arsenal have come close: Jurrien Timber headed in an Odegaard delivery against Sunderland only to be ruled marginally offside. Eight games is a small sample against a season of evidence. Both things can be true, and how quickly the first corner goes in after the break will tell us which is dominant. The other selection question is the centre-forward. Viktor Gyokeres scored 21 goals in all competitions last season, 14 in the league, and finished as Arsenal 's top scorer. He has started twice in six this season and has not scored. At Napoli , where Arsenal generated more than four expected goals, he did not have a single shot. Tim Stillman 's diagnosis at Arseblog is that he is a specialist in a system that does not have a specialism for him: limited in hold-up play, weakly involved in build-up, and not a volume scorer who compensates for either. Kai Havertz started the Champions League final. That is the hierarchy, whatever the fee said. On the injury front there is genuine cause for optimism. k: Europe's great managerial reshuffle faces its first verdicts as Maresca's Manchester City go four from four and Mourinho's Real Madrid chase Barcelona.
x: World football, every Wednesday The Weekly Soccer Digest Edition of Wednesday, September 16, 2026 · Arsenal covered separately In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead The Great Reshuffle Meets Its First Reckoning Seven of Europe's biggest clubs changed manager inside a single calendar year. Four games into the new season, the early returns are already brutally uneven. There is a version of this season that will be written in a year's time as the most consequential managerial turnover in the modern history of the European game, and the remarkable thing is that we are only four matchdays into finding out whether that is true. Pep Guardiola is gone from Manchester City . Jose Mourinho is back at Real Madrid . Arne Slot was dismissed by Liverpool three weeks before the World Cup final and Ruben Amorim , sacked by Manchester United in January, is now standing in the technical area at AC Milan . Almost every door in the sport swung at once. The scale is easier to grasp in numbers than in names. Between the first day of January and the end of May, the Premier League's traditional big six lost seven managers: six sackings and one voluntary departure, an average of one every twenty-one days. Chelsea alone got through two, dismissing Enzo Maresca on New Year's Day and Liam Rosenior in April before settling on Xabi Alonso , who began work on the first of July. Tottenham Hotspur also burned through two before landing on Roberto De Zerbi . Only Mikel Arteta , in post since December 2019, has watched the whole carousel from a fixed seat. What makes this week the right moment to take stock is that the evidence has finally started arriving. The Champions League league phase opened on September 8 and the domestic leagues have now played four or five rounds. That is a small sample, and anyone claiming certainty from it is selling something. But it is no longer nothing, and the spread between the best and worst of these appointments is already wider than anybody would have predicted in July. The best of it, and the worst of it At the top of that spread sits Enzo Maresca , which is not where most people expected to find him. Handed the hardest inheritance in football, he has taken Manchester City to four wins from four in the Premier League, a 2-0 win at Porto in Europe and a 1-0 victory at Old Trafford, all while presiding over a squad that has been rebuilt around him rather than for him. Rodri , the 2024 Ballon d'Or winner and a World Cup winner with Spain in July, was sold to Barcelona for 65.4 million pounds. Savinho went to Tottenham Hotspur . Tijjani Reijnders went to Al-Qadsiah . Bernardo Silva left for Real Madrid on a free. In their place came Elliot Anderson for 116 million pounds, Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille , and, on the window's final day, Enzo Fernandez for a fee that equalled the British record. It is a total rebuild conducted at full speed, in public, by a manager in his first month. At the other end sits the season's genuine emergency. Tottenham Hotspur have played four Premier League matches and scored zero goals. Not one. They sit seventeenth with two points and a goal record of nought scored and five conceded, which is the sort of line that normally belongs to a side already cut adrift in April, not one four games into September under a coach hired precisely because he is supposed to make teams play. Roberto De Zerbi arrived from Marseille on March 31 on a long-term deal, with sporting director Johan Lange calling him one of the most creative and forward-thinking coaches in world football. The creativity has not yet shown up on a scoresheet. “We worked four years in the same structure and we always felt comfortable. Now, we need time.” Unai Emery , whose Aston Villa won the Europa League in May and have one point from four Neither a triumph nor a disaster, yet Between those poles, the picture is genuinely difficult to read. Andoni Iraola , who left Bournemouth for Liverpool in June, has one win and three draws from four: unbeaten, but blunted, and a goalless home afternoon against Fulham did nothing to quiet the question of whether his high-pressing model survives contact with the expectation at Anfield. He did at least win his European opener, edging Atletico Madrid 2-1. Michael Carrick 's Manchester United are thirteenth in the league but put four past Sabah in Europe. Matthias Jaissle inherited a Newcastle United side that sold its three best players in a single summer. And then there is Madrid. Jose Mourinho returned to the Bernabeu on June 11, signing until 2029, sixteen years after he first walked in and three managers after Xabi Alonso left in January. His Real Madrid have twelve points from five, beat Inter 2-1 on the opening night in Europe through Kylian Mbappe and Federico Valverde , and put four past Rayo Vallecano at the weekend. They are also, already, three points behind a Barcelona side that has won all five of its league games with a goal difference of plus seventeen. The reshuffle gave Madrid a serial winner. It did not give them a head start. The honest summary is that the market for managers behaved this year less like a market and more like a panic. Clubs did not so much choose replacements as grab whoever was nearest when the music stopped, and the reason the table already looks strange is that several of them grabbed well and several grabbed badly. The next three months will sort them. What is not in doubt is that the sport has never asked so many new men to answer so many questions at once.
