Arsenal lead on goal difference. Also in the lead Europe's Second Tier Opens, and Three English Clubs Step Into the Unknown The Europa League league phase begins tonight and tomorrow. Sunderland , Crystal Palace and Bournemouth have never been here in this form, and AC Milan and Juventus would rather not be. The Europa League returns this evening with the first of its eight league-phase matchdays, and the entry list tells you a great deal about how the last eighteen months have gone for some very large football clubs. AC Milan open at home to Benfica . Juventus host N.E.C. tomorrow. Celtic , Lyon , Marseille , Real Sociedad and Bayer Leverkusen are all here too. This is a deep field by any historical standard. For the three English entrants it is something closer to genuinely new territory. Sunderland begin at home to AZ Alkmaar tonight, seeded thirty-third of thirty-six and playing continental football for the first time in decades. Crystal Palace host Lech Poznan tomorrow, and Bournemouth , seeded eighth and the best placed of the three, travel to Real Sociedad under Marco Rose , who replaced Andoni Iraola in the summer. The format rewards consistency over survival. Each of the thirty-six clubs plays eight different opponents, the top eight go straight to the last sixteen, ninth to twenty-fourth drop into a knockout playoff round, and twenty-fifth or lower means elimination from Europe altogether. There is no group to escape and no easy draw to hide behind, which is why a slow start here is far more expensive than it used to be. The holders are not in the field. Aston Villa won this competition in May, beating SC Freiburg 3-0 in Istanbul through Youri Tielemans , Emiliano Buendia and Morgan Rogers for a first trophy in thirty years, and were promoted into the Champions League for their trouble. Two of those three scorers have since been sold. That is a story for the transfer pages, and it is not a happy one. Transfer News City Pay the British Record to Undo Their Own Midfield Enzo Fernandez cost 125 million pounds and reunites with the manager who sold him. Rodri went the other way. The single largest transaction of the summer was also its strangest. On deadline day, Manchester City paid Chelsea 125 million pounds for Enzo Fernandez , a fee that equals the British record set when Liverpool bought Alexander Isak from Newcastle United in 2025. The Argentine signed a five-year deal. The move was confirmed by Sky Sports , ESPN and Al Jazeera . Status: official. The symmetry is almost too neat. Enzo Fernandez now plays for Enzo Maresca , the manager who coached him at Stamford Bridge and was sacked by Chelsea on New Year's Day. Chelsea, meanwhile, booked an 18 million pound profit on a player they bought for 107 million three and a half years ago, which is a respectable piece of accounting and an awkward piece of squad-building. It was awkward because the replacement did not arrive. Chelsea had a 47 million pound deal in place for Lamine Camara when Monaco withdrew from the sale late, leaving Xabi Alonso a midfielder short on the day he lost his most expensive one. Chelsea honoured the Fernandez sale regardless. Set that against City's other business and a coherent, if severe, logic appears. Rodri was sold to Barcelona for 65.4 million pounds in mid-August after seven years and a World Cup win with Spain . Savinho and Omar Marmoush went to Tottenham Hotspur , the latter initially on loan. Tijjani Reijnders went to Al-Qadsiah for around 52 million pounds and Bernardo Silva left for Real Madrid for nothing at all. In came Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for 116 million pounds, Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for a reported 81 million, and Iliman Ndiaye . City spent roughly 319 million pounds. They also tore out the spine of the most successful English side of the last decade and replaced it with players whose combined age barely reaches the one they sold. Madrid Build a Spine and Pay For Almost None of It Two of Jose Mourinho 's six signings arrived on free transfers. The one they did pay heavily for cost 140 million euros. Real Madrid 's summer is the clearest demonstration this year of what a club can do when it plans two years ahead of a contract cycle. Ibrahima Konate joined from Liverpool on a free transfer on a four-year deal, a move confirmed by ESPN and Sky Sports . Bernardo Silva arrived from Manchester City , also free, on a two-year deal. Status on both: official. The paid-for business was substantial. Marc Cucurella came from Chelsea in a deal Sky valued at 51.8 million pounds and Madrid's own books at around 60 million euros, announced by the club on June 15. Denzel Dumfries joined from Inter . And Yan Diomande arrived from RB Leipzig for a reported 140 million euros on a deal to 2033, the second-largest fee of the entire window. Endrick returned from a loan at Lyon . Out went an era. Dani Carvajal left at the end of his contract after twenty-three seasons at the club. David Alaba also departed as a free agent, and Dani Ceballos left by mutual agreement. Antonio Rudiger signed a one-year extension to 2027. Newcastle Sold Their Three Best Players, and Say They Would Do It Again Bruno Guimaraes , Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon all left in one window. The sporting director is unapologetic. No club in Europe had a stranger summer than Newcastle United . Sandro Tonali went to Tottenham Hotspur for 92.5 million pounds. Anthony Gordon went to Barcelona for a reported 69.3 million. Bruno Guimaraes , the captain and the emotional centre of the side, went to a Premier League rival for 75 million. The club then spent roughly 295 million pounds rebuilding. Eddie Howe had already gone, replaced by Matthias Jaissle . What is unusual is not the churn but the candour about it. Sporting director Ross Wilson told reporters that if you want to be a successful club in the Premier League you have to trade players, and that if you do not, you get stuck. He went further, naming Lewis Hall and Tino Livramento as players who may themselves leave in time. Chief financial officer Simon Capper was equally blunt about the mechanics, explaining that one incoming deal required Nick Woltemade 's loan to Juventus to clear the wage space first. This is profit and sustainability regulation as a design constraint rather than a threat, and it is worth watching closely, because Newcastle are describing openly what several of their rivals do quietly. The early league evidence is inconclusive: twelfth after four, one win, one defeat at home and a trip to face Hull City on Saturday. Paris Sold an Attack, Bought Another, and Forgot How to Win at Home Bradley Barcola left for Liverpool in a deal worth up to 123 million pounds. Luis Enrique says he could not promise him a starting place. Paris Saint-Germain are the reigning European champions and the five-time reigning champions of France. They are also, this morning, seventh in Ligue 1 with five points from four matches. The gap between those two sentences is the most interesting thing in French football. The squad turnover explains a good deal of it. Bradley Barcola joined Liverpool in a deal reported at up to 123 million pounds including variables. Goncalo Ramos went to AC Milan for around 63.7 million. In came Ferran Torres from Barcelona , among others. Luis Enrique was unusually direct about the Barcola exit, telling reporters that the player's desire was to play a more important role in the side, something the manager could not guarantee him. He called the window exceptional. The results have not agreed. Paris went four matches without a win, drawing twice from two goals down and losing 2-1 at home to Monaco on September 4, before finally beating Brest 1-0 on Sunday through, appropriately enough, Ferran Torres . Ousmane Dembele , the reigning Ballon d'Or holder, Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia had gone four games without a goal between them. Then, on September 9, the same team put six past Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League with a Ferran Torres hat-trick. Whatever is wrong in Paris, it is not the forwards' finishing, and it is probably not permanent. Luis Enrique 's own assessment, offered with characteristic serenity, was an invitation to bet on who would be champion at the end of the season. The Window in One Picture The Six Biggest Fees of the Summer Window Enzo Fernandez Chelsea to Manchester City 125 Morgan Rogers Aston Villa to Chelsea 117 Elliot Anderson Nottingham Forest to Manchester City 116 Yan Diomande RB Leipzig to Real Madrid 107 Bradley Barcola Paris Saint-Germain to Liverpool 106 Sandro Tonali Newcastle United to Tottenham Hotspur 92.5 Reported fees in millions of pounds, on a single consistent basis. Arsenal's business is covered in the companion edition and is not shown. The Rumour Mill The window shut on September 1, so everything below is January business or contract business. Certainty labels are attached to each. Treat the unlabelled as gossip, because that is what it is. Bruno Fernandes and the option year Advanced talks, no agreement David Ornstein reported to Sky Sports after the Manchester derby that Bruno Fernandes remains in discussions with Manchester United over a new contract but that the parties have not found common ground. His deal expires at the end of this season and United hold a one-year extension option. The 32-year-old is the reigning PFA Players' Player of the Season, is nominated for this year's Ballon d'Or and has five goal involvements in five matches. This is the most consequential contract situation in England. JJ Gabriel wants out of Old Trafford Reported, single-sourced on the destination The Sun reports that Manchester United fear teenage forward JJ Gabriel will join Manchester City after asking to leave. The Athletic separately places Real Madrid in the running. Gabriel is fifteen. Both strands are credible on the player's desire to go and thin on where he goes. Endrick to United in January Speculative link AS in Spain suggests Manchester United could move for Endrick in January if the Brazilian becomes available. He has just returned to Real Madrid from a loan at Lyon and is behind Kylian Mbappe in the order. No talks have been reported by either club. Branthwaite, revived Concrete interest The Daily Mail reports that Manchester United have restarted their long pursuit of Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite . This link has been live in some form for three windows and has never yet reached a bid that Everton were willing to discuss. Araujo's option to buy Loan active, purchase undecided Ronald Araujo joined Liverpool from Barcelona in August on loan with an option to buy, confirmed by Liverpool and Sky Sports . Fabrizio Romano reported on September 13 that Liverpool are pleased with how the move has gone. Whether the option is exercised is the question that will define Liverpool's January. Barcelona want a number nine Gossip talkSPORT lists Harry Kane , Erling Haaland , Julian Alvarez and Nick Woltemade as Barcelona striker targets. That is less a shortlist than a list of good strikers, and it should be read accordingly. Separately, Sport reports the club is negotiating a contract extension with Raphinha , who has six league goals already. The Raphinha strand is the one worth following. Henderson set for a Palace payday Reported The Daily Mail reports Dean Henderson is poised to become Crystal Palace 's highest-paid player on a new contract, despite interest from Nottingham Forest . Around the Leagues Premier League Four matchdays in, the table has two perfect records at the top and a genuine curiosity beneath them. Manchester City are unbeaten with twelve points and won the Manchester derby 1-0 at Old Trafford on Sunday, a result that said as much about Michael Carrick 's side as Enzo Maresca 's: Manchester United are thirteenth with four points despite Bruno Fernandes playing some of the best football of his career. Behind the leaders, Leeds United and Hull City are third and fourth on eight points apiece, which nobody forecast in August. Daniel Farke 's Leeds are unbeaten. Sergej Jakirovic 's newly promoted Hull have taken points off Chelsea and Aston Villa already. The bottom of the table is where the season's real stories are. Tottenham Hotspur have not scored a league goal. Four matches, nought goals, two points, seventeenth, and a 0-0 at home to Everton on Saturday that extended the drought. Aston Villa are nineteenth with one point, which is remarkable for a team that lifted the Europa League in May. Their summer explains most of it: Morgan Rogers sold to Chelsea for 117 million pounds, Youri Tielemans and Ezri Konsa both gone, two of the three scorers from the final in Istanbul now playing elsewhere. Unai Emery has asked for patience, saying after a goalless draw with Hull City that his side deserved more and that he feels the team is progressing. Reports that the club is weighing Emery's position trace to a single former club scout speaking to Football Insider, and should be treated as exactly that thin. Villa did at least win 3-2 at Club Brugge in the Champions League through John McGinn , Emiliano Buendia and a first goal for Nicolas Jackson . Below Villa, Coventry City have the worst start of any promoted side in recent memory: four defeats, no points, no goals scored and ten conceded, including a 5-0 home defeat to Brighton on Sunday. Frank Lampard took them up and is discovering how unforgiving the step is. Liverpool sit eighth, unbeaten but drawn three times under Andoni Iraola , the goalless afternoon against Fulham the most telling of them. Brighton have scored thirteen in four, more than anyone. And Fulham are eighteenth with a point under Alvaro Arbeloa , who was managing Real Madrid in January and is now fighting relegation in west London, which may be the single most 2026 sentence in this edition. La Liga Barcelona have won all five, scored seventeen, conceded two and lead by three points. Raphinha is the division's top scorer with six. Lamine Yamal scored twice in Sunday's 4-2 win at Levante , where Karim Adeyemi also found the net. This is a side playing with the confidence of a double champion, which is what they are. Real Madrid are second on twelve, having beaten Rayo Vallecano 4-1 with two from Kylian Mbappe and goals for Alvaro Carreras and Jude Bellingham . Atletico Madrid are quietly excellent, winning 3-0 at Real Sociedad through Alejandro Grimaldo , Jonathan David and Giuliano Simeone . The genuine surprise is Alaves , third on ten points. The promoted clubs have brought real romance. Racing Santander are back after fourteen years and beat Alaves 2-1. Deportivo La Coruna are back after eight and sit sixth. Malaga , also back after eight, drew at Celta Vigo . At the other end, Valencia have one point from five, which for a club of that history is an alarm rather than a slow start. Bundesliga Three matchdays in and Bayern Munich are fourth. Above them, improbably, are SC Freiburg and Borussia Dortmund , both perfect on nine points. Freiburg, beaten Europa League finalists in May, thrashed Borussia Monchengladbach 5-0 on Saturday and have a goal difference of plus nine. Bayern have seven points from three after winning 2-1 at newly promoted SV Elversberg . More striking is who is not on the scorers list: Harry Kane , winner of the Torjagerkanone in each of his three seasons in Germany, is not among the leaders. The top of that chart is shared on three goals by Younes Ebnoutalib of Eintracht Frankfurt , Yuito Suzuki of Freiburg , Phillip Tietz of Mainz , Patrik Schick of Bayer Leverkusen and Michael Gregoritsch of Augsburg . SV Elversberg have become the fifty-ninth club to play in the Bundesliga and sit sixth with six points, having already beaten Monchengladbach 4-3 away. Schalke 04 are back after three years and won 3-1 at Union Berlin on Friday. RB Leipzig beat Hamburg 5-0 under Martin Demichelis , and Bayer Leverkusen have four points from three in Carles Martinez Novell 's first season. Serie A Saturday evening in Rome is the fixture of the European weekend. Roma and Inter are the only unbeaten sides, level on points with Roma ahead on goal difference, and they meet at the Stadio Olimpico at 18:00 local time. Gian Piero Gasperini called it an opportunity to measure up against the best and show his side can do better, which is about as close to a gauntlet as he throws. Roma's form is built on Donyell Malen , who has six goals in four matches, equalling a club record set by Francesco Totti in 2001-02, with Paulo Dybala supplying him. Gasperini has praised how the two complete each other. Inter, the reigning champions, have won all three of theirs but lost 2-1 at Real Madrid in Europe. Elsewhere the champions-elect narrative is getting complicated. Juventus lost 3-2 at Sassuolo on Sunday after leading, with former Juventus player Vasilije Adzic scoring the winner, and Luciano Spalletti is already fielding questions about his future despite public backing. AC Milan drew 2-2 at Lazio in Ruben Amorim 's latest outing, with Christian Pulisic registering his first assist of the season. And Fiorentina , who lost their first three, won 4-2 at Venezia thanks to a hat-trick from Franco Mastantuono , who became the youngest Argentinian to score one in Europe's top five leagues, a record previously held by Lionel Messi . Ligue 1 Three clubs share the lead on ten points: Lille , Monaco and Rennes . Davide Ancelotti 's Lille beat Troyes 2-0 on Sunday through Santos and a stoppage-time goal from Ethan Mbappe . Filipe Luis 's Monaco were held 1-1 at Strasbourg . Rennes beat Marseille 1-0 on Friday through Adrien Thomasson . Paris Saint-Germain finally won, 1-0 at Brest through Ferran Torres , and are seventh on five points. Marseille have now lost two in a row under Bruno Genesio and travel to Besiktas in the Europa League tomorrow. Auxerre claimed a first win of the season, 1-0 over Nice . French football also spent the summer in mourning. Eric Roy , who coached Brest to the Champions League and was still in post last season, died on June 17 at the age of 58 after an illness. Julien Lachuer has succeeded him at Brest. Major League Soccer Nashville SC are eight points clear at the top of the overall standings and closing on a first Supporters' Shield. They drew 2-2 at Inter Miami at the weekend in the fixture of the regular season, Lionel Messi putting Miami ahead before Sam Surridge equalised late. Tonight at Portman Road Arsenal restart the competition that humiliated them in March, with a defence held together by improvisation. Six months ago Arsenal walked up the Wembley steps as losers. Manchester City beat them 2-0 in the Carabao Cup final on 22 March, Nico O'Reilly scoring twice, and a season that ended with a first league title in twenty-two years began its run-in with a reminder that one pot has eluded this club since 1993. Tonight, at 12 noon Pacific, the Gunners walk out at Portman Road to start it all again. They do so having won everything they have played. The Community Shield against the same Manchester City , 3-0 . Coventry City at home, 3-0 . Aston Villa away, 1-0 . Chelsea at the Emirates, 2-1 . Napoli away in the Champions League, 1-0 . Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Saturday, 2-0 . Eight goals scored in the Premier League, one conceded, twelve points from twelve, first on goal difference. What makes the run remarkable is who has not played a minute of it. William Saliba was withdrawn after half an hour of France 's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain in July with a back problem the club described, in a statement on 23 July , as requiring a managed recovery programme and an absence of an extended period . There has been no surgery and, as of Mikel Arteta 's press conference on 11 September, no new timeline. That single absence reshaped the summer. Arsenal spent GBP 51m plus GBP 4m on Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa on 21 August, a signing the club framed explicitly as cover for a centre-back crisis, and Konsa made his full debut against Chelsea because Cristhian Mosquera had gone off injured at Villa Park. Jurrien Timber only returned to team training in the second week of September after a groin problem dating to March. Ben White limped out of Saturday's win with a groin strain and missed Monday's session. “He will have his chance. He will have his minutes, and he will have to earn them like anybody else.” Mikel Arteta on Max Dowman, 14 September So the team that lines up in Suffolk will be a guess. Kepa Arrizabalaga is the expected goalkeeper. Timber needs minutes and may take one centre-back slot; the other could go to Marli Salmon , the seventeen-year-old who signed his first professional contract on 29 August and has not appeared for the senior side since the FA Cup tie at Mansfield Town in March. Piero Hincapie and Myles Lewis-Skelly are the likelier full-backs. Further forward the interest is in the players who have been watching. Martin Zubimendi has not started a Premier League or Champions League match this season. Viktor Gyokeres has played twenty-seven minutes across the opening four league games and has yet to start one. Noni Madueke , Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze are all in the same bracket: expensive, capable, and short of rhythm. And then there is Max Dowman , who is sixteen until New Year's Eve, sits outside the twenty-five-man Premier League list because of his age, and has been an unused substitute four times already, including in Naples. He played an hour for the under-21s against Chelsea on Saturday instead of travelling to Sunderland. Arteta would not promise a start, which in the current climate is its own kind of answer. Ipswich Town , back in the division and tenth with six points from four, are not a soft landing. They have scored seven and conceded ten, which is to say they will have a go. Arteta 's line all week has been that there is no second tier to this squad, and that every competition counts. The argument for taking him at his word is sitting in the Wembley record books, unpleasantly recent. According to Fabrizio Romano that is about to stop being true. Mikel Arteta 's contract expires at the end of this season, a fact that has hovered over the club since the spring. Fabrizio Romano reported on 14 September that the extension is in its final stages , with lawyers working through the remaining details, and described Arteta as very, very close to signing. The proposed term is three years. The timeline matters. First contact with his representatives came in March or April, before the title was mathematically won. Josh Kroenke called a new deal an utmost priority in May. Arteta himself, speaking to Sky Sports on 15 August, said he wanted to stay and that the club would resolve it in a very organic way when the possibility arose. Nothing is signed. But a manager who has won the league, reached a domestic cup final and started the defence with six straight wins is not a difficult negotiation, and the direction of travel is unmistakable. Expect an announcement rather than a saga. Transfer News Zubimendi, Madrid and the January question nobody at the club wants asked A Spanish journalist says it is done. The evidence that matters is the team sheet. On 14 September Javi Roldan of El Confidencial said flatly that Martin Zubimendi is going to be Madrid's signing in the winter window . The figure attached by Spanish outlets is EUR 70m , the same sum Arsenal paid Real Sociedad in the summer of 2025. Treat the claim itself with care. It is one reporter, amplified by aggregators, with no corroboration from David Ornstein , Fabrizio Romano , the BBC or Sky. Nothing in it has reached even the concrete-interest tier. The underlying fact is another matter, and it is not in dispute. Zubimendi has made four substitute appearances in the Premier League and one in the Champions League this season. He has started neither competition. He lost his place late last season and the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes for GBP 75m has not made getting it back any easier. TEAMtalk add, on their own sourcing, that Zubimendi would be willing to push for an exit if he is not playing regularly by January, that Real Madrid have kept contact with his camp, and that Chelsea are watching. That is a plausible shape for a story rather than a story. It is also the kind of thing that becomes true if a player spends autumn on a bench. The window that was: a level-raiser that never arrived David Ornstein 's verdict on Arsenal's summer was blunt, and the numbers behind it are stranger than the headline suggests. Arsenal spent heavily and ended the window without the attacking signing they wanted. Ornstein 's assessment, published on 2 September and relayed by Daily Cannon, was that the club failed to land a level-raiser in attack, having pursued Vinicius Junior as the primary target and then Julian Alvarez , Malick Fofana , Bradley Barcola and Morgan Rogers . Christos Tzolis , at GBP 34m from Club Brugge , was a replacement for Leandro Trossard , not an addition. The Vinicius thread is worth closing properly, because it keeps being resurrected. Ornstein reported that Arsenal were prepared to commit major funds and that the move had been approved at every level of the club. Romano reported on 5 August that Real Madrid had improved their offer materially. On 6 August the player signed a six-year extension to 2032. Anyone still writing that link is recycling. Alvarez failed for a different and more bruising reason. Ornstein , on 29 August : the Argentine spoke to Mikel Arteta and said he doesn't want to come , his heart set on Barcelona . Atletico Madrid would have done a deal. Arsenal were prepared to agree one club to club. The player said no. Reports of a January return are aggregator speculation and should not be attributed to Ornstein , who said the opposite. Two late near-misses give the window its texture. The Daily Mail's Isaan Khan reported that assistant manager Gabriel Heinze personally contacted Inter Milan about Lautaro Martinez in the final week; Inter refused to entertain it. Gabriel Martinelli went to Al-Hilal on 3 September for GBP 60m guaranteed , a club-record sale, two days after the English window had shut and so at a moment when the money could not be reinvested. x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World Football, Every Wednesday The Weekly Soccer Digest Vol. 1, No. 37 Wednesday, September 9, 2026 In This Edition The Lead · The Benches · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Europe Reopens on a Map Nobody Recognises The Champions League league phase began on Tuesday with the holders in disarray at home, a returning heavyweight in the Real Madrid dugout and a Manchester City side that has spent a decade being one thing learning to be another. Eighteen matches across three nights, and the shape of the season is already arguing with itself. T here is a version of this competition that reads exactly as you would expect. Real Madrid beat Inter . Manchester City won at Porto because Erling Haaland scored twice. Borussia Dortmund came from behind in front of the Yellow Wall. Read the six Tuesday scorelines cold and you would conclude that European football has spent the summer standing still. It has done the opposite. The men in the dugouts have almost all changed. The champions of Europe are 14th in their own league. The best player in the Premier League for a decade is playing in Turkey. And the two clubs who contested last season's final have between them lost a manager, a talisman and, in one case, an entire idea of themselves. Matchday one was not a continuation. It was an audit. Start at the Bernabéu, because that is where the noise is. José Mourinho returned to Real Madrid in June on a three-year deal, installed by a president who had just survived an election fought over a trophyless season, and his first European night back ended 2-1 against Inter . It should have been a coronation. Instead it was a survival exercise. Kylian Mbappé finished neatly on 14 minutes, Fede Valverde punished a calamitous piece of goalkeeping three minutes later, and then Madrid spent an hour missing chances while Thibaut Courtois made save after save. Carlos Augusto scored late. There were whistles at the final whistle of a home win. That anxiety has a cause, and it is not the Champions League. Four days earlier Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis , beaten by a Troy Parrott goal and by Álvaro Valles saving a stoppage-time Mbappé penalty. Madrid demanded a retake for encroachment; the referee and VAR said no, correctly under the letter of the law, since Marc Bartra still had a foot planted outside the area. Mourinho's response was pure Mourinho. "If the VAR did not order the penalty retaken because they do not know the rulebook," he said, "they need to go home." Madrid are third in La Liga, three points off Barcelona , with Rodrygo out until 2027 and Ferland Mendy out until April. Four matches without a win, seven points behind Monaco, and Paris Saint-Germain responded by extending the manager who won them back-to-back European Cups until 2030. On the same day they lost. Which brings us to the genuine oddity of this September. Paris Saint-Germain are the double defending champions of Europe. They beat Arsenal on penalties in Budapest in May after a 1-1 draw, then beat Aston Villa 2-1 in the Super Cup in August. They are also, as of Sunday night, 14th in Ligue 1 with two points from three games, beaten at the Parc des Princes by Monaco and beaten before that by Lens in the Trophée des Champions. Luis Enrique is not having it. Asked whether his players were physically short after a summer in which most of them went deep into a World Cup, he answered "No, no, no," pointed at the expected-goals numbers, and called the Monaco defeat "inexplicable". His club backed him on the spot: on Friday, hours before kick-off against Monaco, PSG announced contract extensions for Luis Enrique to 2030 and for João Neves , Willian Pacho , Lucas Beraldo , Senny Mayulu and Fabián Ruiz . The French press has settled on the word "préoccupant". Concerning, not yet a crisis. It is worth remembering they sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool for a reported £106m and Gonçalo Ramos to Milan , and are integrating Ferran Torres and Maghnes Akliouche in their places. Manchester City , meanwhile, look ominously well. Enzo Maresca took a job nobody has held since 2016 and has won his first three league games and now his first European one, 2-0 at the Estádio do Dragão. Haaland scored on 67 and in stoppage time to reach 59 goals in 59 Champions League appearances, four days after his winner against Coventry City became the 300th goal of his career. City spent something close to £320m rebuilding a midfield they had gutted, selling Rodri to Barcelona and buying Elliot Anderson , Ayyoub Bouaddi and, on deadline day, Enzo Fernández from Chelsea . "The squad is complete," Maresca said. On the evidence of eleven days, he is not wrong. The romance came from further down the pots. AEK Athens won a Champions League match for the first time in 20 years, Răzvan Marin bending in a free kick to beat LASK . Real Betis , in their first Champions League game in 21 years, went to Lille, fell behind twice and won 3-2 with two Marc Bartra headers either side of half-time and a Parrott finish on the hour. Aston Villa , who won the Europa League in May and have not scored a Premier League goal all season, went to Club Brugge and won 3-2 through John McGinn and Nicolas Jackson . That is the competition doing what the 36-team format promised: giving good clubs somewhere to be extraordinary. Borussia Dortmund 's 3-2 over Villarreal was the strangest of the six: five goals in the second half, an own goal by Renato Veiga , two from Serhou Guirassy including a penalty he won himself, then a Guirassy own goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time. It was also overshadowed. Konstantinos Karetsas , the 18-year-old signed from Genk in the summer, collapsed with circulatory problems in the 27th minute and was taken to hospital. The club said afterwards that he "is doing well under the circumstances", which was the only line from the night that mattered. The rest of matchday one lands across Wednesday and Thursday, and it is the better half of the card. Liverpool host Atlético Madrid at Anfield, which pitches Andoni Iraola 's high-line, high-pressing Liverpool against the one manager in Europe who has built a twelve-year career out of making that style look naive. Iraola has inherited a club that finished fifth, sacked Arne Slot , lost Mohamed Salah on a free transfer and replaced him with £161m of Barcola and Jérémy Jacquet . Diego Simeone arrives with Julián Álvarez , Ademola Lookman , Cristian Romero and Jonathan David , and having just been beaten 3-0 at Athletic Club . Anfield against Atlético has never once been dull. Elsewhere on Wednesday, Barcelona open at a Camp Nou now licensed for 62,652 and still being rebuilt around them, having scored 17 goals in four league games. Napoli , two straight league defeats in and missing Scott McTominay , host a visitor Massimiliano Allegri has publicly told his players is worth chasing 12 points in this phase for. And PSG, mercifully, get Slovan Bratislava . Thursday is the competition's exclusive night: Bayern Munich host Bodø/Glimt , Manchester United are back in the Champions League against Sabah , Roma return after seven years away at Fenerbahçe , and Como play the first Champions League match in their history at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, a 13,602-seat ground on the lake that UEFA formally cleared only five days ago. Eight games each, one table of 36, and a final in Madrid on June 5. This edition closed before Wednesday's results were confirmed, so treat the card below as the state of play at press time. The early reading is that the favourites are Manchester City and Barcelona, that Real Madrid are a better team than their nerves suggest, and that the holders have a great deal of work to do before anyone should write them off. Champions of Europe rarely stay 14th for long. Key Facts · The Route to Madrid Format. 36 clubs, one league table, eight matches each against eight different opponents. Top eight go straight to the last 16. Ninth to 24th play a knockout play-off round. Matchdays. MD1 Sept 8 to 10 · MD2 Oct 13 to 14 · MD3 Oct 20 to 21 · MD4 Nov 3 to 4 · MD5 Nov 24 to 25 · MD6 Dec 8 to 9 · MD7 Jan 19 to 20 · MD8 Jan 27, all kicking off simultaneously. Final. Europa League league phase begins Sept 16 to 17. Conference League begins Oct 15 and runs to six matchdays, with the final at the Beşiktaş Stadium in Istanbul on June 2. Klopp came back, for a country. Mourinho went home. Zidane took France. If you stopped watching in May, almost nothing you knew about who stands on the touchline is still true. The scale of it only registers when you list it. Pep Guardiola resigned at Manchester City on May 22 after a decade, and did not take another club: he is now a global ambassador for City Football Group. Arne Slot was sacked by Liverpool eight days later, a year after winning the league, having taken 20 defeats in all competitions. Eddie Howe stepped down at Newcastle United at the end of July after nearly five years and a 12th-place finish. Neither Slot nor Howe has taken a new job. The vacancies cascaded. Enzo Maresca left Chelsea in January and, after a spell out, took the City job in June. Xabi Alonso , who left Real Madrid by mutual consent in January, is now at Stamford Bridge on a four-year deal, having succeeded a caretaker regime that followed Liam Rosenior 's April dismissal. Andoni Iraola went from Bournemouth to Liverpool; Marco Rose replaced him. Oliver Glasner left Crystal Palace for Nottingham Forest , and Pierre Sage came the other way from France. Álvaro Arbeloa , who managed Real Madrid for part of last season, is at Fulham . Marco Silva left Fulham for Benfica , where he replaced Mourinho. Mourinho, of course, went to the Bernabéu, appointed on June 11 and confirmed as one of Florentino Pérez 's explicit election promises. Pérez was re-elected on June 7 with 64.79 per cent against the challenger Enrique Riquelme , whose ticket had promised Jürgen Klopp as coach and Raúl as sporting director. Klopp went somewhere else entirely: on July 24 he was appointed manager of Germany , taking over from Julian Nagelsmann on a contract to 2030 after Germany went out of their own generation's World Cup in the round of 32, beaten on penalties by Paraguay . His Red Bull contract contained an exit clause written for precisely this job. He has not yet taken charge of a competitive game. His first is on September 27. Italy changed almost as completely. Rúben Amorim is at Milan , Massimiliano Allegri at Napoli , Luciano Spalletti at Juventus , Gian Piero Gasperini at Roma , Maurizio Sarri at Atalanta , Gennaro Gattuso at Lazio , Cristian Chivu at Inter . Nine of the twenty Serie A clubs changed coach before a ball was kicked, and Fiorentina have already changed again. In France, Zinedine Zidane has succeeded Didier Deschamps as national coach, Filipe Luís has taken Monaco to the top of Ligue 1, and Davide Ancelotti has his first job in charge of a major club at Lille . What ties it together is the World Cup. A tournament that finished on July 19 compressed every pre-season in Europe, delayed the Premier League by a week and the Bundesliga by another, and gave clubs a natural moment to end things. The cost is being paid now, in September, by squads that had four weeks instead of eight and by managers being asked to install new ideas in players who have not stopped running since February. Read the tables in that light and the surprises look less like accidents. Transfer News The European windows shut on September 1. What follows is the reckoning: who spent, who was dismantled, and which threads are still live. Then they rebuilt from scratch. Elliot Anderson arrived from Nottingham Forest for £116m. Ayyoub Bouaddi , 19, came from Lille for a reported £81.4m on August 26. "The squad is complete," Enzo Maresca said afterwards, which is the sort of line a manager only gets to use once. Three league wins from three and a 2-0 in Porto suggest the money has landed. Newcastle United sold Anthony Gordon to Barcelona for £69.3m on July 1, Sandro Tonali to Tottenham for £92.5m five days later, and Bruno Guimarães for £75m on August 8. Their manager of nearly five years, Eddie Howe , had resigned at the end of July. Three of their four best players and the man who built the side, gone inside six weeks. That is not a club raising cash. That is a club changing its mind about what it wants to be. Nine years, and it ended on a technicality of contract law. Liverpool replaced him at the top of the market. Operational since September 2025 under the Football Governance Act, it issued its first formal reprimand in August, to Morecambe of the National League North, for failing to answer information requests. x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World football, reported and explained Wednesday, September 2, 2026 · The Deadline Week Edition In this edition The Lead · Messi Steps Away · The Boardroom War · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead The night the window broke its own record, then broke its word English clubs spent 3.46 billion pounds and sent a British record fee across Manchester. Then, in the two hours after the 11pm buzzer, two agreed deals fell apart and left Chelsea, Everton and Monaco staring at each other across the wreckage. T he 2026 summer window did not so much close as buckle. By the time the Premier League's 11pm deadline passed on Tuesday night, English clubs had committed a record 3.46 billion pounds in gross spending, comfortably beating the previous high of 3.14bn, with 475m of it transacted on the final day alone. The figures come from FootballTransfers founder Paul Macdonald , supplied to BBC Sport. They describe a market with no ceiling, only a clock. The headline act was a 200-mile move that felt like a defection. Enzo Fernandez left Chelsea for Manchester City for 125 million pounds , equalling the British record set twelve months earlier when Liverpool paid the same for Alexander Isak. Sky Sports and ESPN both reported a five-year contract. The Argentine had told Chelsea he wanted to go more than three months ago; the club set a bid deadline a fortnight out and held to it. Chelsea banked an 18m profit on the 107m they gave Benfica three and a half years ago, a modest return on a player of that stature and a sign of how completely the Stamford Bridge trading model now governs football decisions. There is a symmetry to where he landed. Enzo Maresca , Fernandez's head coach at Chelsea for a year and a half until December 2025, is now in the City dugout, appointed on 29 June to replace Pep Guardiola after a decade and costing around 17m in compensation. He inherits the two domestic cups, the most expensive midfield reconstruction in the sport's history, and two wins from two. Key Facts Manchester City rebuilt a midfield from scratch Out this summer: Rodri to Barcelona, Bernardo Silva to Real Madrid on a free, Tijjani Reijnders In: Enzo Fernandez 125m, Elliot Anderson 116m, Ayyoub Bouaddi 86m Combined outlay on those three: 327m pounds Club-record gross spend for the window: 458m pounds , net 154m Sources: Sky Sports, ESPN, FootballTransfers via BBC Sport And then the deadline passed, and the evening turned strange. Chelsea had spent the day executing a plan: sell Fernandez, replace him with Lamine Camara of Monaco for 47m. Sky's Kaveh Solhekol , who drove the coverage, reported that the agreement was written, signed and subject only to a medical, with a six-year contract waiting and the player booked to fly into London. Monaco had been willing to sell a first-team midfielder because they believed they were about to receive 40m from Everton for Folarin Balogun . That Balogun deal wobbled. The striker travelled to Merseyside and something in the medical gave Everton's doctors pause. Reporting from RMC Sport and Get French Football News described a failed medical; Monaco and the player's camp insisted he was fit, having played through the World Cup with a minor problem. Everton went back and renegotiated the terms. Monaco, suddenly comfortable again that the money was coming, informed Chelsea in writing that they were withdrawing from the Camara agreement . That notification arrived after 11pm. “Everything was done, written, agreed, signed. He was flying into London.” Kaveh Solhekol, Sky Sports, on Chelsea's collapsed move for Lamine Camara Then came the last turn of the screw. Shortly after midnight, with the deal sheets still running and Everton believing they had their striker, Balogun changed his mind and pulled out. Everton were described in Sky's reporting as stunned. So Monaco kept both players, Chelsea got neither, and Everton, having already sold Beto to Fiorentina for 15.4m, went to bed with Thierno Barry as their only recognised centre-forward. The detail that matters most is what Chelsea did next, which was nothing. They held a contractual option to cancel the Fernandez sale if the replacement fell through. They chose not to use it. Sky reported the club described Monaco's conduct as extraordinary and deeply unprofessional, and honoured their side anyway. It will be relitigated every time Chelsea's midfield looks light between now and January, and it has left a live grudge between two clubs who must talk again in four months. Zoom out and the window's shape is clear enough. The money moved toward two poles: Manchester City rebuilding for a new manager, and Liverpool spending 123m on Bradley Barcola to replace a departed Mohamed Salah . Four of the five largest transfers in Premier League history were completed in this single window. Tottenham spent 302m and have started the season with two defeats, no goals and bottom place. Ipswich Town , promoted in May, spent 171m. This is the first window run under the league's new Squad Cost Ratio regime, which replaced PSR in November on a 14 to 6 vote and caps squad spending at 85 per cent of revenue with a six-point deduction waiting at the red threshold. The first assessment checkpoint arrives in October. Somebody is going to fail it. What the numbers cannot capture is the sense that the deadline has stopped functioning as a deadline. Deal sheets extended completions by two hours. A signed agreement was torn up after the buzzer with no consequence. A player who had passed a medical walked away at half past midnight. The transfer window is supposed to be the one moment in football where the paperwork binds. On Tuesday night it was a suggestion. Messi closes the international book, and then scores four Six weeks after losing a World Cup final, Argentina's most capped player and record scorer said goodbye to the shirt. Two days earlier he had produced the best individual night of his MLS career. On Monday, Lionel Messi announced on Instagram that he had played his last match for Argentina . He is 39. The statement was drafted on 21 July, two days after the World Cup final, and he said the death of his father Jorge on 8 August made him more certain of it. He leaves with 207 caps and 125 goals, both national records, alongside the 2022 World Cup, the 2021 and 2024 Copa America titles and Olympic gold from 2008. He also holds the World Cup records for appearances, 34, and assists, 12, and is the oldest outfield player ever to start a final. The timing is worth sitting with. Argentina lost the final in New Jersey to Spain , 1-0 after extra time, to a goal from Ferran Torres . Messi finished as the tournament's second-highest scorer and made the Best XI. There was no decline to point at and no injury to blame. He decided a sixth World Cup was the end of the road and closed it himself rather than waiting to be closed out. A 2028 Copa America appearance has not been formally ruled out, but nothing in the statement invited that reading. Club football, meanwhile, is going rather well. On Saturday night Inter Miami beat CF Montreal 7-1, a club record for goals in a match, and Messi scored four of them and assisted a fifth . Two were direct free kicks. It took him to 927 career goals, to 74 free-kick goals, third all-time, and to 98 for Inter Miami. He is the 19th player in MLS history to score four in a game, and reached 20 multi-goal MLS matches in 72 appearances, faster than anyone before him. The win also ended a five-game winless run, which was the actual point of the evening. He now leads the Golden Boot race on 18 goals and 10 assists, and is chasing a third straight MVP. UEFA moves to prosecute the FIFA president A plan to sell a fifth of the World Cup's commercial arm to private investors has been withdrawn. The war it started has not been. The most consequential football story of the week involves no players. FIFA proposed creating a private commercial vehicle, FIFA Forward Enterprise, to run World Cup commercial operations, and selling a 21 per cent minority stake at a 20 billion dollar valuation to raise roughly 4.2bn. The lead investor was to be Thrive Capital, run by Joshua Kushner , with JP Morgan involved. Member associations were offered 40m dollars each over four years to approve it, on a 53-day deadline. All 55 UEFA members rejected it unanimously and threatened to withdraw European teams from every FIFA competition, which put the Women's Under-20 World Cup in September, the Under-17 tournament in October and the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil directly at risk. Concacaf's 41 nations also refused, citing the artificially short deadline and the absence of any review. FIFA folded. On 27 August, UEFA published a statement from its national association representatives confirming that FIFA had committed in writing to withdrawing the scheme irrevocably and permanently, and that the boycott threat was suspended. The same statement called the affair a profound failure of judgement and an abuse of presidential power, said the trust required to hold the FIFA presidency has been broken and cannot be restored, and committed the signatories to backing alternative candidates should Gianni Infantino seek re-election. Sky Sports reported the same day that UEFA is preparing criminal proceedings against Infantino in Switzerland for criminal mismanagement under Article 158, and has filed in the Southern District of New York to subpoena FIFA and its banks. Kushner, speaking publicly on Monday, said Thrive had failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football. Aleksander Ceferin has called the proposal a shady, opaque backroom deal. The tournaments are safe. The presidency is not. Transfer News Liverpool spend 123m to fill a hole Salah left Andoni Iraola's first window emptied the dressing room of its landmarks and replaced them with one very expensive winger. Liverpool completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday, one day before the deadline, for a total Sky Sports put at 123m pounds : 106m guaranteed plus add-ons, on a five-year contract. It is the second most expensive signing in the club's history behind Isak. French coverage frames the same deal at around 140m euros rising to 145m, and reports it as the largest sale in PSG's history, beating the 90m Neymar fee, and the biggest fee ever paid for a player leaving Ligue 1. Lyon , his first club, collect around 4.9m in solidarity payments. Reporters Mark McAdam and Lyall Thomas had the 120m agreement in principle on 29 August; PSG had been asking 145m. The scale of the churn at Anfield is what makes the fee legible. Mohamed Salah left on a free for Trabzonspor in August, ending his contract a year early by mutual consent after a season in which Arne Slot dropped him, and departing as the club's third-highest scorer with 257 goals in 442 games. Ibrahima Konate and Andy Robertson also left on frees, Konate to Real Madrid . Curtis Jones went to Inter for 30m on 21 August after 16 years, and Harvey Elliott joined Valencia on loan on deadline day. In came Barcola, Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes for 72m in July, and Lucca Brughmans from Genk for 30m, immediately loaned back. Jamie Carragher, on Sky, put the obvious question about fit: he called Barcola a great player but a left winger, which is a polite way of noting that Liverpool already have Cody Gakpo there. Which brings us to the loose end. ESPN reported that Liverpool rejected an 80m bid from Manchester City for Gakpo, who was understood to be open to the move, and that City then pivoted to Ndiaye. He is still a Liverpool player. He will not be a quiet one in January. Spain closes: Madrid stand still, Barcelona register at the buzzer Jose Mourinho wanted a midfielder and a left-footed centre-back. He got neither, and said so through intermediaries rather than in a press conference. Real Madrid did no deadline-day business at all. Journalist Jose Felix Diaz reported that the club had closed the window, with Mourinho's requested midfielder unavailable because Barcelona had already taken Rodri , and Inter refusing to sell Alessandro Bastoni . Eduardo Camavinga attracted Premier League interest and Raul Asencio was made available; both declined to leave. It caps a window in which Madrid still spent around 225m euros, their heaviest since 2019: Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig for a club record reported between 125m and 140m, Marc Cucurella at 55m, Denzel Dumfries at 20m and free transfers for Konate and Bernardo Silva . One Madrid player did move, and it is a homecoming. Dani Ceballos signed for Real Betis on a free in the early hours of Wednesday, a three-year deal to June 2029, at the club that developed him between 2014 and 2017 before Madrid paid 16.5m for him. Fabrizio Romano confirmed it with the phrase he reserves for done deals. Betis had to clear salary-cap room to register him. Barcelona finished theirs on Wednesday morning by registering Gabriel Jesus , signed for around 10m euros plus variables on a deal to 2029, and goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic , bought from Fenerbahce for 2m plus 500,000 in variables. Both cleared La Liga registration with room to spare, which is not a sentence Barcelona have been able to write in recent summers, though club reporting notes the limits were less severe rather than absent. Livakovic had been close to a loan back to Dinamo Zagreb had it failed. Elsewhere, Atletico Madrid took Jonathan David on loan from Juventus with a 25m euro purchase option spread over four financial years, giving Diego Simeone a third senior centre-forward behind Julian Alvarez and Alexander Sorloth. And Sevilla closed 27 operations across the window, 16 of them exits, and did three on the final day: Felix Correia from Lille, Lucas Stassin from Saint-Etienne and Youssouf Fofana from Milan, registered five minutes past midnight. x: One Club · Every Angle · Every Tuesday The Weekly Arsenal Digest No. 3 · Tuesday, September 1, 2026 · Deadline Day Edition · North London In This Edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Squad · Hale End · Arsenal Women · Gunners Abroad · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Arsenal Sell the Summer and Back What They Already Have Gabriel Jesus is a Barcelona player. Gabriel Martinelli is bound for Riyadh in the biggest sale the club has ever made. Julian Alvarez is still not an Arsenal player. With hours left in the window, the champions look leaner, considerably richer, and unbeaten. T here is a version of this deadline day in which Arsenal look like a club in retreat. Two forwards gone in twenty-four hours. A first-choice target who never wanted to come. A late alternative lost to Sunderland over a few million pounds. Read the outgoing column alone and you would guess the champions were dismantling something. The table says otherwise. Arsenal have played three competitive matches since lifting the title in May. They have won all three, scored seven, and conceded none. They beat Manchester City 3-0 in Cardiff, Coventry City 3-0 at home, and Aston Villa 1-0 at Villa Park on Monday night without ever looking troubled. That is the context for everything Andrea Berta has done this summer. Arsenal did not need to buy from a position of weakness, and they have not. Bruno Guimaraes arrived from Newcastle United for £75m on August 9 . Ezri Konsa followed from Aston Villa for £55m on August 21 . Neither was a panic buy. The selling has been just as deliberate, and rather more brutal. Gabriel Jesus completed his move to Barcelona for £8.6m after four years, 123 appearances and 32 goals. He took a pay cut to go. Gabriel Martinelli is on his way to Al-Hilal for a fee that will comfortably break the club's record for a sale. Key Facts: Deadline Day Window closes: 11pm BST Tuesday, September 1, which is 3pm Pacific. The women's window runs until 11pm BST on Thursday, September 3. Confirmed today: Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona . Fabio Vieira to Hamburg . Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund on a season-long loan. Agreed, awaiting announcement: Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal . Unresolved at press time: Julian Alvarez. Gone elsewhere: Malick Fofana, to Sunderland . Two departures of that size would normally be balanced by a marquee arrival. That is where the summer has stalled. Julian Alvarez has been the target since the spring, and the pursuit has never once looked comfortable. Atletico Madrid will not sell to Barcelona , the club the player actually wants. Arsenal have spent weeks trying to be a destination rather than a fallback. Sky Sports reported on Friday that Atletico had set the player a deadline to commit or engage. Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin said publicly that Alvarez was "really struggling" and that "there were people who misled him, who left him confused." Not the language of a club expecting a clean resolution. "We have to sell what we want to sell as well, not just to sell. We have to be very careful, because some of the assets, after maybe they grow and we still want them." Mikel Arteta, August 30 Deadline Day Churn The reporting since has pulled hard in both directions, which is what deadline day does to a story. Spanish outlets suggested on Tuesday morning that Arsenal had stepped back and were assessing alternatives . Hours later, TEAMtalk and the Evening Standard were reporting the opposite: a green light at roughly £130m, a willingness to write a future Barcelona release into the contract, and help relocating the player's family. Treat that second version carefully. It is single-sourced, it is not carried by David Ornstein or Fabrizio Romano , and it arrived precisely when deadline-day traffic peaks. What is solid is Romano 's line that Barcelona now consider their incoming business closed after signing Jesus , and will not activate the €100m bid president Joan Laporta confirmed was still live. Which leaves Arteta where he has been all summer: with Kai Havertz fit and scoring, Viktor Gyokeres unused, and a squad that has not yet needed rescuing. He was blunt on Monday night. "We are trying to improve the squad, and until tomorrow night we're going to try to do that." He also warned against selling for the sake of it. The honest reading is that this window has been a success in structure and a frustration in ambition. Arsenal have upgraded midfield and defence, cleared £80m or more of wages and fees from players who were not going to start, and kept their powder dry on a striker they were never going to get cheaply. Whether that reads as discipline or as a missed opportunity depends entirely on what Havertz 's hamstrings do between now and January. Race Tracker: The Table After Two Pos Club P GD Pts 1 Manchester City 2 +4 6 2 Arsenal 2 +4 6 3 Hull City 2 +3 6 4 Chelsea 2 +2 6 5 Brentford 2 +3 4 Four clubs remain unbeaten. Arsenal are the only one of them yet to concede. Standings via Sports Mole . Seven Scored, None Conceded, and No Saliba The champions have started their defence with their best defender in rehabilitation and a 22-year-old centre-half nobody expected to be first choice. It has not cost them a goal. William Saliba came back from the World Cup with a back problem picked up in France's semi-final. Surgery was considered and rejected in favour of a managed rehabilitation programme . He is not expected back until winter. Jurrien Timber has not played since the Champions League final and had minor groin surgery over the summer. Arteta says he is progressing well but remains weeks from full training. September or October is the realistic window. So the back line at Villa Park read Ben White , Cristhian Mosquera , Gabriel Magalhaes and Riccardo Calafiori , with David Raya behind them. Villa did not register a single shot on target all night. They are still without a goal after two matches. Mosquera is the story inside the story. Signed as depth, he has started every competitive match and handled Nicolas Jackson and Emiliano Buendia without fuss on Monday. He came off on 79 minutes holding the back of his leg, which is how Konsa got his debut against his old club. Arteta said afterwards: "He is fine. But he was feeling like he was about to have something. He could not continue." Transfer News Martinelli to Al-Hilal: the Biggest Sale in Arsenal's History Seven seasons, 278 appearances, 62 goals, and a fee that pushes past Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's 2017 departure. Gabriel Martinelli has been left out of Arsenal matchday squads since the season began, which is usually its own kind of announcement. He is 25. He arrived as a teenager from Ituano and leaves as a Premier League champion. The fee has climbed as the week has gone on. Daily Cannon reported a verbally agreed £56.5m on Saturday. By Sunday, David Ornstein was reporting a €70m fixed fee , up from an earlier structure of €58m plus €8m in add-ons. James Benge reported that the two clubs had been working through a sell-on clause. At any of those numbers it is a club record for an outgoing transfer, comfortably clear of the £40m Liverpool paid for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain nine years ago. Fabrizio Romano reported that Arsenal granted authorisation for the player to travel. Announcement is expected before the window shuts. Certainty tier: fee agreed and personal terms done, awaiting official confirmation. Reported by Ornstein and Romano independently, which is about as firm as it gets without a club statement. Gabriel Jesus Joins Barcelona, and Takes a Pay Cut to Do It A four-year Arsenal career that never quite recovered from a knee injury ends for £8.6m and a three-year deal in Catalonia. Gabriel Jesus arrived from Manchester City in 2022 for £45m and changed the mood around the club almost immediately. He leaves having started three Premier League matches last season, his campaign wrecked by the knee injury he suffered in the FA Cup in January 2025. Barcelona paid €10m, around £8.6m, on a contract running to June 2029. Jesus has since confirmed he reduced his salary to make the move happen. He consulted Raphinha , Joao Cancelo , Rodri and Eric Garcia before deciding. "I have the opportunity now to be here at Barca," he said on arrival. "It's a dream for me." He finishes with 123 appearances and 32 goals for Arsenal , plus a title medal he did much of the early work for. There is a strategic footnote. Romano reported that signing Jesus is what closed Barcelona 's incoming market and killed any late move for Alvarez . In selling a squad striker cheaply, Arsenal may have removed their own competition for a better one. Certainty tier: official. Announced by both clubs on September 1. Fofana Slips Away on a Question of Structure Personal terms agreed, structure not. Sunderland moved, Crystal Palace counter-moved, and the Belgian ended up doing his medical in France without knowing who for. Arsenal 's late look at Malick Fofana was first reported on Sunday night by the Evening Standard's Matt Verri . The 21-year-old Lyon winger fits an obvious hole: pace and directness from the left, which the champions have lacked since Martinelli stopped playing. According to Ornstein , Arsenal got as far as agreeing personal terms before refusing to meet Lyon 's €40m valuation. Romano added the detail that mattered: Arsenal only ever wanted a loan or a loan with an obligation, not a permanent purchase at that price. Sunderland had no such reservations and agreed roughly €30m plus add-ons, with a five-year contract to 2031. Crystal Palace then matched the package and tried to win the player on personal terms. What followed was the most deadline-day scene of the day. Two private jets waited at Lyon airport, one bound for the north east and one for London. French journalist Romain Molina reported that Fofana completed his medical in France while still deciding where he was going. He went to Sunderland . Certainty tier: dead for Arsenal . Confirmed independently by Ornstein and Romano . Nwaneri Goes to Dortmund, and the Reason Is Eze A season-long loan with a recall option for the 19-year-old, after a Marseille spell that fell apart through no fault of his own. Ethan Nwaneri flew to Germany on Tuesday morning and completed a season-long loan to Borussia Dortmund . He remains under contract at Arsenal until 2030, and the deal carries a recall option. The reasoning is straightforward and slightly sad. The arrival of Eberechi Eze pushed him down a pecking order that already contained Bukayo Saka , Martin Odegaard and Mikel Merino . Club and player agreed he needed regular football. His January loan to Marseille was undone almost immediately when Roberto De Zerbi was dismissed shortly after he arrived. Dortmund is a better bet: they have an excellent record with young attackers, and they moved after losing Giannis Konstantelias to an ACL injury. A neat detail: Nwaneri scored against Dortmund in Arsenal 's 3-2 pre-season defeat, which is reported to have sharpened their interest. Certainty tier: official. Gyokeres and Barcelona Spanish radio station Cope reported on August 20 that Viktor Gyokeres ' agent is in daily contact with Barcelona sporting director Deco , and that Deco is not interested at this stage. The striker has been talked about as a makeweight in an Alvarez deal. He denied any unhappiness in July: "I feel extremely comfortable at Arsenal." Single-sourced rumour. Nothing from tier-one reporters. A £7m windfall from Everton Everton have agreed to sign Folarin Balogun from Monaco for €45m plus €5m in add-ons, around £42.8m. Sam Dean of the Telegraph reports Arsenal hold a 17.5 per cent sell-on clause , worth between £6.74m and £7.49m. Add it to the £35m from the original sale and Balogun becomes one of the most profitable players the academy has produced. Reported by Romano on September 1. Bartishvili, pre-agreed for 2027 Arsenal have agreed terms to sign Georgian attacking midfielder Andria Bartishvili from Kolkheti 1913 when he turns 18 in March 2027. The player has publicly thanked supporters for the reaction. Agreement reported, not yet a registrable transfer. The bookmakers' list Several outlets ran deadline-day pieces listing Marcus Rashford , Adam Wharton and Eli Junior Kroupi as Arsenal possibilities. Those lists are built from betting odds, not reporting, and none of the three has been linked by a credible Arsenal source. Treat as noise. The Squad Arteta Has Found a Midfield Two, and One Half of It Is a Left-Back Myles Lewis-Skelly started alongside Declan Rice at Villa Park. A £75m midfielder watched from the bench until the 71st minute. The XI at Villa Park was Raya ; White , Mosquera , Gabriel , Calafiori ; Rice , Lewis-Skelly , Odegaard ; Saka , Havertz , Tzolis . A 4-2-3-1 in name, closer to a 4-3-3 in practice. The interesting selection is Lewis-Skelly . He came through as a midfielder, was converted to left-back out of necessity, and is now being converted back. He was excellent on Monday, progressing the ball cleanly and giving Rice licence to push. That has an immediate consequence for Bruno Guimaraes . Signed for £75m three weeks ago, he picked up a thigh problem in the Community Shield, missed the opener, and got 19 minutes at Villa Park. Reviewers liked what they saw: a different passing register, more forward risk. He is being eased in rather than built around. Christos Tzolis is having the harder introduction. Excellent against Coventry , where he was involved in the first two goals, he was withdrawn at half-time at Villa Park after a poor 45 minutes. The Premier League's physicality is the standard first hurdle for a Belgian league arrival. Nobody at the club will be worried yet. Eberechi Eze replaced him and changed the game. He was the link in the winning goal, receiving from Mosquera and finding Calafiori , whose low cross Saka turned in on 59 minutes. That is Calafiori 's second assist in consecutive matches, and he is quietly the most productive left-sided player at the club right now. The Number Nine Question The number nine question has an answer, at least for now. Havertz starts. Gyokeres , who scored 21 goals in 56 appearances last season, has played 15 minutes all campaign and was an unused substitute in both league games. Arteta put it carefully on Tuesday: "Sometimes you have certain issues with players physically that you have to make changes, and I'm sure there are going to be minutes for everybody." Scorers So Far, All Competitions Kai Havertz 2 (Community Shield, Coventry) Bukayo Saka 2 (Coventry, Aston Villa) Martin Odegaard 2 (Community Shield, Coventry) Riccardo Calafiori 1 (Community Shield, after 24 seconds) Odegaard is the other quiet subplot. Arteta was pointed about him last week: "He's fit and available, I think that's the baseline. Last season he had too many incidents where it didn't allow him to have any consistency." Two goals in three games is a start. He was withdrawn on 71 minutes at Villa Park, which reads as management rather than concern. One theme worth watching all season is squad size. Arteta renewed his campaign against the 20-outfield-player matchday limit last week: "That's what I've been begging the Premier League. Every squad needs more than 20 outfield players, ideally, to sustain the level of demands, games, international games that we have." With eight Champions League league-phase fixtures plus two domestic cups, he will make that argument again. Injuries & Availability William Saliba (back). Injured on World Cup duty with France. Surgery declined in favour of rehabilitation. Expected back in winter. Jurrien Timber (groin). Minor summer surgery. Has not played since the Champions League final. Targeting September or October. Cristhian Mosquera (precautionary). Withdrawn on 79 minutes at Villa Park. Arteta expects him available for Chelsea . Bruno Guimaraes (thigh, resolved). Missed the opener, returned as a substitute on Monday. Full round-up here . Hale End A Restocked Academy, a New Interim Coach, and Two Red Cards Six recruits in a fortnight, a debut goal at Brighton, and an under-18 side that has not won a game yet. The academy recruitment department has had the busiest week of anyone at the club. James Scanlon , a 19-year-old winger with 24 caps for Gibraltar , arrived from Manchester United . So did Habeeb Ogunneye , a 20-year-old right-back who spent last season on loan at Newport County , taking squad number 62. They were joined by Axel Donczew , a 16-year-old Welsh winger from Cardiff City who signed scholarship terms and turns professional in February 2027, and Igor Tyjon , an 18-year-old striker from Blackburn Rovers with three senior appearances, wearing 64. Both new arrivals went straight in at Brighton on Monday and both looked the part. Scanlon scored on debut after 24 minutes, set up by Ife Ibrahim . Ogunneye started at right-back. Marli Salmon , who signed his first professional contract on turning 17 last week, captained the side. Brighton led 2-1 through Younes Ibrahim and Bailey Palmer before Evan Mooney equalised in the 88th minute. That is two points from two Premier League 2 games, after a 1-1 draw with Crystal Palace . The EFL Trophy has been less kind: a 5-1 defeat at Barnet on August 18. The Under-18s The under-18s are struggling more seriously. They lost 2-1 at Brighton on August 29 with nine men. Emerson Nwaneri , younger brother of Ethan, was sent off for a second bookable offence in the first half. Goalkeeper Jack Talbot followed late on. Abraham Owusu-Gyasi had put the ten men ahead on 61 minutes before Daniel Rudin equalised three minutes later and Raffaele Oppong won it on 84. That leaves the under-18s with one point from three league games and no win in four in all competitions. Josh Smith has been promoted from assistant to interim head coach. Out on Loan On the loan front, Ismeal Kabia has settled fast at St Mirren , debuting the day after his August 17 move and playing 59 minutes in a 5-1 defeat to Rangers . Four academy players trained with the first team before the Villa game: Josh Ogunnaike , Ceadach O'Neill , Archie Stevens and Theo Julienne . Arsenal Women Slegers Rebuilds Around Stanway, and Finally Buys a Centre-Half Seven in, ten out, a new build-up structure, and Elisa de Almeida arriving from PSG days before the champions open at Brighton. This has been the most aggressive summer Arsenal 's women's team has had in years, and it needed to be. Renee Slegers won the WSL last season with 51 points from 22 games, lost one match all campaign, and won the inaugural FIFA Women's Champions Cup by beating Corinthians 3-2 in February. Then she lost half her spine. The Turnover Beth Mead left for Manchester City after nine years. Katie McCabe went to Chelsea , Victoria Pelova to Tottenham , Laia Codina to West Ham , Manuela Zinsberger to Borussia Dortmund . Jenna Nighswonger , Rosa Kafaji , Laila Harbert and Vivienne Lia also went. In came Georgia Stanway from Bayern Munich , Ona Batlle from Barcelona , Misa Rodriguez from Real Madrid , Geraldine Reuteler from Eintracht Frankfurt , Selina Cerci from Hoffenheim , Lisa Baum from RB Leipzig and Isabella Damm from Brondby . Kim Little , Steph Catley , Leah Williamson and Caitlin Foord all extended. The Signing One hole stayed open all summer, and it is being filled this week. BBC Sport's Emma Sanders reported on Tuesday that Arsenal have agreed a deal for Elisa de Almeida , the 28-year-old France defender, from Paris Saint-Germain for around £550,000 . Arseblog News sources say it is in the final stages. She would be the first centre-half Arsenal have signed since Codina in 2023, and she is needed. Katie Reid is recovering from an ACL injury, and in the Charlton friendly Slegers was reduced to playing midfielder Smilla Holmberg at centre-back. The women's window stays open until 11pm BST on Thursday. Pre-season Form Pre-season suggested the rebuild is coming together. Arsenal beat Paris FC 1-0 on August 23 through an Olivia Smith goal in the 91st minute, then beat Charlton Athletic 5-1 on August 26. Stanway scored her first Arsenal goal, with Mariona Caldentey from the penalty spot, Kyra Cooney-Cross , Smith and Frida Maanum adding the rest. Cooney-Cross ' goal was the one that mattered. The Australian returned to competitive football after five months away on compassionate leave following her mother's terminal cancer diagnosis, and marked it with a long-range strike. Slegers called her "amazing" since coming back. How They Will Play Tactically, the interesting change is Stanway 's role. She is dropping between the centre-backs in build-up with Kim Little ahead of her as a shield, a 3-1-6 shape that takes progression duties off Little and Mariona and adds a genuine long diagonal passer. Arsenal are also shooting from range far more often, a direct response to their trouble breaking low blocks. "We had more shots and more end product," Slegers said. "That is something we spoke about." The other pattern to watch is the rotation between Holmberg and Baum , both 19, on the right: one holds the touchline while the other inverts as a right-sided ten. Individual honours arrived last week too. Alessia Russo , Emily Fox and Mariona Caldentey were all named in the PFA WSL Team of the Year, and Olivia Smith won the PFA Women's Young Player of the Year award for a second consecutive season. Russo scored 24 goals in all competitions last term. Gunners Abroad A Rare Week With Nobody Away, and a Diaspora That Keeps Growing The post-World Cup calendar pushed the first international window to late September. In the meantime, the list of Arsenal players plying their trade elsewhere has grown by five in a fortnight. There is no international football this week and none next. Because the World Cup ran into July, UEFA pushed the opening Nations League league-phase window into the second half of September. The headline fixture of that window is England against Spain at Wembley on September 26, a game likely to feature Arsenal players on both sides. So this section belongs to the departed and the loaned. Ethan Nwaneri is now a Borussia Dortmund player for the season, and will be in Germany when Arsenal host his loan club in the Champions League on November 24. He remains recallable. Ismeal Kabia is the only other current Arsenal player out on loan in the men's game. He has played once for St Mirren , 59 minutes in a heavy defeat at Rangers , which is exactly the sort of chastening Scottish Premiership afternoon a loan is for. Among the recently departed, Jakub Kiwior is at Porto , Leandro Trossard at Besiktas , Karl Hein at Werder Bremen , Fabio Vieira now at Hamburg , Gabriel Jesus at Barcelona and Gabriel Martinelli heading to Al-Hilal . That is a lot of recent Arsenal football scattered across Europe and the Gulf. On the women's side, Sophie Harwood is at Sheffield United and Jessie Gale at Newcastle United for the season, with Cecily Wellesley-Smith at FC Rosengard in Sweden until December. In Brief Emirates renews through 2033. Arsenal announced a five-year extension of their shirt, training kit and stadium naming rights deal on August 6, described as a significant increase on the previous £45m a year. Chief executive Richard Garlick tied it to the title win. Fabio Vieira joins Hamburg. The Portuguese midfielder completed a permanent move for a reported €9m to €10m on deadline day, four years after arriving from Porto . Reiss Nelson's 19 years end. The 26-year-old winger had his contract terminated by mutual consent on August 27, closing an association with the club that began in the academy. Coventry could not lay a glove on them. In Arsenal 's 3-0 opening-day win, Frank Lampard 's side did not make a single tackle in the first half and registered their first on 69 minutes, a rarity in Opta's records since 2007. Konsa's homecoming. The £55m defender made his Arsenal debut at Villa Park against the club he left ten days earlier, coming on for the injured Mosquera on 79 minutes. A penalty given, then taken away. VAR overturned a second-half penalty at Villa Park after determining Ian Maatsen 's contact on Saka occurred outside the area. Arsenal scored three minutes later anyway. The Champions League draw is done. Made on August 27, it gave Arsenal Real Madrid , Borussia Dortmund , Lille and Sabah at home, and Bayern Munich , Napoli , Real Betis and Slavia Praha away. x: The Weekly Soccer Digest World football, reported and weighed Edition No. 1 · Wednesday, August 26, 2026 Deadline week In this edition The Lead · Transfer News · The Rumour Mill · Around the Leagues · Numbers of the Week · In Brief · What to Watch The Lead Six days left, and the money has not stopped moving The summer window shuts on Tuesday. A World Cup pushed every European calendar back, so for the first time in years the most expensive week of the football year is being played out with the league tables already on the wall. T he transfer window closes on Tuesday, September 1, at 23:00 in England and just before midnight on the continent. Major League Soccer follows a day later, on September 2. That is the ordinary rhythm of a European summer. What is not ordinary is where the season sits when the whistle goes on it. The World Cup finished on July 19 at MetLife Stadium, where Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time through Ferran Torres in the 106th minute, with Enzo Fernandez and Leandro Paredes both sent off. Every domestic calendar in Europe slid back to accommodate it. The Premier League did not start until August 22. The Bundesliga has not started at all: matchday one is Friday. So clubs are now conducting the single most consequential week of their financial year with points already on the board and, in several cases, with a crisis already in the building. The Deadline Board Ten deals that could still land before Tuesday, and how far each has actually travelled.
