Sourcing for each item appears in the write-ups below. One morning, one teenager Consider Wednesday morning as a single data point. Manchester City confirmed the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi , 18, from Lille . Sky Sports reported the structure as £81.3m guaranteed with £4.3m in add-ons, a total of roughly £86m; Lille announced it in euros at £100m equivalent, or a shade under. Whichever currency you prefer, it is the most expensive teenager in Premier League history, comfortably past the £58.9m Manchester United paid for Leny Yoro in 2024. Lille, for their part, called it the largest sale a Ligue 1 club has ever made to a foreign buyer, beating the €80m Nicolas Pepe fetched in 2018. Bouaddi is worth pausing on. He made his European debut at 16 years and three days, a competition record, and became the youngest player of the century in Ligue 1 at 16 years and 20 days. He had 96 senior appearances for Lille before his 19th birthday and started five of Morocco's six matches at the World Cup. In his farewell message he wrote that Lille is “where I grew up, where I learned, and where I experienced my first emotions at the highest level.” City are buying a succession plan, not a squad player. They need one. This is the first City summer without Pep Guardiola , who was replaced on June 29 by Enzo Maresca on a three-year deal. Since then City have sold Rodri to Barcelona for €76.5m, Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah , Savio to Tottenham for £85m and let Bernardo Silva and John Stones go for nothing. Marmoush is at a medical at Spurs, Nico Gonzalez is expected at Newcastle , and Jack Grealish is still unresolved. Money in the other direction has gone on youth: £116m to Nottingham Forest for Elliot Anderson , now £86m to Lille for a teenager. Maresca was asked on Sunday whether more was coming. “We will see, it's eight days to go,” he said. “For sure something is going to happen.” “I would give that an 85 to 90 per cent chance. I think that's gonna happen. I don't think Liverpool would've come this far to walk away from it.” David Ornstein on Bradley Barcola, The Athletic FC Podcast, August 25 Selling as a strategy The second thing this window has confirmed is that selling well is now a strategy rather than an admission of defeat. Chelsea are the purest expression of it. On Tuesday they agreed to send Liam Delap to Nottingham Forest for £45m rising to £50m, a Forest club record, with the medical set for Wednesday. Delap scored three goals in 47 Chelsea appearances. Chelsea paid Ipswich Town £30m for him a year ago. That is a profit of roughly £20m on a player who did not work out, and it is not an accident. In the same seven days Chelsea loaned Benoit Badiashile to Napoli with a purchase option, sold Omari Kellyman to Strasbourg for around €6m, and moved close to selling Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa . Santi Aouna of Foot Mercato reported on Wednesday that the clubs are near an agreement but that Jackson has not yet approved it. Meanwhile Chelsea are the ones saying no: Manchester City want Enzo Fernandez , valued at roughly £120m, and as of Tuesday had not submitted a formal offer. Xabi Alonso , four days into his Chelsea tenure, was careful about it. “My wish is that we know what will happen for the future,” he said, “but we will see this week.” Newcastle have run the same play at a larger scale, banking more than £240m in sales including Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and Anthony Gordon to Barcelona for £69.3m, then spending it across five signings. Tottenham have gone past £300m under Roberto De Zerbi . And on the opening Saturday Tottenham lost 3-0 at Brentford , their joint-heaviest opening-day defeat in Premier League history, conceding 5.63 expected goals. De Zerbi did not hide behind the scoreline. “Our physical condition was not at the right level for all players,” he said, “because many came later after the World Cup.” Spending is not the same as a team, and this summer has left almost nobody time to build one. There is a counterweight, and it is Italy. Juventus lost Dusan Vlahovic for nothing this month when his contract expired and he signed for Besiktas . Asked about the market after his side's opening win at Frosinone , Luciano Spalletti shrugged: “potremmo anche rimanere cosi,” we could even stay as we are. He also conceded that without Champions League football, everyone is available. Calcio e Finanza marked the season's start with a blunt accounting: Serie A's domestic television deal is worth about €900m a season against a €1.2bn target, and of the dozen or so clubs on earth who can spend €100m on a single player, not one of them is Italian. The players stop waiting Which brings us to the third and least comfortable feature of the week: the players have stopped waiting politely. Moise Kean arrived late at Fiorentina's training ground on Wednesday, refused to train with the squad and was fined. Julian Alvarez did not turn up to Atletico Madrid training at all, the club citing indisposition, three days after being whistled by his own supporters. Rafael Leao is training away from the Milan group despite being fit. Ousmane Dembele has been given a week off by PSG that RMC's Daniel Riolo flatly called a punishment. Ollie Watkins has turned down a new Villa contract and made clear he would take the Saudi offer. Five clubs, five different countries, one common cause: a window this short, arriving this late, hands leverage to whoever is willing to make a scene. Six days remain. The tell to watch is not the biggest name but the first domino: if Chelsea blink on Enzo Fernandez, City will have spent north of £200m in a fortnight and Chelsea will have another nine-figure sum to reinvest in January. If they hold, this becomes a window remembered for teenagers rather than superstars. Either way, Tuesday night will be busy. Secondary Feature Nine new managers, and a record that had stood for eighty years Almost half the Premier League changed its head coach this summer. Opta had to go back to 1946 to find anything comparable. Nine of the twenty Premier League clubs began the season with a manager taking charge of his first league game for them. Opta's line, carried by Sky Sports, is that this is the most in an English top-flight season since 1946-47. Serie A very nearly matched it: nine of that league's twenty benches also changed hands, four of them going to men who had never managed in Italy before. The English list reads like a reshuffle of the entire coaching class. Enzo Maresca left Chelsea for Manchester City to replace Pep Guardiola . Xabi Alonso took the Chelsea job Maresca vacated. Andoni Iraola left Bournemouth for Liverpool in succession to Arne Slot , and Marco Rose took the Bournemouth job. Matthias Jaissle replaced Eddie Howe at Newcastle on August 5, the latest appointment of the nine. Oliver Glasner moved from Crystal Palace to Nottingham Forest , with Pierre Sage taking over at Selhurst Park. Alvaro Arbeloa has Fulham after Marco Silva 's departure on June 2, and Gary O'Neil has promoted Ipswich Town . Opening weekend split them neatly. Maresca won on debut, and did it by playing a centre-back in midfield: Marc Guehi scored the 85th-minute equaliser against Bournemouth before Josko Gvardiol won it in stoppage time. “I know Marc from Palace and I always thought he could play as a midfielder because he is very good,” Maresca said. Alonso won too, 3-2 at Fulham , though his goalkeeper Robert Sanchez was at fault for both home goals. “It's a process. It's day one,” Alonso offered. The others got a harder education. Iraola needed a penalty deep into stoppage time from Dominik Szoboszlai to draw 2-2 at Newcastle, where Jaissle, twenty days into the job, had led 2-1. “Hard luck, I would say,” Jaissle said. “I'm really, really happy with the performance after such a short amount of time.” Glasner lost at home to Leeds United to an 88th-minute Anton Stach free-kick, then lost to Leeds again three days later in the Carabao Cup, the only Premier League club knocked out in round two. Sage lost at Everton . Rose lost at City. Arbeloa lost and sounded delighted anyway: “If we continue to play in that way, we're going to win a lot of games.” Only O'Neil, among the newcomers at a promoted club, took three points, courtesy of a 90th-minute Jack Clarke winner against Sunderland . The structural point underneath the churn is that all nine are managing squads they did not assemble, in a window that does not shut until Tuesday, having had a pre-season shortened at both ends by a World Cup. De Zerbi named three of his own players as physically unready after the Brentford defeat. Maurizio Sarri , one of Serie A's new arrivals at Atalanta , made the same complaint in gentler language: “De Ketelaere arrived on August 4, and the new signings arrived recently too.” Judgements formed in the next three weeks will be formed on incomplete evidence. They will be formed anyway. Transfer News Tottenham have spent past £300m. On Saturday they were beaten 3-0 by Brentford. Savio arrived for a Manchester City club-record sale, Marmoush is at a medical, and the squad that took the field on opening day conceded four first-half goals' worth of chances. Tottenham confirmed the signing of Savio on Monday: £75m plus £10m in add-ons, of which around £5m is effectively guaranteed. At £85m it is the largest fee Manchester City have ever received for a player, past the £82m Julian Alvarez brought from Atletico. Omar Marmoush , 27, is following him, on loan with a £60m obligation to buy, with a medical booked as of Wednesday morning per PA and Sky. City will recoup roughly the £59m they paid Eintracht Frankfurt in January 2025. Those two follow Sandro Tonali from Newcastle at a club-record fee, Mateus Fernandes from West Ham at £85m, Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton at £52m, and free transfers for Andy Robertson , Marcos Senesi and Martin Dubravka . On the reported Tonali figure the sources diverge, Sky carrying £100m and Football365 £92.5m, so treat the exact number with care. The direction of travel is not in doubt. Against all that, Saturday at the Gtech was chastening. Brentford's 3-0 was their largest top-flight win and Tottenham's joint-heaviest opening-day defeat, matching a 3-0 at Manchester United in 2011-12. Archie Gray , at 20 years and 163 days, became the club's youngest Premier League captain, breaking Harry Kane 's record. Spurs are still trying to sell. Lucas Bergvall has submitted a transfer request with Newcastle's £46m bid rejected and Spurs holding out for close to £60m, and David Ornstein reports the move now looks unlikely. Pape Matar Sarr and Richarlison are both available, the latter at £35m, which Everton consider too much. Manchester United paid £70m for Carlos Baleba, then lost at Hull Michael Carrick has his midfielder. He says he still needs a left-back, and he is running out of days to find one. Manchester United completed the signing of Carlos Baleba , 22, from Brighton on Tuesday for £65m guaranteed plus £5m in add-ons, on a five-year deal with a further year's option. There is a footnote worth noting: Lille , who sold Baleba to Brighton in 2023, collect roughly €10m from a resale clause that sporting director Olivier Letang inserted at the time. Lille have therefore banked around €110m in a single week from two players they no longer own. Carrick is not finished. “We want more, we need more,” he told Sky Sports. Left-back is the stated priority. United enquired about Lewis Hall and Newcastle refused to sell; Antonee Robinson of Fulham is under consideration. Harry Amass is expected to leave before September 1. No forward is expected, because Marcus Rashford has returned from Barcelona and made his first competitive United appearance in 618 days as a substitute at Hull. That appearance came in a 2-0 defeat at newly promoted Hull City , Semi Ajayi heading in on 17 minutes and Nobel Mendy scoring on his Premier League debut on 38. “We are bitterly disappointed with the result today,” Carrick said. “But it won't knock us.” His captain was less diplomatic. “Same mistakes as we did last season,” Bruno Fernandes said. “Every away game we give too much of the ball to them.” Serie A's late window is being run by the players Moise Kean refused to train. Rafael Leao is working alone. Christopher Nkunku went home to Leipzig. Italy's deadline week has turned personal. Moise Kean , 26, wants to join Como . Como have bid €35m plus €5m in bonuses and asked for an answer inside 48 hours. Personal terms of around €5m a year, roughly matching what he earns now, are understood to be agreed. On Wednesday, La Nazione reported, Kean arrived late at the Viola Park, declined to train with the group, left before his teammates and did a solo session. He was fined and threatened with further sanctions. Fiorentina 's position, stated publicly, is that the club “is solid, it has no need to sell any player.” Director Fabio Paratici set the conditions plainly: “Our players are for sale only if they ask, if a suitable offer arrives, and if we find an equal or better replacement.” At Milan , Rafael Leao is training separately from the squad with no injury to explain it. Corriere dello Sport reports he is outside Ruben Amorim 's project and that Aston Villa are pushing, with Milan asking €50m to €60m and Villa negotiating below it. Galatasaray are also involved. Leao is said to have turned down a large Al-Hilal proposal, preferring to stay in Europe. Amorim would not be drawn: “Right now the good of the team matters far more to us.” Milan did move one attacker on. Christopher Nkunku , 28, returned to RB Leipzig on loan with a purchase option on August 25, back at the club where he scored 126 direct goal involvements in 172 games and won two DFB-Pokals. “When the opportunity to join RB Leipzig came up, I wanted to seize it,” he said. “I'm top fit and eager to help the team immediately.” Elsewhere: Atalanta have had two bids for Bologna 's Jonathan Rowe rejected, the second worth €35m plus bonuses, which would be a club-record signing if it landed; Franck Kessie is in advanced talks with Juventus, who hold his preference, though Roma met his agent on Tuesday to try to intervene; and Napoli have offered €15m to €16m for Chelsea's Marc Guiu against a £25m equivalent asking price. Atletico Madrid say Julian Alvarez is not for sale. Julian Alvarez did not come to training. Whistled by his own supporters on Sunday, absent on Wednesday, and holding an understanding with Barcelona that his club will not honour. The sequence matters. On Sunday Julian Alvarez came off the bench in Atletico Madrid 's 2-2 draw with Villarreal , his first appearance at the Metropolitano in more than three months, and was whistled by sections of his own crowd. At full time he walked down the tunnel rather than join the squad in saluting the supporters. On Wednesday morning he did not appear at training. The club's stated reason was indisposition. Infobae and El Espanol both reported it as an escalation rather than an illness. The underlying position is that Alvarez has had an understanding with Barcelona since May and that Atletico will not sell to a domestic rival. Matteo Moretto of Relevo, speaking on August 21, said Barcelona now regard the deal as “basically impossible” and that the club's plan is a cheaper attacker of similar profile with a view to revisiting Alvarez in a year. A Premier League bid, from Arsenal , has been reported at up to €150m; the player is said to be reluctant to return to England. His release clause is €500m. Atletico's public line has not moved: he is not being sold. Atletico have otherwise had an eventful summer under new ownership. Apollo Sports Capital completed a majority takeover in March, taking 55 per cent at a valuation of €2.5bn including debt, adding a €100m capital increase for the Ciudad del Deporte project and expanding the board from five members to eleven. Enrique Cerezo and Miguel Angel Gil Marin remain in place through June 2029 under a lock-up, and David Villa has joined the board. On the pitch, Cristian Romero arrived from Tottenham for around €40m and Diego Simeone , whose contract runs to June 2027, has four points from two matches. Around the Leagues England: Premier League One round played, and it was a strange one. Two of the three promoted clubs won: Hull City beat Manchester United 2-0 in front of 24,470 at the MKM Stadium in their first top-flight game since 2017, and Ipswich Town beat Sunderland 2-1 through Emersonn and a 90th-minute Jack Clarke strike. Coventry City , back in the top division after 25 years under Frank Lampard , lost 3-0 away. The heaviest defeat of the weekend went to a club that finished fourth last season: Aston Villa lost 4-0 at Brighton , conceding all four inside the first half and losing Joao Gomes to a red card on 40 minutes for kicking out at Georginio Rutter . He faces a three-match ban. Opta noted that only one other side in Premier League history has conceded four, taken a red card and scored an own goal in a single first half: Southampton, in the 9-0 against Manchester United in February 2021. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in 79 seconds for Brighton and has four goals in his last four home league games, one more than in the previous 26 at the Amex. Lewis Dunk made his 300th Premier League appearance for the club, the first player to reach it. Elsewhere Manchester City beat Bournemouth 2-1 with late goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol , both created by Rayan Cherki ; Everton won their first opening weekend in five years, 2-0 over Crystal Palace ; and Chelsea won 3-2 at Fulham , Joao Pedro scoring after 31 seconds and Morgan Rogers marking his debut. The week's refereeing row came at St James' Park, where Stuart Attwell gave a stoppage-time penalty for Lewis Hall 's challenge on Victor Munoz and VAR confirmed it. The Premier League's Match Centre published its reasoning verbatim: Hall “doesn't play the ball. He makes clear contact.” Newcastle, 2-1 up, drew 2-2. Off the pitch Off the pitch, two structural stories. First, Profit and Sustainability Rules are gone. From this season clubs are governed by a Squad Cost Ratio capping on-pitch spending, wages, head-coach salary, agent fees and transfer amortisation, at 85 per cent of football revenue, with a Red Threshold at 115 per cent. Breaches between the two trigger financial levies; above the Red Threshold the penalty is a six-point deduction rising by a point for every £6.5m of overspend. A separate Sustainability and Systemic Resilience regime adds working capital, liquidity and positive equity tests. Second, Liverpool 's owners FSG sold a minority stake in mid-August to a consortium led by Amit Bhatia and including Jeff Bezos , reported at around 38 per cent on a valuation near $7bn with an option to take control at roughly $8bn within twelve months. FSG's statement was categorical: it “continues to retain majority ownership and operational control.” Sky reported the investment brings no separate transfer budget. Also of note: the Women's Super League expands from 12 clubs to 14 this season, starting September 4, with Sky showing 163 matches live. Spain: La Liga Spain's opening rounds have been played out of order. Matchday one was spread from August 15 to August 27 because clubs with World Cup semi-finalists were given extra rest, so several sides have played matchday two before matchday one. The consequence is a table that will look nothing like itself by Friday. It is also, briefly, a table topped by Sevilla , who have six points from two and are top of La Liga for the first time in 189 matchdays, since the second round of 2021-22. Matias Almeyda 's side beat Rayo Vallecano 2-1 with a 97th-minute penalty, then won 3-1 at San Mames against a ten-man Athletic Club , who are bottom with nothing. That Athletic red card produced the week's cleanest institutional story. On the debut edition of the referees' committee's new review programme, the CTA ruled that Cesar Soto Grado 's 11th-minute dismissal of Yuri Berchiche was a “clear and obvious error” and that VAR should have intervened. The committee's reasoning was that Sevilla's Miguel Sierra pushed the ball away from himself, so there was no genuine goalscoring opportunity. The correct decision was a free kick and no card. Four other reviewed decisions from the round were upheld. Mourinho, and a Madrid without limits Real Madrid are being managed by Jose Mourinho , appointed on June 11 on a contract to June 2029. He won his league return 2-1 at Espanyol through a 90th-minute goal from Carlos Espi , a 21-year-old debutant signed from Levante who now has 11 goals in 14 games. Madrid's summer has been extraordinary in scale: Yan Diomande arrived from RB Leipzig for €125m, the largest fee in the club's history, alongside Marc Cucurella , Denzel Dumfries , and free transfers for Ibrahima Konate and Bernardo Silva . Vinicius Junior renewed to June 2032 on August 6. Mourinho has also imposed a set of dressing-room rules, per AS: prescribed meals, latecomers training alone in the gym rather than being fined, and all rehabilitation done in-house at Valdebebas. On the market he was dismissive on Tuesday: “For me it is closed, but with the market open.” Barcelona , the defending champions, opened with a 5-0 win at Elche : Raphinha two goals and an assist, Fermin Lopez two, Karim Adeyemi scoring on debut and Anthony Gordon assisting twice off the bench on his. The registration crisis that has defined recent Barcelona Augusts did not materialise; Rodri , Adeyemi and Gordon were all registered on August 21 with the club operating under the 1:1 rule after shedding payroll. The Gamper Trophy was staged at the rebuilt Spotify Camp Nou on August 19, and the league opener against Athletic on Thursday is at the stadium too. What Barcelona do not have is a recognised centre-forward. Matteo Moretto's summary of the shortlist was withering: “I don't think it will be Tresoldi, I don't think it will be Gyokeres, I don't think it will be the names that have come out.” The surprise signing he teased turned out to be a goalkeeper, Dominik Livakovic , on a small fee from Fenerbahce . Two more. Rayo Vallecano are homeless in their 50th-anniversary season: Vallecas has failed safety clearance, so they played Alaves at Butarque in Leganes in front of 4,280 people, the smallest crowd of the round, and Getafe have refused them the Coliseum for September 5. And Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang , now 37, has signed for promoted Deportivo La Coruna from Marseille and scored twice in his first two games. Germany: Bundesliga Germany has not kicked off. Matchday one is Friday, Bayern Munich against VfB Stuttgart , the latest start in years and another consequence of the World Cup. What Germany has had is a Supercup and a cup round, and both were instructive. Bayern beat Borussia Dortmund 2-1 at Signal Iduna Park on August 22 in front of 81,365. The goals came from Nathaniel Brown , a left-back signed from Eintracht Frankfurt who was fielded at number ten and scored on his competitive debut, and Michael Olise in first-half stoppage time. Fabio Silva pulled one back on 75 minutes; Ramy Bensebaini was sent off on 90 and has since been given a two-match cup suspension. Vincent Kompany on Brown: “Sometimes the full-backs' spaces are similar to those of a number ten. He is unbelievably good between the spaces.” It was a fitting start to a week in which Bayern also extended Max Eberl and Jan-Christian Dreesen to June 2029, sold Joao Palhinha permanently to Benfica , and watched Harry Kane collect Germany's Footballer of the Year award, with 272 of 659 votes, days after picking up the European Golden Shoe for 36 league goals. Kompany was named Coach of the Year for last season's double. The DFB-Pokal first round produced a record haul of goals and two proper shocks, both against clubs relegated from the second tier rather than the first: fifth-tier SSV Jeddeloh II beat Heidenheim 5-2, and Rot-Weiss Essen knocked out St Pauli 2-0. Eintracht Frankfurt won 11-0 at SC St Tonis, the biggest cup win in the club's history. Hamburger SV won 3-0 at SC Verl, where Louis Lemke , aged 16 years, 10 months and 16 days, became the youngest goalscorer in HSV history. And at Halle, Edin Dzeko , 40, scored twice for promoted Schalke 04 , roughly fifteen years and eight months after his previous appearance in German top-flight football. “My plan from the very beginning was to come back,” he said. “I really only wanted to keep playing for Schalke.” The week's saddest news came on August 23, when Klaus-Michael Kuhne died aged 89. The logistics billionaire was the second-largest shareholder in HSV's football company, financed the buy-back of the stadium naming rights that restored the Volksparkstadion name, and was for a decade the single most-cited figure in Germany's argument about outside investment in football. He last attended a match in 2015. What happens to his holding is, at the time of writing, unreported. Italy: Serie A Serie A began on August 22 and the opening round belonged to one player. Donyell Malen scored a hat-trick inside 68 minutes as Roma beat Fiorentina 4-0, taking three shots on target and scoring all three, with 11 touches in the opposition box. All three were laid on by Paulo Dybala . Gian Piero Gasperini , who has heard a decade of jokes about Dybala's fragility, took the opportunity: “Paulo is extraordinary, world-class. He could have played extra time too, never mind silk muscles.” Malen now has 17 goals in Europe's top five leagues in the calendar year 2026, level with Kane, albeit in more appearances. Nine of the twenty benches changed over the summer. Ruben Amorim took Milan and won 2-1 at Torino , with 18-year-old Alphadjo Cisse scoring on his Serie A debut. Massimiliano Allegri took Napoli and won 2-0 at Genoa , where the game's flashpoint arrived: Kevin De Bruyne 's 82nd-minute opener came after contact with Genoa's Johan Vasquez that referee Marco Di Bello waved away and VAR did not review. Daniele De Rossi called it “one of the ugliest episodes of my career.” The refereeing body, led by Daniele Orsato , backed Di Bello while conceding that giving a foul would not have been a serious error. The disciplinary fallout landed on Genoa: director Diego Javier Lopez was banned until September 8 for entering the pitch and obstructing the referee. Reigning champions Inter beat Monza 4-1, Pio Esposito scoring with a backheel. Underneath that placid surface, the champions are dismantling and rebuilding their attack with less than a week of the window left, and the outcome rests on two men who have not yet decided anything. T here is a particular kind of quiet that settles over a club that has just won the league. Arsenal have spent this month enjoying it. They beat Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield at the Principality Stadium on August 16, a match settled inside 24 seconds by Riccardo Calafiori and finished off by Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard . Five days later they opened the Premier League season at the Emirates by beating newly promoted Coventry City 3-0 on a Friday night, and the visitors did not register a single tackle in the first half. Two matches, six goals, none conceded, and a manager who described the evening as having "a lot to like" about it. And yet the most consequential Arsenal story of the past seven days did not happen on a pitch. It happened on the phone lines between north London, Riyadh and Madrid, and it concerns the shape of the attack that Mikel Arteta will take into a Champions League campaign that begins in a fortnight. The Premier League window closes at 11pm UK time on Tuesday, September 1, which is 3pm Pacific. That leaves six days for a set of decisions that will define the season more than any of the five signings already made. The Two Undecided Men The first is Gabriel Martinelli . David Ornstein of The Athletic reported on August 23 that Arsenal have placed a valuation of around 70 million euros, roughly 60 million pounds, on the Brazilian, and that the player is open to a move to the Middle East. Al Hilal have been circling for a fortnight. Sky Sports reported on Monday that the two clubs are closing on an agreement, with a sell-on clause understood to be part of the structure, and that the decision now belongs to the player himself. Martinelli turned down an approach from Galatasaray last week. He has been left out of both matchday squads so far this season. Whichever figure the deal eventually lands on, it will comfortably break Arsenal's record for a player sale. The second is the man Arsenal would like to sign with the proceeds, and here the picture is genuinely unresolved. Fabrizio Romano said on Tuesday that Arsenal remain attentive to Julian Alvarez , that the club has an internal feeling it could reach agreement with Atletico Madrid on the financial terms, and that Arsenal will not lodge a formal bid until the striker signals he actually wants to come. That last clause is the whole story. Alvarez has made no secret of preferring Barcelona , a move Spanish reporting describes as financially close to fiction, and the Argentine press is split on whether Atletico are desperate to sell or determined to keep him and rehabilitate him in front of a crowd that whistled him. Arsenal are not, on the current evidence, prepared to spend anything close to 150 million on a player who regards them as a fallback. This is a more disciplined position than Arsenal have historically taken in the last week of a window, and it is worth pausing on. Andrea Berta , in his second summer as sporting director, has run a window of unusual decisiveness. Piero Hincapie made permanent from Bayer Leverkusen for a reported 34.5 million in June, Illan Meslier taken on a free from Leeds United in July, Christos Tzolis bought from Club Brugge for a reported 34 million as the designated replacement for Leandro Trossard , Bruno Guimaraes prised out of Newcastle United for a reported 75 million, and then Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa on the eve of the season for 51 million plus 4 million in add-ons. That is roughly 198.5 million pounds of gross spending before deadline week has even started. "He's done enough with this squad to be treated with a little bit more respect than he's being treated with at the moment." The same day, Sporting Kansas City signed the 24-year-old Brazilian winger Andre Luiz from Olympiacos for $18m plus add-ons on a five-year Designated Player deal, also a club record, despite sitting bottom of the Western Conference on 14 points. It is a sign of how the extended MLS window, open until 2 September for the first time in nearly two decades, has changed the league's appetite. Charlotte also handed Allan Saint-Maximin , signed from Lens , his debut in a 3-1 win over Columbus . The Rumour Mill Everything still simmering, with the certainty of each item stated plainly. Nothing here is done. Ollie Watkins to Al Hilal is the loudest live saga in England. Sky's Paper Talk on 19 August, crediting Fabrizio Romano , reports a £38.5m bid and a player who is keen; Read Aston Villa says a third bid of around £38m has been rejected and that Villa expect a fourth, per Simon Jones of the Daily Mail. Villa will not sell without a replacement. Several lower-tier outlets have reported that personal terms are agreed. Sky and Romano's own wording do not support that, and this newspaper will not print it as fact. Tier: bids rejected, talks live. Moise Kean to Como is Italy's best-sourced unresolved deal. Como made a formal offer of a €5m loan with a €25m obligation, a €30m total, and Fiorentina rejected it and want €40m, per Corriere dello Sport , Sky Sport Italia and Tuttosport. Kean is receptive: Champions League football under Cesc Fabregas and a reported €4.5m salary. Tier: offer made and rejected, gap of €10m. Jack Grealish to Everton on a second loan has moved from speculation to acknowledged contact. Everton chief executive Angus Kinnear told The Times, quoted by Goal : "Jack is a player we've remained in contact with. He's a player who's fallen in love with the right shade of blue but ultimately he's a Manchester City player at the moment and we need to respect that." Tier: contact confirmed, no agreement. Giannis Konstantelias to Borussia Dortmund has reached the medical stage and a fan revolt. The 23-year-old flew to Germany on 16 August, with fees reported between €25m and €32m including add-ons, the story originating with Ruhrnachrichten. PAOK 's ultras group Gate 4 called the club's decision-makers "crooks and traitors" and gathered outside the stadium. There is precedent: in 2025 owner Ivan Savvidis killed a move to Stuttgart under identical pressure. Tier: medical stage, with a history of collapse. Malick Fofana to Roma had personal terms agreed on 17 August, per Romano via Foot Mercato , at a fee Italian sources put near €40m, contingent on Roma completing the Mora deal. Christopher Nkunku to RB Leipzig on loan with a €30m to €35m option is pointed at from both sides but has no agreed fee, and Nicolas Jackson of Chelsea, price cut to €70m, has interest from Villa, Tottenham, Atletico and Napoli, with nobody yet willing to pay it. Two collapses worth recording. Nayef Aguerd 's move from Marseille to Real Sociedad died on 13 August, and the two best-connected reporters in Spain tell opposite stories: Santi Aouna of Foot Mercato says Aguerd passed the medical and withdrew after a conversation with Pellegrino Matarazzo , while Matteo Moretto says he failed it. On 15 August Aguerd said publicly that his medical "went perfectly" ( El Desmarque ). And Julian Alvarez is staying at Atletico Madrid , Diego Simeone saying on 18 August: "there is still market left and you know nothing surprises me." Around the Leagues Premier League With no football played, the week belonged to the boardroom and the treatment table. The largest story is at Chelsea , where the Financial Times reported on 18 August that Todd Boehly and Mark Walter are in talks to sell their 12.8 per cent stakes each to majority owner Clearlake Capital , which holds 61.5 per cent and is led by Behdad Eghbali . The club is valued at £5bn, which would roughly double the £325m each man put in four years ago. Boehly is set to step down as chairman at the end of this season, at the close of his five-year term. Ownership terms bar co-owners from selling to outside investors for the first ten years, and a rift over stadium plans has been reported since 2024. No party has commented. At Everton , chief executive Angus Kinnear spent the week conducting an unusually frank public audit. He confirmed the club will not have a right-back available for Saturday's opener against Crystal Palace , said "I'm confident we'll bring a right-back in," and, on Iliman Ndiaye , offered the sentence every Everton supporter has learned to read carefully: "Our vision is very much that our best players like Ili are retained and they help us achieve what we all want." Everton and Palace have already done business, swapping Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil straight across on 11 August, both on four-year deals, both fees undisclosed. It is a genuinely rare structure, and it tidies up two awkward January stories at once: Johnson had joined Palace in January for £35m and made 26 appearances without scoring, while McNeil's move the other way had collapsed when paperwork was not filed in time. The promoted clubs are not behaving like promoted clubs. Ipswich Town and Coventry City spent a combined £49.2m in a single day on 17 August, Ipswich taking Julio Enciso and Abdoul Ouattara from Strasbourg and Coventry signing Taiwo Awoniyi from Forest for £9m. Newcastle added Amar Dedic from Benfica for a reported £30m on 18 August, having already sold Tonali and Guimaraes. Elsewhere, Manchester City 's 115 charges remain unresolved, with no verdict since the hearing ended in December 2024, and the Women's Super League returns on 4 September expanded from 12 clubs to 14, Manchester City defending the title. La Liga Spain is the only one of the six leagues actually playing, and even then only partly. Matchday 1 has been split: five matches went ahead between 15 and 17 August, while the openers of clubs with players who reached the World Cup semi-finals or beyond were deferred to between 19 and 27 August, an agreement between LaLiga, the RFEF and the players' union to reduce injury risk. Espanyol lead the table on goals scored after a 3-0 win over Levante , Roberto Fernandez scoring twice inside 40 minutes. Alaves beat Getafe 3-0 and Deportivo marked their return to the top flight after eight years with a 1-1 draw against Elche in which Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang scored on debut. Atletico Madrid host Malaga as this edition goes out. Two rows are already running. The opening night produced an immediate refereeing controversy at Sevilla , where Ricardo de Burgos Bengoetxea awarded a penalty, saw it overturned by VAR, then gave another in the seventh minute of stoppage time that El Debate and others reported the replays did not support. Sevilla won 2-1. Rayo Vallecano 's Alvaro Garcia said afterwards: "Three penalties. The match was even, but too much of a leading role for the person who should not be a lead character." Separately, Celta against Osasuna was postponed on 13 August because of a problem with the Balaidos turf , identified in Spanish reporting as a fungus. Osasuna issued a statement expressing "absolute disagreement" with the new date of 27 August, saying both clubs had agreed the September international break would work and that the team most harmed by the postponement is once again the team most harmed by the fix. Meanwhile Real Madrid open their season at Espanyol on Saturday under Jose Mourinho , their third head coach in eight months, after beating Schalke 3-0 in Gelsenkirchen to finish pre-season unbeaten. Bundesliga Germany starts last, on 28 August, but Saturday brings the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup at Signal Iduna Park, where Borussia Dortmund host Bayern Munich as last season's runners-up. Bayern arrive as champions of a league they won on 19 April with four games to spare while scoring a record 122 goals, and with Harry Kane collecting the European Golden Shoe in Munich on 19 August for 36 Bundesliga goals, ahead of Erling Haaland and Kylian Mbappe . Bayern beat RB Leipzig 3-1 and Heidenheim 4-2 in friendlies, with Kane and Michael Olise returning as substitutes after extended post-World Cup breaks. Below Bayern the picture is uneven. Eintracht Frankfurt lost 7-0 at Brentford on 15 August in their final friendly, captain Robin Koch going off injured at half time; the club's own report called it an expensive education. RB Leipzig lost their record signing Yan Diomande to Real Madrid for a reported €140m including bonuses and their replacement target Moreira to Milan, and Martin Demichelis said publicly that his sporting director "has work to do." Sebastian Hoeness of Stuttgart , contracted to 2028, acknowledged on 19 August that clubs including Manchester City and Milan have made enquiries about him, saying it would "not now be surprising if there were perhaps one or two clubs that made an enquiry about me," as reported by sport.de on 19 August. And the Bundeskartellamt delivered its final assessment on the 50+1 rule on 12 August, accepting the rule's aims while ruling that enforcement must be consistent and naming Leverkusen , Wolfsburg , RB Leipzig and Hannover 96 as needing to change. That is currently single-sourced in English and the authority's own document is worth reading before anyone declares 50+1 saved. Serie A Italy kicks off on Saturday and has already produced its first disaster. Lazio , beaten finalists in last season's Coppa Italia, went out of this season's competition at the first hurdle, losing 2-0 at home to Serie B side Mantova in Gennaro Gattuso 's competitive debut, Ruocco scoring on 75 minutes and Cajazzo in stoppage time. Gattuso was without six players through injury or fatigue. "It's a devastating blow," he said, per ANSA . "We must apologise and move forward with focus and unity rather than seeking excuses." Il Messaggero and Leggo both marked him four out of ten for a nightmare debut. In the same round Palermo knocked out Lecce 2-0, Pisa went through on penalties against Empoli , and of the Serie A clubs playing on 17 August only Sassuolo won. The league also arrives with a new refereeing regime. On 18 August the AIA held an online meeting with all 20 clubs, run by technical director Domenico Messina and the new CAN designator Daniele Orsato , whose predecessor Gianluca Rocchi self-suspended in late April while under investigation for sporting fraud over allegedly steered appointments. Calcio e Finanza set out the changes , which broadly mirror England's: VAR confined to clear and obvious error, a one-minute exile for treated players, a visible five-second count on restarts, and a strengthened captain protocol. "The legacy of the World Cup is that we saw how the central figure was the referee," Orsato said. Not everyone is charmed by the calendar: Maurizio Sarri , now at Atalanta , called the transfer window dates "madness" and said that discussing the market endlessly is "an insult to my profession," per Tuttosport . Ligue 1 France produced the result of the week. RC Lens beat Paris Saint-Germain 1-0 at Stade Bollaert-Delelis on 16 August to win the Trophee des Champions for the first time in the club's history, Florian Thauvin scoring on 32 minutes and Lens then playing roughly 47 minutes of normal time with ten men after Kyllian Antonio was sent off. Nuno Mendes was dismissed late for PSG, who had 69 per cent of the ball and 22 shots to Lens's eight. Goalkeeper Robin Risser made six saves. Zinedine Zidane , confirmed as France head coach on 28 July, watched from the stand. Lens head coach Dino Toppmoller 's dressing-room speech, published the next day by RMC, is the quote of the French week: "Lens is this: we fear no one. We said it before the match, we can beat everyone here." Luis Enrique 's verdict, on PSG's own site, was one line: "I'm pleased with what I saw, but frustrated." Four days earlier PSG had won a second consecutive UEFA Super Cup, beating Aston Villa 2-1 in Salzburg, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue scoring and Villa's 17-year-old Brian Madjo becoming the youngest player to start and score in the fixture, which was refereed by Omar Artan of Somalia, the first non-European to take a Super Cup. Elsewhere Monaco and Paul Pogba ended their partnership by mutual consent on 19 August , the club saying "the objectives initially set were only partially achieved" and Pogba replying that he would "always be grateful." Nice signed the 37-year-old Axel Witsel on a free from Girona on 18 August as emergency cover after a serious knee injury to Laurent Abergel . And the league itself changes shape commercially: with beIN Sports declining to renew, Ligue 1+ becomes the sole broadcaster of every match, with the subscription rising to €19.99. The season also has zero midweek matchdays, a deliberate scheduling choice. Major League Soccer America is the only league of the six in the thick of it, and Nashville SC have taken it over. They sit on 43 points from 19 matches with a goal difference of plus 24 and only 15 conceded, five clear of Inter Miami , and they demolished them 4-1 on 15 August, Hany Mukhtar scoring twice in the second half after goalkeeper Brian Schwake saved a first-half Lionel Messi penalty. Miami's fortnight has been grim: they went out of the Leagues Cup in the league phase on 12 August, losing 3-2 at home to Club Leon with three points from three matches, their worst campaign of the Messi era. Messi came on at half time to a standing ovation, days after the death of his father and long-time agent Jorge Messi at 68. "For people to understand what Leo Messi is, I think it was proven today," Leon coach Javier Gandolfi said. "He's a competitive animal, a player who, in my opinion, is the best in history." In the West, Vancouver Whitecaps lead on 37 points from 18 with the best goal difference in the league, and clinched a record ninth Cascadia Cup by winning 2-0 at Seattle Sounders on 17 August, Rayan Elloumi and Thomas Muller scoring in front of 30,026. Seattle are in freefall, that defeat extending a league losing run to seven, with Jesus Ferreira going off injured after 36 minutes and Brian Schmetzer conceding his team managed only "30 to 35 good minutes." Petar Musa of FC Dallas leads the Golden Boot race on 14 goals. Chicago Fire have won five straight in all competitions for the first time since 2000. And at Orlando City , Antoine Griezmann has two goals, one assist and 14 chances created in his first six appearances since arriving from Atletico, team-mate Griffin Dorsey telling MLSsoccer that "as much as he's a star, it's very easy to be in a room with Grizi and feel like he's just another human being." Numbers of the Week 76.5m euros The total value of Rodri's move from Manchester City to Barcelona, per ESPN. Sky reported the fee as £65.4m. 10 of 20 new benches Premier League clubs starting the season with a manager they did not have a year ago. 43 points Nashville SC's total from 19 MLS matches, five clear at the top and only 15 goals conceded. 36 goals Harry Kane's Bundesliga tally last season, enough for the European Golden Shoe, presented in Munich on 19 August. Borussia Dortmund signed Joey Veerman from PSV on 18 August after activating a €21.5m release clause. Managing director Lars Ricken said the club had "deliberately focused our transfer activities this summer on the central midfield." Niclas Fullkrug has returned to Werder Bremen on loan, taking a pay cut. Nico Elvedi left Borussia Monchengladbach for Leeds United for a reported €10m after 11 years. k: Arsenal begin their Premier League title defence against Coventry on Friday, three days after a 3-0 Community Shield win and with the centre-back department still unfixed.
x: North London Since 1886 The Weekly Arsenal Digest One club, every week, all of it. Edition No. 1 Tuesday, August 18, 2026 The Lead Champions Again, and Already One Defender Short Arsenal open the defence of a first league title in twenty-two years on Friday night against Coventry City. The Community Shield said one thing about this squad. The treatment room says another. T wenty-five seconds. That is how long Arsenal waited to score the first goal of their post-championship life. Myles Lewis-Skelly slid a ball into the space that Manchester City had not yet decided to defend, and Riccardo Calafiori arrived at the end of it. By the time the Principality Stadium had settled into its seats on Sunday afternoon the Community Shield was already tilting. It finished 3-0. It could reasonably have finished by more. That is the version of this football club the rest of the league will be looking at on Friday evening, when Coventry City arrive at the Emirates for the curtain-raiser of the 2026-27 season. It is not the whole picture. The whole picture includes a centre-half who cannot play, a right-sided defender who cannot play, and a sporting director with under a fortnight to do something about both. The injury that shapes everything William Saliba came off after half an hour of France's World Cup semi-final in July and has not been right since. Arsenal confirmed on July 23 that specialist reviews had found a back injury requiring "a period of rehabilitation," and that he would be out for an extended spell. Surgery was considered and rejected, which is the good news: the operation would have cost four to five months. The BBC's Sami Mokbel has since put the realistic floor at two to three months, pointing at the home fixture with Leeds United on October 10 as a plausible re-entry point. Jurrien Timber , who had a small procedure on a stubborn groin problem, is further along but not close. Mikel Arteta said on August 10 that there were still "a few weeks to go." Key Facts / Arsenal v Coventry City Kickoff Friday, August 21, 12:00pm Pacific (8:00pm BST), Emirates Stadium Occasion Matchweek 1. Arsenal open a season as reigning champions for the first time since 2004-05. The visitors Coventry won the Championship by 11 points under Frank Lampard. First top-flight season in 25 years. Head to head Arsenal have won the last five meetings, aggregate 16-2. They last met in the FA Cup in 2014. Unavailable Saliba (back), Timber (groin). Ben White is fit and started the Shield. Losing Saliba is not a squad-depth inconvenience. It is a structural one. Sky Sports noted alongside the club's July statement that Arsenal 's win rate falls from 68 per cent to 50 per cent in matches he does not start. The reason is visible in the way Arteta asks his team to play. The high line that lets Arsenal compress the pitch and win the ball 60 yards from their own goal is underwritten by a defender who can recover 40 metres in a straight line without panicking. Take him out and either the line drops, which costs territory, or it does not, which costs goals. On Sunday the answer was Cristhian Mosquera alongside Gabriel Magalhaes , with Ben White at right-back and Calafiori at left, and it worked well enough that the question got quieter for ninety minutes. Manchester City , under Enzo Maresca for the first time in a showpiece, never really got Erling Haaland into the game. Jeremy Doku was doubled up on the touchline every time he took possession. David Raya made the two saves that mattered. But a Community Shield in the third week of August is not a Tuesday in Naples in November, and Arteta knows the difference. Asked afterwards about the window, he did not bother with the usual manager's shrug. "We know there are certain areas that through injuries we are weaker and we need to strengthen. We're trying to do that and we've been trying to do that for weeks." Mikel Arteta, August 17 Selection, and too many good players The selection questions for Friday sit further forward. Kai Havertz scored the second goal on Sunday and started ahead of Viktor Gyokeres , who came off the bench, and a real debate has opened about which of them leads the line in the games that decide seasons. Gyokeres was Arsenal 's leading league scorer last season with 14: a respectable debut return for a 55-million-pound striker, and a slightly underwhelming one for a player who arrived from Sporting CP with a reputation as an unstoppable force. Havertz offers the link play that makes Martin Odegaard 's job easier, and Odegaard was the best player on the pitch in Cardiff. There is also the matter of who plays on the right. Bukayo Saka went to the World Cup, played in England's bronze-medal match against France on July 18, and returned late; he was a substitute on Sunday. Noni Madueke started in his place and kept it through most of the game. Arteta has more players than shirts, which is the position every champion wants to be in and the position that creates a specific problem. Gabriel Jesus , Gabriel Martinelli and Ethan Nwaneri were all left out of the Shield squad entirely: all three fit, all three now the subject of transfer conversations. Do not dismiss the visitors Coventry City should not be treated as a formality even though the bookmakers treat them as one. Frank Lampard 's side won the Championship by eleven points, which is not a play-off scramble but a procession. They have spent the summer sensibly: Carl Rushworth made permanent in goal after his loan from Brighton , six new arrivals in all, Gustavo Hamer and Taiwo Awoniyi to carry the attack. They beat Monaco 2-0 and Espanyol 3-1 in pre-season. A newly promoted team playing its first top-flight match in twenty-five years, away, in front of the champions' crowd, under lights, is a team with nothing to lose and a manager who will have spent a fortnight thinking about nothing else. The larger frame is what makes Friday interesting rather than routine. Arsenal have not defended a Premier League title since 2004, and the last time they tried they were coming off an unbeaten season and still finished second. The 2025-26 team won it by seven points with the best defence in the division, and it has been strengthened rather than dismantled: Bruno Guimaraes for 75 million, Christos Tzolis for 34, Piero Hincapie made permanent. What has not been solved, three days before kickoff, is the one thing that broke on its own. The Title Defence Tracker The Premier League has not kicked off. The baseline Arsenal are defending, from 2025-26: 85 Points, 1st +44 Goal diff 27 Conceded 19 Clean sheets Record 26-7-5 from 38, seven points clear of Manchester City . First title since 2003-04, ending a 22-year wait, and Arsenal's 14th English championship. Clinched on May 19 when City drew at Bournemouth. Last Season's Scorers Viktor Gyokeres, Premier League goals 14 Arsenal goals from corners, an all-time record 18 Erling Haaland, Golden Boot winner 27 The 75-Million-Pound Rewiring of the Arsenal Midfield Bruno Guimaraes played 45 minutes in Cardiff. It was enough to see what Arteta has bought, and what it does to everybody else. The signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United on August 9, for a fee reported at 75 million pounds on a four-year deal with a further year at the club's option, was the most expensive piece of business Arsenal have done this summer and the least obviously necessary. This was a squad that already contained Declan Rice , Martin Zubimendi , Mikel Merino and Odegaard . Adding a 28-year-old Brazilian international to that group looks, on a team sheet, like hoarding. Watch the Community Shield and it looks like something else. Guimaraes started in a three with Lewis-Skelly and Odegaard , which is not the shape anybody predicted, and the effect was to give Arsenal a midfielder who breaks lines with a pass rather than with a carry. Rice destroys and drives. Zubimendi circulates. Guimaraes plays the ball that skips a phase. Against a City side pressing in a mid-block, that was the difference between working the ball around the outside and getting through the middle of it. He was withdrawn at half-time for Rice , which reads less like a hook than like a manager who signed a player nine days ago and is not going to break him in week one. The knock-on effects are real. Lewis-Skelly , nineteen, started in midfield rather than at left-back and produced the pass for the opening goal. Zubimendi , a World Cup winner five weeks ago, came off the bench. Merino did not get on. That is why the outgoing side of this window has become as consequential as the incoming one. Transfer News Thirteen Days to Find a Centre-Half Konsa, Quansah, Kounde, Pubill. Four names, four different problems, and a deadline that does not move. The furthest advanced of the four is Ezri Konsa , and "furthest advanced" is doing heavy lifting in that sentence. Arsenal have made at least two approaches to Aston Villa for the England defender, with reported figures in the 30 to 45 million range. Villa have valued him at 60 million and not blinked. As of Monday the second proposal had fallen short and the two clubs were not close. Certainty: bid made, fee not agreed . The alternative that emerged over the weekend is Jarell Quansah , the 23-year-old former Liverpool defender now at Bayer Leverkusen . ESPN reported on August 16 that Arsenal had opened talks and that Leverkusen want somewhere around 50 million euros. This is the deal that makes the most institutional sense: a Premier League-schooled defender still on the right side of 24, at a club Arsenal have just done business with over Hincapie , at a price that does not require selling anybody. Certainty: early talks . The glamour option is Jules Kounde . Catalan outlets including Mundo Deportivo and SPORT reported in the middle of last week that Arsenal were prepared to pay a substantial fee for the Barcelona defender, with Liverpool also circling. Treat this one with care. It is sourced entirely to the selling market, no bid has been confirmed, and Barcelona 's financial calendar has a way of generating stories about players they might sell. Certainty: concrete interest, single market, unconfirmed . The fourth is already dead. Arsenal made contact with Atletico Madrid about Marc Pubill , and Fabrizio Romano and Jorge Garcia Hernandez of AS both reported around August 13 and 14 that Atletico had declared the defender non-transferable, pointing at a release clause of 500 million euros by way of punctuation. Certainty: rejected . Read those four together and a pattern emerges. Andrea Berta is not shopping for a squad player. He is shopping for someone who can start thirty games at the heart of a title defence and then hand the shirt back when Saliba returns. That is a strange and expensive brief, and it explains why the club has been willing to look at four different leagues rather than settle for the obvious. It also explains Arteta 's unusually direct language on Sunday. Managers do not normally say they are weaker. Ins & Outs / Summer 2026 Confirmed and official. The window closes in the first week of September. The most delicate decision of Arsenal's summer involves a player who is not going to start. He was fit. He had trained. He had played through pre-season. And on Sunday, Ethan Nwaneri was not in the Community Shield squad at all, which is the loudest thing Arteta has said about him all summer. The manager's public phrasing was more diplomatic. Nwaneri , he said, "needs consistent minutes at this stage of his career." The nineteen-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Marseille , a move that went wrong for reasons largely outside his control. Roberto De Zerbi , the coach who wanted him, left shortly after he arrived, and under Habib Beye he managed a little over 400 minutes across nine appearances, with two goals. He came back to a club that had just won the league and then added Tzolis and Guimaraes on top of a forward line that already had Saka , Madueke , Eberechi Eze and Martinelli in it. The most concrete reporting so far comes from Italy. Carlo Pellegatti has described RB Leipzig as being in advanced talks, with the German club prepared to offer between 35 and 40 million euros for a permanent transfer, and Arsenal exploring a buy-back clause valued at 55 to 60 million. Leipzig expect funds from an outgoing sale of their own and have capped individual spending at 45 million this summer, which makes the arithmetic plausible. AC Milan made an enquiry in late July and have been linked with a loan. Borussia Dortmund , Fulham and Galatasaray have all been mentioned. Certainty: exit expected, structure undecided . The complication is that Nwaneri is contracted to 2030, so Arsenal face no pressure at all. Selling a Hale End graduate who broke the Premier League's youngest-player record is the kind of decision that gets re-litigated for a decade if it goes wrong. A loan protects the asset and solves nothing. A sale with a buy-back solves the minutes problem and transfers the risk to whether the buy-back price stays sane. Somebody at London Colney has to pick one within a fortnight. The Turkish Channel Galatasaray bid for Martinelli and were turned down. What else was on the table in that conversation is the more interesting story. David Ornstein reported on August 14 that Galatasaray had bid 45 million euros, around 38.4 million pounds, for Gabriel Martinelli , and that the Brazilian had declined the move. Arsenal are understood to be open to selling him at the right number, but to a club in one of Europe's leading leagues rather than to Turkey, and Martinelli 's own preference appears to run the same way. He scored eleven goals in 53 appearances last season and was left out of the Shield squad. Certainty: bid made, declined by player . The detail worth filing away came from the BBC's Sami Mokbel , also on August 14. In the course of those talks, the future of Victor Osimhen is understood to have been discussed as well. Berta and his assistant Maurizio Michele have long-standing relationships in Turkey, and Berta 's brief this summer explicitly includes making Arsenal active sellers rather than only buyers. Nothing about this constitutes a pursuit of Osimhen . It does tell you that the channel between the two clubs is open in both directions, which is worth remembering if a striker becomes available in the last week of the window. Certainty: single-source, exploratory, no bid . The Rumour Mill The smaller threads, the ones still simmering, and where each of them honestly sits. Chelsea are willing to sell, but the asking price has travelled from around 70 million on August 10, per Simon Phillips , to close to 100 million by Monday, and Arsenal are in a queue with Manchester City and Tottenham . Given that Tzolis arrived in July and produced six assists and a goal in six pre-season matches, spending nine figures on another wide forward would be a strange use of the remaining budget. Certainty: interest, no bid . The Squad What Cardiff Told Us, and What It Did Not Ninety minutes against Manchester City is a poor sample and a good sign. Reading it honestly. Arteta sent out Raya behind White , Mosquera , Gabriel and Calafiori , a midfield of Guimaraes , Lewis-Skelly and Odegaard , and a front line of Madueke , Havertz and Tzolis . Read that back and note how many players you would call automatic starters are missing from it: Saka , Rice , Zubimendi , Gyokeres , Eze . All five were on the bench. All five came on or could have. The press, and the corner The pressing was the most striking feature. Arsenal scored inside half a minute because they were already hunting the ball when City tried to play out, and they never really stopped. This is the pattern that produced 27 goals conceded and 19 clean sheets last season, and it survived the loss of the defender who anchors it, at least for one afternoon. Set pieces remain the club's most distinctive weapon and the one most likely to suffer if the personnel change. Arsenal scored 18 goals from corners in 2025-26, an all-time Premier League single-season record, beating a mark that had stood for 32 years. More than 40 per cent of their league goals arrived from dead-ball situations. That routine depends heavily on aerial threat from centre-backs. It is another quiet argument for signing a defender who can head a ball, not just defend a counter. The armband The captaincy was settled without drama. Odegaard retained the armband after a vote of players and staff that Arteta described as unanimous "by a big, big 100 miles," and then won man of the match in the Shield. He has held the role since 2022, but the manner of the confirmation matters in a dressing room about to shed several senior names. Availability / Men's First Team William Saliba , back. Injured on World Cup duty with France, surgery ruled out in favour of rehabilitation. Arsenal said on July 23 he would miss an extended period. The BBC's estimate is a minimum of two to three months, pointing at October. Jurrien Timber , groin. Underwent a small procedure and is doing individual pitch work. Arteta said on August 10 there were still "a few weeks to go," with a late-September return the realistic target. Ben White , knee. Fully recovered from surgery, back in training since late July, started the Community Shield at right-back. Louie Copley , knee. The under-21 defender suffered a season-ending anterior cruciate ligament injury in the pre-season friendly against Real Betis. Form and the number nine On individual form, the debate that will not go away is Havertz against Gyokeres . Havertz started in Cardiff and scored. Gyokeres came off the bench. The case for the German is the one Arteta has always made, that a centre-forward in this system is a connector as much as a finisher, and Havertz 's passing numbers are considerably better. The case for the Swede is that 14 league goals in a first season in England, at a club that scored 71, is a platform rather than a ceiling. Expect them to share it, and expect the question again in November. The one to watch quietly is Tzolis . Six assists and a goal in six pre-season appearances, then the header that set up Havertz for the second in the Shield, and a body of work at Club Brugge that reads 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. At 34 million pounds, in a market where Chelsea want three times that for Pedro Neto , he already looks like the shrewdest thing Berta has done. Hale End A New Academy, Top to Bottom Mertesacker gone, De Maesschalck in, and a new under-21 head coach appointed yesterday. The pathway that produced Saka and Lewis-Skelly has new management. The most recent piece of news here is the freshest thing in this edition. On Monday, Arsenal confirmed David Horseman as the new under-21 head coach, filling the vacancy created when Max Porter left for Stoke City . It completes a summer of change. Per Mertesacker stepped down as academy manager after eight years, a decision confirmed in January and effective at the end of last season, and has since taken a senior role with the German federation. His replacement started on August 1 with a new job title. Pascal De Maesschalck arrives as Academy Director, rather than academy manager, from a technical director role at Strasbourg and with previous academy stints at Monaco and Club Brugge . Berta cited his "outstanding track record in youth development." He inherits a department with an outstanding recent record for producing first-team players, a rather less outstanding one in the youth leagues themselves, and the perennial problem of holding on to the best fifteen-year-olds in London. The season starts now Competitive football is only now beginning. The under-21s open their EFL Trophy campaign today away at Barnet , in a group that also contains Leyton Orient and AFC Wimbledon , and start their Premier League 2 season at home to Crystal Palace on Saturday. That competition has been restructured again: 31 teams across three tiers, 20 league games each, top 16 into the play-offs. The under-18s started their season on August 15 away at West Bromwich Albion . The names to know, according to Jeorge Bird 's pre-season review published on August 13, are Marli Salmon and Theo Julienne . Salmon , a centre-back who turns 17 later this month, was the second-youngest Englishman ever to appear in the Champions League last season, at 16 years and 103 days. Julienne was described as the biggest winner of pre-season and played 62 minutes at right-back in the first-team friendly against Como at the Emirates on August 12, alongside Josh Ogunnaike , who signed his first professional contract on July 17. And then there is Max Dowman , who is the reason the rest of English football keeps checking the Hale End team sheets. He does not turn 16 until December and is already the youngest player and youngest goalscorer in Premier League history, at 16 years and 73 days for the latter. He scored, assisted and was named man of the match in the pre-season win over Girona on August 1, and he was on the bench in Cardiff on Sunday. He has signed scholarship terms; a professional contract follows when he turns 17. Nine first-year scholars were confirmed for 2026-27, among them Emerson Nwaneri , a midfielder and the younger brother of Ethan , who scored a hat-trick against Chelsea at under-16 level. The one bad piece of academy news is Louie Copley 's cruciate injury, which ends his season before it starts. Loan Watch Unusually thin this year. Two names, both this week. Charles Sagoe Jr , 21, at Kalmar FF in Sweden until January. Scored and assisted against Mjallby, scored again at IFK Goteborg on August 9, then started and played 73 minutes in a 4-0 defeat to Hammarby on Sunday. Manager Craig McLeish said the club had beaten off competition from Britain and Europe to get him. Arsenal Women Seven In, Six Out, and Three Weeks to Build a Team Renee Slegers has rebuilt half a squad in a summer. La Manga produced a defeat, a first goal for a new signing, and a very welcome sight at centre-back. The most significant thing that happened to Arsenal Women last week was not the result. It was Leah Williamson heading in an equaliser from an Olivia Smith corner in the 46th minute against AC Milan in La Manga on August 13. The England captain spent much of last season managing recurring knee, hamstring and calf problems, and missed the June World Cup qualifiers with a hamstring picked up in rehabilitation. Seeing her rise for a set piece at competitive tempo is the best piece of news of the women's pre-season. The match itself finished 3-2 to Milan , and it ended the Spanish training camp on a sour note. Thea Kyvag put the Italians ahead on 25 minutes after a defensive mix-up, Williamson levelled straight after the break, and Sara Stokic restored the lead around the 70th. Selina Cerci , one of seven summer arrivals, scored her first Arsenal goal with a strike from outside the area before Monica Renzotti won it in stoppage time. New goalkeeper Isabella Damm , signed from Brondby in July, made a smart double save. The rebuild, in full Seven players in, all but one on free transfers: Georgia Stanway from Bayern Munich , Ona Batlle from Barcelona on a four-year deal with an option, Geraldine Reuteler from Eintracht Frankfurt , Cerci from Hoffenheim , and goalkeepers Misa Rodriguez from Real Madrid and Damm from Brondby . The exception is Lisa Baum , 19, signed from RB Leipzig for a reported 600,000 euros, understood to be a record fee for a German women's league transfer. The departures cut deeper than the arrivals suggest. Katie McCabe left for Chelsea after ten years and the captaincy. Beth Mead went to Manchester City on a three-year deal. Laia Codina joined West Ham and Victoria Pelova crossed north London to Tottenham . Manuela Zinsberger went to Borussia Dortmund and Rosa Kafaji to London City Lionesses . That is a captain, a European Championship winner and a first-choice goalkeeper out of one dressing room in a single window. What they are rebuilding from Arsenal finished second in the Women's Super League last season, four points behind Manchester City , who won their first title in a decade and ended Chelsea 's six-year run. Second place was secured on the final day with a 3-1 win at Liverpool , Alessia Russo scoring twice. In Europe, the defending champions finished third in the league phase, beat Chelsea 3-2 on aggregate in the quarter-finals and lost the semi-final 4-3 on aggregate to OL Lyonnes . They did add a trophy: the inaugural FIFA Women's Champions Cup, won 3-2 after extra time against Corinthians at the Emirates on February 1, with goals from Olivia Smith , Lotte Wubben-Moy and Caitlin Foord . Slegers herself is secure, having signed an extension understood to run to the summer of 2029. Behind her, set-piece coach Chris Bradley left after two seasons and was replaced on July 31 by Nikita Runnacles , a former Ipswich Town goalkeeper and Brighton assistant, who will also help with goalkeeper coaching. The Season Ahead / Arsenal Women The league. The WSL expands to 14 clubs and 26 matches and begins on September 4. Arsenal open away at Brighton on the 6th. The venue. All thirteen home league fixtures will be played at the Emirates for a second consecutive season, confirmed in May. The audience. Nearly 500,000 tickets sold across all competitions last term, an average league attendance of 34,677, and 17,000 season-ticket holders. Europe. The Women's Champions League draw is on September 4 and Arsenal are in pot one. Gunners Abroad The World Cup Bill Comes Due There is no international break in August. There is, however, a squad still absorbing the cost of a tournament three Arsenal players won. The 2026-27 calendar has no August window, with the next international break falling in September in an extended format. So there are no Arsenal internationals to report on this week. The European calendar is equally quiet: the UEFA Super Cup was played in Salzburg on August 12 between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa , with no Arsenal involvement. What is still shaping the season is the summer that has just finished. Spain won the World Cup on July 19, beating Argentina 1-0 after extra time, and three Arsenal players were world champions: David Raya , Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino . A day earlier, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka had played in England's extraordinary 6-4 win over France in the third-place match, a game in which William Saliba lined up on the losing side. The consequences are visible in every team sheet. Raya , Zubimendi and Merino did not return to training until around August 10. Saka and Rice came back late enough that both began the Community Shield on the bench. And Saliba came back with an injury that will cost him the first two months of the title defence. Players from nations eliminated earlier, among them Kai Havertz with Germany, Viktor Gyokeres with Sweden, Piero Hincapie with Ecuador and Gabriel and Martinelli with Brazil, were back in mid to late July and are correspondingly further ahead. Arsenal have engaged the architects Populous, who designed the current stadium, to study expansion options. Reporting through the spring suggested anything from an additional 5,000 hospitality seats to a full redevelopment towards 80,000. No planning application has been submitted and executives are said to feel no pressure to decide. SHIRT SPONSOR. The new agreement covers the men's, women's and academy teams, training kit and stadium naming rights, and was negotiated by chief commercial officer Juliet Slot, who leaves the club later this year. THE ACCOUNTS. Arsenal's most recently published figures, for the year to May 2025 and released in March, showed record revenue of around £690m against a pre-tax loss of roughly £1m, with a wage bill of £346.8m at just over 50 per cent of turnover. The title and the run to the Champions League final should push the next set higher: the European campaign alone was worth about £123m in UEFA prize money. PRE-SEASON, FOR THE RECORD.
